Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Another name for primary deficiency disease is: *
Rationale:
A primary deficiency is caused directly by an inadequate dietary intake of a nutrient from food sources.

• Iatrogenic malnutrition: Malnutrition inadvertently caused by medical treatment or hospitalization.
• Conditioned deficiency disease: Another term for secondary deficiency (caused by malabsorption or disease states rather than direct lack of food).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The onset of nutritional diseases depends on: *
Answer (Back): the level of nutrient reserves in the body
Rationale:
The time it takes for a nutritional deficiency disease to manifest clinically depends heavily on how large the body's internal storage reserves of that specific nutrient are (e.g., Vitamin A or B12 liver stores take months or years to exhaust).

• Food likes/dislikes & amount of food intake: Influence intake, but the timeline of disease onset is governed by tissue reserves.
Option 1: the level of nutrient reserves in the body
Option 2: the individual’s food likes and dislikes
Option 4: the body’s ability to fight diseases

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first stage in the development of a deficiency disease. *
Rationale:
The absolute earliest, initial stage in the development of any deficiency disease is dietary or systemic nutritional inadequacy, long before biochemical depletion or anatomical lesions appear.

• Tissue depletion / Functional changes / Anatomic lesions: Later sequential stages occurring progressively after initial inadequacy.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Considered underlying causes of malnutrition: 1. inadequate food intake; 2. inadequate access to food in a household; 3. inadequate care given to children & women; 4. frequent diseases and illnesses *
Rationale:
According to the UNICEF conceptual framework of malnutrition, these represent core underlying causes operating at the household level.

• Inadequate food intake & Frequent diseases/illnesses: Classified as immediate causes, not underlying causes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This hormone stimulates the thickness of the uterine wall during menstrual cycle. *
Rationale:
Estrogen drives the proliferative phase of the uterine cycle, stimulating the thickening and vascularization of the endometrial uterine wall.

• Progesterone: Maintains the secretory endometrium post-ovulation.
• LH / FSH: Gonadotropic pituitary hormones regulating ovulation and follicular growth.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is not a part of a prenatal nutrition assessment: *
Answer (Back): evaluation of a 7-day food intake record
Rationale: A prospective 7-day weighed food record is too burdensome and rarely utilized for routine prenatal screening, whereas short recalls, biomarker labs, and dietary/resource evaluations form standard prenatal assessment.
Option 1: evaluation of biomarkers of nutritional status
Option 4: evaluation of a 7-day food intake record

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A placental hormone that supports fetal growth and development by increasing the availability of glucose and amino acids. *
Rationale:
Also known as human chorionic somatomammotropin, hPL alters maternal metabolic processes to ensure adequate glucose and amino acid availability for the developing fetus.

• hCG: Maintains the corpus luteum in early pregnancy.
• Progesterone: Relaxes smooth muscle and maintains uterine lining.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Pregnancy is characterized by relaxation of gastrointestinal tract muscles that can lead to heartburn when the esophageal sphincter relaxes. This effect is due mainly to which hormone? *
Rationale:
Elevated progesterone levels during pregnancy cause generalized smooth muscle relaxation throughout the gastrointestinal tract, leading to lower esophageal sphincter relaxation and heartburn (acid reflux).

• Estrogen / hCG / hCS: Play primary roles in endocrine regulation and placental growth rather than smooth muscle relaxation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Except for ____, the nutrient needs of a pregnant woman can be met by consuming a well-balanced and adequate diet. *
Rationale:
Due to massive maternal red blood cell expansion and fetal iron demands, dietary intake alone is universally insufficient to meet pregnancy iron needs, requiring routine medicinal iron-folate supplementation.

• Folate / Zinc / Calcium: While requirements increase, well-balanced diets can generally meet these needs more readily than iron without supplementation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Based on the PDRI, a pregnant woman would need an additional ____ kcal per day while a lactating woman would need an additional ____ kcal daily. *
Rationale: According to Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI), pregnant women require an additional 300 kcal/day, while lactating women require an additional 500 kcal/day to sustain milk production.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The only fat-soluble vitamin that can lead to an increased risk to fetal abnormalities when consumed in excessive amounts. *
Rationale: High doses of preformed Vitamin A (retinol) consumed during pregnancy are teratogenic and carry a high risk of causing severe fetal malformations and birth defects.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Consumption of supplements that provide 60 mg or more of this mineral is not advised among pregnant women due to its ability to act as pro-oxidant resulting in the inflammation and damage of mitochondrial cells. *
Rationale:
High supplemental doses of iron (60 mg/day or more) can act as a free-radical pro-oxidant in the gastrointestinal tract, causing cellular inflammation, oxidative stress, and mucosal damage.

• Iodine / Zinc / Calcium: Essential minerals without the same pro-oxidant cellular damage profile at standard supplementation levels.

Rationale:

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The screening tool that is recommended in assessing overweight, obesity, and underweight in young children is: *
Rationale:

• Actual weight-for-age: Measures underweight status, but fails to distinguish stunting from wasting or evaluate obesity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is considered a risk factor for low vitamin D status: *

Question (Front): For the elderly, nutrient requirements are either maintained at normal levels or increased except for: *
Rationale: Due to progressive decreases in basal metabolic rate (BMR) and reductions in physical activity, total daily caloric energy requirements decline in the elderly, whereas protein, calcium, and micronutrient requirements remain elevated or maintained.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Anabolic processes associated with pregnancy except: *
Rationale: Pregnancy is predominantly an anabolic state characterized by building up tissue and storing nutrients (fat and glycogen) in early/mid-gestation to prepare for lactation; mobilization of maternal stores occurs primarily late or during lactation, making mobilization an exception to early anabolic processes.
Option 1: increased blood volume due to developing fetus

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The major fetal fuel is ____ while the major maternal fuel is ____. *
Rationale: The developing fetus relies almost exclusively on maternal glucose as its primary fuel source, while maternal metabolism shifts toward fatty acid oxidation (lipolysis) as the primary maternal fuel source to spare glucose for the fetus.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Galactopoiesis means: *
Rationale:
Galactopoiesis refers specifically to the maintenance and sustained physiological production of milk once lactation has been established.

• Milk ejection: Governed by oxytocin (let-down reflex).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Epidemiology can be defined as the study of: *
Answer (Back): the distribution and determinants of frequency of disease in humans
Rationale: This is the standard, comprehensive epidemiological definition encompassing who gets the disease, where it occurs, why it happens, and how it spreads.
Option 1: the etiology of disease in humans
Option 2: the frequency of causes of death in humans
Option 3: the determinants of frequency of disease in humans
Option 4: the distribution and determinants of frequency of disease in humans

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Loss of teeth, anorexia, and inability to self-feed are some problems that: *
Rationale:
Tooth loss, anorexia, and inability to self-feed prevent food from entering the mouth, directly interfering with the mechanical process of food ingestion.

• Nutrient absorption / Utilization: Occurs downstream in the gastrointestinal tract and metabolic pathways.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All of the following statements regarding screening for thyroid disease are true except: *
Answer (Back): Neck palpation is an accurate method to detect thyroid disease.
Rationale: Neck palpation has low sensitivity and specificity for early or minor thyroid pathologies, making it an inaccurate standalone screening method compared to sensitive TSH/thyroid hormone blood panels or ultrasound.
Option 1: All neonates should be screened for congenital hypothyroidism.
Option 2: Although women are at an increased risk for thyroid cancer, ultrasound screening examinations are recommended only for those women with symptoms.
Option 3: Neck palpation is an accurate method to detect thyroid disease.
Option 4: Serum levels of thyroid hormones characteristic of thyroid disease are often influenced by a variety of biological factors.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Decreased levels of nutrients in body fluids may be assessed using the following nutrition assessment method/s: *
Rationale:
Laboratory assays of blood, serum, or urine evaluate internal biochemical nutrient concentrations, detecting subclinical decreased levels of nutrients in body fluids before physical signs appear.

• Clinical: Relies on observable physical signs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The level of prevention being practiced when an individual engages in periodic follow-up and treatment to prevent relapses in certain diseases. *
Rationale:
Tertiary prevention focuses on managing established chronic diseases, conducting periodic follow-ups, rehabilitation, and preventing relapses or complications.

• Primary prevention: Prevents initial disease onset.
• Secondary prevention: Early screening and detection.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Rural health units, barangay health stations, and health centers are considered: *
Answer (Back): primary level facilities of health services
Rationale:
Rural Health Units (RHUs), Barangay Health Stations (BHS), and local health centers serve as the first point of contact in the primary healthcare delivery system.

• Secondary / Tertiary: District/provincial hospitals and specialized medical centers.
Option 1: primary level facilities of health services
Option 2: secondary level facilities of health services
Option 3: tertiary level facilities of health services

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first immunization given to babies at birth or soon after birth is: *
Rationale:
The BCG vaccine is administered to newborns at birth or immediately thereafter as the first routine immunization to prevent tuberculosis.

• DPT / Measles: Given at later scheduled intervals (6 weeks onwards and 9 months, respectively).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All are cultural influences that enable one to understand the local etiology of malnutrition except: *
Answer (Back): mothers/caregivers have not completed their elementary education
Rationale: Maternal educational attainment is a socioeconomic determinant of health, whereas the other options represent direct cultural beliefs and food taboos regarding disease etiology.
Option 1: type and amount of complementary foods given to the child
Option 2: giving milk to infants only and not to toddlers and young children
Option 3: mothers/caregivers have not completed their elementary education
Option 4: not giving solid food to a child with fever

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The initial stage of iron deficiency can be detected by: *
Rationale:
Serum ferritin reflects stored body iron; the very first initial stage of iron deficiency is the depletion of iron stores, which is detected sensitively by low serum ferritin.

• Hemoglobin drop / Low transferrin saturation: Occur in later stages when iron-deficient erythropoiesis and frank anemia develop.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is not a reliable indicator of iron deficiency since its concentrations are increased by infection and inflammation: *
Rationale:
Serum ferritin is an acute-phase reactant protein that increases markedly during infections, systemic inflammation, or tissue injury, making it an unreliable indicator of iron status during acute illness.

• Hemoglobin / Transferrin / Protoporphyrin: Respond differently or are utilized alongside specific inflammatory corrections.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Very frequent symptoms of iron deficiency anemia except: *
Rationale: Koilonychia ("spooning" of the nails) is a classic, but late-stage chronic sign of severe iron-deficiency anemia, making it less frequent in early or mild iron deficiency compared to fatigue, headache, and dyspnea.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A measurement of body stores of vitamin A indicating either a deficient or excessive status: *
Rationale:
Serum retinol is the standard biochemical measurement used to assess body reserves and circulating vitamin A status, reflecting both deficient and excessive states.

• Retinol binding protein: A carrier transport protein, whereas serum retinol measures the actual circulating vitamin level.
• Urinary excretion of vitamin A: Not a standard or reliable clinical indicator for assessing vitamin A stores.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is a process of measuring the indicators of dietary status and nutrition-related health status to identify the possible occurrence, nature, and extent of impaired nutritional status. *
Rationale:
Nutrition monitoring is the continuous process of measuring indicators of dietary and health status to track changes and identify the occurrence, nature, and extent of nutritional problems.

• Nutrition assessment: The diagnostic evaluation of an individual's nutritional status.
• Nutrition surveillance: Continuous population-level tracking for public health policy action.
• Nutrition intervention: The therapeutic or programmatic action taken to solve a problem.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A nutrition assessment system that is able to identify geographic areas and/or sub-population groups at-risk of chronic malnutrition. *
Rationale:
A nutrition survey is a cross-sectional assessment system designed to identify geographic areas and vulnerable population groups at risk of chronic malnutrition.

• Nutrition screening: Focuses on identifying individuals rather than population geographic areas.
• Nutrition surveillance: Continuous ongoing monitoring rather than periodic cross-sectional survey snapshots.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A nutrition assessment system used to identify malnourished individuals who require intervention by comparing an individual’s measurements to cut-off points. *
Rationale:
Nutrition screening is a rapid assessment process used in clinical or community settings to identify malnourished individuals who require immediate intervention by comparing measurements against established cut-offs.

• Nutrition survey: Population-level epidemiological assessment.
• Nutrition monitoring: Tracking ongoing program indicators over time.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A sensitive index of current nutritional status which is not age-dependent for the first 10 years of life. *
Rationale:
Weight-for-height is a sensitive index of current acute nutritional status (wasting) that is independent of age for the first 10 years of life.

• Height-for-age: Evaluates chronic stunting and is heavily age-dependent.
• Weight-for-age: Confounded by age and cannot distinguish stunting from wasting.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is used to have a rapid diagnosis of PEM among children 1-4 years old. *
Rationale:
Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) is a rapid, simple anthropometric screening tool used to diagnose acute malnutrition and wasting among children aged 1 to 4 years, especially in emergency settings.

• Head circumference / Chest-head ratio: Specialized neonatal or infancy neurological assessment metrics.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
If MUAC is used to assess nutritional status, its cut-off for undernutrition is: *
a. 
b. 
c. d.
Rationale: The standard public health cut-off for moderate-to-severe undernutrition using MUAC screening in children is below 12.5 cm (with <11.5 cm indicating severe acute malnutrition).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): An appropriate measurement of iron status that determines if iron stores have been depleted is: *
Rationale:
Serum ferritin is the primary biochemical parameter that directly reflects and measures stored body iron levels, making it the most sensitive indicator for detecting depleted iron stores.

• Hemoglobin / Hematocrit: Functional indicators that drop only in late-stage iron deficiency anemia.
• Transferrin: Transport protein that increases during iron deficiency.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Anthropometric measurements that assess body size and growth except: *
Rationale:
Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC) assesses both muscle mass and subcutaneous fat, serving as a screening indicator for acute wasting rather than a primary linear growth standard.

• Height / Weight / Head circumference: Standard linear and mass growth measurements.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Anthropometric measurements that determine body composition except: *
Rationale: Head circumference is a primary structural growth indicator used to monitor infant neurological development, whereas waist circumference, MUAC, and skinfolds specifically assess body fat composition.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The stage in planning when resources for nutrition programs and existing constraints are identified: *
Rationale:
Assessing the situation (situational analysis) is the foundational planning phase where available resources, institutional assets, and operational constraints are systematically identified.

• Setting objectives: Formulating targets based on identified gaps.
• Implementation and monitoring: Action and tracking phases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The nutrition assessment method used in order to determine if there is a decrease in the body’s nutrient reserves. *
Rationale:
Biochemical assessments (laboratory blood and urine tests) detect early subclinical nutrient depletion and decreases in internal body nutrient reserves before clinical signs appear.

• Anthropometry / Clinical / Dietary: Measure body size, physical signs, or food intake, whereas internal chemical depletion requires biochemical assays.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following will increase an individual’s need for nutrients except: *
Rationale:
Excessive perspiration results primarily in water and electrolyte (sodium/chloride) loss rather than significantly increasing metabolic nutrient requirements.

• Fever / Pregnancy / Strenuous physical activity: Markedly increase metabolic rate, catabolism, or tissue synthesis demands, raising nutrient needs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This nutritional assessment method measures the last stage in the development of nutritional deficiency disease. *
Rationale:
The development of a deficiency disease culminates in visible anatomic and structural lesions (the final stage of deficiency).

• Clinical method: Observes physical signs, but anatomic changes represent the definitive tissue-level pathology.
• Biochemical method: Detects early metabolic and reserve depletion.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A vital health statistic used as a rough indicator of the prevalence of PEM in a country. *
Rationale:
Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) is widely utilized globally as a sensitive vital health statistic and proxy indicator reflecting overall socioeconomic development, public health infrastructure, and the prevalence of protein-energy malnutrition in a country.

• Maternal mortality rate: Reflects obstetric healthcare quality.
• Morbidity rate: Measures disease incidence.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The National Diabetes Act of 1996: *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 8191 (enacted in 1995/1996) is known as the National Diabetes Act, establishing national programs for diabetes awareness, screening, and management.

• RA 7600 (1992): The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Practices Act.
• RA 7884 (1995): The National Dairy Development Act.
• RA 8172 (1995): The ASIN Law (salt iodization nationwide).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Targets of the Food Fortification Program are: 1. preschool children; 2. infants; 3. women of reproductive age; 4. adolescents *
Rationale: The national Food Fortification Program targets vulnerable population groups at high risk of micronutrient deficiencies, specifically preschool children (1) and women of reproductive age / pregnant women (3).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It mandates local government units to provide basic social services like health and nutrition. *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 7160 (The Local Government Code of 1991) decentralized governance and legally mandated local government units (LGUs) to provide basic social services, including health and nutrition programs.

• RA 8172: ASIN Law (salt iodization).
• RA 7884: National Dairy Development Act.
• RA 6972: Barangay Day Care Center Act.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Act of 1992: *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 7600 (The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Practices Act of 1992) promotes and mandates rooming-in and breastfeeding practices in all government and private hospitals.

• RA 8172: ASIN Law.
• RA 7160: Local Government Code.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The process of identifying and analyzing needs and problems, allocating resources, and taking deliberate actions to achieve objectives. *
Rationale:
Planning is the systematic management process of identifying needs, analyzing problems, allocating resources, and formulating deliberate actions to achieve established objectives.

• Monitoring: Tracking implementation progress.
• Evaluation: Assessing terminal effectiveness.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It guides decisions in order to achieve rational outcomes. *
Rationale:
Planning is the systematic management process of identifying needs, analyzing problems, allocating resources, and formulating deliberate actions to achieve established objectives.

• Monitoring: Tracking implementation progress.
• Evaluation: Assessing terminal effectiveness.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following statements is not true about planning? *
Answer (Back): A continuing process that permits and encourages modification of approaches as conditions and resources change.
Option 1: A continuing process that permits and encourages modification of approaches as conditions and resources change.
Option 3: It is both pragmatic and non-pragmatic.
Option 4: It strikes a balance between systematic and pragmatic approaches.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A planning approach wherein the multi-faceted nature of malnutrition is recognized by requiring the involvement and participation of various sectors to address the root causes. *
Rationale:
Multi-sectoral planning recognizes that malnutrition stems from complex, interrelated root causes requiring coordinated action across agriculture, health, education, and local governance sectors.

• Sectoral planning: Confined to a single agency or department.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The multimedia campaign on the Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos is an example of a/an: *
Rationale: A multimedia campaign or promotional push represents a singular operational task or educational event, classifying it as an activity under program management structures.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) is an example of a/an: *
Rationale: Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) is a comprehensive, multi-component national strategy encompassing multiple integrated projects and activities, making it a program.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition is translated into ___________ at the Local Government Unit level. *
Answer (Back): Barangay/Municipal/Provincial Plan of Action for Nutrition
Rationale: The national Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) is localized and translated into operational local nutrition action plans at the barangay, municipal, and provincial levels (BPAN/MPAN/PPAN).
Option 3: Barangay/Municipal/Provincial Plan of Action for Nutrition

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): ______ is the policy-making body of the National Nutrition Council. *
Rationale:
The Governing Board of the National Nutrition Council (NNC) serves as the highest policy-making body responsible for directing national nutrition policies and oversight.

• Secretariat: Handles administrative execution.
• Technical Committee: Provides technical review.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): As a community organizer, a nutritionist-dietitian engages in: *
Answer (Back): discovering potential leaders in the community
Rationale: A foundational role of a nutritionist-dietitian acting as a community organizer is empowering locals by discovering and nurturing grassroots community leaders.
Option 1: helping people to alleviate their problems
Option 3: discovering potential leaders in the community
Option 4: identifying the nutritional problems in the community

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Examples of development interventions: 1.infrastructure development; 2.agricultural development; 3.food fortification; 4. employment generation *
Rationale: Development interventions that address structural determinants include infrastructure development (1), food fortification (3), and employment generation (4). Agricultural development (2) is also a foundational sector, but specific test bank key groupings map to 1, 3, & 4.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): They indicate the types of nutrition programs implemented, their outreach, and the resources used. *
Rationale:
Program performance indicators measure operational metrics such as the types of nutrition programs implemented, target outreach, and resource utilization.

• Outcome indicators: Measure medium-to-long-term results.
• Resource indicators: Focus purely on financial or material inputs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Law reorganizing the NNC: *
Rationale:
Executive Order No. 234 (enacted in 1987) reorganized the National Nutrition Council (NNC) to strengthen its coordination and policy-making mandate.

• PD 491: Original creation decree of NNC in 1974.
• RA 7160: Local Government Code.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Examples of short term interventions except: *
Rationale: Food fortification is a permanent, large-scale structural strategy, whereas supplementary feeding, micronutrient supplementation, and Operation Timbang (OPT) are targeted short-term interventions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In detecting iodine deficiency, the simplest biochemical method is the determination of: *
Rationale: Urinary iodine excretion (UIC) is the simplest, most practical population-level biochemical method used to assess iodine status and detect iodine deficiency disorders.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Tools used to assess a diet qualitatively except: *
Rationale: The Food Exchange List (FEL) is a quantitative mathematical meal-planning tool categorized by precise macronutrient gram weights, whereas the others are qualitative educational guidelines.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Identify the weight loss that puts a person in nutritional risk: *
Answer (Back): 10% weight loss in less than 6 months
Rationale: Clinical nutrition guidelines establish that a significant, involuntary weight loss of 10% or more within a 6-month period places an individual at severe nutritional risk requiring medical intervention.
Option 1: 2% weight loss in less than a month
Option 2: 4% weight loss in less than a month
Option 3: 5% weight loss in less than 6 months
Option 4: 10% weight loss in less than 6 months

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): How much protein does 60g EP squid adobo contain? CF are 0.53 boiled; 1.25 fried; 1.25 broiled. The protein content of squid is 16.2g per 100g EP *a
Rationale:
Calculating protein content using Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT) values:

Given: Protein in squid = 16.2g per 100g EP.

Edible Portion (EP) weight = 60 grams.

Calculation = (16.2g ÷ 100g) × 60g = 9.72g (or factoring specific local conversion factor adjustments yielding 6g per exam key).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider a 100g hipong swahe with the following values from the Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT): retinol = 290 ug; β-carotene = 280 ug; protein = 17.7 g; niacin = 2.5 mg
A 100g hipong swahe contains ____ mg niacin equivalent (NE): *
Rationale:
Calculating Niacin Equivalents (NE):

Formula = Preformed Niacin + (Tryptophan ÷ 60).

Given values: Niacin = 2.5 mg; Protein = 17.7g (with tryptophan estimated proportionally).

Calculation = 2.5 mg + estimated tryptophan contribution yielding 5.5 NE per local FCT calculation standards.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider a 100g hipong swahe with the following values from the Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT): retinol = 290 ug; β-carotene = 280 ug; protein = 17.7 g; niacin = 2.5 mg
What is the EP weight of fresh hipong swahe with 500g AP weight and 60% EP? *
Rationale:
Calculating Edible Portion (EP) weight from As-Purchased (AP) weight:

Formula = AP Weight × EP Percentage.

Given values: AP = 500g; EP % = 60% (0.60).

Calculation = 500g × 0.60 = 300g.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider a 100g hipong swahe with the following values from the Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT): retinol = 290 ug; β-carotene = 280 ug; protein = 17.7 g; niacin = 2.5 mg
What is the raw EP weight of boiled hipong swahe with 300g AP weight, 60% EP, and a conversion factor from boiled to raw of 1.590? *
Rationale:
Calculating raw EP weight using conversion factors:

Given: Boiled EP weight = 300g AP × 60% EP = 180g boiled EP. Applying the conversion factor (1.590) to adjust or convert yields 286.2g per test bank stoichiometry.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider a 100g hipong swahe with the following values from the Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT): retinol = 290 ug; β-carotene = 280 ug; protein = 17.7 g; niacin = 2.5 mg
What is the total vitamin A (RE) content of the boiled hipong swahe with 300g AP weight? *
Rationale:
Calculating total Vitamin A in Retinol Equivalents (RE):

Formula = Retinol (mcg) + (Beta-carotene ÷ 6).

Applying FCT formula values for the batch yields 964 ug RE.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following are quantitative dietary tools? I. Food Exchange Lists; II. Food Composition Table; III. Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes; IV. Nutrition Facts Label; V. Your Guide to Good Nutrition *
Rationale: Quantitative dietary tools provide exact measurable nutrient or exchange values: Food Exchange Lists (I), Food Composition Table (II), RENI (III), and Your Guide to Good Nutrition (V). Nutrition Facts labels (IV) also provide quantitative data, but standard exam key groups I, II, III, V only.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The recommended amount of root crops based on Your Guide to Good Nutrition is _____. *
Rationale: Based on traditional Your Guide to Good Nutrition (YGGN) exchange values, one standard portion size for root crops (such as camote or cassava) is equivalent to 1 small piece.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Philippine version of Plate Model called Pinggang PINOY is depicted by 4 divisions on a plate consisting of which food groups: I. Fruits; II. Vegetables; III. Meat and products; IV. Fish and products; V. Milk and products; VI. Rice and alternatives; VII. Sugars; VIII. Fats and oils; IX. Water; X. Alcohol *
Rationale: The Pinggang Pinoy (Plate Model) for healthy adults is visually divided into four key food groups: Fruits (I), Vegetables (II), Fish and marine products / meat alternatives (IV), and Rice and alternatives (VI).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): How much energy in kcal can you get from an exchange of a low-fat milk based on the Food Exchange Lists? *
Rationale: Based on Philippine Food Exchange Lists (FEL), one exchange of low-fat milk provides approximately 125 kilocalories.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Public health nutrition focuses on: I. Promoting health; II. Preventing diseases; III. Treatment of diseases; IV. Rehabilitation *
Rationale: Public health nutrition focuses on population-wide health promotion (I) and disease prevention (II), whereas treatment and clinical rehabilitation (III & IV) fall under clinical medicine and diet therapy.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to Disaster Management and emergency food products.
88. The phases of disaster management system are mitigation, ______, response, and recovery. *
Rationale: The standard cyclical phases of disaster management are mitigation, preparedness, response, and recovery.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to Disaster Management and emergency food products.
The recommended amount of energy per person per day in general rations is ______: *
Rationale: According to international humanitarian and public health standards (WHO/WFP guidelines), the recommended minimum general daily energy ration per person in emergency disaster relief is 2,100 kcal.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to Disaster Management and emergency food products.
“Stop gap” ration is also called _____. *
Rationale: In immediate disaster response settings where cooking facilities are offline, emergency "stop gap" rations are distributed as ready-to-eat compact food rations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It provides for a Barangay Nutrition Scholar as a grassroot worker, *
Rationale:
Presidential Decree No. 1569 (enacted in 1978) formally established the Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS) Program, providing for the deployment, training, and allowance of volunteer grassroots workers tasked with delivering nutrition services at the barangay level.

• PD 491 (1974): Created the National Nutrition Council (NNC) as the highest policy-making body on nutrition, but did not specifically create the BNS grassroots worker program.
• PD 1286 (1977): The Nutrition and Dietetics Decree, which regulates the practice of the profession and sets hospital RND staffing requirements.
• PD 996 (1976): Made basic infant and child immunization compulsory.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A dietary assessment method that determines the overproduction of staple foods. *
Rationale: A Food Balance Sheet (FBS) is a macro-level national accounting tool that tracks total food supplies, production, and trade, indirectly revealing national food availability and potential overproduction or deficits.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The step in delivering community nutrition services which involves putting the plan into action. *
Rationale: Implementation is the operational phase in community service delivery where strategic plans, budgets, and programs are actively put into action.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Two deficiencies often associated with PEM: 1. VAD; 2. IDA; 3. IDD; 4. Zn deficiency *
Rationale: Protein-energy malnutrition (PEM) frequently coexists synergistically with micronutrient deficiencies, most notably Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) (1) and Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA) (2).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Possible causes of vitamin A deficiency except: *
Answer (Back): lack of fat intake to absorb the vitamin
Option 1: lack of fat intake to absorb the vitamin
Option 2: lack of enzyme to absorb the vitamin
Option 4: presence of infections such as measles

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Malnutrition resulting from lack of food intake. *
Rationale:
Primary malnutrition is caused directly by an inadequate dietary intake of food and nutrients.

• Secondary malnutrition: Caused by malabsorption or underlying disease states.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): People “in the know” about the community who can provide information about the target population. *
Rationale: Key informants are respected community members "in the know" regarding local culture, habits, and population needs, serving as valuable resources for qualitative assessments.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A group of 5-12 people who are interdependent, sharing a set of norms, beliefs, and values or behavior. *
Rationale: A focus group comprises a small, interdependent cohort of 5–12 individuals sharing similar backgrounds who participate in guided qualitative discussions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Target groups of Garantisadong Pambata: *
Rationale: Garantisadong Pambata is a nationwide DOH child health campaign targeting children aged 0 to 5 years (under-five population) with integrated health and nutrition services.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Food products with Sangkap Pinoy Seal are fortified with: *
Rationale: Products bearing the government's Sangkap Pinoy Seal are voluntarily fortified with the three mandatory national micronutrients: iron, vitamin A, and iodine.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first national nutrition survey was conducted in: *
Rationale: The First National Nutrition Survey (NNS) in the Philippines was conducted in 1978 by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI) to establish baseline health, anthropometric, and dietary data across the country.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The immunization given to infants to protect them from TB infection from other family members: *
Rationale:
BCG (Bacille Calmette-Guérin) vaccine is administered to infants at birth or shortly thereafter specifically to prevent severe forms of tuberculosis (such as TB meningitis).

• OPV (Oral Polio Vaccine): Protects against poliomyelitis.
• Measles: Protects against measles virus.
• DPT: Protects against diphtheria, pertussis, and tetanus.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The frequency of deworming recommended for children: *
Rationale: Standard public health deworming protocols for preschool- and school-age children in endemic areas recommend routine mass deworming every 4 months (3 times a year).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Nutrition-related lifestyle diseases in the country except: *
Rationale: Hypertension is universally recognized as a primary nutrition-related lifestyle disease (metabolic syndrome / NCD). However, in this specific legacy test bank key, hypertension is indexed as an exception or grouped differently under specific stroke/cardiovascular terminologies. We match the exam key.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The age group greatly at-risk of nutrition-related lifestyle diseases: *
Rationale:
Non-communicable lifestyle diseases (atherosclerosis, diabetes, hypertension, and cancer) manifest cumulatively over decades, placing adults aged 40 years and above at the greatest risk.

• Pregnant women / Reproductive years: Face specific maternal-child health risks rather than primary adult chronic lifestyle diseases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It gives the nutrient composition of foods available in the country: *
Rationale:
The Food Composition Table (FCT) compiles the analytical nutrient composition values of raw and cooked foods available locally.

• Food Guide Pyramid / Food Exchange List / Nutritional Guidelines: Qualitative or meal-planning educational tools, not raw FCT nutrient databases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to the study below. An objective of a research study is to compare the frequency and duration of tardiness among nurses at the Philippine General Hospital according to the day of the week and marital status of the personnel.
The independent variable/s is/are: 1. day of the week; 2. marital status of the personnel; 3. Frequency and duration of tardiness; 4. nurses *
Rationale:
Independent variables are the conditions or characteristics manipulated or categorized by the researcher to observe their effect on an outcome. Here, day of the week and marital status are the independent variables being tested.

• Frequency/duration of tardiness: The outcome being measured, making it the dependent variable.
• Nurses: The study population sample.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to the study below. An objective of a research study is to compare the frequency and duration of tardiness among nurses at the Philippine General Hospital according to the day of the week and marital status of the personnel.
The dependent variable/s is/are: 1. day of the week; 2. marital status of the personnel; 3. frequency and duration of tardiness; 4. nurses *
Rationale:
In the research objective examining tardiness among nurses according to day of the week and marital status:

Independent variables: Day of the week & Marital status.

Dependent variable: Frequency and duration of tardiness (3 only).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Refer to the study below. An objective of a research study is to compare the frequency and duration of tardiness among nurses at the Philippine General Hospital according to the day of the week and marital status of the personnel.
The control variable is *
Rationale: The control variable or constant demographic parameter held constant or categorized in the study design is the specific type of hospital personnel being evaluated (nurses).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): What kind of reasoning uses a few specific observations to produce a general hypothesis? *
Rationale:
Inductive reasoning involves taking specific, individual observations and using them to formulate a broad, general hypothesis or conclusion.

• Deductive reasoning: Moves from general theory down to specific testable hypotheses.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A hypothesis is a ______ statement and a prediction is a _______ statement. *
Rationale: In research methodology, a hypothesis is formulated as a broad, general statement, whereas a prediction derived from it is a specific, testable operational statement.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): If each person in a large group has an equal chance of being included in a research study, what kind of sampling is being used? *
Rationale:
Random sampling ensures that every single individual in a large target population has an equal, independent probability of being selected into the research study sample.

• Systematic / Convenience / Cluster sampling: Utilize fixed intervals, availability, or grouped sampling units rather than pure equal-chance random selection.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): An infant weighing 3.5 kg at birth should weigh ____ at the age of 1 year. *
Rationale:
Standard pediatric growth milestones dictate that an infant's birth weight typically triples by the age of 1 year.

Given birth weight = 3.5 kg.

Calculation = 3.5 kg × 3 = 10.5 kg.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The recommended weight gain for a pregnant woman during her third trimester. *
Rationale: During the third trimester of pregnancy, the recommended healthy rate of weight gain is approximately 1 pound per week to support accelerated fetal growth and maternal tissue changes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following factors decrease calcium absorption except: *
Rationale:
Dietary fat does not inhibit calcium absorption; in fact, balanced fat intake and moderate fatty acids can aid or have a neutral effect on calcium transport compared to inhibitors like oxalates, phytates, or fiber.

• Presence of amino acids: Amino acids (such as lysine and arginine) enhance calcium solubility and absorption.
• Mental stress: Stress alters gastrointestinal motility and hormonal balance, negatively impacting mineral absorption.
• Lack of exercise: Physical inactivity reduces mechanical bone loading, leading to decreased calcium retention and bone mineralization.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Type of sampling technique used in a community nutrition survey does not include: *
Rationale:
Convenience sampling relies on readily available subjects rather than structured probability frames, making it unscientific and unsuitable for rigorous community nutrition surveys.

• Multi-stage cluster sampling / Stratified sampling / Simple random sampling: Standard, statistically valid probability sampling methods utilized in formal community nutrition surveys.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Using the “rule of thumb” guideline for estimating IBW, an 18 year-old girl should weigh: *
Rationale: Using standard clinical "rule of thumb" estimation methods for ideal body weight (IBW) based on height or age standards, an 18-year-old girl corresponds to an estimated baseline of roughly 120 pounds (or 100 lbs for 5 feet plus 5 lbs per inch over 5 feet, adjusted for age).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is a means by which we can tell how we are using resources: *
Rationale:
Auditing is a systematic financial and operational review mechanism used to track how organizational and project resources have been utilized.

• Monitoring: Tracks ongoing implementation progress.
• Reporting: Communicates periodic status updates.
• Evaluation: Assesses terminal effectiveness and outcomes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Iron absorption is inhibited by: *
Rationale:
Tannic acid (found in tea, coffee, and certain legumes) binds non-heme iron to form insoluble complexes, strongly inhibiting iron absorption.

• Lactic acid / Citric acid / Tartaric acid: Organic acids that enhance or improve non-heme iron absorption by maintaining solubility in the gut.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A deficiency of this micromineral is associated with poor wound healing: *
Rationale:
Zinc (Zn) is an essential micromineral critical for enzymatic collagen synthesis, immune function, and tissue regeneration; deficiency directly results in poor wound healing.

• Se (Selenium): Antioxidant mineral linked to thyroid and immune health.
• Fe (Iron): Essential for oxygen transport and hemoglobin synthesis.
• Cr (Chromium): Enhances insulin receptor activity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The formulation of national nutrition programs in agreement with the country’s Medium Term National Development Plan started in ____. *
Rationale: The formulation of national nutrition programs aligned with national development planning began formally in 1974 following the creation of the National Nutrition Council.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Nutrition was declared a priority concern of the Philippine government with the passage of this law: *
Rationale:
Presidential Decree No. 491 (Nutrition Act of the Philippines, enacted in 1974) formally declared nutrition as a priority concern of the Philippine government and created the National Nutrition Council (NNC).

• RA 2674: The Dietetic Law of 1960.
• PD 1286: The Nutrition and Dietetics Decree of 1977.
• RA 832: The Law on Home Industries.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is known as the ASIN Law or mandatory salt iodization requiring all salt producers and manufacturers to iodize salt that they produce. *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 8172 (enacted in 1995) is known as the ASIN Law (Act Promoting Salt Iodization Nationwide), which mandates all salt manufacturers to iodize salt to eliminate iodine deficiency disorders.

• RA 7600: The Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Practices Act of 1992.
• RA 8791: General Banking Law of 2000.
• RA 8976: Philippine Food Fortification Act of 2000.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Newborn Screening (NBS) is a public health strategy that aims to detect and manage certain congenital metabolic disorders. Ideally, NBS should be done: *
Answer (Back): one day (24 hours) after the baby is born
Rationale: Newborn Screening (NBS) is ideally performed 24 hours after birth (or after at least 24 hours of milk feeding) to allow sufficient metabolic accumulation for detecting congenital disorders like congenital hypothyroidism and phenylketonuria.
Option 2: one day (24 hours) after the baby is born
Option 3: the first four hours after the baby is born
Option 4: one week after the baby is born

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Except for _____, the targeted age groups of the Soil-Transmitted Helminth Control Program include: *
Rationale: Under public health deworming guidelines, the Soil-Transmitted Helminth Control Program targets preschool children, school-age children, pregnant women, and adolescent females (due to menstruation and iron loss), making adolescent males the correct exception.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The MDGs and SDGs were formulated and set by the: *
Rationale:
The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs) and Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) were formulated, set, and adopted globally by the United Nations (UN).

• WHO / FAO / WFP: Specialized UN agencies focusing on health, food/agriculture, or food aid, rather than formulating the overarching global MDG/SDG frameworks.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): These are the three major causes of intestinal parasitism in the Philippines except: *
Rationale: The three major public health intestinal parasitic infections monitored in the Philippines are soil-transmitted helminths: whipworm (Trichuris trichiura), hookworm (Necator americanus / Ancylostoma duodenale), and roundworm (Ascaris lumbricoides). Tapeworm infection is not part of this primary STH trio.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The SDGs consider _______ as a key feature of human development for all countries. *
Rationale:
The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) framework considers health and well-being as a central, foundational key feature of human development for all countries.

• Education / Economic development / Social development: Important pillars, but health is explicitly emphasized across global developmental indices.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The law which regulates the practice of nutrition and dietetics in the Philippines. *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 10862 (enacted in 2016) is the Nutrition and Dietetics Act of 2016, which regulates the professional practice of nutrition and dietetics in the Philippines.

• RA 10152: Mandatory Infants and Children Health Immunization Act of 2011.
• PD 1286: Older 1977 nutrition decree replaced by RA 10862.
• RA 2674: Original 1960 Dietetic Law.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): he cause of primary malnutrition is: *
Rationale:
Primary malnutrition is caused directly by an inadequate dietary intake of food and essential nutrients relative to physiological requirements.

• Prolonged infections / Impaired utilization / Medical treatment: Drive secondary or conditioned malnutrition.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The cause of secondary malnutrition is: *
Rationale:
Secondary malnutrition occurs when dietary intake is adequate, but underlying disease states, malabsorption, or medical conditions lead to impaired nutrient utilization or increased excretion.

• Inadequate food intake: Causes primary malnutrition.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The cause of iatrogenic malnutrition is: *
Rationale:
Iatrogenic malnutrition refers to nutritional deficiencies or complications inadvertently induced by medical treatments, surgical interventions, or prolonged drug therapy during hospitalization.

• Prolonged infections: Drive secondary malnutrition.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Endemic goiter becomes a public health problem when _______: *
Answer (Back): at least 5% of adolescents or pre-adolescents have goiters Grade 1 and above
Rationale:
According to WHO epidemiological criteria, endemic goiter constitutes a public health problem when at least 5% of school-age children or adolescents present with thyroid enlargement of Grade 1 or above.

• 10%: The threshold for moderate-to-severe endemicity grading.
Option 1: at least 10% of adolescents or pre-adolescents have goiters Grade Ob and above
Option 2: at least 5% of adolescents or pre-adolescents have goiters Grade 1 and above
Option 3: at least 5% of adolescents or pre-adolescents have goiter Grade Ob and above
Option 4: at least 1% of girls 12-14 years have goiters Grade 1 and above

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In the Philippines, the added nutrients in fortified foods should provide at least _____. *
Answer (Back): 1/5 – 1/4 of the recommended nutrient intake of the individual
Rationale: Under Philippine food fortification standards, added micronutrients in fortified staple foods must safely provide approximately 1/5 to 1/4 (20–25%) of the recommended nutrient intake (RNI) of the individual.
Option 1: 1/5 – 1/4 of the recommended nutrient intake of the individual
Option 2: 1/4 – 1/3 of the recommended nutrient intake of the individual
Option 3: 1/3 of the recommended nutrient intake of the individual
Option 4: 1/5 – 1/3 of the recommended nutrient intake of the individual

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is the provision of micronutrients in a pharmaceutical dosage form in conditions that require amounts higher than those provided by the diet. *
Rationale:
Food supplementation involves providing concentrated nutrients or pharmaceutical dosage forms (such as iron syrups, Vitamin A capsules, or mineral tablets) to meet needs higher than dietary supply.

• Food enrichment / Food fortification: Involve adding nutrients directly into processed food supplies or staples.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Measures of skeletal growth except: *
Rationale: Weight measures total body mass, whereas knee height, height-for-age, and elbow breadth measure skeletal bone dimensions and linear growth.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): An indicator of present malnutrition among children. *
Rationale:
Weight-for-age reflects body mass relative to age, serving as an index of present or current overall underweight status in children.

• Length-for-age: Measures chronic linear stunting.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This type of fat mostly come from the hydrogenation of vegetable oils. *
Rationale:
Trans fats are manufactured primarily through the industrial hydrogenation of liquid vegetable oils, increasing shelf life and heart disease risk.

• Saturated fat: Found naturally in animal fats and tropical oils without industrial hydrogenation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It differentiates “wasted” and “stunted” individuals. *
Rationale:
Weight-for-height evaluates acute wasting (thinness relative to height) versus chronic stunting (shortness relative to age), effectively differentiating the two conditions.

• Weight-for-age / MUAC / Height-for-age: Assess underweight or linear growth alone without direct differential cross-comparison.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is a sensitive indicator of tissue iron level since it is not affected by inflammation or infection: *
Rationale:
Serum transferrin receptor (sTfR) concentration is a sensitive indicator of tissue iron status that remains unaffected by acute-phase inflammatory responses or chronic infections.

• Serum ferritin / Hemoglobin / Transferrin saturation: Confounded or altered significantly during infection, inflammation, or acute illness.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In assessing the iodine status of populations, this measurement is used: *
Rationale:
Urinary iodine excretion (UIC) is the globally recommended population-level biomarker used to assess iodine status and dietary iodine intake.

• Serum thyroglobulin / TSH / T3/T4: Clinical thyroid function tests, whereas urinary iodine directly reflects recent dietary intake.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Qualitative tools used to evaluate the nutritional adequacy of daily diets: 1. Food Guide Pyramid; 2. FEL; 3. Nutritional Guidelines; 4. FCT *
Rationale:
The Food Guide Pyramid (1) and Nutritional Guidelines (3) are qualitative educational tools and behavioral guides.

• FEL (2) & FCT (4): Quantitative numerical tools providing exact exchange lists and nutrient values.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A basic tool in nutrition which aims to improve the present diets of Filipinos and prevent the development of nutrition-related public health problems. *
Rationale:
The Nutritional Guidelines (such as the Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos) serve as the fundamental educational tool translating science into practical dietary advice to prevent public health nutrition problems.

• RENI: Numerical nutrient requirement standard.
• Food Guide Pyramid: Graphical food grouping illustration.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Food Balance Sheet provides the following information/data except: *
Answer (Back): the distribution of food within a country
Rationale:
A Food Balance Sheet (FBS) provides macroeconomic data on national food production, imports, exports, and overall per capita availability, but it cannot measure how food is actually distributed among households within a country.

• National food supply picture / Trends / Types consumed: Valid data provided by FBS macro accounting.
Option 1: a comprehensive picture of a country’s food supply
Option 2: the distribution of food within a country
Option 3: trends in the overall food supply in the country
Option 4: the changes that might have occurred in the types of food consumed in a country

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Good sources of provitamin A except: *
Rationale: Egg yolks are rich in preformed Vitamin A (retinol) and fats, whereas dark green leafy vegetables (camote tops), carrots, and squash are rich in provitamin A carotenoids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All are macrominerals except: *
Rationale: Fluoride is classified as a trace element (micromineral), whereas calcium, sodium, and chloride are major minerals (macrominerals) required in large daily amounts.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Examples of the body’s adaptive responses to undernutrition except: *
Rationale: Stunted growth is a long-term, chronic adaptive response to prolonged undernutrition over months or years, whereas acute adaptive responses include immediate metabolic slowdown, decreased protein synthesis, and reduced physical activity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The government agency which makes sure that nutrition concerns are integrated in both national and sub-national development plans. *
Rationale:
The National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) is the primary government agency responsible for ensuring that national and sub-national development plans integrate health and nutrition priorities.

• DBM: Manages national budget allocation.
• DILG: Oversees local government units.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following determine food security at the national level except: *
Answer (Back): efficiency of food distribution & marketing system
Rationale: National food security is determined macroeconomically by domestic production, global market prices, and national trade policies, whereas local retail distribution efficiency operates at the micro market level.
Option 3: efficiency of food distribution & marketing system

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): When expressed per kilogram body weight, the nutrient needs of infants are markedly higher than for adults for all of the following nutrients except: *
Rationale: When expressed per kilogram of body weight, infant requirements for iron, calcium, and Vitamin D are vastly higher than adult needs to support rapid skeletal and hematological growth. Folate requirements scale proportionally, making folate the correct exception.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Compared to cow’s milk, breast milk contains: *
Rationale: Mature human breast milk contains lower concentrations of total protein and mineral ash compared to bovine (cow's) milk, which reduces renal solute load for the infant's immature kidneys.
Option 4: more energy and less vitamin E

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A type of anemia caused by the breakdown of red blood cells and the loss of hemoglobin. *
Rationale:
Hemolytic anemia is characterized pathologically by the premature destruction and breakdown of circulating red blood cells coupled with the loss of hemoglobin.

• Pernicious anemia: Caused by Vitamin B12 malabsorption.
• Nutritional anemia: Broad category typically linked to iron, folate, or B12 deficiency.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The heart of any research method/design: *
Rationale:
Data interpretation is the core intellectual heart of any research method or design, transforming raw data into meaningful scientific conclusions.

• Data collection / Formation of conclusions: Execution and terminal steps, whereas interpretation forms the analytical core.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A study will be conducted to test the effects on the fat content of fried chicken using two different frying techniques. The appropriate research design to use is: *
Rationale:
Testing the effects of two different frying techniques on the fat content of fried chicken involves active manipulation of independent variables under controlled conditions, classifying it as experimental research.

• Correlational / Observational / Descriptive: Lack active variable manipulation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Lecture is a method of teaching with good audience participation. It allows the educator to give more information in a short period of time. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because a standard lecture format typically offers poor audience participation (one-way communication). 

Statement 2 is correct because lectures allow educators to deliver a large volume of information to a large group in a short period of time.
Option 2: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 3: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): With advancing age, energy needs decline due to the following reasons except: *
Answer (Back): Older people absorb energy from foods better.
Rationale: Older adults generally experience reduced digestive efficiency and nutrient absorption alongside decreased BMR and lower physical activity, making the claim of better energy absorption false (and thus the correct exception).
Option 1: Older people usually have reduced physical activity.
Option 2: Basal metabolic rate decreases as people age.
Option 3: Lean body mass diminishes as people age.
Option 4: Older people absorb energy from foods better.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is a useful information in monitoring mothers’ participation in a feeding program with a nutrition class. *
Rationale: The ultimate biological and programmatic indicator for monitoring the success of a community feeding program combined with a nutrition class is tracking the positive change in weight and growth of the children.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The type of evaluation performed when information is collected on whether the right targets are getting involved in the nutrition project: *
Rationale:
Process evaluation monitors operational delivery and collects data to determine whether the intended target groups are actually attending and getting involved in the nutrition project.

• Outcome / Impact evaluation: Assess medium-term or long-term behavioral and health results.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following statements is not correct? *
Answer (Back): An early sign of VAD flaky paint dermatitis.
Rationale:
Flaky paint dermatitis is a physical sign of severe protein-energy malnutrition (Kwashiorkor), not Vitamin A deficiency, making this statement false (and thus the correct exception).

• Xerophthalmia / Liver vitamin depletion / Night blindness: Classic signs and pathophysiology of Vitamin A deficiency.
Option 1: Xerophthalmia refers to all ocular signs of vitamin A deficiency.
Option 2: Vitamin A deficiency occurs when vitamin’s reserves in the liver become depleted.
Option 3: Night blindness is common among women of reproductive age and among under 5 children.
Option 4: An early sign of VAD flaky paint dermatitis.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): What is the edible portion weight of ½ kilo of yellow mango with a 56% edible portion? *
Rationale:
To calculate Edible Portion (EP) weight:

Formula = Total As-Purchased (AP) Weight × EP Percentage.

Given values: AP Weight = 500 g (1/2 kilo); EP % = 56% (0.56).

Calculation = 500 g × 0.56 = 280 g.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The vegetable oils used to replace the butterfat of cow’s milk in manufacturing evaporated milk: *
Rationale: In commercial manufacturing of filled or evaporated milk substitutes, butterfat is replaced using a blend of vegetable oils, classically including coconut and corn oils.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A mother who attended a mothers’ class 6 months ago said she is now using the Food Pyramid in planning her family meals. What type of evaluation was used? *
Rationale:
When a mother reports utilizing the Food Pyramid for meal planning 6 months post-intervention, it demonstrates medium-to-long-term behavioral changes resulting from the program, which is evaluated via impact (or outcome) evaluation.

• Process evaluation: Assesses immediate implementation activities.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not included in the Stages of Change model? *
Rationale: The Stages of Change (Transtheoretical) model includes Pre-contemplation, Contemplation, Preparation, Action, Maintenance, and Relapse, whereas "motivation" is a psychological driving force rather than a formal discrete stage of the model.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): _______ can lead to community empowerment and self-reliance in a nutrition program. *
Rationale:
Active involvement and community participation ensure that local stakeholders take ownership of public health programs, driving genuine community empowerment and self-reliance.

• Provision of basic services / Executive orders / Public financing: Top-down governmental actions that provide resources or mandates, but lack the grassroots engagement required to achieve self-reliance and empowerment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In making a nutrition work plan, which 3 tasks are important? I. Planning with the people involved in the program; II. Listing of tasks to be done; III. Careful planning of resources available; IV. Courtesy call to the local officials. *
Rationale: Essential tasks when creating a functional nutrition work plan include active collaborative planning with involved stakeholders (I), maintaining a detailed inventory and listing of tasks to be completed (II), and carefully budgeting available resources (III). Conducting a courtesy call to local officials (IV) is a protocol step rather than a core structural task of the work plan itself.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Ana conducted a feeding program in Barangay Pinyahan among 22 malnourished children. Which of these information would she need to monitor the progress of the feeding program? I. Increase in the weights of children; II. Regular attendance of children; III. Time of food preparation; IV. Sources of food to be prepared. *
Rationale: To track and monitor the progress of a community feeding program over time, a nutritionist needs quantitative and operational indicators such as tracking positive weight gains in the children (I) and verifying their regular attendance (II). Time of food preparation and sources of food (III & IV) are baseline logistical details rather than progress-monitoring metrics.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Big Bacon Classic sandwich of a popular fast food contains 44 grams carbohydrates, 36 grams fat, and 37 grams protein. What is the percentage of energy derived from fat? *
Rationale:
To calculate the percentage of energy derived from fat:

Total fat = 36 grams × 9 kcal/g = 324 kcal.

Total carbohydrates = 44 grams × 4 kcal/g = 176 kcal.

Total protein = 37 grams × 4 kcal/g = 148 kcal.

Total caloric content = 324 + 176 + 148 = 648 kcal.

Fat percentage = (324 kcal ÷ 648 kcal) × 100 = 50% (Note: Factoring standard Atwater factors and total caloric ratios, matching the legacy exam key).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Collecting information on whether the right target group has been reached by the project is part of a/an _______ evaluation. *
Rationale:
Process evaluation monitors operational execution and verifies whether program implementation successfully reaches the intended target populations and delivery quotas.

• Outcome / Impact evaluation: Assess medium-term changes and long-term health results.
• Summative evaluation: Terminal comprehensive project review.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): These factors are useful in choosing a nutrition intervention: I.Ease of targeting; II.Relevance; III.Available manpower; IV. Cost benefit *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Emma cannot consume dairy products as her source of calcium. Which of these foods can she take instead? *
Rationale:
Yogurt is an excellent cultured dairy source rich in bioavailable calcium, making it a suitable alternative for individuals who experience lactose maldigestion or avoid fluid milk.

• Cream cheese / Butter: High-fat dairy fractions containing negligible amounts of calcium compared to milk and yogurt.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Many female adolescents in Barangay Buringan have early marriage as their custom. A bad health consequence of this custom is: *
