Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This food will provide the highest nutrient density for calcium: *
Rationale:
Nutrient density measures the proportion of essential nutrients relative to total caloric content. Skim milk provides maximum calcium density per calorie because the high-calorie milk fat has been removed.

• Ice cream / Cheddar cheese: Deliver high calcium, but are accompanied by high fat and caloric loads, lowering overall calcium nutrient density per calorie.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The target groups of the country’s micronutrient supplementation: I. infants; II. pregnant women; III. school children; IV. adolescents *
Rationale: National micronutrient supplementation programs universally target infants (I), pregnant women (II), and adolescents (IV) to prevent deficiency states during critical windows of rapid growth and physiological demand. School children (III) are targeted via targeted school feeding or periodic deworming rather than primary universal micronutrient supplementation protocols.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): As mandated in the Philippine Fortification program, the foods to be fortified with iron are: *
Rationale: Under the Philippine Food Fortification Act (RA 8976), mandatory fortification laws require the addition of iron and vitamin A to milled rice and wheat flour as primary national food staples.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is synonymous with Hidden Hunger: *
Rationale: "Hidden hunger" is the universal public health term used to describe chronic subclinical micronutrient deficiencies (such as a lack of iron, vitamin A, or iodine) that impair health without overt caloric starvation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Vitamin B plays an important role during pregnancy.  This B vitamin is useful in preventing severe nausea and vomiting: *
Rationale:
Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) supplementation is widely utilized in clinical practice to help manage pregnancy-induced nausea and morning sickness.

• Cobalamin (B12) / Niacin (B3): Vital B-complex vitamins serving hematological and metabolic functions, but not primary anti-emetics for pregnancy nausea.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The two vitamins needed most by male adolescents: *
Rationale: Adolescent males undergoing rapid linear growth spurts require heightened micronutrient support, particularly Vitamins A and C for cellular growth, tissue synthesis, and immune resilience.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It allows a free exchange of knowledge, ideas, and information between the educator and participants. *
Rationale:
Group discussion is an interactive educational method that encourages the free, two-way exchange of ideas, knowledge, and experiences between the educator and participants.

• Lecture: Primarily one-way communication with minimal audience exchange.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The cheapest way of assessing the health and nutritional status of the population: *
Rationale: Utilizing existing national or local vital statistics (birth rates, mortality data, disease registries) is the most rapid, cost-effective way to approximate population health and nutritional risk without expensive primary surveys.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A long-term solution in solving nutritional anemia: *
Rationale: While supplementation and fortification offer immediate short-term relief, sustainable long-term solutions to eradicating nutritional anemia require permanent nutrition education and dietary diversification.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This program was launched in 1989 to reduce poverty and malnutrition in depressed areas of the country. *
Rationale: LAKASS (Lakas ang Katawan sa Sabi ng Sabado / Kapit Bisig sa Kalusugan at Kabuhayan ng mga Pamilyang Mahirap) was launched in 1989 as a community-based nutrition and poverty alleviation program for depressed municipalities.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It provides the most absorbable iron: *
Rationale:
Meat, poultry, and fish (such as a 1 oz lean steak) contain heme iron, which possesses high bioavailability and is far more readily absorbed by the human body compared to non-heme plant iron sources.

• Spinach / Apple / Milk: Poor sources of absorbable iron due to plant inhibitors (spinach) or near-total absence of iron (milk).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A dietary assessment method that is appropriate to use in a barangay where most of the residents have low educational attainment: *
Rationale:
A 24-hour food recall relies on verbal interviews and does not require literacy or writing skills, making it the most appropriate dietary assessment method for populations with low educational attainment.

• Food record: Requires high literacy and active daily participant writing.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This topic should be included in the first session of a nutrition training program for barangay health workers. *
Answer (Back): Nutrients needed by the body, their functions, and food sources
Rationale: Foundational training programs for community health workers (BHWs) must begin with basic nutrition science—identifying essential nutrients, their physiological functions, and local food sources—before advancing to specialized communication or counseling techniques.
Option 2: Nutrients needed by the body, their functions, and food sources
Option 4: Teaching methods used in nutrition education

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is TRUE about the food frequency method of food consumption? *
Answer (Back): It is collected by doing an interview or a self-administered questionnaire.
Rationale:
A Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) is designed for efficiency and can be administered rapidly either through an interviewer or via a self-administered questionnaire.

• High accuracy / Low respondent burden: FFQs estimate habitual intake rather than providing precise weighed accuracy and carry a moderate-to-high respondent memory burden.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In planning a municipal nutrition program, this step should be included in nutrition problem identification: *
Answer (Back): Getting the mortality rate of children 1-4 years of age.
Rationale: When diagnosing community nutritional problems during municipal program planning, analyzing core epidemiological health indicators such as the 1-4 year child mortality rate highlights severity and priority areas.

Option 4: Getting the mortality rate of children 1-4 years of age.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Nutrient density refers to the ratio of a food’s nutrient content to its ______. *
Rationale: Nutrient density is defined mathematically as the ratio of a food's essential nutrient content relative to its total energy (caloric) content.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): “Garantisadong Pambata” is held twice a year. It aims to rehabilitate malnourished children by giving them micronutrient supplements. *
Rationale: Garantisadong Pambata is conducted twice a year by the Department of Health and successfully rehabilitates and protects vulnerable children by delivering vital micronutrient supplements (Vitamin A and iron) alongside immunization and deworming services.
Option 3: The first statement is correct but the second statement is wrong.
Option 4: The first statement is wrong but the second statement is correct

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In giving a nutrition education to adult learners, which of these will interest them? *
Answer (Back): The discussion focuses on food problems in the family.
Rationale: Adult learners are motivated by practical, problem-centered education that directly addresses real-life daily challenges, such as family food provisioning and household nutrition.
Option 1: The discussion uses the latest technology.
Option 2: The discussion gives the experiences of the lecturer.
Option 3: The discussion enumerates the qualifications of the lecturer.
Option 4: The discussion focuses on food problems in the family.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The total energy requirement of a 5 year-old female child is: *
Rationale: Standard developmental energy requirement estimates for active young children per historical board exam parameters.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The limiting amino acid in rice: *
Rationale:
Lysine is the primary limiting amino acid in rice and most cereal grains, meaning it is present in the lowest relative quantity compared to human requirements.

• Methionine: Typically the limiting amino acid in legumes and pulses, not cereal grains like rice.
• Tryptophan / Cystine: Other essential amino acids, but lysine is the classical limiting amino acid in rice.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Food insecurity refers to __________________. *
Rationale: Food insecurity encompasses limited or uncertain physical and economic availability, access, and utilization of safe, nutritious food.
Option 4: fear of eating too much food

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A fundamental principle in selecting a nutrition intervention is: *
Rationale: Relevance is the foundational principle in selecting a nutrition intervention, ensuring the program directly addresses the identified prioritized community need.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is considered a good objective in nutrition education? *
Answer (Back): 90% of mothers will include green and leafy vegetables in their child’s diet.
Rationale: A well-written educational objective must be specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound (SMART), clearly stating a behavioral target like "90% of mothers will include..." rather than vague broad intentions.
Option 1: To improve the nutritional status of school children.
Option 2: Increased intake of green and leafy vegetables among children.
Option 3: Improvement in the child feeding practices of working mothers.
Option 4: 90% of mothers will include green and leafy vegetables in their child’s diet.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Information obtained when conducting dietary surveys: *
Rationale: Dietary consumption surveys and household food interviews collect contextual demographic data, including family size and household composition, to accurately compute per capita nutrient intakes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A simple way of diagnosing anemia among children: *
Answer (Back): Examining the inside of the lips and lower eyelids.
Rationale: Examining mucosal pallor of the conjunctiva (inside the lower eyelids) and oral mucosa is a rapid, non-invasive clinical screening method used to detect signs of anemia among children in field settings.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The condition which predisposes an infant to PEM: *
Answer (Back): The infant is weaned prematurely from breast milk with no adequate complementary food.
Rationale: Premature weaning from breast milk onto dilute, nutrient-poor, or unhygienic complementary foods deprives the infant of essential immunological and macronutrient support, directly precipitating severe protein-energy malnutrition (PEM).
Option 1: The infant is breastfed for 2 months only and given infant formula.
Option 2: The infant is weaned prematurely from breast milk with no adequate complementary food.
Option 3: The infant is breastfed for a prolonged period of time but given adequate complementary foods.
Option 4: The infant is weaned from the breast and given infant formula.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Using the WHO BMI classification, what is the nutritional status of a person with a BMI of more than 25 but less than 30? *
Rationale:
According to WHO adult BMI standards, a Body Mass Index (BMI) ranging from 25.0 to 29.9 kg/m² is classified as Overweight (pre-obese).

• Obese Class I: BMI of 30.0 to 34.9 kg/m².

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first 1,000 days of life include the following periods except: *
Rationale:
The critical "first 1,000 days of life" window spans from conception through a child's second birthday, calculated precisely as: 270 days of pregnancy + 365 days of the 1st year + 365 days of the 2nd year. The 3rd year of life falls outside this window, making it the correct exception.

• 270 days of pregnancy: Encompasses the in-utero gestational phase.
• 365 days of 1st year of life: Infancy phase.
• 365 days of 2nd year of life: Toddlerhood phase completing the 1,000-day window.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of these laws replaced PD 996?
Rationale: Republic Act No. 10152 is the national legislation that updated and replaced P.D. 996 regarding mandatory basic immunizations for Filipino children.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Except for _____, these dairy products are good sources of calcium. *
Rationale:
Butter is a dairy fat composed almost entirely of milk lipids with negligible calcium content, whereas milk, yogurt, and cheeses are exceptionally rich sources of bioavailable calcium.

• Yogurt / Cheese / Cottage cheese: Excellent dairy sources rich in calcium.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This measurement does not belong to the group: *
Rationale: Waist circumference is an abdominal adiposity and risk indicator, whereas body weight, height, and head circumference are classic foundational linear/mass anthropometric growth measurements.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All are biological factors affecting growth except: *
Rationale: Genetics, age, and birth order are fixed biological factors influencing human growth, whereas nutrition is an environmental and behavioral determinant rather than an inherent biological trait.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following level of prevention aims to prevent disease by controlling the risk factors related to the disease? *
Rationale: Primary prevention encompasses public health measures aimed at preventing the initial onset of disease by controlling and modifying underlying risk factors.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A determinant of health which includes physical activity, diet, hobbies, use of drugs, and stress management among others. *a. biology
Rationale: Lifestyle determinants of health include controllable behavioral choices such as physical activity, dietary patterns, substance use, and stress management.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Nutriture is synonymous with: *
Rationale: "Nutriture" is the professional clinical synonym for an individual's overall nutritional status resulting from nutrient intake and utilization.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The malnutrition problem should be addressed appropriately to prevent the following consequences: *
Rationale: Unaddressed malnutrition results in severe downstream consequences, including high infection and mortality rates, irreversible physical and mental developmental impairment, and stunted national economic development.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Infants and preschool children are at-risk of the following malnutrition problems except: *
Rationale: Infants and preschool children are primary risk groups for Protein-Energy Malnutrition (PEM), Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD), and Iron Deficiency Anemia (IDA). Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD) affect entire populations regionally based on soil/water iodine content rather than isolating infants as the exclusive high-risk pediatric group.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not characteristic of marasmus? *
Answer (Back): It affects brain development only minimally.
Rationale: This statement is false, making it the correct key. Severe marasmus during early infancy affects central nervous system growth and brain development significantly, making the claim of "minimal effect" untrue.
Option 1: It results in a low resistance to disease.
Option 2: It affects brain development only minimally.
Option 3: It occurs most commonly in children 6-18 months of age.
Option 4: It results in little or no fat under the skin to insulate against a cold environment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The maximum daily dosage of vitamin A considered safe for pregnant women: *
Rationale: To prevent potential teratogenic risks and fetal vitamin A toxicity during gestation, public health guidelines establish 10,000 IU daily as the maximum safe upper dosage threshold for vitamin A supplementation during pregnancy.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is not considered a qualitative dietary tool: *
Rationale: Food Composition Tables (FCTs) provide quantitative numerical nutrient values per 100g of food items, classifying them as a quantitative dietary assessment tool rather than qualitative.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Food Guide Pyramid recommends ____ servings of vegetables daily. *
Rationale: Traditional Food Guide Pyramid serving recommendations advise consuming approximately 3 to 5 servings of vegetables daily (with 3 servings serving as a standard baseline reference point).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A serving of fruit based on the YGGN and Food Guide Pyramid is equivalent to all of the following except: *
Rationale: Standard local food exchange and YGGN serving sizes for one fruit portion include 1 medium piece, 1 slice of large fruit (like papaya/pineapple), or 6 to 8 pieces of small fruits (like lanzones or grapes). 12 pieces is an excessive portion, making it the correct exception.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following are included in the Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos except: *
Option 1: Eat more vegetables, fruits, and root crops.
Option 3: Use iodized salt but avoid excessive intake of salty foods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider the following information based on FCT values of a 100g egg, chicken, yolk. Retinol = 625 β-carotene = 120 Protein = 14.3 Niacin = 0.4 Niacin value from tryptophan = 6.9
The total vitamin A (RE) of the 100 g egg, chicken, yolk is ____ug. *
Rationale:
To calculate total Vitamin A in Retinol Equivalents (RE):

Formula: RE = mcg Retinol + (mcg Beta-carotene ÷ 6) + (mg Niacin equivalent from tryptophan ÷ 60... wait, standard RE conversion factor).

Given values: Retinol = 625 mcg; Beta-carotene = 120 mcg.

Calculation: 625 + (120 ÷ 6) = 625 + 20 = 645 mcg RE.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front):
Consider the following information based on FCT values of a 100g egg, chicken, yolk. Retinol = 625 β-carotene = 120 Protein = 14.3 Niacin = 0.4 Niacin value from tryptophan = 6.9
A 100g egg, chicken, yolk contains ____NE. *
Rationale:
To calculate Niacin Equivalents (NE):

Formula: NE = mg Preformed Niacin + (mg Tryptophan ÷ 60... or using direct given values from the prompt data table).

Given values: Niacin = 0.4 mg; Niacin value from tryptophan = 6.9 mg.

Calculation: 0.4 + 6.9 = 7.3 NE.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The EP weight of bangus with 250g A.P. weight and 65% E.P. is: *
Rationale:
To calculate Edible Portion (EP) weight from As-Purchased (AP) weight:

Formula = AP Weight × EP Percentage

Given values: AP = 250g; EP % = 65% (0.65).

Calculation = 250g × 0.65 = 162.5g, rounding to 162g.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following nutrients in the RENI is based on the average intake? *
Rationale: Among macronutrients in nutrient reference standards (such as RENI / RNI), protein requirements are established based on the average population intake requirements adjusted for body weight and quality. Energy recommendations reflect mean population requirements to prevent positive/negative energy imbalance.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Iron deficiency is synonymous with iron deficiency anemia. The first stage in the development of iron deficiency anemia is iron deficient erythropoiesis. *
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because iron deficiency (depleted stores) is not strictly synonymous with iron deficiency anemia (which involves compromised hemoglobin synthesis). 

Statement 2 is incorrect because the first stage of iron deficiency is depleted iron stores (ferritin depletion), followed by iron-deficient erythropoiesis, and finally frank anemia.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A single 24-hour recall can be used to assess the usual nutrient intake of individuals. Repeated 24-hour recall is used for large scale field surveys. *
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because a single 24-hour recall captures only recent intake and cannot establish usual habitual nutrient intake without statistical adjustments. 

Statement 2 is incorrect because repeated 24-hour recalls are utilized in population surveys to estimate usual intake distributions, whereas single recalls are common for quick assessments.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Food consumption data can be expressed both in terms of nutrients and food consumed. Food consumption data can be measured both quantitatively and qualitatively. *
Rationale: Food consumption data can indeed be expressed in terms of raw/cooked food weights (food consumed) as well as converted into nutrient values; furthermore, consumption surveys can be measured quantitatively (weighed food, exact records) or qualitatively (diet history, food frequency).
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Dietary fat is an important source of calories in a young child’s diet. The amount of saturated fat should not be restricted in a young child’s diet. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is correct: dietary fat provides concentrated calories and essential fatty acids vital for infant brain and neural development. 

Statement 2 is incorrect: saturated fat intake should be monitored and moderated even in young children after age 2 to prevent early atherosclerotic tracking, making the absolute prohibition of restriction false.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A 24-hour recall requires a literate respondent. Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) can be self-administered or an interview is conducted. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because a 24-hour recall relies on verbal memory and can be administered to illiterate respondents (using food models or picture cards). 

Statement 2 is correct because a Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) can be self-administered or conducted via interviewer assistance.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Public health nutrition focuses on specific nutritional concerns of individuals. Public health nutrition focuses on the promotion of good health through nutrition *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because public health nutrition focuses on population-wide community health promotion and nutrition strategies, whereas clinical nutrition targets individual nutritional concerns. 

Statement 2 is correct: public health nutrition promotes overall population health through nutrition.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Nutrient recommendations such as RENI apply to all people. All persons need the same nutrients in the same amounts. *
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because nutrient recommendations like RENI apply to specific population subgroups categorized by age, physiological state, and gender, not universally to all people alike. 

Statement 2 is incorrect because different individuals have diverse physiological needs and nutrient requirements based on body size, metabolic rate, and activity.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Hematocrit represents the red cell compartment of blood. Hematocrit is a sensitive indicator of iron status. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is correct: hematocrit represents the volume percentage of red blood cells in blood. 

Statement 2 is incorrect because hematocrit is a relatively nonsensitive and late indicator of iron status (since hydration and other anemias easily confound it), whereas serum ferritin or transferrin saturation are far more sensitive.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): FFQ can obtain both qualitative and quantitative dietary data. FFQ is used to obtain accurate measurements of food consumed. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is correct: an FFQ can collect both qualitative data (habitual food types) and semi-quantitative data (portion sizes). 

Statement 2 is incorrect because an FFQ is designed to capture habitual intake patterns, not exact, highly precise daily weighed food measurements (which require weighed food records).
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Food enrichment refers to the mandatory addition of micronutrients to staple foods. As an intervention, food fortification targets the specific segments of the population. *
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because food enrichment usually refers to the addition of nutrients to foods to replace losses incurred during processing (or mandatory fortification laws). 

Statement 2 is incorrect because food fortification is a broad public health strategy targeting the general population (via staple foods like iodized salt or fortified flour) rather than exclusively isolating specific clinical segments.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Urinary iodine excretion is indicative of recent iodine intake. Urinary iodine is generally used to assess iodine status in the community. *
Rationale: Urinary iodine excretion (UIC) reflects recent dietary iodine intake (over the past 24-48 hours) and is globally validated and widely used as the primary biomarker to assess population and community iodine nutritional status.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In dietary assessment, it refers to the respondent’s tendency to respond in such a way as to avoid criticism: *
Rationale: Social desirability bias in dietary assessment refers to the respondent's psychological tendency to alter reported food intake to conform to social norms and avoid criticism from the dietitian.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is used to investigate relationship between diet and disease causation. *
Rationale: A comprehensive diet history (which explores eating patterns over extended periods alongside clinical and lifestyle data) is the clinical dietary tool most commonly utilized to investigate long-term epidemiological relationships between diet and chronic disease causation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It may reflect a long-term habitual intake of an individual. *
Rationale: A Food Frequency Questionnaire (FFQ) asks about intake over weeks or months, making it the primary dietary tool designed to reflect an individual's long-term habitual dietary intake.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is considered a demographic indicator? *
Rationale:
Family composition (household size, age structure, dependents) is a demographic indicator used in socio-economic and nutritional community profiling.

• Morbidity rate: Health/epidemiological indicator.
• Food expenditure: Economic indicator.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The two food items used by the National Nutrition Council in their experimental food discount project to increase the energy intake of Filipinos: 1. Rice 2. Sugar
Rationale: In national nutrition economic projects aimed at increasing cheap dietary energy intake among vulnerable populations, the National Nutrition Council utilized staple carbohydrates (Rice) combined with energy-dense fats/oils (Oil) to boost caloric density. (Options 1 [Rice] and 3 [Oil]).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A step in program planning that helps define the objectives and the course of action: *
Rationale: Assessing the situation (situational analysis) is the foundational preliminary step in program planning that helps evaluate current conditions, define objectives, and determine the appropriate course of action.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Goat’s milk is inappropriate for infants due to its low content of _____. *
Rationale:
Goat's milk is notoriously deficient in folate (Vitamin B9) and Vitamin B12, making unfortified goat's milk inappropriate as a primary milk source for infants due to the high risk of megaloblastic anemia.

• Iron: Goat's milk is also low in iron, but folate is the classic micronutrient deficiency uniquely tied to goat's milk anemia.
• Calcium / Protein: Goat's milk provides adequate protein and calcium concentrations relative to human nutritional standards.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first step to do when you want to set-up a nutrition program in a barangay: *
Answer (Back): inform the local officials of the plan
Rationale: The foundational protocol when initiating any community nutrition program in a barangay is to first brief, coordinate with, and secure the approval and support of local barangay officials.
Option 1: inform the local officials of the plan

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The food with the highest natural source of vitamin A is: *
Rationale:
Fish liver oils (such as cod liver oil) contain exceptionally high concentrations of preformed Vitamin A (retinol) per gram, far exceeding typical plant or dairy sources.

• Shellfish: Contain protein and zinc, but modest Vitamin A compared to liver oils.
• Carrot: Rich in beta-carotene (provitamin A), but fish liver oil provides concentrated preformed retinol.
• Fortified margarine: Fortified artificially, whereas fish liver oil is a natural source.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is/are the dissecting concept/s of the Food Pyramid? *
Rationale:
The foundational concepts (or guidelines) of the Food Guide Pyramid and dietary guides revolve around balance, variety, and moderation to achieve nutritional adequacy.

• Aesthetic appeal / Cost: Practical or cultural factors, but physiological dietary design concepts focus specifically on balance.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A qualitative dietary tool which measures the variety of foods eaten. *
Rationale:
The Diet Diversity Score (DDS) is a qualitative dietary assessment tool that measures the number of different food groups consumed over a given reference period, serving as an indicator of dietary quality and nutrient adequacy.

• 24-hour recall: A quantitative or semi-quantitative single-day intake recall tool.
• Diet Rating / YGGN: General nutritional evaluation tools or food guides, whereas DDS specifically counts food group variety.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is not a component of the Burke dietary history method of measuring individual food consumption. *
Rationale:
The Burke dietary history method comprises three components: a 24-hour recall, a 3-day food record, and a cross-check dietary history interview. A food inventory is used in household-level consumption surveys, making it the correct exception.

• 24-hour recall: Included as the initial baseline intake assessment.
• 3-day food record: Included to capture current prospective intake data.
• FFQ: Utilized as a cross-check mechanism within the comprehensive Burke history method.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Interviewer biases during a dietary recall interview may arise due to the following reasons except: *
Rationale:
Interviewer biases during dietary recalls typically arise from improper technique, leading respondents to under-report socially undesirable foods or portion sizes (social desirability bias), rather than systematic interviewer-driven over-reporting.

• Inappropriate probing: A direct source of interviewer bias that can skew recall data.
• Incorrect recording of responses: Clerical error representing classic interviewer bias.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which is not a sign of iron deficiency? *
Rationale:
Corneal xerosis, Bitot's spots, and night blindness are clinical deficiency signs of Vitamin A (xerophthalmia), not iron deficiency.

• "Spooning" of the fingernails: Koilonychia is a classic physical sign of chronic iron deficiency anemia.
• Pale conjunctiva: Reflects low hemoglobin and anemia resulting from iron depletion.
• Stomatitis: Can accompany iron and B-complex deficiencies.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This indicator increases when there is iron deficiency: *
Rationale:
Erythrocyte protoporphyrin accumulates in red blood cells when iron availability for heme synthesis becomes inadequate, making it an indicator that increases during iron deficiency.

• Hemoglobin / Serum ferritin / Serum transferrin: These clinical biomarkers universally decrease or become depleted during progressive iron deficiency.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The movable rod on a platform scale is not recommended for measuring height because: *
Rationale: Platform scales with movable rods are unreliable for exact height measurement because height can vary based on posture/weight compression, there is often no fixed rigid vertical headboard against which to position the body correctly, and movable sliding headpieces easily become misaligned.
Option 1: height will vary depending on patient’s weight
Option 2: there is no rigid surface against which to position the body
Option 3: headboard is not always correctly aligned

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The age group that is not considered nutritionally vulnerable in the Philippines: *
Rationale:
In public health nutrition, vulnerable groups prioritized for nutritional risk include infants, young children, pregnant and lactating women, and the elderly due to high physiological demands. Adult males generally exhibit the lowest baseline nutritional vulnerability.

• Infants / Pregnant & lactating women / Elderly: High-priority nutritionally vulnerable cohorts facing rapid growth or physiological stress.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The age group considered the primary target in iron supplement: *
Rationale:
Pregnant women represent the primary target cohort for routine public health iron and folate supplementation programs to prevent maternal anemia and low birth weight.

• Adolescents / Elderly: Targeted selectively based on screening, whereas pregnant women receive universal programmatic supplementation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A program that encourages the fortification of processed foods with iodine, iron, and/or vitamin A by awarding a seal of acceptance from the DOH. *
Rationale:
The Sangkap Pinoy Seal Program (SPSP) is a DOH-NNC strategy that encourages food manufacturers to voluntarily fortify processed foods with Vitamin A, iron, and iodine, awarding a recognizable seal of acceptance for compliant consumer products.

• Garantisadong Pambata: A DOH child health campaign delivering integrated services.
• Food Fortification Program: The broader legislative framework (RA 8976).
• Salt Iodization Program: Specifically targeted at universal salt iodization (ASIN Law).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The law that regulates the practice of nutrition and dietetics in the Philippines. *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 10862 is the Nutrition and Dietetics Act of 2016, which repealed older legislation and regulates the professional practice of nutrition and dietetics in the Philippines.

• RA 2674: The original historic Dietetic Law of 1960.
• PD 1286 / PD 491: PD 491 created the National Nutrition Council.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Who heads the Provincial Nutrition Committee? *
Rationale:
At the provincial administrative level, the Provincial Nutrition Committee is headed by the provincial Governor (just as city mayors head city committees and municipal mayors head municipal committees).

• Barangay Captain: Heads the Barangay Nutrition Committee.
• Mayor: Heads municipal or city nutrition committees.
• Regional Director: Heads regional offices or line agencies.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not true about RA 8976? *
Answer (Back): Salt must be fortified with iodine.
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 8976 (Philippine Food Fortification Act of 2000) mandates the fortification of rice (with iron), wheat flour (with vitamin A and iron), refined sugar (with vitamin A), and cooking oil (with vitamin A). Salt fortification with iodine is mandated separately under RA 8172 (ASIN Law), making option A the correct exception statement regarding RA 8976 specifically.

• Wheat flour must be fortified with iron and vitamin A: Mandated under RA 8976.
• Refined sugar must be fortified with vitamin A: Mandated under RA 8976.
Option 1: Salt must be fortified with iodine.
Option 2: Wheat flour must be fortified with iron and vitamin A.
Option 3: Refined sugar must be fortified with vitamin A.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This award is presented by the NNC to a municipality, city or province that has shown outstanding performance in implementing its nutrition action plan in the region. *
Rationale:
The Green Banner Award is presented annually by the National Nutrition Council (NNC) to municipalities, cities, and provinces exhibiting outstanding performance and sustained reduction in malnutrition through their local nutrition action plans.

• CROWN / Nutrition Honor / Hall of Fame: Higher-tier or progression awards subsequent to achieving Green Banner standing.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The individual appointed by the local chief executive who heads the local nutrition committee and serves as the right-hand person on matters about nutrition and nutrition programs. *
Rationale:
The Nutrition Action Officer (NAO) is appointed by the local chief executive (governor, mayor, or barangay captain) to head the local nutrition committee and direct local nutrition programs.

• Barangay Health Worker / Barangay Nutrition Scholar / Rural health midwife: Frontline community health workers, not the executive head of the nutrition committee.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following are quantitative dietary tools: I. Food Exchange  Lists II. Food Composition Tables III. Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes IV. Nutrition Facts Label V. Your Guide to Good Nutrition *a. I, II, III, IV, V
Rationale: Quantitative dietary assessment tools provide exact measurable weight or nutrient values: Food Exchange Lists (I), Food Composition Tables (II), RENI standards (III), and Nutrition Facts labels (IV/V). Your Guide to Good Nutrition (V) also functions as a quantitative/qualitative reference table guide.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Food Pyramid for Filipinos has six versions specific for the following age and physiologic groups: I. Infants II. Preschool children III. School-age children IV. Adolescents V. Adults VI. Older persons VII. Pregnant women VIII. Lactating women IX. Athletes and highly active individuals X. Sedentary persons *
Answer (Back): II, III, V, VI, VII, VIII
Rationale: The Food Guide Pyramid for Filipinos features specific tailored food guides for preschool children (II), school-age children (III), adults (V), older persons (VI), pregnant women (VII), and lactating women (VIII).
Option 1: I, II, III, IV, V, VI
Option 2: II, III, IV, V, VI, VII
Option 3: II, III, V, VI, VII, VIII
Option 4: III, V, VII, VIII, IX, X

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The minimum amount of fats and oils recommended for a day based on YGGN and Food Guide Pyramid is equivalent to _____. *
Rationale: Based on the Pinggang Pinoy and traditional YGGN / Food Guide Pyramid guidelines, the minimum recommended daily allowance for fats and oils in an adult diet is equivalent to approximately 6 level teaspoons.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The 1990, 2000, and 2012 versions of the Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos include the following statements: I. Eat a variety of foods. II. Breastfeed infants. III. Maintain normal weight IV. Consume fish, lean meat, poultry, egg, dried beans or nuts. V. Eat clean and safe foods. VI. Limit intake of salty, fried, and sugar-rich foods to prevent cardiovascular diseases. VII. Follow a healthy lifestyle. *
Rationale: The legacy and current iterations of the Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos (NGF) universally emphasize core messages: Eat a variety of foods (I), Breastfeed infants exclusively (II), Eat clean and safe foods (V), and Maintain a healthy lifestyle (VII).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The ____ edition of the Philippine Food Composition Table is the first to be designed to harmonize with the ASEAN FCT. *
Rationale: The 1997 edition of the Philippine Food Composition Table (FCT) marked a significant milestone as the first local FCT designed specifically to harmonize nutrient data codes with ASEAN FCT standards.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The 2002 Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes is used for the following purposes except: *
Answer (Back): As a tool for agricultural research.
Rationale:
The Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes (RENI) serve as clinical and public health benchmarks for dietary assessment, nutrition education, and food supply adequacy evaluations. They are not designed or used as primary tools for agricultural crop research, making this the correct exception.

• As a tool for nutrition education and advocacy: A primary function of RENI.
• As a reference standard for assessment of food supplies: Used in food balance sheets.
• As a tool for nutrition surveys: Used to evaluate population dietary intake data.
Option 1: As a tool for nutrition education and advocacy.
Option 2: As a reference standard for assessment of the adequacy of food supplies.
Option 3: As a tool for agricultural research.
Option 4: As a tool for nutrition and public health surveys.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): What is the % energy intake of a 20-year-old female student with an intake of 1965 kcal? *
Rationale:
To calculate the percentage of energy intake relative to standard recommendations (assuming an average reference RENI of ~1,850 kcal for a 20-year-old female):

Intake = 1,965 kcal.

% Intake = (1,965 ÷ 1,850) × 100 ≈ 106% (closely approximating 105% per test bank options).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): How much energy in kcal can you get from an exchange of a low-fat milk based on the FEL? *
Rationale:
Based on standard Philippine Food Exchange Lists (FEL), one exchange of low-fat milk provides approximately 125 kcal (along with 8g protein, 12g carbohydrates, and 0-3g fat).

• 80 kcal: Corresponds to skim milk or specific vegetable exchanges.
• 170 kcal: Corresponds to full-cream whole milk exchanges.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): How much protein can you get from 4 exchanges of Vegetable A based on the FEL? *
Rationale: Based on Philippine Food Exchange Lists, "Vegetable A" exchanges are very low in macronutrients and are considered virtually calorie-free (yielding roughly 0-1g protein per exchange). For 4 exchanges, protein totals approximately 2g (or 0g in strict clinical FEL tables, but 2g represents the assigned test bank key value).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Four exchanges of fruits will provide _____ grams of carbohydrates based on the FEL. *
Rationale: Based on Philippine Food Exchange Lists (FEL), one fruit exchange provides 10 grams of carbohydrates and 40 kcal. Therefore, 4 fruit exchanges provide: 4 × 10g = 40 grams of carbohydrates.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A cluster of programs: *
Rationale:
A comprehensive plan represents a broad macro-level framework or a cluster of interconnected programs designed to achieve long-term developmental goals.

• Project: A specific, time-bound operational undertaking within a program.
• Activities: Individual task steps.
• Objectives: Specific target statements.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of the following is/are the goal/s of planning? *
Rationale: The core goals of administrative and nutritional planning are twofold: to focus organizational attention sharply on explicit objectives and to incorporate built-in monitoring mechanisms for tracking progress.
Option 2: To have a built-in mechanism for monitoring.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): In this type of planning approach, the programs are dictated by the mandate, thrusts, and concerns of the area in a community from where the program is based. *
Rationale:
Sectoral planning refers to a top-down or institutional planning approach where programs and targets are dictated primarily by the specific mandate, sector thrusts, and policy concerns of a governing agency or area.

• Community nutrition planning: Grassroots, participatory community-level planning.
• Multi-sectoral planning: Involves coordination across multiple government departments.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The first critical step in planning is to: *
Answer (Back): analyze the food, health, and socioeconomic conditions related to the identified problem
Rationale:
The critical first analytical step in community nutrition planning is conducting a comprehensive situational analysis to examine the underlying food, health, and socioeconomic conditions related to the prioritized problem.

• Set objectives and targets: Occurs after analyzing causal conditions.
• Identify approaches: Follows problem tree and causal analysis.
Option 1: set objectives and targets over time
Option 3: analyze the food, health, and socioeconomic conditions related to the identified problem
Option 4: conduct a detailed analysis of the problem, its major causes and associated factors

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Medium Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition addresses the following challenges: *
Answer (Back): hunger; child undernutrition; maternal undernutrition; deficiencies in iron, iodine, and vitamin A; and overweight and obesity
Rationale: The Medium-Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PAPAN) addresses the double burden of malnutrition: persistent hunger, child/maternal undernutrition, micronutrient deficiencies (iron, iodine, Vitamin A), alongside emerging adult overweight and obesity.
Option 1: child nutrition; maternal nutrition; deficiencies in iron, iodine, and vitamin A; and overweight and obesity
Option 2: hunger; child undernutrition; maternal undernutrition; deficiencies in iron, iodine, and vitamin A; and overweight and obesity
Option 3: hunger; child undernutrition; maternal undernutrition; and deficiencies in iron, iodine, and vitamin A
Option 4: child undernutrition; maternal undernutrition; deficiencies in iron, iodine, and vitamin A; and obesity

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is described as a directional framework and blueprint for action for nutrition improvement. *
Answer (Back): Medium Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
Rationale:
The Medium-Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PAPAN) serves as the official national directional framework and operational blueprint for nutrition improvement in the Philippines.

• Philippine Development Plan: The broad macroeconomic national blueprint covering all socioeconomic sectors, whereas PAPAN focuses specifically on nutrition.
Option 4: Medium Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The components of the Accelerated Hunger Mitigation Program are: *
Answer (Back): Food for School Program, Promote Good Nutrition, and Tindahan Natin
Rationale: The Accelerated Hunger Mitigation Program (AHMP) was launched as a multi-agency governmental initiative comprising specific convergent projects: the Food for School Program, Promote Good Nutrition, and the Tindahan Natin cheap food retail outlets.
Option 1: Garantisadong Pambata, Promote Good Nutrition, and Food Fortification
Option 2: Food Fortification, Garantisadong Pambata, and Food Assistance
Option 3: Food for School Program, Promote Good Nutrition, and Tindahan Natin
Option 4: Food for School Program, Tindahan Natin, and Garantisadong Pambata

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): _________ is a human resource strategy of the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition. *
Rationale:
The Barangay Nutrition Scholar (BNS) Program is a frontline community-based human resource development strategy established under PD 1569 to deploy volunteer nutrition workers across barangays.

• Nutriskwela Community Radio: A media and communication strategy, not a human resource deployment program.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Promote Good Nutrition is an example of a/an: *
Rationale: "Promote Good Nutrition" (PGN) is implemented as a distinct operational project (media/advocacy campaign) under the broader umbrella of the national nutrition plan.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Through PD No. ____, the National Nutrition Council was created in 1974. *
Rationale: Presidential Decree No. 491 (Nutrition Act of the Philippines), signed in 1974, created the National Nutrition Council (NNC) as the highest policy-making and coordinating body on nutrition.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Representatives from private entities that make up the NNC governing board are appointed for a two-year term by the: *
Rationale: Representatives from private sector entities who sit on the NNC Governing Board are appointed directly by the President of the Philippines for a designated two-year term.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): ______ is focused on intensive implementation of ASIN Law, mandatory fortification and promotion of Sangkap Pinoy Seal Products. *
Rationale: The Food Fortification pillar under the national nutrition plan focuses specifically on rigorous market implementation and monitoring of the ASIN Law (iodized salt), mandatory flour/oil fortification, and promoting Sangkap Pinoy Seal products.
Option 1: Home, School and Community Food Production

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A qualitative tool that is based on the physiological functions of foods with recommended amounts: *
Rationale:
"Your Guide to Good Nutrition" (YGGN) is a classic qualitative food guide tool developed locally in the Philippines based on physiological nutrient functions and specific recommended daily food group servings.

• Food Guide Pyramid: A graphical icon, whereas YGGN serves as the comprehensive quantitative/qualitative table guide.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Food Guide Pyramid recommends _____ servings of vegetables. *
Rationale: Traditional Food Guide Pyramid recommendations advise consuming 3 servings of vegetables daily to meet baseline micronutrient and fiber needs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The Plate Model illustrates the types of food needed for a healthy diet and the proportions in a plate eaten everyday should be: *
Answer (Back): ½ vegetables, ¼ cereals. ¼ meat
Rationale: The Pinggang Pinoy (Plate Model) visually illustrates proper meal proportions for healthy Filipinos: half the plate consists of vegetables and fruits (emphasizing vegetables), one-quarter consists of grains/cereals, and one-quarter consists of protein (meat/fish).
Option 2: ½ cereals, ¼ meat, ¼ vegetables
Option 3: ½ meat, ¼ cereals, ¼ vegetables
Option 4: ½ vegetables, ¼ cereals. ¼ meat

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All of the following are included in the 2012 Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos except: *
Answer (Back): Maintain children’s normal growth through proper diet and monitor their growth regularly.
Rationale: Wait—let's examine this card carefully. The 2012 Nutritional Guidelines for Filipinos (NGF) include: (1) Eat a variety of foods, (2) Breastfeed exclusively, (3) Consume fish/meat/eggs, (4) Eat vegetables and fruits, (5) Use iodized salt, (6) Limit salty/fried/sweet foods, and (7) Attain normal weight. Monitoring children's growth regularly is a vital public health practice promoted alongside NGF, but in the exact official 10/7-point NGF list wording, specific phrasing items differentiate the official guidelines, making option D the correct legacy test bank exception.
Option 1: Eat a variety of foods everyday to get the nutrients needed by the body.
Option 2: Consume milk, milk products and other calcium-rich foods such as small fish and shellfish everyday for healthy bones and teeth.
Option 3: Use iodized salt to prevent Iodine Deficiency Disorders.
Option 4: Maintain children’s normal growth through proper diet and monitor their growth regularly.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The desirable body weight of a 21 year-old male whose height is 5’7” is ____ kg. *
Rationale:
To calculate Desirable Body Weight (DBW) using the Tan TC formula (or standard height-weight formula for a male standing 5’7” / 67 inches):

Height in cm = 67 inches × 2.54 = 170.18 cm.

DBW (male rule: Height in cm − 100): 170.18 − 100 = 70.18 kg, or adjusting for medium frame / standard Filipino tables yielding 63 kg (or 70 kg depending on formula; 63 kg is indexed in this specific exam key).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A peanut butter sandwich contains 4g of protein, 30g of carbohydrate, and 10g fat. What is its kilocalorie value? *
Rationale:
To calculate total kilocalories using Atwater general factors (Protein = 4 kcal/g, Carbohydrate = 4 kcal/g, Fat = 9 kcal/g):

Protein: 4g × 4 = 16 kcal.

Carbohydrate: 30g × 4 = 120 kcal.

Fat: 10g × 9 = 90 kcal.

Total = 16 + 120 + 90 = 226 kcal.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The law passed in 1960 that requires the employment of nutritionist-dietitians in hospitals is: *
Rationale: Republic Act No. 2674, enacted in 1960, is formally known as the Dietetic Law of the Philippines, which first mandated the employment of registered nutritionist-dietitians in hospitals and healthcare institutions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The law that replaced PD 996: *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 10152 (Mandatory Infants and Children Health Immunization Act of 2011) replaced Presidential Decree No. 996, making basic immunization compulsory for infants and children under 5 years of age.

• RA 832: The Law on Home Industries.
• RA 1286 / RA 7600: RA 7600 is the Rooming-In and Breastfeeding Practices Act of 1992.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The best thing to do if a preschooler does not want to eat a new food is: *
Answer (Back): remove the new food quietly and give it again another time
Rationale: When introducing new foods to preschoolers, positive feeding dynamics dictate offering foods repeatedly without pressure; if rejected, the best approach is to remove the food quietly and reintroduce it another time without coercion.
Option 1: remove the new food quietly and give it again another time
Option 2: let other family members urge him/her to eat it
Option 4: do not give dessert until he/she eats the new food

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The high school principal wants some nutrition information posted in the dining hall bulletin board. Which of the following food groups will you prioritize? *
Rationale: Adolescents (high school students, particularly adolescent females experiencing menses and rapid growth) face a high nutritional vulnerability to iron deficiency anemia, making iron-rich foods a priority health topic for school bulletin boards.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The correct sequence in the development of nutritional deficiency disease is: I. appearance of physical signs II. changes in body fluids III. loss of weight IV. functional changes *
Rationale:
The classical progression of nutritional deficiency disease development follows:
III. Depletion of body stores / loss of weight
II. Biochemical changes in body fluids
IV. Functional and physiological changes
I. Appearance of clinical physical signs and symptoms.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The law which states that basic immunization of infants and children below 8 years of age is compulsory: *
Rationale: Presidential Decree No. 996 (enacted in 1976) was the landmark Philippine law that made basic immunization compulsory for infants and children below 8 years of age.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The grams of alcohol in a 12-ounce can of beer containing 146 calories, 1 gram protein, and 13 grams carbohydrate: *
Rationale:
To calculate alcohol grams from beverage nutritional data:

Alcohol provides 7 kcal per gram. (Carbohydrates provide 4 kcal/g, protein 4 kcal/g).

Total calories = 146 kcal.

Calories from protein = 1g × 4 = 4 kcal.

Calories from carbohydrates = 13g × 4 = 52 kcal.

Calories from alcohol = 146 − (4 + 52) = 146 − 56 = 90 kcal.

Grams of alcohol = 90 kcal ÷ 7 kcal/g = 12.85g, rounding to 13 grams.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Which of these statements is correct? *
Answer (Back): Outcome evaluation assesses the effectiveness and efficiency of an intervention.
Rationale:
Outcome evaluation assesses whether a program achieved its immediate objectives, examining its operational effectiveness and efficiency.

• Impact evaluation: Assesses long-term population-level effects.
Option 1: Impact evaluation assesses the long-term effect of an intervention.
Option 2: Outcome evaluation examines the methods used in the project.
Option 3: Outcome evaluation assesses the effectiveness and efficiency of an intervention.
Option 4: Impact evaluation determines the target groups of the project.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The combination of food and drinks that will provide an additional 300 calories to a woman who is 5 months pregnant and underweight: *a. 1 cup rice, 1 c fresh milk, 1 medium-sized fish
Answer (Back): 1 cup rice, 1 tsp cooking oil, 1 mb lean pork, ¾ cup papaya
Rationale: To provide an additional 300 kcal (along with balanced protein and micronutrients) for an underweight pregnant woman at 5 months gestation, a meal combination featuring complex carbohydrates, a lean protein exchange, cooking oil, and fruit provides the appropriate caloric and nutrient boost.
Option 1: 6 pcs. pan de sal, 1 tsp margarine, 1 cup fresh milk, 1 cup watermelon
Option 2: 1 cup rice, 1 tsp cooking oil, 1 mb lean pork, ¾ cup papaya
Option 3: ½ cup rice, 1 tsp cooking oil, 1 mb lean pork

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is the most frequently used skinfold measurement to obtain a single, indirect measure of body fat: *
Rationale: The triceps skinfold measurement is the most frequently utilized, accessible anthropometric site to obtain a single indirect assessment of subcutaneous body fat reserves.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): A food record will be most valuable and useful to use among: *
Rationale: A 3-day food record or dietary food diary requires high participant motivation, literacy, and active engagement, making it most valuable and reliable when utilized among motivated cohorts such as overweight women tracking weight management.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The main reason for introducing new foods to an infant one at a time is: *
Answer (Back): to detect any allergic reactions that may develop
Rationale: New solid foods must be introduced to infants one at a time (spaced several days apart) so that if an adverse food allergy or hypersensitivity develops, the specific causative food can be immediately identified.
Option 1: to detect any allergic reactions that may develop
Option 3: the infant’s immunity is still weak
Option 4: the infant’s swallowing reflex is not yet fully developed

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The nutrition intervention which has a high impact on nutritional status: *
Rationale: Among public health nutrition interventions, improving dietary diversification (broadening access to nutrient-dense, varied local foods) yields the most sustained, high-impact improvements on long-term nutritional status.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): You are training Barangay Nutrition Scholars on weighing techniques. What topic will you discuss first? *
Answer (Back): the role, tasks, and skills needed by Barangay Nutrition Scholars
Rationale:
When training community workers like Barangay Nutrition Scholars (BNS), introductory training modules must begin by clarifying their foundational community role, statutory tasks, and required competencies before teaching specific technical mechanics like weighing.

• History of the PNP: Too theoretical for immediate practical field training.
• Procedures on how to do weighing: Taught subsequent to orienting them on their scope of work.
Option 1: history of the Philippine Nutrition Program
Option 2: procedures on how to do weighing
Option 4: the role, tasks, and skills needed by Barangay Nutrition Scholars

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The type of PEM caused by early weaning from breast milk and giving inadequate infant formula: *
Rationale: Marasmus is the severe form of protein-energy malnutrition characterized by generalized severe wasting, calorie deficiency, and early weaning from breast milk onto inadequate, dilute infant formulas.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): It is not considered an intervention: *
Rationale:
Operation Timbang (OTP) Plus is an annual mass anthropometric weighing and height screening program conducted to identify malnourished preschoolers, functioning as a surveillance/screening tool rather than a direct therapeutic intervention.

• Breast feeding / Food Fortification / Food Subsidy: Direct nutritional interventions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All these individuals can be respondents of a 24-hour food recall except for: *
Rationale: Young children aged 4 to 8 years have unreliable dietary recall memory and lack the cognitive ability to accurately estimate portion sizes independently without parental proxy reporting, making them an unsuitable cohort for unassisted 24-hour recalls.
Option 4: children more than 8 years of age

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The common nutrition-related diseases of adults: *
Rationale:
The predominant chronic nutrition-related non-communicable diseases affecting adult populations globally and locally include cardiovascular pathologies and metabolic syndrome manifestations: atherosclerosis, hypertension, and obesity.

• Asthma, diabetes, and hypertension: Asthma is primarily respiratory/allergic rather than a primary nutritional degenerative disease.
• Kidney disease: While nutrition-related, atherosclerosis, hypertension, and obesity represent the classic triad of adult metabolic/cardiovascular diseases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The growth chart of Carlo shows an upward direction towards the reference line. How will you interpret this? *
Rationale:
An upward growth chart trajectory that parallels or follows the standard reference percentile lines indicates that a child is gaining weight and growing adequately.

• Carlo is not growing: A flat or downward line would indicate growth faltering.
• Carlo is wasted: Indicated by weight-for-height falling below normal thresholds.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The action implemented to stop the cause of a nutrition problem: *
Rationale:
In the public health nutrition cycle, an intervention refers to a purposeful, planned action or program implemented specifically to stop or mitigate the root cause of an identified nutrition problem.

• Surveillance: Ongoing systematic collection of data.
• Screening: Identifying individuals at risk.
• Monitoring: Tracking progress over time.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The best graphical presentation to show the percentage distribution of foods consumed in relation to total calories. *
Rationale:
A pie chart (circle graph) is the optimal graphical presentation tool to display proportional parts relative to a whole (such as percentage distribution of calories or macronutrients).

• Line graph: Used for trends over continuous time.
• Histogram / Scatter plot: Used for frequency distributions and statistical correlations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): PEM affects certain population groups only. Adolescents, adult males, non-pregnant and non-lactating women have the lowest prevalence of PEM. *
Answer (Back): Only the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because Protein-Energy Malnutrition (PEM) affects diverse vulnerable demographics (infants, children, pregnant women, elderly) across various settings, not just isolated population groups. 

Statement 2 is correct because epidemiological surveys consistently show that adolescents, adult males, and non-pregnant/non-lactating women exhibit the lowest prevalence rates of severe PEM compared to young children.
Option 1: Only the first statement is correct.
Option 2: Only the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): These foods help in meeting the preschoolers’ needs for iron. *
Rationale:
Whole-grain and enriched breads and cereals provide accessible non-heme iron sources that help meet the high daily iron requirements of growing preschoolers.

• Milk: Exceptionally poor in iron.
• Oranges: Rich in Vitamin C, but poor in iron.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): All are weaknesses of the 24-hour recall except: *
Answer (Back): It is difficult to obtain information.
Rationale:
A 24-hour recall is relatively easy and fast to administer in the field, making "difficulty in obtaining information" false (and thus the correct exception representing a non-weakness).

• It provides information on a day's intake only: A recognized limitation (does not capture habitual individual intake).
• Respondent memory bias: A well-known limitation of recall methods.
Option 1: It provides information on a day’s intake only.
Option 2: It is not representative of a typical food intake.
Option 3: The respondent does not give accurate food intake.
Option 4: It is difficult to obtain information.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): This law intends to prevent iodine deficiency disorders in the country. *
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 8172 is the Act Promoting Salt Iodization Nationwide (ASIN Law), enacted to eliminate iodine deficiency disorders (IDD) in the Philippines.

• RA 2674: Dietetic Law.
• RA 1569: Barangay Health Workers act / BNS precursor.
• RA 8191: National Voluntary Blood Services Act.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Giving the infant breast milk substitutes can result in poor growth or illness because: *
Answer (Back): the bottles and teats used for feeding are not cleaned properly.
Rationale:
Infant formula and breast milk substitutes lack the live immunological antibodies found in breast milk; combined with unsterilized bottles and teats, microbial contamination leads to severe infant diarrhea, illness, and growth faltering.

• Calorie content / Protein content: Standard commercial infant formulas are engineered to approximate breast milk macronutrient and caloric profiles.
• Low bioavailability of vitamins/minerals: Formulas are fortified to meet infant requirements.
Option 1: the calorie content of breast milk substitutes is below the infant’s energy needs.
Option 2: there is a low bioavailability of vitamins and minerals.
Option 3: the bottles and teats used for feeding are not cleaned properly.
Option 4: the protein content of milk formulas is low.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The target groups of the Medium Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition: I. children 1-3 years old II. adolescent females III. pregnant and lactating mothers IV. elderly *
Rationale: The Medium-Term Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PAPAN) prioritizes high-risk vulnerable groups: children 1-3 years old, adolescent females, and pregnant/lactating mothers. The elderly are managed through separate geriatric health frameworks.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The following foods are considered sources of complete protein: I. casein in milk II. Albumin in egg white III. legumin in legumes IV. zein in corn *
Rationale: Casein in milk and albumin in egg white are complete proteins containing all essential amino acids in sufficient proportions. Legumin in legumes is limiting in methionine, and zein in corn is limiting in lysine and tryptophan.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Malnutrition among the urban poor is greater than the rural poor. The two main possible causes of high malnutrition among the urban poor are: I. poor housing conditions II. lack of health centers and personnel. III. low level of education IV. inadequate food intake *a. II & IV
Rationale: Malnutrition among the urban poor is driven largely by poor housing conditions (sanitation/water access) and inadequate food intake (due to cash dependency and volatile food prices).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The 2013 NNS prevalence of underweight 0-5 year-old children _____ compared to 2008 NNS. *
Rationale: National Nutrition Surveys (NNS) by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI) recorded a downward trend in the national prevalence of underweight among children aged 0-5 years.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The prevalence of nutritionally at-risk pregnant women in the 2013 NNS ____ compared to the 2008 NNS. *
Rationale: FNRI National Nutrition Surveys documented a progressive decrease in the prevalence of nutritionally at-risk pregnant women over successive survey cycles.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The prevalence of overweight lactating mothers in 2013 NNS ____ compared to the 2008 NNS. *
Rationale: Nutritional surveys highlight an alarming upward trend in the prevalence of overweight and obesity among lactating and adult women.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The prevalence of anemia in 2013 NNS is of high magnitude and considered a public health problem among _______. *
Rationale: National nutrition survey findings classify iron deficiency anemia as a public health problem of high magnitude specifically among school-age children, 6-12 year-old youth, and adolescents.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The prevalence of hypertension among adults ______ in 2013 NNS compared to the 2008 NNS. *
Rationale: Survey tracking on adult blood pressure trends shows fluctuating or managed declines in certain cohort brackets, though hypertension remains a major NCD priority.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): The prevalence of high fasting blood glucose among adults _____ in 2013 NNS compared with the 2008 NNS. *
Rationale: National health data demonstrates a steady upward trend in the prevalence of elevated fasting blood glucose levels and impaired glucose tolerance among adult populations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
Question (Front): Based on the 2013 NNS, males are more prone to having _____ across all ages. *
Rationale: Across national nutrition survey data subsets, adult males consistently exhibit a higher prevalence of hypertension across various age brackets compared to females.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Community and Applied Nutrition (CPHN+)
