Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Local term for “all spice” is: *
Rationale:
In Philippine culinary terminology and HE (Home Economics) textbook translations, pimiento (or pimienta) is often used to refer to allspice. This is derived from the plant's botanical name, Pimenta dioica, and its Spanish name, Pimienta de Jamaica (Jamaican pepper). While colloquially in modern times "pimiento" is frequently associated with red bell peppers (pimientos), in the context of traditional spice translations on the board exam, it stands for allspice.

• Linga: The local term for sesame seeds, commonly used in making palitaw or various Asian sauces.
• Kolantro: The local term for coriander (the seeds). The fresh leaves of this plant are locally referred to as wansoy (cilantro).
• Laurel: The local term for bay leaf, an indispensable aromatic in Filipino adobo.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A fermented soybean cake but is softer than “tokwa”. *
Rationale:
In Philippine culinary terminology, tahure refers to fermented soybean curd (often known in English as fermented bean curd). It is sold as small blocks or cakes preserved in brine, occasionally with red yeast rice or chili. The fermentation process breaks down the proteins, resulting in a texture that is significantly softer, creamier, and more pungent than regular firm tokwa. It is commonly used as a flavor enhancer in dishes like pesang isda (fish stew) or mashed into dipping sauces.

• Tofu: This is the general English term for soybean curd. While it comes in soft varieties, standard tofu is unfermented. Tokwa is simply the local term for the firm variety of tofu.
• Miso: While this is a fermented soybean product, it is processed into a thick paste, not formed into cakes or blocks.
• Taho: This is an unfermented, extremely soft, silken soybean curd typically served warm as a sweet snack with brown sugar syrup (arnibal) and sago pearls. It is not fermented and does not hold a cake-like shape.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If cornstarch is used instead of flour, this produces a sauce that is: *
Rationale: Cornstarch possesses a much higher proportion of pure amylose starch compared to wheat flour (which contains proteins and less concentrated starch per cup). Because of this higher concentration of starch granules, substituting cornstarch for flour weight-for-weight or volume-for-volume yields a noticeably thicker glossy sauce or gravy.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is used in chopsuey or “linaga”/”nilaga”: *
Rationale:
Kutsay (garlic chives) is a traditional aromatic herb widely used in local Filipino vegetable dishes like chopsuey or boiled broths such as nilaga to impart a mild, garlic-onion aroma and green garnish.

Katuray: Edible white flowers used in Ilocano pinakbet or salads.

Kinchay: Chinese celery, used for soups and pancit.

Tanglad: Lemon grass, used for grilled or stewed aromatic meats (like tinola or adobo variations).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Homogenized milk refers to milk with reduced: *
Rationale:
Homogenization is a mechanical high-pressure process that forces milk through microscopic nozzles, shattering and reducing the fat particle size (globules) uniformly so they remain permanently suspended in the liquid rather than separating and rising as cream.

Bacterial count: Addressed by pasteurization, not mechanical homogenization.

Total fat content: Homogenization redistributes fat globules but does not change the total chemical fat percentage of the milk.

Protein content: Protein structures remain stable during physical fat droplet breakdown.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If cocoa is substituted for chocolate in a chocolate cake recipe, you should:
Rationale: Note: This is a classic trick question from local board exam pools. While substituting cocoa powder for solid chocolate usually requires adjusting liquids or fats because cocoa is far more absorbent, the official exam key designates increase the fat to compensate for the missing cocoa butter previously supplied by whole chocolate liquor.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): 101. A cake recipe has the following ingredients: ½ cup butter; 1 cup milk; 3 cups cake flour; 3 teaspoons baking powder; 1 ½ cups granulated sugar. Butter is not available so that margarine will be used. How much margarine is needed? *
Rationale: Margarine can be substituted for butter on a direct 1:1 volume-for-volume ratio in standard baking recipes because both fats contain equivalent proportions of fat emulsions and moisture. Since the original recipe calls for 1/2 cup of butter, exactly 1/2 cup of margarine is needed.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Left-over meat from Arroz ala Cubana may be restyled to: *
Rationale:
Leftover cooked minced or ground meat from Arroz ala Cubana (seasoned ground beef with peas, raisins, and carrots) is easily repurposed and restyled into a savory omelet or tortilla by folding the seasoned meat filling into beaten eggs.

Arroz Valenciana: A complex Spanish-Filipino one-pot rice dish traditionally made with raw or freshly cooked chicken and chorizo, not a direct restyling vehicle for leftover seasoned ground beef.

Hamburger: Requires specific ground meat fat-to-lean ratios and bun pairings, making an egg omelet a more immediate and flexible restyling option for cooked minced meat leftovers.

Fritada: A stewed meat dish prepared from raw cuts simmered with potatoes and tomato sauce, not leftover ground meat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The best location of storing milk, meats, fish, and poultry in a cooling unit is: *
Answer (Back): at the bottom of the shelves
Rationale: In food safety and sanitation, raw meats, poultry, and fish must always be stored on the bottom shelves of a cooling unit (refrigerator). This is a critical rule designed to prevent cross-contamination; it ensures that blood and raw juices—which may contain dangerous pathogens—cannot drip down onto ready-to-eat foods, produce, or cooked items. Additionally, because heat rises, the bottom shelves are typically the coldest and most temperature-stable area of the refrigerator, making it the ideal environment for highly perishable items like milk and raw proteins.
Option 1: at the back of the door
Option 2: at the top of the shelves
Option 3: at the bottom of the shelves
Option 4: at the middle of the shelves

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Two ways recommended in sanitizing foodservice utensils: 1. washing with soap and water; 2. immersion in hot water; 3. by chemical treatment; 4. washing with detergent and water *
Rationale:
Under standard sanitation codes for food establishments, the two approved and recommended sanitizing methods for cleaned foodservice utensils and equipment after washing are immersion in hot water (thermal sanitizing) or chemical treatment (using sanitizing solutions like chlorine, quaternary ammonium, or iodine).

1 & 4: Washing with soap/detergent and water represents the cleaning stage, not the final sanitizing stage.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A type of foodservice system with the advantage of lowering operating costs and wastage: *
Rationale:
An assembly-serve foodservice system (often called the "kitchen-less kitchen") utilizes fully prepared, convenience, or frozen food items that require only thawing, portioning, heating, and assembling, which drastically lowers operational labor costs, specialized equipment needs, and food wastage.

Ready prepared: Prepares food on-site ahead of time and blast-chills or freezes it in bulk, requiring specialized rethermalization equipment.

Commissary: A centralized mass-production kitchen that distributes food to satellite units, involving large-scale capital investments.

Conventional: Prepares food from scratch on-site daily, carrying higher labor overhead and potential waste if forecasting is inaccurate.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A standardized recipe for Chicken Pork Adobo has a yield of 25 servings. You need 75 servings in your catering. What will be your adjustment factor? *
Rationale: To calculate the recipe adjustment factor (multiplier), divide the desired yield by the original recipe yield: 75 servings / 25 servings = 3. Every ingredient in the original recipe must be multiplied by 3 to scale it correctly for the catering order.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An ISO 9000 certification of a company means that the company: *
Answer (Back): complies with minimum standards of quality management
Rationale: An ISO 9000 certification indicates that an organization has implemented and maintains a rigorous quality management system that strictly complies with internationally recognized minimum standards and quality assurance protocols.
Option 1: is a member of the International Standards Organization
Option 2: complies with minimum standards of quality management

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The Philippine Code on Sanitation: *
Rationale:
Presidential Decree No. 856, promulgated in 1975, is officially known as the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines, establishing comprehensive sanitary standards for food establishments, water supply, waste disposal, and public health.

PD 1286: Not the sanitation code decree.

PD 491: The Nutrition Act of the Philippines, which created the National Nutrition Council (NNC).

PD 568: Relates to other administrative or agricultural decrees.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An establishment with a par stock of 10 cartons of milk needs to order how many cartons after an inventory showed that 4 cartons are left? *
Rationale:
The formula for calculating the required order quantity using par stock is: Order Quantity = Par Stock − Quantity on Hand.

Par Stock = 10 cartons

Quantity on Hand = 4 cartons

Order Quantity = 10 − 4 = 6 cartons.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The recommended clearance of shelves off the floor in storage rooms is: *
Rationale: In institutional sanitation and food storage guidelines, all food, ingredients, and storage shelves must be elevated a minimum of 6 inches (15 cm) off the floor to allow proper air circulation, facilitate easy cleaning beneath shelves, and prevent pest infestation or moisture damage.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Based on the Sanitation Code, what is the recommended storage temperature for dairy products? *
Rationale:
In foodservice management and sanitation codes (like ServSafe), the numerical range 50 to 70 is the universal standard for Dry Storage temperatures (50°F to 70°F / 10°C to 21°C). This applies to dry goods, including powdered dairy products, unopened canned milk, and unopened UHT tetra-pak milk.

Here is why the question as written is technically incorrect, but why A is the forced answer:

1. The Unit Error: The options are written in Celsius (°C). Storing any food at 50°C to 70°C (122°F to 158°F) is actually hot holding and would severely spoil, curdle, and ruin dairy products. The author intended Fahrenheit (°F).

2. The Category Error: It is highly likely the original question meant to ask for the storage temperature of dry products, not dairy products.

3. The True Dairy Standard: According to the Sanitation Code, fresh, perishable liquid dairy products must be stored under strict cold refrigeration at 41°F (5°C) or below.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If the delivered supplies are incomplete, the receiving personnel must accomplish what type of form to be submitted to the accounting department? *
Rationale:
In foodservice purchasing and accounting, a credit memo (credit memorandum) is the vital financial document issued when a delivery is short-shipped, incomplete, or contains damaged/rejected goods. The receiving clerk uses this form to notify the accounting department that the restaurant should not pay the full original invoice amount, but instead apply a financial credit for the missing items.

• Receiving form: This is merely a log used by the receiving clerk to record what actually arrived at the loading dock. It is not a financial adjustment document.
• Requisition form: This is an internal document used by kitchen staff to request ingredients from the restaurant's own dry storeroom or walk-in cooler.
• Discrepancy report form: While this might be used internally by management to track vendor performance, the credit memo is the specific, formal document required by accounting to adjust the accounts payable.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The type of inventory performed when the peso value is computed after a specific period of time: *
Rationale:
physical inventoryA physical inventory is the literal, manual counting of every single item sitting on the shelves in the storeroom and refrigerators at the end of a specific accounting period (e.g., end of the month). Once the physical count is finished, the quantities are multiplied by their unit purchase price to determine the total peso value of the inventory on hand, which is required to calculate the true Cost of Goods Sold.

• Perpetual inventory: This is a continuous, running paper or digital record of what should be in the storeroom based on daily deliveries and requisitions. It tracks theoretical quantities in real-time, not the actual physical count evaluated at period-end.
• Daily inventory: While high-value items (like expensive meats or liquor) might be counted daily for security, a full peso-value inventory of the entire facility is done periodically, not daily.
• Financial inventory: This is a general business term, but "physical inventory" is the exact standard operational terminology used in foodservice management.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): To adjust a standardized recipe to 150 servings using the factor method, the amount of ingredients of a recipe that yields 10 servings must be multiplied by which value? *
Rationale: In foodservice quantity recipe conversion using the factor method, the conversion factor is calculated by dividing the desired yield by the original recipe yield. Therefore, 150 desired servings divided by 10 original servings gives a multiplication factor of 15. Every ingredient in the original recipe must be multiplied by 15.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Take out counters are classified under which service type? *
Rationale:
Take-out counters and food pickup windows operate within the physical boundaries of the main food facility (on-premise), but the food is packaged and handed over to customers to be carried away or consumed elsewhere, categorizing it under portable service formats.

Off-premise portable service: This refers to catered events, mobile food trucks, or home delivery services where food preparation and consumption occur completely away from the base kitchen facility.

Decentralized service: This describes institutional food systems where bulk food is transported from a central kitchen to distant pantries or ward kitchens for final assembly and service.

Centralized service: This is a system where plates and meals are completely assembled and portioned directly in the main kitchen before being dispatched to the consumer.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): These pests feed not only on foodstuffs but also on non-food items like soap: *
Rationale:
The German cockroach is notorious for its omnivorous, highly adaptable scavenging habits. In addition to contaminating human food stocks, they readily consume non-food organic household items such as soap, glue, book bindings, leather, and toothpaste.

American cockroach: While large and destructive, they typically prefer damp, decaying organic matter, basements, and sewers rather than household non-food items like soap.

Oriental cockroach: Commonly known as waterbugs, these pests favor extremely damp, cool environments like floor drains and damp basements, feeding primarily on starchy garbage.

Asian cockroach: This species closely resembles the German cockroach in appearance, but it is an outdoor flyer attracted to bright lights and plant material rather than indoor household soaps and non-food goods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Gnawed cartons in the storage room indicate the presence of which pest? *
Rationale:
Rodents (such as mice and rats) possess continually growing incisor teeth, forcing them to constantly gnaw and chew on hard surfaces—including cardboard packaging, paper bags, and wooden crates—to keep their teeth worn down and to access stored food.

Cockroaches: Cockroaches damage food packaging through rasping mouthparts that leave microscopic scrape marks or thin holes, but they do not produce large, aggressive gnawed carton edges.

House fly: House flies feed exclusively on liquid or semi-liquid organic matter through sponging mouthparts and are physically incapable of gnawing through solid paper cartons.

Fruit fly: Fruit flies feed on fermenting organic debris and overripe fruit, leaving packaging completely intact.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A “reactive” type of manager: *
Answer (Back): responds to problems as they arise
Rationale: In organizational behavior and management principles, a reactive manager operates in a "firefighting" mode. They wait for situations, crises, or problems to occur and then react to them as they arise, rather than anticipating them in advance.
Option 2: responds to problems as they arise

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): NSF and UL indicate that an imported equipment complied with certain quality standards. “Kawa” is an example of NSF-certified equipment. *
Rationale: NSF (National Sanitation Foundation) and UL (Underwriters Laboratories) are internationally recognized certification bodies that evaluate and ensure imported and local foodservice equipment complies with rigorous public health, safety, and sanitation standards. Furthermore, in the context of specialized local culinary equipment standards, a "kawa" (a large, heavy-duty wok-like traditional Filipino vessel used for mass cooking) can be manufactured to meet these certified sanitary stainless steel fabrication standards for commercial kitchens.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is an example of a local piece of equipment? *
Rationale:
In the context of Philippine foodservice operations and institutional equipment classification, a "local piece of equipment" generally refers to heavy-duty, commonly utilized cooking vessels that are often manufactured or adapted locally for Asian/Filipino cooking methods (like large-scale boiling and tenderizing meats for broths and stews). The Chinese pressure cooker fits this description as it is a staple in many local commercial kitchens for quickly tenderizing tough cuts of meat (like beef shank for bulalo or pork hocks).

• Split vat fryer: This is highly specialized commercial deep-frying equipment, typically imported and associated with Western-style fast-food chains (for frying fries and chicken separately without flavor transfer).
• Salamander: A specialized, high-heat broiler used in professional (often Western/European style) kitchens to quickly brown the tops of dishes, melt cheese, or toast ingredients. It is not considered a local piece of equipment.
• Rotary oven: A massive, complex, and usually imported piece of commercial baking equipment featuring rotating racks to ensure even baking for high-volume bread production.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What is the recommended distance of septic tanks from drinking water supply? *
Rationale: The primary purpose of establishing a minimum distance between a septic tank (or leaching field) and a drinking water supply (such as a well) is to prevent cross-contamination. While the baseline national Sanitation Code of the Philippines (PD 856) sets a minimum of 25 meters, many stringent local ordinances, environmental guidelines, and board exam references recommend a more conservative buffer of 50 meters. This wider distance accounts for highly porous soil, sloping topography, and heavy rains, ensuring that harmful pathogens, coliform bacteria, and untreated effluent have absolutely no chance of seeping into the groundwater aquifer.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following does not contribute to food cost variance? *
Answer (Back): price increase with increased price of ingredients
Rationale:
In foodservice accounting, food cost variance is the gap between your actual food cost (what you actually spent/used) and your theoretical standard food cost (what you should have spent based on the recipes sold). Variance is caused by operational errors, waste, or theft.

If the market price of ingredients goes up, and management properly documents this by adjusting the standard recipe costs and raising the menu prices to match ("price increase with increased price of ingredients"), this is a controlled economic adjustment. It does not cause a variance because the system's theoretical cost is updated to reflect the new reality.
Option 2: price increase with increased price of ingredients

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What does high profitability mean? *
Answer (Back): Food items with low raw food cost.
Rationale:
In menu engineering, an item's profitability is determined by its contribution margin (Selling Price minus Raw Food Cost). The contribution margin is the actual cash amount that goes toward paying off overhead and generating pure profit. To achieve a high contribution margin (high profitability), the item must have a low raw food cost relative to its selling price (like pasta or beverage items).

• Food items with high food cost: High food costs eat directly into the gross margin, resulting in low profitability (menu "Dogs").
• High-priced items: A high menu price does not guarantee high profitability if the ingredients to make it are also extremely expensive (e.g., imported steak or lobster). The margin might still be slim.
• Low-priced items: While these might sell at a high volume, the actual cash profit generated per plate is usually very small.
Option 1: Food items with low raw food cost.
Option 2: Food items with high food cost.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Each element in the foodservice system needs to work independently to meet its own objective. The elements are interrelated to meet the overall objective of the system. *
Rationale: In systems theory applied to foodservice management, an organization functions as a dynamic system composed of interdependent parts. Each subsystem or element must maintain its own operational focus and efficiency (working independently to meet its internal objectives, such as a kitchen handling production or accounting managing finance), while remaining tightly interconnected and synchronized to achieve the overarching mission of the entire organization.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Souffle is a fluffy dish with a hard meringue. The equipment used to harden the meringue is: *
Rationale:
A salamander is a specialized commercial kitchen broiler characterized by intense overhead infrared heating elements. It is widely used in professional kitchens for browning the tops of dishes, melting cheese, toasting, and rapidly crisping or hardening a meringue topping on items like baked alaska or savory soufflés.

Rotisserie: This equipment uses a rotating spit to roast meats evenly via surrounding heat, not suitable for top-down surface browning of a delicate soufflé.

Ovenette: This is a small, portable tabletop baking appliance used for basic baking, lacking the direct high-intensity overhead broiling power needed to quickly crisp meringue.

Microwave: This appliance uses dielectric heating (microwaves) to excite water molecules internally, which would instantly deflate, rubberize, or destroy a delicate meringue rather than hardening its surface.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following foodservice system is usually compared to a food factory? *
Rationale:
A commissary foodservice system (centralized production kitchen) is frequently compared to a food factory because large quantities of food are mass-produced, processed, packaged, and stored in a central facility before being shipped out to separate, remote satellite service units for final reheating and distribution.

• Conventional: In this system, food is prepared, cooked, and served from the same location with minimal holding time, resembling traditional home-style cooking on a larger scale rather than a factory.
• Assembly serve: This system relies heavily on convenience foods and fully prepared commercial items that require only thawing, portioning, and heating, acting more like an assembly line than a primary manufacturing food factory.
• Ready-prepared system: Food is produced on-site, blast-chilled or frozen, and stored in bulk for future reheating, focusing on inventory flexibility rather than factory-style centralized mass distribution.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The most ideal water temperature in manual dishwashing: *
Rationale:
For manual dishwashing in a three-compartment sink, the wash water must be maintained at a minimum temperature of 100°F to 120°F (38°C to 49°C). This temperature range is hot enough to effectively melt and dissolve grease and food residues while remaining comfortable and safe for the dishwashing staff's hands.

120°F – 130°F: While acceptable in some specific commercial wash cycles, water kept consistently at or above this upper threshold can cause discomfort or minor burns during prolonged manual scrubbing without heavy-duty protection.

90°F – 100°F: This temperature range is too cool; fats and greases will congeal rather than dissolve, making manual cleaning inefficient.

80°F – 90°F: This is far too cold for effective manual dishwashing and creates an ideal lukewarm breeding environment for microbial growth in the sink basin.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A cleaning agent that is ideal for glasswares: *
Rationale:
Detergents contain surface-active agents (surfactants) that lower the surface tension of water, allowing it to penetrate and lift soils without scratching delicate surfaces. They are the ideal, safe cleaning agents for smooth, non-porous items like glassware and fine china.

Abrasive cleaners: These contain gritty chemical or mineral particles designed to scour away baked-on or stubborn soils, which will permanently scratch, etch, and ruin glass surfaces.

Alkaline cleaners: These are heavy-duty degreasers formulated to strip baked-on grease from stainless steel ovens and fryers; their high pH can cloud or damage glassware over time.

Acid cleaners: These are specialized descalers used to remove mineral buildup, lime deposits, or rust (delime equipment), and are too harsh for routine glassware washing.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The ideal solution for chemical sanitizing: *
Rationale:
According to standard foodservice sanitation guidelines (including ServSafe), the ideal and minimum effective concentration for a chlorine-based chemical sanitizer used on food-contact surfaces is 50 parts per million (ppm).

At 50 ppm (mixed with water between 75°F to 100°F), the chlorine solution effectively destroys pathogenic vegetative bacteria with just 7 seconds of contact time.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This type of cockroach is described as being both omnivorous and scavenger. *
Rationale:
The German cockroach is scientifically and behaviorally characterized as both an aggressive omnivore and a scavenger. They feed on an exceptionally wide variety of human foods, waste, and household organic materials, making them the most common and resilient indoor pest in foodservice facilities.

Oriental cockroach: Often called waterbugs, these pests prefer damp, cool, dark environments like floor drains and basements, focusing primarily on starchy garbage rather than general scavenging.

American cockroach: This is the largest common indoor cockroach species, favoring warm, moist areas like commercial plumbing tunnels and sewers rather than general food-prep scavenging.

Asian cockroach: This species is primarily an outdoor flyer that resembles the German cockroach but avoids indoor environments, being strongly attracted to outdoor lights and vegetation.

Question (Front): A component of Emotional Quotient that describes the ability of the employee to identify his/her strengths: *
Rationale:
In emotional intelligence (EQ) theory, self-awareness is the foundational core competency that describes an individual's ability to accurately recognize and understand their own emotions, personal triggers, internal states, and inherent strengths and limitations.

Empathy: This EQ component involves the ability to understand, recognize, and sensitively relate to the emotional needs, perspectives, and feelings of other people.

Self-regulation: This refers to the ability to control or redirect disruptive impulses, manage one's moods, and adapt successfully to changing circumstances.

Social skills: These are interpersonal competencies focused on managing relationships, building effective networks, communicating clearly, and leading teams collaboratively.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The recommended finishing of stainless steel for equipment in foodservice establishments is: *
Rationale:
In commercial foodservice equipment fabrication, a #4 finish (a brushed, polished, satin finish with fine parallel polish lines) is the industry gold standard for stainless steel surfaces. It provides an optimal balance of durability, ease of cleaning, corrosion resistance, and a professional aesthetic that hides minor scratches and fingerprints.

#3: This finish is a coarser, rougher polished surface with visible abrasion lines that trap food particles more easily than a #4 finish, making it less ideal for food-contact zones.

#8: This is an ultra-smooth, mirror-like reflective finish. While visually striking, it scratches easily, shows every fingerprint and smudge, and is impractical for heavy-duty commercial kitchen prep counters.

#14: This is not a standard commercial stainless steel mill finish designation used in foodservice equipment manufacturing.

Question (Front): According to the Sanitation Code of the Philippines, how many water closet facilities should be provided for disabled persons if the dining area accommodates 150 people? *
Rationale:
Under the National Building Code of the Philippines (BP 344 / Accessibility Law) and sanitary code plumbing provisions for public establishments, buildings or dining spaces accommodating up to 150 patrons must provide at least one accessible water closet facility specifically designed, equipped, and designated for persons with disabilities (PWD).

2: Requiring two PWD water closets is mandated for much larger capacities or multi-floor facilities, exceeding the baseline requirement for a 150-capacity dining area.

3: Three accessible water closet stalls are reserved for high-capacity public assembly venues or very large commercial complexes.

None: Providing no PWD facilities is a direct violation of accessibility laws and sanitary codes governing commercial food and dining establishments.

Question (Front): If the total area for a foodservice establishment is 280 sqm, what is the estimated space allocated for the dining area? *
Rationale: In standard foodservice facility layout and design principles, the dining room is typically allocated approximately 60% (or 0.60) of the total establishment area to ensure optimal customer comfort and operational flow. Multiplying the total area by this standard ratio (280 sqm x 0.60) yields exactly 168 sqm for the dining space.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The type of fire extinguisher that must be used for electrical-based fire: *
Rationale:
Fire extinguishers are categorized by the class of fire they are designed to suppress. Class C fire extinguishers are specifically rated for energized electrical equipment fires (such as appliance short circuits, faulty wiring, or electrical panels) because the extinguishing agent is non-conductive (like carbon dioxide or dry chemical), preventing the user from getting electrocuted.

A: Class A extinguishers are formulated for ordinary combustible solids like paper, wood, cloth, and trash, using water or water-based agents that would conduct electricity and worsen an electrical fire.

B: Class B extinguishers are designed for flammable liquid and gas fires (such as oil, grease, gasoline, or paint).

D: Class D extinguishers are strictly specialized for combustible metal fires (such as magnesium, titanium, or sodium).

Question (Front): If a seat at a table-serviced restaurant is estimated at 2.23 sqm, what is the estimated total area of the restaurant if the seating capacity is 150? *
Rationale:
To find the estimated area required for the dining space, you multiply the total seating capacity by the space allowance per seat.

Step-by-step calculation:

• Total Area = Seating Capacity × Space per seat
• Total Area = 150 seats × 2.23 sqm/seat
• Total Area = 334.5 sqm

Rounding to the nearest whole number gives 335 sqm.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A hospital serves 200 servings of Arroz Caldo at 240g per portion. What should be the capacity of equipment to be purchased? *
Rationale:
To determine the required equipment capacity, first calculate the total mass of the recipe: 200 servings × 0.240 kg (240g) = 48 kg of Arroz Caldo. 

Assuming a density close to water (1 kg ≈ 1 L), the total volume is roughly 48 liters. In food service engineering, cooking equipment (such as steam-jacketed kettles or stock pots) must never be filled to 100% capacity to prevent boiling over and allow for safe agitation; therefore, adding a standard 5% to 10% headspace safety margin means a 50 L capacity equipment is the proper selection.

Question (Front): What management theory emphasizes the interaction and cooperation among the subsystems? *a. Scientific Management
Rationale:
The Systems Approach to management views an organization as a unified, purposeful system composed of interrelated and interdependent parts (subsystems). It explicitly emphasizes that departments must interact and cooperate seamlessly, recognizing that a change or action in one subsystem directly impacts the entire organizational network.

Human Relations: Focuses primarily on interpersonal relationships, employee motivation, social needs, and group dynamics within the workplace.

Organizational Behavior: Studies the broad impact that individuals, groups, and organizational structure have on human behavior inside workplaces to improve organizational effectiveness.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The leadership style that fosters emotional bonds and harmony in an organization: *
Rationale:
In Daniel Goleman's leadership styles, the affiliative leader focuses heavily on building emotional bonds, promoting harmony, creating a friendly team environment, and boosting morale and loyalty among staff members.

Democratic: Focuses on building consensus and commitment through widespread employee participation in decision-making.

Pacesetting: Sets extremely high performance standards and models obsessive drive, which can sometimes demoralize teams if expectations become unrealistic.

Coaching: Focuses primarily on long-term professional development, mentoring employees, and aligning their personal goals with organizational goals.

Question (Front): According to Acquired Needs Theory, what should be done to employees who seek achievement? *
Answer (Back): They should be given challenging projects with reachable goals.
Rationale:
According to David McClelland’s Acquired Needs Theory (Three-Needs Theory), individuals with a high need for achievement are intrinsically motivated by tasks that offer personal responsibility, clear feedback, and moderate, calculated risks. To keep them engaged and productive, they must be assigned challenging projects with reachable goals.

They should be given opportunity to manage others: This aligns more closely with a high need for power, not necessarily a pure need for task achievement.

They should be given a task with people they like: This addresses the need for affiliation, focusing on social belonging and group harmony.

They should be given a supporting role for projects: This fails to challenge high-achiever profiles who thrive on personal accountability and driving results.
Option 1: They should be given opportunity to manage others.
Option 2: They should be given a task with people they like.
Option 3: They should be given challenging projects with reachable goals.
Option 4: They should be given a supporting role for projects.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): According to Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, what should be done to accomplish the needs of acquiring a status? *
Rationale:
According to Abraham Maslow’s Hierarchy of Needs, higher-level needs include esteem and status, which involve recognition, prestige, respect, and personal accomplishment in the workplace. Providing performance-based benefits, awards, promotions, and public recognition directly satisfies these status and esteem needs.

Provision of basic needs: Addresses Maslow's foundational physiological needs (food, water, shelter, basic salary).

Provision of security and safe policies: Satisfies safety and security needs (job security, health insurance, safe working conditions).

Provision of training and development: Relates to self-actualization and esteem growth, but specific status recognition is best driven by performance rewards and benefits.
Option 2: Provision of security and safe policies

Question (Front): The number of servings obtained in 1 gallon of ice cream when a #10 scoop is used: *
Rationale:
In institutional food service, standard scoop (disher) sizing numbers indicate how many level scoopfuls fit into one quart (32 fluid ounces). A #10 scoop holds 1/10 of a quart per serving. Since 1 gallon contains 4 quarts:

4 quarts x 10 servings per quart = 64 servings (using standard 16 oz pints/fluid ounces conversion conventions tested in board exams where 1 gallon = 128 oz divided by a #10 scoop's capacity equivalent).

32 servings: This would correspond to a larger scoop size (like a #5 or #8) yielding fewer portions per gallon.
48 servings: An incorrect intermediate calculation that does not match standard disher math matrices.
56 servings: Also an incorrect arithmetic distractor not aligned with standard #10 disher conversion tables.

Question (Front): It is the primary consideration when planning the equipment layout: *
Rationale: In facility layout and kitchen design, the menu is universally recognized as the single most critical primary consideration. Question (Front): Which of the following is greatly expected from the first line management? *
Rationale:
According to Robert L. Katz's management skills framework, technical skills (the proficiency, specialized knowledge, and hands-on ability to perform specific operational tasks) are most heavily expected from first-line or lower-level management. First-line supervisors work directly with operational employees, requiring them to understand and train staff on daily execution.

Human skills: Important across all levels of management, but not uniquely prioritized over technical skills at the frontline supervisory tier.

Interpersonal skills: Vital for team communication, yet operational oversight at the base level relies most on direct technical know-how.

Conceptual skills: These are the cognitive abilities to see the big picture and strategize, which are primarily required at top-level management rather than first-line supervisors.

Question (Front): Historical sales data can be used in the following except: *
Rationale:
Historical sales data tracks past revenues and customer counts, making it directly useful for food production forecasting, manpower scheduling, and daily sales projections. However, expenses forecasting relies heavily on projected price fluctuations from suppliers, fixed overhead changes, inflation rates, and future purchasing contracts rather than historical sales revenue alone.

Food production forecasting: Directly derived from historical sales mix and guest count data to predict how much food to prep.

Manpower forecasting: Uses past sales trends and customer volume patterns to schedule labor efficiently.

Daily sales forecasting: Relies directly on historical day-of-the-week sales records to project upcoming daily revenue targets.

Question (Front): The following are strategies to control cost except: *
Answer (Back): hiring staff with high educational attainment
Rationale:
Hiring staff based purely on high educational attainment does not inherently control or reduce food and labor costs. In fact, overqualified staff may demand higher wages or experience turnover if the job does not match their credentials, making it an ineffective cost-control strategy.

Training employees: Directly controls cost by reducing food waste, minimizing over-portioning, and improving operational efficiency.

Use of financial records: Crucial for monitoring food costs, labor percentages, and budget variances to prevent financial loss.

Establishment of rules: Enforces operational standardization, waste reduction, and compliance with safety and portion guidelines.
Option 4: hiring staff with high educational attainment

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If the target is not consistently met, what is the best initial course of action to take? *
Rationale:
When performance targets are consistently missed over a sustained operational period, the most professional and strategic initial management action is to reforecast. Reforecasting involves re-evaluating baseline assumptions, market conditions, pricing strategies, and operational budgets to establish realistic, attainable goals rather than blindly pushing unreachable quotas.

Retrain staff: While training helps, chronic target failures often stem from flawed initial budget forecasting or macroeconomic shifts rather than just staff incompetence.

Increase price: Raising menu prices without analyzing market elasticity can drive remaining customers away, worsening the shortfall.

Increase sales: Merely stating a desire to increase sales is not a strategic planning step without a revised financial reforecast.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Uncalibrated measuring equipment will most likely result in the following except: *
Rationale:
Uncalibrated measuring equipment leads to inaccurate scaling, inconsistent recipe proportions, and heavy ingredient over-portioning or waste. While this directly drives up food cost, it does not inherently increase administrative or fixed operating costs (like rent, utilities, or insurance), making operating cost the correct exception.

Unequal serving portion sizes: Inaccurate measuring tools cause portions to vary wildly from plate to plate.

Increased food cost: Using more ingredients than specified due to uncalibrated scales directly inflates raw food costs and food cost percentages.

Incorrect proportion of ingredients: Poor measurement disrupts chemical baking ratios and recipe flavor profiles.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): In conducting an ocular inspection for a restaurant, the site is usually evaluated in terms of the following except: *
Rationale:
During an initial site evaluation or ocular inspection for a new restaurant, the physical location is evaluated based on its logistical viability and market reach. Affordability relates strictly to internal financial budgeting and lease negotiations managed during business planning, not an external physical site evaluation metric.

Accessibility: Evaluated by checking if customers and delivery trucks can easily reach the site via roads and public transport.

Availability (utilities): Assessed by confirming if stable water, electricity, drainage, and gas lines are connected to the site.

Visibility: Evaluated by checking if the building can be easily seen by passing foot and vehicular traffic.

Question (Front): A first step to follow in solid waste management is to: *
Answer (Back): separate the biodegradable from non-biodegradable waste
Rationale:
The mandatory foundational first step in solid waste management programs (in compliance with environmental laws like RA 9003 in the Philippines) is waste segregation—separating biodegradable organic waste from non-biodegradable, recyclable, and residual waste right at the source.

Burn biodegradable waste: Open burning of waste is illegal under clean air acts and environmental health codes due to toxic emissions.

Compress the non-biodegradable waste: Compression is a secondary volume-reduction step performed after proper sorting and collection.

Grind the solid waste: Grinding requires specialized equipment and is only done after initial segregation and organic waste processing (e.g., food pulpers).
Option 2: separate the biodegradable from non-biodegradable waste

Question (Front): It is considered the foundation of Human Resource Management: *
Rationale:

It serves as the bedrock for all Human Resource Management functions, directly supplying the data needed to write job descriptions and specifications.

• Job description: A formal document outlining duties and reporting lines, which is directly derived from the results of a job analysis.
• Job schedule: A timeline or shift roster assigning working hours to employees.

Question (Front): Among the members of the planning team, this professional is mainly responsible for ensuring that the building’s construction adheres to local fire regulations: *

Interior designer: Focuses on aesthetics, finishes, color schemes, lighting ambiance, and dining room spatial comfort.

Architect: Designs the overall spatial layout, exterior styling, and functional flow of the facility, working alongside engineers for regulatory compliance.

Food service consultant: Specializes in kitchen workflow design, equipment selection, and menu engineering, not structural fire code compliance.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It emphasizes the importance of putting efforts in people as a key goal in organizations. *
Rationale:
In management and organizational behavior, the Human Relations Approach (pioneered by Elton Mayo and the Hawthorne Studies) marked a massive shift in how organizations were run. It established that workers are not just cogs in a machine driven by money, but social beings motivated by psychological needs, recognition, and interpersonal dynamics. Therefore, it emphasizes that management must put significant effort into understanding, supporting, and developing its people to achieve organizational success.

• Japanese Theory: Often referred to as Theory Z (developed by William Ouchi), this blends American and Japanese management styles, focusing on long-term employment, consensus decision-making, and holistic concern for the employee. While it values people, the foundational concept of prioritizing people over tasks originates from the broader Human Relations Approach.
• Classical Scientific Management Theory: Pioneered by Frederick Taylor, this is the exact opposite. It treats the organization as a machine and focuses entirely on maximizing the efficiency of tasks, often ignoring the psychological and social needs of the workers.
• Game Theory: This is a mathematical and economic model used to analyze strategic decision-making and competition between different parties. It is not a management theory focused on organizational human behavior.

Question (Front): Management can be viewed as organic or mechanistic. Between the two, the mechanistic approach is closely associated with the views of human relations theory. *
Answer (Back): Only the first sentence is correct.
Rationale:
Sentence 1 is true: In organizational theory (notably by Burns and Stalker), management structures are broadly categorized into two systems: mechanistic (rigid, highly centralized, and bureaucratic) and organic (flexible, decentralized, and adaptable).

Sentence 2 is false: The mechanistic approach is strongly associated with Classical Management Theory (such as Frederick Taylor’s Scientific Management and Max Weber’s Bureaucracy), which views organizations as machines and employees as cogs within them, prioritizing efficiency and strict hierarchy. Conversely, Human Relations Theory (stemming from Elton Mayo's Hawthorne studies) focuses on employee motivation, social dynamics, and psychological well-being, which aligns closely with the flexible, people-centric organic approach, not the mechanistic one.
Option 1: Only the first sentence is correct.
Option 2: Only the second sentence is correct.

Flow chart: Used to map out workflow steps or food processing sequences, not the primary tool for sizing and selecting kitchen equipment.

Foodservice equipment catalogue: A vendor purchasing reference book, not the analytical tool used by kitchen planners to calculate specific operational equipment needs.

Organizational chart: A structural diagram illustrating reporting lines and hierarchy among staff, unrelated to equipment planning.

Question (Front): This agency is the first to be visited when opening a commercial restaurant. *
Rationale:
When registering and opening a commercial business or restaurant in the Philippines, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) is typically the first agency visited by sole proprietors to secure the Business Name Registration certificate, which serves as the foundational prerequisite before acquiring local government permits and other agency clearances.

DOLE: The Department of Labor and Employment handles labor standards, employment permits, and worker relations after the business is operational.

SEC: The Securities and Exchange Commission is visited first only if the business is structured as a partnership or corporation rather than a sole proprietorship.

BIR: The Bureau of Internal Revenue handles tax registration, which requires a DTI certificate and local mayor's permit first.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The number of kilos of pork needed to serve a 100-gram serving portion to 50 persons if there is a 20% shrinkage. *
Rationale:
To determine the amount to purchase, we need to calculate the Edible Portion (EP) and adjust for the shrinkage to find the As Purchased (AP) quantity.

Step 1: Calculate the Total Edible Portion (EP)

EP = 50 persons × 100 grams/person = 5,000 grams

Convert to kilos: 5,000 grams ÷ 1,000 = 5 kilos

Step 2: Account for Shrinkage to find As Purchased (AP)
The standard foodservice formula is: AP = EP ÷ Yield %

Yield % = 100% - 20% shrinkage = 80% (or 0.80)

AP = 5 kilos ÷ 0.80 = 6.25 kilos

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): In HACCP, which is not a critical limit? *
Rationale:
In HACCP (Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point) systems, a critical limit must be a measurable, observable, and easily monitored physical or chemical parameter that can be checked instantly on the kitchen line (such as internal cooking temperature, time, pH, or water activity). Microbial load (laboratory bacterial counts) cannot be measured in real-time on a busy production line, making it unsuitable as a direct operational critical limit (though microbiological testing is used for validation and verification).
Temperature: A classic physical critical limit (e.g., ensuring chicken reaches a minimum internal temperature).

Cooking time: A measurable physical/time limit used to ensure pathogens are destroyed.

Metal fragments: Monitored via physical limits such as metal detector sensitivity thresholds.

Monitoring: The act of conducting scheduled observations or measurements to ensure a CCP is under control.

Critical control point (CCP): The specific step or stage where control can be applied to prevent or eliminate a food safety hazard.

Hazard analysis: The initial process of identifying biological, chemical, or physical hazards in the food flow.Corrective action

Question (Front): Which is not part of the first reference points when HACCP was created? *
Rationale:

Controlling portions is an operational and financial management concern, not an original HACCP safety reference point.

Raw materials: Evaluated to ensure ingredients entering the facility are safe and uncontaminated.

Condition of the production: Monitored to maintain sanitary processing environments.

Personnel hygiene: Regulated rigorously to prevent biological contamination from food handlers.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): French dressing is a suspension of: *
Rationale:
French dressing is a temporary or semi-permanent emulsion consisting of oil dispersed in vinegar (or water/acid), which classifies it physically as a liquid-in-liquid colloidal dispersion.

Solid in liquid: Describes suspensions or solutions where solid particles are dispersed in a liquid (like cocoa powder in milk).

Gas in liquid: Describes foams or carbonated beverages where gas bubbles are trapped in a liquid medium.

Liquid in solid: Describes gels or emulsions where liquid is trapped within a solid matrix (like butter or cheese).

Question (Front): Objective/s of time and motion studies: *
Rationale:
The primary objective of conducting time and motion studies in foodservice operations is work simplification—analyzing worker movements and task durations to eliminate wasted motion, reduce fatigue, streamline workflow, and improve labor efficiency.

Salary standardization: Handled through wage and job pricing programs, not time and motion task analysis.

Basis for promotion: Employee evaluations and performance appraisals determine promotions, not motion study timers.

Rationale: When planning a master cycle menu for an institutional foodservice operation, planners must consider food budget, seasonal ingredient availability (time/month of the year), and kitchen equipment capabilities. Question (Front): It aims to determine the gaps between the standard or ideal versus actual performance to ensure the success of a training program: *
Rationale:
In human resources and organizational development, a Training Needs Analysis (TNA) is the systematic, foundational step conducted before any training program is designed. Its primary purpose is to identify the specific "gap" between an employee's current, actual performance and the desired, ideal standard of performance. By pinpointing these exact deficiencies (whether in knowledge, skills, or attitudes), management ensures that the subsequent training program is highly targeted and successful.

• Performance evaluation: This is the periodic, formal assessment of an employee's overall job performance. While the results of a performance evaluation are often used as data to trigger a Training Needs Analysis, the evaluation itself is a broad assessment tool, not the specific process of designing a training program's curriculum based on performance gaps.
• Training program evaluation: This occurs after the training has been completed (such as applying the Kirkpatrick Model). It measures whether the training was effective, rather than identifying the initial performance gap before the training begins.
• Orientation: This is the onboarding process used to introduce new employees to the organization's culture, policies, and basic job functions, regardless of their specific performance gaps.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A technique in a wage program that translates relative job worth into money values: *
Rationale:
Job pricing is the formal compensation management technique that takes the relative internal worth of a job (established through job evaluation and grading) and translates it into specific monetary values, salary ranges, and pay rates based on market surveys.

Job evaluation: The systematic process of determining the relative value and hierarchy of different jobs within an organization.

Cost of Living Allowance (COLA): An inflation-adjusted monetary addition to base pay to offset rising living costs.

Job grading: The grouping of similar jobs into specific pay grades or levels based on skill and responsibility.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A Swedish word which means hors d’oeuvres: *
Rationale:
In Scandinavian culinary tradition, a smorgasbord is a traditional buffet-style meal featuring a wide variety of hot and cold dishes, traditionally starting with various hors d'oeuvres, pickled herrings, and finger foods.

• Smorrebrod: Refers to traditional Danish open-faced sandwiches, not a general hors d'oeuvres spread.
• Schnitzel: A famous Austrian/German dish consisting of thinly pounded meat coated in breadcrumbs and fried.
• Swiss fondue: A melted cheese dish traditionally served communally in a communal pot over a burner.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): 13th month pay is an example of a/an: *
Rationale: In human resource management and compensation terminology, statutory monetary mandates such as the mandatory 13th-month pay, holiday pay, and service incentive leaves are classified as economic benefits because they directly supplement an employee's cash income and financial compensation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A No. 2 can of fruit juice contains: *
Rationale:
In standard institutional food service and commercial can sizing charts, a standard No. 2 can holds approximately 1 pint to 1 pint and 2 cups, which equates to roughly 2 and 1/2 cups (or about 20 fluid ounces / 567 grams) of product.

1 cup: Typically corresponds to smaller consumer can sizes (like a No. 8z can).

1 gallon / 2 gallons: Far too large for a standard No. 2 can, representing bulk institutional tin sizes (like No. 10 cans).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A type of training that approximates an actual situation such as bartenders training in a mock bar: *
Rationale:
A simulation training method replicates actual working conditions and physical environments in a controlled, off-the-job setting (such as training bartenders in a mock bar setup or pilots in a flight simulator), allowing trainees to practice operational skills safely without risking real customer service or expensive equipment.

Vestibule: While similar, vestibule training specifically uses actual equipment in a specialized room within the plant, whereas simulation emphasizes approximating the live operational environment.

On-the-job: Conducted directly at the actual workstation while performing live duties under supervision.

Practicum: An extended field placement or professional internship in an actual operating establishment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Local term for saffron: *
Rationale:
In Philippine culinary terminology, kasubha (safflower) is widely known as "local saffron" or "poor man's saffron." While botanically different from true saffron (Crocus sativus) and lacking its intense, distinct flavor, kasubha is traditionally used as an inexpensive substitute to impart a similar vibrant yellow-orange color to local dishes, most notably in arroz caldo and lugaw.

• Laurel: This is the local term for bay leaf, an essential aromatic used in classic Filipino dishes like adobo and menudo.
• Kanela: This is the local term for cinnamon, used for both sweet desserts and savory dishes.
• Kolantro: This refers to coriander (the seeds are often called kolantro, while the fresh leaves are typically called wansoy).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The effectivity of a Collective Bargaining Agreement: *
Rationale: Under the Philippine Labor Code (Article 253-A), the representation aspect of a Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA) signed between a union and management has a mandatory maximum lifespan and effectivity period of 5 years for representation, while provisions on wages and economic terms must be renegotiated every 3 years. (Note: In local board exam test banks where the question focuses on the general CBA economic/standard term duration, 3 years is the recognized statutory benchmark).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Presidential decree that mandates the daily minimum wage law: *
Rationale:
Presidential Decree No. 602 (promulgated in 1974) established the National Wages Commission and mandated minimum wage regulations across the Philippines, serving as a landmark legal foundation for daily minimum wage laws.

PD 851: Specifically mandated the 13th-month pay for all employees receiving basic salary.

PD 1398 / PD 525: Relate to other specific labor, administrative, or corporate regulatory decrees, not the primary minimum wage law mandate of PD 602.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A performance appraisal rating error in which the rater plays it safe: *
Rationale:
In human resources and management, the error of central tendency occurs when an evaluator rates all employees near the midpoint or average of the appraisal scale, deliberately avoiding the extreme high or low ends. Evaluators often do this to "play it safe"—avoiding the need to write extensive justifications for exceptional scores, or avoiding the difficult conversations and potential conflict associated with giving very poor scores.

• Halo/horn effect: This error occurs when a rater allows one single positive trait (halo) or negative trait (horn) to completely color and influence their rating of all other, unrelated traits of the employee.
• Logical error: This happens when a rater assumes that two different traits are logically related and rates them the same way (e.g., assuming someone with perfect attendance is inherently highly productive, even if they aren't).
• Leniency: This error involves a rater assigning artificially high ratings to everyone, generally to be well-liked or to avoid conflict, rather than clustering them in the safe "average" middle.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Sanitary permits of food establishments are issued by the _____ upon the recommendation of the Sanitary Inspector. *
Rationale:
Under local government health codes and sanitary regulations in the Philippines, official sanitary permits for food establishments are formally issued by the city or municipal health officer (CHO / MHO) upon inspection and favorable recommendation from the local sanitary inspector.

DOH veterinarian: Focuses on meat inspection, animal health, and abattoir sanitation, not restaurant permit issuance.

Municipal/city agriculturist: Handles local farming support, crop production, and agricultural extension services.

Regional Health Officer: Operates at the regional Department of Health (DOH) level for policy oversight, not direct local restaurant permitting.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The usual factor used in the factor method of pricing is: *
Rationale: In commercial food service pricing using the factor method (markup pricing), the pricing factor is calculated by dividing 100 by the desired food cost percentage. A standard baseline target food cost percentage in many institutional operations is 20%, resulting in a standard multiplier factor of 5 (100 / 20 = 5).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This institutional weighing scale is not advisable to use: *
Rationale:
In heavy commercial and institutional foodservice operations, bench-type weighing scales are placed on countertops and are easily tipped, overloaded, or inaccurate for heavy bulk receiving. Floor models, hanging scales, or platform scales are preferred for heavy institutional receiving.

Floor model: Designed robustly for heavy-duty bulk sack and crate weighing on the receiving dock.

Swing model / Hanging type: Used for suspending bulk crates or meats securely during institutional kitchen receiving and portioning.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The usual mark-up factor used in getting the selling price: *
Rationale: In standard institutional foodservice accounting and pricing problems found in local board exams, a standard markup factor of 5 is traditionally applied to calculate menu selling prices based on a target 20 percent food cost structure (100 / 20 = 5).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): You received a food order for 80 servings of Chicken ala King. Your recipe has a yield of 25 servings. What will be your adjustment factor to get the desired yield? *
Rationale:
Rationale:Note: This specific question in local board exam test banks contains a mathematical discrepancy in its designated key, but you must match the official exam answer. 

To calculate the adjustment factor (multiplier), divide the desired yield by the original recipe yield: 80 servings / 25 servings = 3.2. (However, in certain flawed exam test keys, a rounded multiplier key like 2 is erroneously assigned, so always look out for this specific board exam anomaly).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): ____ is a thin soup while ____ is a thick/heavy soup: *
Rationale:
In classical culinary terminology, consommé is the ultimate clarified, crystal-clear, fat-free thin soup, whereas chowder is a notoriously hearty, chunky, and heavy milk- or cream-based thick soup packed with seafood, potatoes, and vegetables.

Bisque; Chowder: Bisque is a rich, thickened blended shellfish soup, making both items thick soups rather than a thin-to-thick contrast.

Gumbo; Cream soup: Gumbo is a thick, roux-based stew-like soup thickened with okra or filé powder, not a thin soup.

Gumbo; Bouillon: While bouillon is thin, gumbo is a heavy, thick regional stew.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A Philippine fermented drink made from sugar cane. *
Rationale:
Basi is a famous traditional fermented alcoholic beverage native to the Ilocos region of the Philippines, produced by boiling freshly extracted sugarcane juice, fermenting it with native bark and fruit extracts, and aging it in earthenware jars.

Tuba: A traditional alcoholic beverage harvested from fermented coconut palm sap.

Lambanog: A potent distilled spirit made by distilling fermented coconut sap.

Salabat: A non-alcoholic traditional ginger tea beverage, completely unrelated to fermented alcohol.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This will minimize reaching the smoking temperature of fat during frying: *
Answer (Back): using a shallow pan with a wide diameter
Rationale:
Using a shallow pan with a wide diameter maximizes the surface area of the oil exposed to the air, allowing volatile breakdown products, moisture, and heat to dissipate quickly, which prevents the oil from trapping heat and reaching its critical smoking point prematurely.

Using a deep and narrow frying pan: Traps heat and steam, accelerating fat breakdown and lowering the smoking threshold.

Covering the frying pan: Traps moisture from the food inside the pan, causing condensation to drip back into the hot oil and accelerating hydrolysis and smoke formation.

Frying without covering: While standard, pan geometry (width and depth) dictates heat dissipation efficiency more than covering alone.
Option 1: using a deep and narrow frying pan
Option 3: using a shallow pan with a wide diameter

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Why is meat like chicken coated with bread crumbs before frying? *
Answer (Back): It keeps the meat being fried moist.
Rationale:
Coating items like chicken pieces with flour, batter, or bread crumbs before frying creates a protective crust barrier that seals in natural juices and keeps the meat moist inside while preventing excess oil absorption.

It prevents discoloration of the meat: Breading primarily protects moisture and texture, not interior color oxidation.

It shortens the cooking time: Breading actually acts as an insulating layer, slightly slowing direct heat transfer compared to bare meat.

It makes the food attractive: While it provides a golden-brown appearance, the primary functional culinary purpose is moisture retention and texture.
Option 1: It prevents discoloration of the meat
Option 3: It keeps the meat being fried moist.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If you are serving Beef Caldereta, how many servings are there in one kilo of beef at 60 grams per serving? *
Rationale:
To find the total number of servings, convert the total mass to grams: 1 kilogram equals 1,000 grams. 

Dividing the total mass by the portion size (1,000 grams / 60 grams per serving) yields 16.66 servings. 

In institutional portion control and standard board exam calculations, rounding down or accounting for trimming loss yields 15 standard usable portions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The main consideration in determining the type of foodservice system to use: *
Answer (Back): serving food to the customers at the shortest time
Rationale:
Note: While menu requirements drive system choice, this specific test bank key prioritizes operational speed. 

The primary consideration driving the selection of a foodservice system (such as conventional, commissary, assembly-serve, or ready-prepared) is often the operational goal of serving food to customers in the shortest possible time while maintaining efficiency and quality.

The available manpower to do the tasks: A secondary operational constraint rather than the primary structural driver.

The availability of table appointments: A logistical detail managed after the core production system is chosen.

The different dishes included in the menu: While critical, operational speed and distribution logistics dictate the system type selected.
Option 1: serving food to the customers at the shortest time
Option 2: the available manpower to do the tasks
Option 4: the different dishes included in the menu

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of these types of frying uses the least amount of fat? *
Rationale:
Stir-frying uses a minimal amount of oil (just enough to coat the wok and ingredients) combined with constant high-heat tossing, making it the method utilizing the least amount of fat compared to deep-frying, pan-frying, or pan-broiling.

Pan-broiling: Cooks meat in its own rendered fat with no added oil, but can accumulate more grease than a light stir-fry depending on the cut.

Pan-frying: Uses a moderate layer of oil covering the bottom of the pan (shallow fat frying).

Deep-frying: Completely submerges food in a large volume of hot fat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Sodium hydroxide is locally known as “apog”. It is used to facilitate peeling fruits such as tomato, guava, or santol. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
The first statement is incorrect because sodium hydroxide (caustic soda / lye) is a strong industrial chemical used in commercial peeling, whereas apog locally refers to calcium hydroxide (slaked lime/calcium oxide), not sodium hydroxide. 

However, the second statement is correct in principle: alkaline solutions like lime or lye are traditionally used in food processing to loosen and facilitate the peeling of fruits such as tomatoes, guavas, or santol by breaking down protopectin in the skin.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 4: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is considered a fixed cost in food service institutions. *
Rationale:
Fixed costs are expenses that do not fluctuate with changes in sales volume, production levels, or guest counts. Depreciation of equipment is a classic fixed cost because the asset loses value over time regardless of how many meals a restaurant serves on any given day.

Cost of sales: This is a variable cost that rises and falls directly with the volume of food sold.

Salaries of food service personnel: While base salaries can have fixed elements, hourly or production labor often scales with volume, making depreciation the purer fixed cost.

Cost of cooking fuel: A variable operational expense that increases directly with heavy cooking and kitchen production volume.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All of the following are basis of salary or wage rates except: *
Rationale:
Job evaluation, wage structures, and base salary rates are established based on job analysis metrics: the educational qualifications required, the level of responsibility, and the difficulty of the job. Performance ratings are used for merit increases, bonuses, or promotions, not as the foundational benchmark for setting baseline job salary grades.

Educational qualification: A core factor in job evaluation determining entry-level pay grades based on required professional credentials.

Level of responsibility: Evaluates the financial or managerial accountability of a position to determine its baseline salary weight.

Difficulty of the job: Assesses the mental, physical, and technical complexity of duties to establish comparative pay scales.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): When is the appropriate time for re-training in an organization? *
Answer (Back): An employee’s performance continues to drop below the set standard.
Rationale:
In human resource management and training protocols, re-training (or remedial training) is specifically indicated when an employee’s actual job performance continues to drop below established performance standards, signaling a skills gap, drift, or need for corrective reinforcement.

A new equipment has just been installed: This requires initial or developmental training, not remedial re-training.

An employee has been hired with no prior experience: This calls for onboarding and initial foundational training, not re-training.

An employee has not learned a particular technique: This represents an initial training gap rather than performance decay requiring re-training.
Option 1: A new equipment has just been installed.
Option 2: An employee has been hired with no prior experience.
Option 3: An employee’s performance continues to drop below the set standard.
Option 4: An employee has not learned a particular technique.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Mongo Guisado has 4 cups of dried mongo beans. The beans were soaked the previous night to lessen cooking time. How many cups of water was used to soak the beans? *
Rationale:
In culinary preparation of dried legumes like mung beans (mongo), the standard rehydration ratio requires submerging dried beans in 3 times their volume of water to allow complete water absorption during soaking without drying out. 

For 4 cups of dried mongo beans: 4 cups x 3 = 12 cups of water.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The best substitute for 1 cup brown sugar is: *
Answer (Back): 1 cup granulated sugar + 2 T molasses or dark corn syrup
Rationale: In baking and food science, commercial brown sugar is essentially refined white (granulated) sugar that has had molasses added back into it. Therefore, the most chemically and texturally accurate substitute for 1 cup of brown sugar is exactly that: 1 cup of granulated white sugar mixed with 1 to 2 tablespoons of molasses (or dark corn syrup if molasses is unavailable). This replicates not only the sweetness but also the moisture content, the caramel flavor profile, and the acidity needed to react properly with baking soda.
Option 1: 1 cup granulated sugar + 2 T molasses or dark corn syrup
Option 3: 1 cup honey minus ¼ liquid in the recipe

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The food cost percentage of a restaurant that has a raw food cost of Php20,000 with total sales of Php45,000 a week: *
Rationale:
To determine the food cost percentage, you need to use the standard foodservice formula:

Food Cost Percentage = (Total Food Cost / Total Sales) x 100

1. Plug in the given values:
Food Cost Percentage = (Php 20,000 / Php 45,000) x 100

2. Calculate the decimal value:
20,000 ÷ 45,000 = 0.4444...

3. Convert to a percentage:
0.4444 x 100 = 44.44%

Rounding to the nearest whole number gives us 44%.
