Mrs. Cruz is giving a party for her daughter. She expects 200 guests, 20% of whom will be adults and the rest will be children.
She plans to serve ice cream as dessert with a serving portion of ½ cup for adults and ¼ cup for children. How many gallons of ice cream does she need to purchase? *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards1 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front):
Mrs. Cruz is giving a party for her daughter. She expects 200 guests, 20% of whom will be adults and the rest will be children.
If she buys 5 gallons of ice cream, what scoop number should she use to serve the guests equally? *
Rationale: In institutional food service, standard disher (scoop) numbers indicate how many scoopfuls fit into one quart (32 fluid ounces). A #10 scoop holds roughly 3.2 fluid ounces (approx. 0.4 cups or standard portion equivalent), making it the designated commercial portioning tool utilized in this problem's test key to distribute bulk ice cream evenly across party guests.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Low-acid foods except: *
Rationale:
Pickles are high-acid foods due to pickling vinegar (acetic acid) preservation, which inhibits bacterial spoilage and botulism spores, making them the correct exception.

• Meat / Corn / Shrimp: Low-acid foods (pH > 4.6) that require pressure canning or strict refrigeration to prevent Clostridium botulinum growth.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All are tender cuts of beef except: *
Rationale:
The brisket is a heavily exercised cut derived from the breast section containing abundant connective tissue (collagen), making it a tough cut requiring slow, moist-heat cooking.

• T-bone / Sirloin / Porterhouse: Tender cuts from the loin and rib sections best suited for dry-heat cooking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): These microorganisms can grow in jams and jellies: *
Rationale:
Osmophilic microorganisms (such as specific spoilage yeasts and molds) are specialized microbes capable of growing in high-osmotic-pressure environments with high sugar concentrations, such as jams, jellies, and honey.

• Halophile: Thrives in high salt concentrations.
• Acidophile: Thrives in low pH acidic environments.
• Alkaliphile: Thrives in high alkaline pH.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Objective tests to determine the color of food except: *
Rationale:
Standard photography captures visual light images but does not provide precise numerical or spectral data, making it an uncalibrated subjective method rather than an objective colorimetry tool.

• Spectrophotometer / Colorimetry / Turbidimetry test: Precise instrumental objective methods for quantifying light absorption, transmission, and color coordinates.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following ingredients contributes to the crustiness in a sponge cake? *
Rationale: Sugar contributes to crust browning (via caramelization and Maillard reactions) and aids crustiness in sponge cakes and baked goods by raising coagulation temperatures and binding moisture.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not a functional food? *
Rationale:
While mangoes contain rich vitamins and phytochemicals, whole fresh fruits are traditional whole foods, whereas functional foods are specifically defined as foods or dietary components marketed or processed to provide health benefits beyond basic nutrition (often fortified or enriched).

• Broccoli / Malunggay / Garlic: Widely classified as functional foods due to specific bioactive compounds (glucosinolates, antioxidants, allicin).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The main protein in egg yolk is: *
Rationale:
Vitellin is the primary lipoprotein-bound protein complex found in egg yolk.

• Livetin: A secondary soluble protein fraction in egg yolk.
• Albumin: The major protein found in egg whites.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If you are using baking soda instead of baking powder, you should: *
Answer (Back): use the same amount and add milk
Rationale: Baking soda is pure sodium bicarbonate and requires an acid ingredient to activate; however, if substituting it in recipes without modifying the acid balance, keeping the amount proportional while ensuring adequate acidic liquid (like buttermilk or milk) prevents chemical off-flavors.
Option 1: reduce the amount of baking soda and add milk
Option 2: increase the amount of baking soda and add acid
Option 3: use the same amount and add milk

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This food item has a shelf life of more than a year: *
Rationale:
Commercially hermetically sealed canned goods undergo thermal sterilization, giving them a long shelf life extending well beyond one year under ambient storage conditions.

• Rice in a sack / Cornstarch / Flavoring extracts: Susceptible to insect infestation, moisture absorption, or flavor degradation over long periods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Flour with the highest protein content. *
Rationale:
Commercially hermetically sealed canned goods undergo thermal sterilization, giving them a long shelf life extending well beyond one year under ambient storage conditions.

• Rice in a sack / Cornstarch / Flavoring extracts: Susceptible to insect infestation, moisture absorption, or flavor degradation over long periods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The chief structural carbohydrate of plants responsible for the crisp texture of salad greens. *
Rationale: Cellulose is an unbranched glucose polymer and the chief structural component of plant cell walls, providing crispness and rigidity to fresh vegetables like salad greens.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Examples of moist heat method of cooking except: *
Rationale:
Fried galunggong uses hot oil (fat) to apply dry heat via conduction, classifying it as a dry-heat frying method rather than moist-heat.

• Steamed / Pesang dalag / Paksiw: Classic moist-heat cooking methods utilizing steam or boiling broths.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This resembles cake flour in composition and in baking properties: *
Rationale: Pastry flour has a protein content (~9–10%) and baking properties that closely resemble soft-wheat cake flour, offering tender crumb structures for pastries and pies.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All are products of lactic acid fermentation except: *
Rationale: Vinegar is produced via acetic acid bacterial fermentation of ethanol, whereas cheese, atchara (fermented papaya), and cultured butter are products of lactic acid bacterial fermentation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is made from pork fat: *
Rationale:
Lard is rendered fat sourced specifically from pork adipose tissue.

• Tallow: Rendered beef or sheep fat.
• Suet: Raw hard beef fat surrounding kidneys.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A crude market form of sugar where sugarcane extract is evaporated into a brown syrup concentrate and molded in a halved coconut shell. *
Rationale: Panutsa (or penoche) is a traditional crude Philippine brown sugar formed by evaporating sugarcane juice syrup into a thick concentrate and molding it inside halved coconut shells.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A physical change undergone by starch gels during storage which leads to an increase in crystalline aggregates and results in a gritty texture. An example is the thin film that forms on top of puddings. *
Rationale: Retrogradation is the physical recrystallization of gelatinized starch molecules upon cooling or storage, causing staling in bread and the formation of a gritty skin or film on top of cooling puddings.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A dark purple-colored rice used in “puto bumbong.” *
Rationale:
Pirurutong is an heirloom Philippine deep purple-colored glutinous rice variety traditionally utilized to make native kakanin like puto bumbong.

• Pinipig: Immature flattened rice grains.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is not included in the group: *
Rationale: Gin is a clear distilled spirit produced from grain mashes and flavored with juniper berries, whereas tuba, lambanog, and basi are traditional indigenous fermented alcoholic beverages derived from coconut sap or sugarcane.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A cereal that is invaluable in yeast bread-making as it is a significant source of gluten. *
Rationale: Wheat is the primary cereal grain containing high proportions of the storage proteins gliadin and glutenin, making it uniquely invaluable in yeast bread-making for gluten network formation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The chief food reserve of plants which is converted to sugar as fruits ripen. *
Rationale: Starch serves as the chief polysaccharide food reserve synthesized by plants, which is enzymatically hydrolyzed into simple sugars as fruits ripen and soften.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Source of sucrose: *
Rationale:
Candies are concentrated commercial sweets formulated primarily from refined sucrose (table sugar).

• Fruit: Contains natural fructose and glucose.
• Honey: Contains invert sugars (glucose and fructose).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Local dessert/snack items made with non-glutinous rice except: *
Rationale: Maja blanca is a traditional Filipino gelatinous dessert made from coconut milk, cornstarch, and sugar, utilizing cornstarch (a non-glutinous cereal starch derivative), whereas champorado, sapin-sapin, and lugaw utilize glutinous rice or regular rice.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Part of the cereal grain which contains oil, protein, and vitamins making it prone to oxidative rancidity.
Rationale: The germ is the nutrient-dense reproductive embryo of the cereal grain, rich in lipids, protein, and vitamins, which makes it highly susceptible to lipid oxidation and oxidative rancidity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): To make a thinner porridge or oatmeal: *
Rationale: To adjust consistency and make porridge or oatmeal thinner, increasing the proportion of cooking liquid (adding more water) is the standard culinary adjustment.
Option 1: increase the stirring using a fork
Option 3: add the cereal gradually to the boiling water

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): When rice is toasted or browned for kare-kare, the starch undergoes: *
Rationale: When dry rice or starch is toasted, browned, or heated without moisture (as in preparing base flour for kare-kare sauce), the starch molecules break down into shorter-chain sweet dextrins, a process called dextrinization.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The function of starch when used in chocolate drinks and cooked dressings is as a ____ agent. *
Rationale: Starch acts as a suspending and thickening agent in formulated beverages like cooked chocolate drinks and cooked dressings by binding free water and increasing viscosity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Gluten formation is brought about by the interaction of ___ with ___ during dough mixing. *
Rationale:
Gluten formation occurs when the two wheat flour storage proteins—glutenin (which provides elasticity) and gliadin (which provides extensibility and stickiness)—are hydrated with water and mechanically kneaded together.

• Globulin / Albumin: Other minor wheat proteins, but they do not form the cohesive gluten matrix.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Microorganisms used for cheese ripening: *
Rationale: Molds (such as Penicillium roqueforti or Penicillium camemberti) are specialized fungi utilized during ripening processes to impart characteristic textures, flavors, and appearance in aged cheeses (e.g., Blue cheese, Brie).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): At the freezing point and below it, microorganisms become dormant because:
Rationale: At and below freezing temperatures, microorganisms enter dormancy because available free water is locked up as ice (a) and intracellular/extracellular enzymatic metabolic rates are drastically retarded (b).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Local term for Chinese cabbage: *
Rationale:
Pechay is the local Tagalog term for Chinese cabbage (Brassica rapa subsp. pekinensis or chinensis).

• Repolyo: Cabbage.
• Remolatsa: Beetroot.
• Kinchay: Chinese celery.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is a rod-shaped bacterium that causes food spoilage: *
Rationale:
Bacilli are rod-shaped bacteria, many species of which are common agents of food spoilage and foodborne illness.

• Cocci: Spherical bacteria.
• Spirilla / Vibrios: Spiral or comma-shaped bacteria.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The location of taste buds that detects sourness: *
Rationale:
Human gustatory mapping identifies that taste buds responsive primarily to sourness (driven by hydrogen ions from acids) are located along the lateral sides of the tongue.

• Tip of the tongue: Sensitive primarily to sweetness and saltiness.
• Back of the tongue: Sensitive primarily to bitterness.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The basis for grading rice is: *
Rationale: Commercial and government grading standards for milled rice are based primarily on physical kernel characteristics, including head rice recovery, broken kernel percentages, and physical size/length of the kernel.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Spoilage of a refrigerated salad is likely caused by microorganisms that are: *
Rationale:
Psychrotrophs are cold-tolerant microorganisms that can grow and multiply at refrigerator temperatures (0°C to 7°C), making them the primary cause of spoilage in refrigerated perishable foods like salads, dairy, and cold cuts.

• Psychrophiles: True cold-loving microbes thriving at lower polar temperatures.
• Mesophiles: Thrive at moderate, ambient room temperatures.
• Thermophiles: Thrive at high heat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Staphylococci contamination of food often occurs through: *
Rationale: Staphylococcus aureus is a common bacterium harbored in human nasal passages, skin, and infected skin lesions or open wounds, frequently contaminating foods during manual preparation by handlers.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What phase in the microbial growth curve is characterized by very rapid cell growth and highestsensitivity to antimicrobial agents? *
Rationale:
During the logarithmic (log) phase of microbial growth, cells divide exponentially at their maximum rate, making them exceptionally metabolically active and highly sensitive to heat, sanitizers, and antimicrobial agents.

• Lag phase: Adaptation period with minimal cell division.
• Stationary phase: Growth rate equals death rate.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Mad cow disease, characterized by degeneration in the central nervous system, is caused by: *
Rationale: Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as "mad cow" disease, is a transmissible spongiform encephalopathy caused not by living organisms or viruses, but by misfolded infectious proteins called prions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Commercial sterility implies that __________. *
Answer (Back): all pathogenic microorganisms in the food were destroyed
Rationale: In food science, commercial sterility refers to the condition achieved in thermally processed (canned) foods where all pathogenic, toxin-forming, and spoilage microorganisms capable of growing under normal non-refrigerated storage conditions have been destroyed.
Option 1: no microorganisms are present in the food
Option 2: all pathogenic microorganisms in the food were destroyed
Option 3: spoilage microorganisms present in the food were removed
Option 4: microorganisms present in the food will not be able to grow under normal storage conditions

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The first stage of ice crystal formation during freezing: *
Rationale: Nucleation is the critical initial thermodynamic stage in freezing where tiny clusters of water molecules begin to form stable micro-crystal nuclei before crystal growth and ripening occur.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What is the effect of heat or cooking on flour mixtures? *
Answer (Back): It coagulates egg and flour proteins.
Rationale: Applying thermal heat to flour mixtures denatures and coagulates egg and flour proteins (such as gluten and albumins), setting the structural matrix and crumb of baked goods.
Option 2: It coagulates egg and flour proteins.
Option 3: It ensures an even distribution of moisture.
Option 4: It provides an even distribution of fat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): These food items should be kept at room temperature except for: *
Rationale:
Bread stales rapidly and develops mold when stored in warm, humid refrigerators due to retrogradation of starch; it should be kept at room temperature for short-term consumption or frozen for long-term storage.

• Onion / Garlic / Banana: Kept at cool ambient room temperatures.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The best environment for storing herbs and spices is: *
Rationale: Herbs and spices contain volatile aromatic essential oils that degrade rapidly when exposed to heat, light, and moisture; they should be stored in a cool, dry place in airtight containers.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Dehydration method most suitable for the production of instant coffee powder: *
Rationale: Spray drying atomizes liquid coffee extract into a hot drying chamber, instantly evaporating moisture and producing fine, soluble instant coffee powder.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The rancidity which results from the exposure of fat to oxygen is called: *
Rationale:
Oxidative rancidity occurs when unsaturated fatty acids react with atmospheric oxygen via free radical mechanisms, producing off-flavors, peroxides, and aldehydes.

• Hydrolytic rancidity: Caused by enzymatic cleavage (lipases) releasing free fatty acids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not true about pH? *
Option 3: It controls many biological and chemical reactions.
Option 4: It affects color brightness and stability of pigments of fruits and vegetables.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The best temperature for beating egg whites into a stable foam is: *
Rationale: Whipping egg whites into a stable, high-volume foam is best achieved at room temperature because lower surface tension allows proteins to denature and trap air more rapidly than cold refrigerator temperatures.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Cross-contamination occurs when: *
Answer (Back): microorganisms transfer from one food or surface to another.
Rationale: Cross-contamination is defined as the physical transfer of harmful microorganisms or allergens from one food item, utensil, or surface to another (typically from raw foods to ready-to-eat foods).
Option 1: delivered food is not stored immediately.
Option 2: growth of microorganisms is not arrested quickly.
Option 3: microorganisms transfer from one food or surface to another.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Proper handwashing involves rubbing hands together: *
Rationale: According to handwashing guidelines established by public health agencies (WHO/CDC), proper handwashing requires vigorously rubbing soapy hands together for at least 20 seconds.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Store raw food: *
Rationale: To prevent cross-contamination from raw meat juices dripping downward, raw foods must always be stored on refrigerator shelves below cooked and ready-to-eat foods.
Option 2: on the same shelf as cooked and ready-to-eat food

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What is the % overrun of an ice cream with an initial ice cream mixture of 160ml and has a final yield of 280 ml? *
Rationale:
To calculate ice cream overrun percentage:

Formula = [(Final Volume − Initial Mix Volume) ÷ Initial Mix Volume] × 100. 
Given values: Initial mix = 160 ml; Final yield = 280 ml. 
Calculation = [(280 − 160) ÷ 160] × 100 = (120 ÷ 160) × 100 = 75%.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A person diagnosed with this pathogen should be excluded from working in a foodservice establishment: *
Rationale: Salmonella typhi is the systemic pathogen responsible for typhoid fever; food handlers diagnosed with typhoid fever must be strictly excluded from working in foodservice establishments to prevent transmission.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A way of preventing lumps in starch cooking is to initially disperse starch in melted fat forming a _____. *
Rationale: A roux is prepared by cooking equal parts flour and fat together to coat starch granules in lipid, which separates them and prevents lump formation when hot liquids are added.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A safe and acceptable way to thaw a pack of frozen marinated chicken is: *
Rationale: Gradual thawing under refrigeration (4°C or below) is the safest, most approved foodservice method because it keeps perishable foods out of the "temperature danger zone" while thawing safely.
Option 4: gradual thawing under hot running water

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following cuts of beef is best for cooking Sinigang? *
Rationale: The brisket is a tougher, heavily exercised cut of beef containing abundant collagen connective tissue that breaks down during slow, moist-heat simmering, making it suitable for savory soups like sinigang.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What can precipitate the casein protein in milk? *
Rationale: Rennet (containing the enzyme chymosin) specifically hydrolyzes and cleaves kappa-casein in milk, causing the destabilization and precipitation of casein protein to form solid curds during cheesemaking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The process involved in removing unsaturations in fatty acids to make the fat stable. *
Rationale: Hydrogenation is the chemical process of reacting liquid unsaturated fatty acids with hydrogen gas under high pressure and temperature in the presence of a catalyst to saturate double bonds, stabilizing the fat into a solid or semi-solid state.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): When Mg++ is replaced by H+ in the chlorophyll structure, this compound is produced: *
Rationale: When green plant tissue is heated or exposed to acid, the magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) in the center of the chlorophyll molecule is displaced by hydrogen ions (H⁺), converting bright green chlorophyll into olive-brown pheophytin.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The enzyme that mediates browning reactions in fruits and vegetables. *
Rationale: Phenolase (polyphenol oxidase) is the copper-containing enzyme responsible for catalyzing the oxidation of phenolic compounds into dark melanin pigments during enzymatic browning in cut fruits and vegetables.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The form of pectic substance predominantly present in under ripened fruits. *
Rationale: Protopectin is the water-insoluble, highly methylated pectic substance predominantly present in firm, hard, under-ripened fruits, which progressively hydrolyzes into water-soluble pectin as fruits ripen.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The compound responsible for the characteristic green coloration of uncooked crustaceans. *
Rationale: Ovoverdine is the carotenoid-protein complex composed of astaxanthin bound to a protein, responsible for the characteristic dark green or blue-green coloration of raw, unheated crustaceans (such as lobsters and crabs).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The local term for taro: *
Rationale: Gabi is the local Filipino term for taro (Colocasia esculenta), a starchy tuber grown for its edible corms and leaves.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A storage form of phosphorus found in cereals and root crops which binds with minerals like Ca, Fe,and Zn making these minerals unavailable for utilization. *
Rationale: Phytate (phytic acid) is the primary storage form of phosphorus found in the bran of cereal grains and root crops; it acts as an antinutrient by binding strongly with divalent minerals like calcium, iron, and zinc, reducing their bioavailability.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): During cooking or processing, the glycosidic bonds joining glucose molecules of starch are broken. This process is called: *
Rationale: Hydrolysis is the chemical reaction where glycosidic bonds joining glucose molecules in starch polymers are cleaved by water molecules in the presence of heat, acid, or enzymes (breaking starch into smaller dextrins and sugars).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The function of starch in soups or gravies. *
Rationale: Starch functions primarily as a thickening agent in liquid foods like soups, sauces, and gravies by gelatinizing and swelling to trap free water molecules, increasing viscosity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is also called cellophane noodles or bean threads being made from mungbean flour. *
Rationale: Sotanghon refers to thin, translucent glass noodles or cellophane noodles traditionally manufactured from mung bean starch flour.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): In jellies and jams, sugar functions as a: *
Rationale: In high concentrations (typically 65%+ soluble solids), sugar acts as a powerful preserving agent in jams and jellies by creating high osmotic pressure that draws water out of microbial cells, preventing spoilage.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A seaweed used to process monosodium glutamate. *
Rationale: Kelp (a large brown seaweed/macroalgae) is naturally rich in glutamates and serves as a commercial raw source utilized in the industrial extraction and production of monosodium glutamate (MSG) and seasoning agents.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Equivalent of 1 brick of butter in cups. *
Rationale: Standard baking and culinary measurement equivalencies state that 1 standard "brick" or block of butter equals exactly 8 tablespoons, which is equivalent to 1 cup (or 2 sticks where 1 stick = 1/2 cup).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Flour mixture products leavened by chemical agents such as baking soda and baking powder. *
Rationale: Quick breads are flour-based baked goods leavened rapidly by chemical leavening agents (baking soda and baking powder) or steam rather than slow biological yeast fermentation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following sugars will crystallize most readily? *
Rationale: Lactose (milk sugar) crystallizes most readily and rapidly out of solution compared to sucrose, glucose, or fructose, which is why improper candy-making or ice cream storage can lead to a sandy, gritty texture caused by coarse lactose crystal formation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): In sugar cookery, fats such as butter and cream function as: *
Rationale: In sugar cookery and confectionery, fats (such as butter and cream) function as interfering agents that physically interrupt and slow down the rapid crystallization of sugar molecules, ensuring smooth textures in fudges and caramels.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): In coffee brewing, prolonged contact of coffee grounds with boiling water results in: *
Answer (Back): a bitter taste due to too much tannin extraction
Rationale: Prolonged contact of coffee grounds with boiling water extracts excess bitter tannins and undesirable phenolic compounds, resulting in an unpalatably bitter, harsh beverage.
Option 2: a bitter taste due to too much tannin extraction
Option 4: a bland taste due to volatilization

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The three basic ingredients of sponge cake: *
Rationale: The three essential, fundamental ingredients that form the structural foundation of a traditional sponge cake are eggs, sugar, and flour.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Hydrolytic rancidity is accelerated by: *
Rationale: Hydrolytic rancidity is accelerated by the enzymatic action of lipases (either naturally present in food or produced by psychrotrophic microbes), which hydrolyze ester bonds in fats to release free fatty acids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Factor that promotes discoloration of carrots: *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The ingredient which serves as substrate for yeast fermentation in dough. *
Rationale: Fermenting yeasts metabolize simple hexose sugars (glucose and fructose) as their primary substrate, producing carbon dioxide gas and alcohol during bread dough fermentation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A dispersion which has the smallest particle size: *
Rationale: A true solution is a homogeneous mixture where solute particles are of molecular or ionic dimensions (<1 nanometer), representing the smallest particle size among dispersions (compared to colloidal dispersions and coarse suspensions).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The first organ used to judge food quality. *
Rationale: The eyes serve as the first organ used to judge food quality visually (evaluating color, gloss, shape, and freedom from defects) before smelling, touching, or tasting.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Organic compound responsible for the characteristic flavor of butter. *
Rationale:
Diacetyl (along with acetoin) is the primary volatile organic compound and aromatic diketone responsible for the characteristic buttery flavor and aroma of butter.

• Glycerol / Fatty acid / Beta-carotene: Structural lipids or pigments, but diacetyl drives the distinct flavor profile.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A flour also known as soft or weak flour due to its low protein content. *
Rationale:
Cake flour is milled from soft wheat and has a low protein content (~7–9%), making it a soft or weak flour ideal for tender, delicate cakes.

• Bread flour: Hard wheat with high protein (~12–14%).
• Pastry flour: Intermediate protein (~9–10%).
• All-purpose flour: General-purpose blend (~10–12%).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Ingredient in baking powder that leavens: *
Rationale: Baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) is the alkaline chemical leavening agent that reacts with acid to release carbon dioxide gas in baking powder formulations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All soups are based on: *
Rationale: Stock—a flavorful liquid simmered from bones, mirepoix, and aromatics—serves as the foundational base for virtually all classical soups.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Shortenings are solid at room temperature since they have gone through: *
Rationale: Hydrogenation is the chemical process of adding hydrogen atoms across unsaturated double bonds in liquid vegetable oils, turning them into solid or semi-solid shortenings at room temperature.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Cream which contains 30% - 36% milk fat. *
Rationale:
Light whipping cream contains approximately 30% to 36% milk fat, making it suitable for whipping into light foams.

• Heavy cream: Contains 36% to 40%+ milk fat.
• Half and half: Contains 10.5% to 18% milk fat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Examples of this shellfish are lobsters, crabs, shrimps, and crayfish. *
Rationale:
Crustaceans are a category of shellfish characterized by segmented bodies and hard exoskeletons, including lobsters, crabs, shrimps, and crayfish.

• Mollusks: Soft-bodied shellfish like clams, oysters, and squids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Sauce of eggyolk, butter, and vinegar. *
Rationale:
Béarnaise sauce is a rich classical emulsion sauce derived from hollandaise, flavored with egg yolk, clarified butter, vinegar/white wine reduction, and tarragon/shallots.

• Allemande / Hollandaise: White or butter-lemon emulsion sauces without tarragon reduction.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Process of pouring meat drippings over the surface of meat while broiling. *
Rationale: Basting is the culinary technique of spooning or pouring melted fat, pan drippings, or sauces over the surface of roasting or broiling meat to prevent drying out and enhance flavor.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Example of a poultry part classified as white meat. *
Rationale:
Chicken and poultry breasts consist predominantly of fast-twitch muscle fibers with low myoglobin content, classifying them as white meat.

• Drumstick / Wings: Dark meat containing higher myoglobin and fat content due to postural support.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Method of cooking egg in which it is broken out of the shell and dropped in simmering water. *
Rationale: Poaching is a gentle moist-heat cooking method where food (such as a shelled egg) is submerged and cooked in simmering liquid maintained just below the boiling point (82°C–96°C).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Property of sugar which is relevant in keeping baked products moist and soft. *
Rationale: Sugar is highly hygroscopic (it readily attracts and binds moisture from the surrounding air), a functional property that helps retain moisture, keeping baked goods soft and preventing rapid staling.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Too much kneading results in a/an ____ dough. *
Rationale: Excessive, prolonged kneading breaks down and over-stretches the gluten protein strands, resulting in an overly tough, rigid, and inelastic dough that snaps back or resists proper shaping.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Locally known as “pata”. *
Rationale:
"Pata" is the local Filipino culinary term for pork knuckles or hocks (front or hind leg joints).

• Spare ribs / Shoulder butt / Jowl: Distinct anatomical cuts of pork.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Light, fluffy, baked or steamed egg dish. *
Rationale:
A soufflé is a light, airy, baked or steamed egg-based dish structured by beaten egg whites folded into a flavored base cream or purée.

• Omelet / Scrambled: Folded or stirred egg dishes without the puffed baked soufflé structure.
• Fondue: Melted cheese dish.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Ice cream with fruits or chocolate syrup. *
Rationale:
A parfait is a layered dessert typically featuring ice cream interspersed with fruits, syrups, liqueurs, or whipped cream.

• Mousse: Lightly whipped, aerated chilled dessert cream.
• Sherbet: Frozen fruit-based dessert containing milk solids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A light, airy crystalline candy containing a large amount of egg white which is added to the syrup while still very hot. *
Rationale:
Divinity is a light, airy, crystalline confectionery candy made by beating a hot sugar-corn syrup mixture directly into stiffly whipped egg whites.

• Brittle / Fudge / Fondant: Confections with different sugar crystal structures and cooking methods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A process of fermenting starch like in beer making. *
Rationale:
Malting is the specialized process of steeping, germinating, and drying cereal grains (like barley) to activate starch-converting enzymes for brewing and distilling.

• Dextrinization: Partial breakdown of starch into dextrins via dry heat.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Process of allowing the dough to rise before baking under controlled temperature: *
Rationale:
Proofing is the final fermentation stage of allowing shaped yeast dough to rise under controlled temperature and humidity conditions right before baking.

• Kneading: Mechanical development of gluten.
• Punching: Deflating fermented dough to redistribute yeast and gases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Method of mixing flour mixture applied to butter cake and pound cake. *
Rationale:
The conventional method (cream-butter method) involves creaming fat and sugar together, beating in eggs, and alternately adding dry and liquid ingredients, which is the standard procedure for butter and pound cakes.

• Muffin method: Liquid fats mixed with dry ingredients quickly.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The use of too much leavening produces a baked product with: *
Rationale: Excessive leavening (baking powder or soda) produces too much gas too rapidly before the gluten and starch structure can set, causing the cell walls to stretch and rupture, leading to structural collapse and a low volume.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Thick soups or stews usually containing seafood, potatoes, and milk or cream. *
Rationale:
Chowders are rich, thick American soups or stews traditionally containing seafood (clams, fish), diced potatoes, onions, and milk or cream.

• Bisques: Smooth, cream-based puréed shellfish soups.
• Potages: General French term for thick or clear soups.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): To brown the surface of meat by a short application of intense heat. *
Rationale: Searing is the culinary technique of browning the outer surface of meat quickly using intense, high dry heat to develop rich Maillard flavors and color.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This refers to the process of reducing the number of pathogenic microorganisms in equipment and utensils. *
Rationale:
Sanitization is the chemical or thermal process of reducing pathogenic microorganisms on cleaned equipment and utensils down to safe public health levels.

• Sterilization: Complete destruction of all microbial forms.
• Cleaning: Removal of visible soil.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which is not a guideline in writing a menu? *
Answer (Back): Do not provide descriptions of products.
Rationale: This guideline is false, making it the correct exception. Effective menu writing should include appetizing, accurate descriptions of food products to guide customer expectations and stimulate sales.
Option 1: Do not provide descriptions of products.
Option 2: The main dish should be given the most prominent space.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A fish stock made with wine or lemon juice. *
Rationale:
A fumet is a concentrated fish stock simmered with fish bones, white wine, lemon juice, and aromatics.

• Veloute: A grand sauce made from stock and roux.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which is not an institution-based food service? *
Rationale: Commercial fast-food chains like McDonald's operate as commercial retail foodservice establishments, whereas institutional foodservices include corporate canteens, university dining halls, military messes, and hospital kitchens.
Option 2: Corporate canteen at the Asian Development Bank

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This tool is used to drain foods when they are lifted from liquid. *
Rationale: A slotted spoon features perforations that allow liquids to drain through while lifting solid food items out of pots or serving vessels.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A versatile equipment in quantity cookery which can be used for both moist and dry heat cookery and at times may even be used as a sink. *
Rationale: A tilting frying pan (brazier/skillet) is a highly versatile piece of commercial kitchen equipment used for frying, braising, simmering, steaming, roasting, and acting as a temporary holding sink.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This refers to the process of putting together different food items to complete a meal. *
Rationale: Assembly is the operational foodservice step of combining and putting together different prepared food items and portions to complete individual meals or trays.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A small heater used in French service. *
Rationale:
A rechaud is a small portable spirit or electric heater used in classic French tableside service to keep food warm.

• Gueridon: The mobile service trolley.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not an appetizer in the strict sense of the word? *

Question (Front): Skills required of managers, described as those relating to their ability to work with abstract ideas and concepts. *

Administrative (conceptual) managerial skills refer to the cognitive ability to view the organization as a whole, understand how its parts interrelate, and work with abstract ideas and complex concepts.

• Technical skills: Proficiency in specific operational tasks.
• Human skills: Interpersonal ability to work well with people.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A manager’s function involving activities which ensures that the organization is moving towards its goals. *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A standard used in human resource planning which is described as the written profile of the job to be filled: *
Rationale:
A job description is a written operational profile detailing the duties, responsibilities, reporting relationships, and scope of a specific job position.

• Job specification: Outlines the required qualifications, skills, and experience of the candidate.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Beef cooked to the rare stage should have an internal temperature of: *
Rationale: According to culinary meat cookery standards, beef cooked to a rare stage reaches an internal temperature of approximately 58°C to 60°C (130°F to 140°F).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following styles of service is considered under wait-service? *
Rationale:
French service is an elaborate form of wait-service where food is prepared, finished, or served tableside from a gueridon cart by trained waiters.

• Cafeteria / Buffet: Self-service or counter-service models.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Considered as the forerunner of the “carinderia”. *
Rationale: The karihan (or carinderia) is historically recognized in Philippine culinary history as the traditional local forerunner of the modern neighborhood eatery and roadside food stall.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): he French term for set menu. *
Rationale:
Table d'hôte is the French culinary term designating a set menu offering a complete multi-course meal at a fixed, single total price.

• À la carte: Individually priced menu items.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The largest controllable item of expenditure in a foodservice institution is/are: *
Rationale: In food service operations, the cost of raw food ingredients represents the single largest controllable variable expenditure item.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The multiplier to determine selling price for a 40% food cost is: *
Rationale:
To determine the pricing multiplier based on a desired 40% food cost percentage:

Formula =  100÷Food Cost Percentage.

Calculation =  100÷40=2.5 (or 2 ½).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It includes not only the basic rate but also fringe benefits such as vacation leave, sick leave, etc. *
Rationale: Total labor cost in foodservice management encompasses basic wages, salaries, and mandatory fringe benefits such as paid vacation leaves, sick leaves, 13th-month pay, and social security contributions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): How many servings will 1 kg of pork with bones yield? *
Rationale: When purchasing bone-in meat (such as 1 kg of pork with bones), standard foodservice yield testing factors in bone weight and trimming loss, typically yielding approximately 8 standard portions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What is the equivalent of scoop no. 30 in household measures? *
Rationale: A Scoop #30 has a volumetric capacity of 1/30 of a quart, which equals approximately 1 ounce or 2 tablespoons (1 fl oz / 6 teaspoons).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An error in performance rating that emphasizes the tendency to rate people higher than what they deserve: *
Rationale:
A leniency error in performance appraisal is a systematic rating bias where a supervisor tends to evaluate and rate all employees significantly higher and more leniently than their actual performance deserves.

• Central tendency: Rating everyone in the middle.
• Halo effect: Allowing one prominent trait to bias all ratings.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It refers to output in relation to input. *
Rationale:
Efficiency measures the operational ratio of useful output produced relative to the inputs expended (doing things right).

• Effectiveness: Achieving stated goals (doing the right things).
• Productivity: Overall measure of output generation relative to resource inputs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It refers to the sequencing of operations in a foodservice system. *
Rationale: Work flow refers to the logical, sequential movement of food, materials, and personnel through the various operational stages of a foodservice system.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An ideal temperature for dry storeroom is: *
Rationale: The ideal ambient temperature for maintaining dry food storerooms ranges between 50°F and 70°F (approx. 10°C to 21°C), with 70°F serving as the standard upper benchmark.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The recommended temperature for storing frozen goods according to the Philippine Sanitation Code is: *
Rationale: According to the Sanitation Code of the Philippines (PD 856), freezers for storing frozen goods must maintain a recommended temperature of -12°C (10°F) or colder (ideally -18°C / 0°F).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Porterhouse steak comes from the portion of beef carcass known as: *
Rationale: High-end, tender beef steaks such as the Porterhouse, T-bone, and strip loin are harvested from the short loin primal cut of the beef carcass.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A no-choice menu. *
Rationale:
A set menu is a fixed, pre-determined ("no-choice") menu where customers are served a predetermined meal without options.

• Selective menu: Offers choices within categories.
• Cycle menu: A repeating set of menus over a set period.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The space allowance for the foodservice facility of a hospital may be based on the: *
Rationale: In foodservice facility planning, spatial allocation and sizing for hospital kitchens are determined primarily by calculating the total volume, census, and types of meals to be prepared daily.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A pallet is a useful equipment in the: *
Rationale: A pallet (wooden or plastic platform) is an essential materials-handling equipment used in dry and cold storage areas to keep food sacks and boxes elevated at least 6 inches off the floor.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Question (Front): One of the following would make the least satisfactory thickening agent in a casserole: *
Rationale: Cornstarch is a pure root starch that undergoes retrogradation or syneresis when subjected to long holding times, freezing, or acidic casserole environments, making it less stable as a long-term casserole thickener compared to wheat flour or waxy starches.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A dairy product not recommended to accompany coffee. *
Rationale: Light whipping cream contains higher fat content and milk solids that can cause an oily separation or feathering when added directly to hot, acidic coffee, making it less ideal than table cream or half-and-half.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Examples of thick soups except: *
Rationale: Consommé is a brilliantly clear, clarified gourmet broth, whereas chowders, egg drop soups, and minestrone are classified as thick or hearty textured soups.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Commercial sterilization is designed to eliminate: *
Rationale: Commercial sterilization (achieved in low-acid canned foods) aims to destroy all pathogenic, toxigenic, and spoilage microorganisms capable of growing under normal storage conditions.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What selling price would you recommend for an item with an RFC of P45.00? *
Rationale: Let food cost percentage be assumed at a standard markup (e.g., evaluating standard markup ratios or reverse-calculating based on P45.00 RFC and typical margins yielding P128.57 per exam key formulas).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): What is the % sales mix of an ice cream sundae that sold 300 units in a day when 656 desserts were sold? *
Rationale:
To calculate sales mix percentage:

Formula =  (Units Sold for Specific Item÷Total Category Units Sold)>100.

Given values: Sundaes sold = 300 units; Total desserts sold = 656 units.

Calculation =  (300÷656)×100=45.73%.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): According to the Sanitation Code of the Philippines, how much space should be provided for the kitchen? *
Rationale: According to the Sanitation Code of the Philippines (PD 856), food establishment regulations recommend that kitchen and food preparation space allocation should be approximately one-fourth (1/4) of the customer dining area space.
Option 4: same amount of space as the dining area

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A technique in a wage program that translates relative job worth into money values. *
Rationale: Job pricing is the compensation technique in wage administration that translates the relative job worth determined via job evaluation into concrete monetary salary scales.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Considered the foundation of Human Resource Management. *
Rationale: Job analysis is the systematic, foundational HR process of gathering data, tasks, duties, and requirements to build job descriptions and specifications.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A test which determines quality standards to be set for commodities that involves coming up with the best count, weight, or quantity of fruits and vegetables. *
Rationale: A raw food test (yield test / butchering test) determines the standard quality, trim loss, edible portion yield, and purchase specifications for raw commodities like fresh fruits and vegetables.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is a term used to refer to equipment that are manufactured according to the buyer’s specifications. *
Rationale:
Custom built equipment refers to specialized machinery and fixtures manufactured precisely according to a buyer's unique architectural and operational specifications.

• Stock equipment: Standard catalog-manufactured equipment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A government agency that settles labor disputes. *
Rationale: The National Labor Relations Commission (NLRC) is the government quasi-judicial agency mandated to arbitrate and settle formal labor disputes, strikes, and employer-employee grievances in the Philippines.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A form of positive reinforcement which aims to provide guidance or advice to an erring employee. *
Rationale: Counseling is a form of positive behavioral reinforcement and coaching used by supervisors to provide constructive guidance, feedback, and advice to an erring employee.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Work stoppage that happens at the instigation of the employer. *
Rationale: A lock-out is a temporary work stoppage or denial of employment initiated by the employer during a labor dispute (as opposed to a strike initiated by employees).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The temperature of Chicken Joy was checked to see if its critical limit of 1800F was met. Which HACCP principle was applied? *
Rationale:
Checking and measuring temperature against established critical limits during food preparation is the core definition of monitoring in a HACCP system.

• Verification: Activities (other than monitoring) that validate the HACCP plan.
• Record keeping: Documenting the monitored data.
• Hazard analysis: Identifying biological, chemical, or physical hazards.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is not a principle of good organization? *
Rationale:
"Commitment to excellence" is a general corporate mission or value statement, whereas the established classical principles of good organization include division of labor, unity of command, and esprit de corps.

• Division of labor / Esprit de corps / Unity of command: Core classical management and organizational principles.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Refers to the basic unit of a layout. *
Rationale: A work center is the basic physical and functional unit of a kitchen layout where specific equipment and tasks are grouped together.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The most sanitary type of food equipment. *
Rationale:
Stainless steel is the premier material for commercial foodservice equipment because it is non-porous, corrosion-resistant, durable, and exceptionally sanitary.

• Copper / Aluminum: Prone to chemical reactivity or pitting.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following is an ideal material flow? *
Rationale: An ideal material and operational flow follows a logical forward progression from receiving to storage, pre-preparation, production, and service, preventing cross-contamination.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Worktable heights for standing tasks are: *
Rationale: Standard ergonomic guidelines specify that worktable heights for tasks performed while standing should be between 36 and 41 inches depending on the operator's height and task type.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Worktable heights for sitting tasks are: *
Rationale: Ergonomic seating standards dictate that worktable heights for seated tasks should be lower, ranging between 28 and 30 inches.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The ideal height of the highest shelf should be: *
Rationale: Sanitation regulations mandate that the highest storage shelf and stacked items must maintain adequate clearance from ceilings and lighting fixtures (typically maintaining safe vertical margins), while floor clearance requires at least 6 inches.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Space allocation for sanitation should consider the following except: *
Rationale: Space allocation for sanitation facilities considers the physical space required for cleaning personnel, dishwashing methods, and tool/chemical storage, whereas the specific chemical volume needed is an operational consumable inventory rather than a structural space-planning determinant.
Option 4: storage area for cleaning equipment, tools, and agents

Rationale: Crisscrossing pathways in a kitchen layout increase traffic congestion and cross-contamination risks between clean and soiled workflows.

Option 2: an employee walks in the kitchen in a crisscross pattern

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Key players in facilities planning design except: *
Rationale: Facilities planning and design teams typically involve architects, builders, engineers, and investors, whereas store managers execute operations rather than serving as primary design engineers.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Considered basic work centers in the facility except: *
Rationale: Receiving is an intake and holding dock rather than a basic internal food production or processing work center (which includes pre-preparation, cooking, and housekeeping/sanitation).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The main determinant of space allocation is the: *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It consists of a group of related work centers: *
Rationale: A section in facility layout terminology consists of a coordinated group of related work centers operating together.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The number of tablespoons in a Scoop #16: *
Rationale: A Scoop #16 holds a capacity of 1/16 of a gallon, which equates to 2 ounces or exactly 4 level tablespoons of food portioning volume.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The section of a feasibility study that describes the company’s product, how it is made, and the facility where the produce will be produced. *
Rationale: The technical section of a feasibility study details the engineering specifications, manufacturing processes, required equipment, raw materials, and facility layout where the product will be produced.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): He proposed the 14 principles of management. *

Henri Fayol proposed the classic 14 principles of management under administrative management theory.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): How many servings will you have for 1 gallon of ice cream using Scoop No. 4? *
Rationale:
To calculate the yield from a gallon of ice cream using Scoop No. 4:

1 gallon = 4 quarts = 128 fluid ounces.

Scoop No. 4 holds 1/4 of a quart (or 8 fluid ounces / 1 cup per scoop).

Calculation = 128 oz ÷ 4 oz (or 4 quarts × 8 scoops per quart) = 32 servings.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): How many 2 ½ cans of evaporated milk are there in 1 case? *
Rationale: Standard commercial cases of No. 2 ½ canned goods (such as evaporated milk) contain exactly 24 cans per case.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Information which may be obtained from a market research except: *
Rationale: Market research focuses externally on customer demographics, spending habits, and market demand/sales potential, whereas internal cost accounting determines approximate expenses.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This tool serves as the blueprint of the restaurant’s operations.
Rationale: A business plan serves as the overarching structural blueprint and strategic roadmap of a restaurant's financial, operational, and marketing goals.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Part of the business plan that provides the approximate capital needed to run the restaurant operations. *
Rationale: The technical and operational section of a business plan outlines production methods, facility layout, equipment needs, and approximate capital requirements needed to launch operations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The provision of ramps and railings is mandated by this law: *
Rationale: Batas Pambansa Blg. 344 (The Accessibility Law) mandates the provision of architectural structural modifications such as ramps, railings, and accessible facilities for disabled persons.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The Temperature Danger Zone is between: *
Rationale: The Temperature Danger Zone—the critical thermal range where pathogenic bacteria multiply rapidly in food—spans between 4°C (40°F) and 60°C (140°F).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): HACCP will help: *
Rationale: HACCP shifts quality control from end-product testing to proactive, preventative process monitoring, which significantly reduces the high costs associated with continuous microbiological end-product testing and analyses.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Potatoes and carrots are blanched before drying in order to: *
Rationale: Blanching root vegetables like potatoes and carrots prior to drying inactivates polyphenol oxidases and leaches out excess reducing sugars, preventing unwanted Maillard browning and caramelization during dehydration.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Why is salt added to flour mixtures? *
Rationale: Salt strengthens gluten protein networks, controls yeast fermentation rates, and helps produce a cohesive, firm dough structure in baking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The practical size of can for institutional preparation and cooking is: *
Rationale: In institutional quantity food preparation, the No. 2 ½ can (holding roughly 3.5 cups / 27-28 oz) is recognized as the standard practical size for catering and quantity recipes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Commissary foodservice systems involve large-scale centralized production followed by bulk transport, holding, and reheating across remote satellite service sites, presenting inherent critical control point risks in temperature maintenance and food safety.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The foodservice system that requires the least kitchen skills. *
Rationale: Assembly-serve systems purchase foods fully prepared or highly processed, requiring the absolute least amount of on-site culinary cooking skills from kitchen staff.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The foodservice system concerned with providing dining service. *
Rationale: Conventional foodservice systems prepare foods from raw ingredients on-site and serve them directly to customers within the same facility.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Open burner gas ranges provide rapid, adjustable heat control, making them ideal for short-order preparations and quick-service cooking stations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Raw poultry and chicken are universally recognized as primary reservoirs for Salmonella bacterial contamination.
