Option 3: Only the first statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards2 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which is not a corrective action? *
Answer (Back): Rejecting a new shipment of chicken.
Rationale: Rejecting an incoming raw food shipment at the loading dock is a preventive receiving control or prerequisite purchasing action, whereas correcting an active deviation during food production constitutes a formal HACCP corrective action.
Option 1: Continuing to cook hamburger until it reaches a minimum internal temperature of 155°F for 15 seconds.
Option 2: Discarding cooked chicken that has been held at 120°F for 5 hours.
Option 3: Sanitizing a preparation table before starting a new task.
Option 4: Rejecting a new shipment of chicken.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Pigments that are very soluble in cooking water. *
Rationale:
Anthocyanins are water-soluble flavonoid pigments (found in red cabbage, berries, and black rice) that leach readily into cooking water, changing hue based on pH.

• Carotenoids / Lycopene: Fat-soluble pigments insoluble in water.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The protein complex formed when flour is manipulated with water. *
Rationale: Gluten is the tough, elastic protein complex formed when the wheat flour storage proteins (gliadin and glutenin) are hydrated with water and mechanically manipulated (kneaded).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The product of ripened cream which is churned until butterfat separates from buttermilk. *
Rationale:
Butter is manufactured by churning ripened cream until the dairy fat globules coalesce and separate from the liquid aqueous phase (buttermilk).

• Margarine: Manufactured from hydrogenated vegetable oils.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A powdered product after chocolate is processed to remove part of its cocoa butter. *
Rationale: Cocoa is the dry, powdered product obtained after roasting cacao beans, grinding them into chocolate liquor, and pressing out a major portion of the cocoa butter.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Water with high amounts of Ca, Mg salt, sulfates, and bicarbonates. *
Rationale: Hard water is defined as water containing high mineral concentrations of calcium and magnesium salts, sulfates, and bicarbonates.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Noodle used in preparing pancit luglog. *
Rationale: Bihon (rice vermicelli noodles) is the traditional rice noodle utilized in preparing classic Filipino pancit dishes like pancit luglog or pancit bihon.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Saturated long-chain fatty acids generally yield: *
Rationale: Saturated fatty acids possess straight carbon chains packed tightly together via intermolecular forces, making them solid or semi-solid fats at room temperature.
Option 4: solid that starts to melt at room temperature

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The factor that promotes the discoloration of carrots except: *
Rationale: Carrots contain stable carotenoid pigments that are resistant to normal cooking and air exposure, whereas acid, excessive heating, or alkaline baking soda alter carrot texture and color stability.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The strong odor produced in the cooking of onion and cabbage family is due to: *
Rationale: Cooking vegetables belonging to the Allium (onion, garlic) and Brassica (cabbage, broccoli) families releases volatile organic sulfur compounds responsible for their characteristic pungent aromas.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A microorganism used in the production of beer: *
Rationale:
Saccharomyces carlsbergensis (along with S. pastorianus) is a bottom-fermenting yeast traditionally utilized in the commercial production of lager beers.

• Saccharomyces cerevisiae: Top-fermenting yeast used for ales and baking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Factors naturally present in food that affect microbial growth except: *
Rationale: Relative humidity is an extrinsic environmental storage factor, whereas pH, oxygen requirement, and moisture content are intrinsic factors naturally present in food.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A change in frozen food due to fluctuation in the temperature of the freezer: *
Rationale: Freezer burn occurs when moisture is lost from frozen food surfaces due to temperature fluctuations in the storage freezer, causing sublimation and surface dehydration.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Another term used to describe freeze-drying: *
Rationale: Lyophilization is the technical scientific term for freeze-drying, where water is removed from frozen material via sublimation under a vacuum.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The amount of moisture available for bacterial growth is known as: *
Rationale: Water activity (aw) measures the ratio of water vapor pressure of a food to pure water, representing the unbound moisture available for microbial growth.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The simplest heat preservation method: *
Rationale: Boiling is the simplest thermal preservation method, applying wet heat to destroy vegetative microorganisms and inactivate spoilage enzymes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A type of solution wherein there is a small amount of solute compared to the solvent. *
Rationale:
A dilute solution is a chemical mixture containing a relatively small amount of dissolved solute compared to the large amount of solvent.

• Concentrated solution: Contains a high amount of solute.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is responsible for the changes in the color of meat as it is oxidized or reduced: *
Rationale: Myoglobin contains a central iron (Fe) atom within its heme ring; changes in the oxidation and chemical state of this iron atom are responsible for the color shifts in meat (from bright red oxymyoglobin to brown metmyoglobin).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The local term for pork spare ribs. *
Rationale:
"Tadyang" is the local Filipino culinary term for pork spare ribs.

• Kasim: Pork shoulder/boston butt.
• Cadera: Hip/rump cut.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The growth of microorganisms is promoted in meat due to its high content of _____. 1. water 2. fat 3. protein 4. Carbohydrate *
Rationale: Meat promotes rapid microbial growth due to its high water content (1) and exceptionally rich protein substrate availability (3). Carbohydrate and fat content do not drive primary bacterial spoilage in fresh meat to the same extent.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An objective test which measures viscosity and consistency of foods. *
Rationale:
The line spread test is a simple objective physical measure of the consistency and viscosity of semi-fluid foods (such as sauces, batters, and purees) by measuring how far a sample flows outward on a calibrated grid.

• Shear test / Tenderness press: Measure meat texture and shear force.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): These factors increase drying rate except: *
Rationale:
Increasing the relative humidity of drying air decreases the moisture concentration gradient between the food and the surrounding air, thereby slowing down (rather than increasing) the drying rate.

• Cutting into smaller pieces / Increasing air velocity / Increasing drying temperature: All accelerate the drying rate.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It will shorten the cooking time of dried legumes or seeds: *
Answer (Back): adding soda to soaking and cooking water
Rationale: Adding baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) creates an alkaline cooking medium that softens plant cell wall hemicellulose and pectin, significantly shortening the cooking time of dried legumes.
Option 1: adding soda to soaking and cooking water
Option 2: adding one tablespoon of fat to cooking water
Option 3: boiling it at the time of cooking
Option 4: soaking the seeds in water with salt

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The term used to describe the quick expansion of dough caused by expanding gases during the first 20 minutes of baking: *
Rationale: Oven spring describes the rapid, sudden expansion of dough caused by expanding gases (carbon dioxide and steam) during the initial phase of baking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It refers to the mixing of flour and fat: *
Rationale:
In baking terminology, "cutting" (or cutting-in) refers to the culinary technique of blending solid fat into dry flour using a pastry blender or knives until crumb-sized particles form.

• Creaming: Beating softened fat and sugar together.
• Folding: Gently incorporating whipped ingredients.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): When is the best time to add sugar when making egg white foam? *
Answer (Back): near the end of whipping time
Rationale: Sugar should be added near the end of whipping egg white foam; adding it too early delays foam formation and decreases volume, while adding it at the end stabilizes the whipped protein structure.
Option 1: combining it with the egg white
Option 2: near the end of whipping time
Option 3: in the middle of whipping time
Option 4: at the start of whipping time

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Pasteurization is the exposure of food to high temperatures. It is done for a short period of time to destroy harmful microorganisms. *
Rationale:
Statement 1 is correct: pasteurization exposes food to elevated temperatures. 

Statement 2 is correct: it is executed for a controlled, short duration specifically designed to destroy pathogenic and spoilage microorganisms without altering food quality.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It simmers food in a small amount of liquid in a covered pot or casserole. *
Rationale:
Braising is a combination cooking method that involves searing meat and then simmering it gently in a small amount of liquid inside a tightly covered pot or casserole.

• Scalding / Steaming: Heat methods using hot liquid or vapor without initial searing/simmering in a covered pot.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All of the following are varieties of mango except: *
Rationale: Cavendish is a commercial variety of banana, whereas Carabao, Pajo, and Pico are distinct Philippine mango varieties.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It causes food spoilage in dairy products and eggs: *
Rationale: Alcaligenes species are common psychrotrophic bacteria responsible for ropiness and spoilage in protein-rich dairy products and eggs.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): How many weeks is the shelf-life of eggs? *
Rationale: Under standard refrigeration conditions, fresh shell eggs maintain acceptable culinary quality and safety for approximately 4 to 6 weeks.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It will minimize reaching the smoking temperature of fat during frying: *
Answer (Back): by using a deep and narrow frying pan
Rationale: Using a deep and narrow frying pan reduces the surface area exposed to oxygen and concentrates the fat, minimizing rapid oxidative breakdown and helping prevent reaching the smoking point prematurely compared to wide pans.
Option 1: by using a deep and narrow frying pan
Option 3: by using a shallow and wide diameter pan

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The sensory qualities of food can be measured objectively and subjectively. Subjective evaluation needs mechanical devices. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is correct: food sensory qualities can be assessed objectively (using instruments) and subjectively (using human senses). 

Statement 2 is incorrect because subjective evaluation relies on human sensory panels, not mechanical measuring devices.
Option 1: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 3: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It makes spinach stems, asparagus spears, and broccoli become tougher as they mature. *
Rationale:
Lignin is a tough, non-carbohydrate complex polymer that deposits in plant cell walls as tissues mature, making vegetable stems (like asparagus and broccoli) and spinach stems woody and tough.

• Cellulose: A structural carbohydrate, but woody toughness is specifically driven by lignification.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Substances used to preserve food by lowering the pH: *
Rationale: Vinegar and citric acid lower food pH, creating an acidic environment that inhibits microbial spoilage and acts as a natural preservative.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Sodium hydroxide is locally known as “apog”. It is used to facilitate the peeling of fruits such as tomato, guava, and others. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Statement 1 is incorrect because sodium hydroxide is locally known as "sosa" or caustic soda, whereas "apog" refers to calcium hydroxide (slaked lime). 

Statement 2 is correct: alkaline solutions like apog are traditionally used in food processing to facilitate fruit skin peeling (such as for tomatoes and guavas).
Option 3: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 4: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Miswa is a thread-like noodle made from rice and wheat flour. It can be cooked instantly. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Rationale:
Miswa (or meesua) is a very thin, thread-like salted wheat flour noodle (not rice flour) that cooks almost instantly in boiling water or hot broth.

• The first statement is incorrect: Miswa is made from wheat flour, not rice flour (which is used for bihon or rice sticks).
• The second statement is correct: Due to its extremely thin strands, it cooks instantaneously when added to boiling liquids.
Option 1: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 2: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which of the following statements is true” *
Answer (Back): As fruits ripen, sugar content increases.
Rationale: During the natural ripening process of climacteric and non-climacteric fruits, complex carbohydrates (like starch) are enzymatically hydrolyzed into simple sugars, causing sugar content and sweetness to increase significantly while acidity typically declines.
Option 1: As fruits ripen, sugar content remains the same.
Option 2: As fruits ripen, sugar content increases.
Option 3: As fruits ripen, sugar content decreases.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Taste panels usually consist of at least ____ individuals. *
Rationale: Standard sensory evaluation protocols and consumer preference testing require a minimum sensory panel size of at least 5 trained or semi-trained individuals (though larger panels of 10 to 20+ are common for robust statistical validity).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A research design that collects data from a group of customers at a single point in time. *
Rationale:
A cross-sectional research design collects observational data from a target population or group of customers at a single, specific point in time without long-term tracking.

• Longitudinal: Collects data from the same subjects repeatedly over an extended period.
• Cohort: Follows a specific cohort forward or backward through time.
• Time series: Evaluates multiple data points across sequential time intervals.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is not the Pilipino translation: *
Rationale:
Abitsuelas is the local Tagalog term for string beans, kidney beans, or common snap beans, whereas cowpea is locally known as paayap, making this statement the correct mismatch (exception).

• Chickpea is garbanzos: Correct translation.
• Mungbean is mongo: Correct translation.
• Soybean is utaw: Correct translation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The cut of pork that is best for cooking sinigang. *
Rationale:
The picnic shoulder cut (kasim or picnic shoulder) contains a balanced amount of lean meat, connective tissue, and fat, making it ideal for slow-simmered local savory soup dishes like sinigang.

• Tenderloin: Extremely tender and lean, best for quick-cooking, dry-heat preparations (stewing causes it to dry out).
• Leg: Lean cut better suited for roasting or ham preparation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): An example of a subjective food evaluation test: *
Rationale:
Creating a human sensory taste (evaluation) panel is a subjective (sensory) food evaluation test relying on human sensory organs (taste, smell, texture).

• Measuring weight / Spectrophotometer / Measuring volume: Objective physical or chemical instrumental tests.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Food preservation is treating food by any method such as drying or smoking. It is done to kill the microorganisms present in food. *
Answer (Back): The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.
Rationale:
Food preservation methods (such as drying, salting, canning, or smoking) are designed to inhibit, control, or reduce microbial growth and enzyme activity, but they do not universally or completely "kill" all microorganisms present in food.

• The first statement is correct: Preservation encompasses techniques like drying or smoking.
• The second statement is incorrect: Preservation inhibits spoilage and pathogens rather than serving as a guaranteed sterilization technique to kill all microorganisms.
Option 2: The first statement is incorrect but the second statement is correct.
Option 4: The first statement is correct but the second statement is incorrect.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): he term referring to goat meat: *
Rationale:
Chevon is the standardized culinary and meat science term for the meat harvested from goats.

• Venison: Meat from deer.
• Mutton: Meat from adult sheep.
• Veal: Meat from calves.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Which ingredient differentiates Sinuam from Tinola? *
Rationale:
Sinuam and tinola are both traditional Filipino ginger-based broths (soup dishes), but sinuam distinctively incorporates shredded or sliced green (unripe) papaya and native ginger paste, whereas traditional tinola typically utilizes chayote or green papaya wedges with ginger and chili leaves.

• Pepper leaves: Used in both tinola and sinuam.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Despite efforts to eliminate spoilage organisms during canning, sometimes canned foods spoil. This may be due to: *
Rationale: Even with advanced industrial canning technology, commercial canned foods can occasionally spoil due to pre-processing raw material spoilage, under-processing (insufficient thermal lethality), or post-processing container leakage where contaminated cooling water enters through defective can seams.
Option 3: leakage of contaminated water through can seams during cooking

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This involves development of new products by making a genetic modification in a living organism. *
Rationale:
Biotechnology encompasses advanced scientific techniques involving genetic modification, gene splicing, and recombinant DNA technology applied to living organisms to create novel food products or crops.

• Epigenetics: The study of cellular gene expression changes without altering underlying DNA sequence.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A symbiotic relationship beneficial to both associates: *
Rationale:
Mutualism is a biological symbiotic relationship where both interacting species derive mutually beneficial fitness outcomes.

• Commensalism: One organism benefits while the other is unaffected.
• Parasitism: One organism benefits at the expense of the host.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The ratio of liquid to flour in popover batters: *
Rationale: Popovers are quick breads characterized by a fluid, high-liquid batter (equal parts flour and liquid by volume, yielding a 1:1 ratio) that creates steam to puff the pastry during baking.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Why does commercial ice cream have more body than homemade ice cream? *
Rationale:
Commercial ice cream incorporates food stabilizers (such as gums, carrageenan, or gelatin) to bind free water molecules, prevent large ice crystal formation, and impart a smooth, uniform "body" and texture.

• Homemade ice cream: Often lacks commercial stabilizers, resulting in faster coarse ice crystal formation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Deionized water is basically purified water without _____. *
Rationale: Deionized water is treated via ion-exchange resins specifically to strip out dissolved mineral ions (such as calcium, magnesium, and sodium), yielding purified water devoid of minerals.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It determines whether coffee is classified as light, medium or dark roast. *
Rationale:
Roasting time (and thermal profile progression) governs the degree of caramelization and Maillard browning reactions, determining whether coffee beans are classified as light, medium, or dark roast.

• Grinding level: Determines particle size for brewing extraction, not the roast profile.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): These are chemical compounds in green tea which act as antioxidants and may have anticarcinogenic properties: *
Rationale:
Green tea contains abundant polyphenolic compounds (such as catechins and flavonoids) that function as powerful biological antioxidants and possess potential anticarcinogenic properties.

• Tannins: Bitter astringent compounds, but polyphenolic phenols are the specific antioxidant agents highlighted.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A sensory phenomenon characterized by a dry, puckery feeling in the mouth: *
Rationale:
Astringency is a tactile oral sensory phenomenon characterized by a dry, puckery, drawing sensation in the mouth caused by the precipitation of salivary proteins by tannins or polyphenols.

• Tartness: A taste sensation driven by organic acids.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The sticky, moist texture of breads resulting from contamination by Bacillus mesentericus bacteria. *
Rationale: Rope is a classic bacterial spoilage defect in bread caused by Bacillus mesentericus spores surviving baking, resulting in a sticky, moist, stringy texture accompanied by a fruity odor.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): One cup gives ____ fluid ounces; _____ tablespoons; _____ teaspoons. *
Rationale: Standard kitchen measurement equivalencies state that 1 standard US cup equals exactly 8 fluid ounces, 16 tablespoons, and 48 teaspoons.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Type of cheese usually used for pizza making. *
Rationale:
Mozzarella cheese possesses high moisture, excellent meltability, and optimal stretch characteristics, making it the classic cheese utilized worldwide for pizza making.

• Parmesan: Hard, aged grating cheese.
• Blue/bleu cheese: Semi-soft, pungent, crumbly cheese.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A mechanical process that breaks up fat globules in milk into smaller globules that do not clump together. *
Rationale:
Homogenization is a mechanical high-pressure process that forces milk through minute valves, breaking large fat globules down into tiny, stable micro-globules that do not separate or clump together.

• Pasteurization: Thermal destruction of pathogens.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The cheese made from soy milk. *
Rationale:
Tofu (bean curd) is a soft, cheese-like food product manufactured by coagulating soy milk and pressing the resulting curds.

• Tempeh: A fermented whole soybean cake from Indonesia.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The formation of tiny syrup droplets on the surface of a baked meringue: *
Rationale:
Beading refers to the formation of amber-colored syrup droplets on the surface of a baked meringue, typically caused by overbaking or und حل (undissolved sugar).

• Weeping: Syneresis or moisture pooling underneath the meringue.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Artichoke and broccoli are classified as: *
Rationale: Artichokes and broccoli represent immature floral buds harvested and consumed as culinary vegetables belonging to the flower classification.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Fatty deposits within muscles of meat which contribute to its flavor and juiciness: *
Rationale:
Marbling refers to the fine, white flecks and intra-muscular deposits of fat distributed within meat muscles, which melt during cooking to enhance flavor, tenderness, and juiciness.

• Subcutaneous fat: Fat layer deposited directly underneath the skin.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The effect of acid on the anthocyanin of red cabbage, changing its to ____: *
Rationale:
Anthocyanin pigments found in red cabbage are water-soluble flavonoids that shift to a bright pink or reddish hue in the presence of an acidic medium.

• Bluish/violet hue: Occurs in neutral or alkaline (basic) environments.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The process of removing fat crystals so that oil remains liquid at refrigerated temperature: *
Rationale:
Winterizing is an industrial food processing technique that chills edible oils and filters out high-melting-point saturated fat crystals so that the oil remains clear and liquid at refrigerated temperatures.

• Hydrogenation: Converts liquid oils into semi-solid fats by adding hydrogen.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Compounds added to fats and oils which help prevent the development of rancidity: *
Rationale: Antioxidants (such as BHA, BHT, tocopherols, and propyl gallate) are chemical compounds added to fats and oils to scavenge free radicals and prevent oxidative rancidity.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): ____ is the acid ingredient and _____ the alkaline ingredient used as components of leavening: *
Rationale: Chemical leavening systems rely on an acid component (cream of tartar / potassium bitartrate) reacting with an alkaline component (baking soda / sodium bicarbonate) in the presence of moisture to release carbon dioxide gas.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The emulsifying agent present in egg yolk: *
Rationale:
Lecithin is a natural phospholipid found abundantly in egg yolk that acts as a powerful emulsifying agent, stabilizing oil-in-water emulsions like mayonnaise.

• Fat: General lipid class, not the specific emulsifier.
• Albumin: Major egg white protein, not the primary yolk emulsifier.
• Avidin: Egg white protein that binds biotin.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The protein in milk which does not form a curd: *
Rationale:
Whey is the liquid fraction of milk containing soluble proteins (such as lactalbumin and lactoglobulin) that remain dissolved and do not form a coagulated curd during acid or rennet precipitation.

• Casein: The primary milk protein that precipitates to form curds.
• Albumin / Ovalbumin: Egg proteins.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Poultry products are a likely source of infection by: *
Rationale:
Poultry products and eggs are well-documented primary vehicles for Salmonella species infections.

• Staphylococcus aureus: Commonly associated with food handlers and protein-rich foods handled manually.
• Vibrio cholerae: Associated with contaminated water and raw seafood/shellfish.
• Clostridium perfringens: Associated with improperly cooled meats and gravies.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Plasmodium, the causative agent for Malaria, is classified as a/an: *
Rationale: Plasmodium species (the protozoan parasites responsible for causing malaria) belong to the phylum Apicomplexa, classified under sporozoa (protozoa characterized by spore-forming life cycle stages).

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A type of illness that arises from a chemical hazard: *
Rationale:
Monosodium glutamate (MSG) poisoning (or "Chinese Restaurant Syndrome") is a classic adverse reaction arising from a chemical food additive (chemical hazard).

• Trichinosis / Shigellosis: Biological hazards caused by parasitic worms and bacteria.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A technique used as a pre-treatment of fruits and vegetables to deactivate enzymes early in the preparation stages for processing is: *
Rationale: Blanching is a thermal pre-treatment where fruits or vegetables are briefly immersed in boiling water or steam to inactivate polyphenol oxidase and other spoilage enzymes prior to freezing, canning, or drying.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): During frozen storage, what causes cell membranes to rupture? *
Rationale: During slow or fluctuating frozen storage, water molecules form large ice crystals that puncture delicate cellular walls and membranes, causing cell collapse and textural softening upon thawing.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A Philippine vegetable dish containing a wide assortment of vegetables, shrimps, pork, and sotanghon. *
Rationale:
Laksa is a savory noodle soup dish featuring a rich broth, a variety of vegetables, shrimp, pork, and vermicelli/sotanghon noodles.

• Pinakbet / Dinengdeng / Laing: Traditional indigenous Filipino vegetable dishes without sotanghon and shrimp/pork noodle soup combinations.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A phenolic substance responsible for enzymatic browning in fruits and vegetables: *
Rationale:
Polyphenol oxidase (often referred to historically in culinary contexts as cathecolase or tyrosinase) is the copper-containing enzyme responsible for catalyzing enzymatic browning reactions in cut fruits and vegetables.

• Bromelin: A proteolytic enzyme found in pineapples.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): It is considered a stiff dough: *
Rationale:

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Excessive baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) used alone without sufficient acid leaves an unpleasant soapy, bitter, alkaline taste and imparts a yellowish chemical discoloration in baked goods.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Cooking an egg transforms liquid egg proteins from a fluid sol state into a firm, set gel/solid state via heat-induced protein denaturation and coagulation.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale:
A hedonic scale (ranging from "extremely like" to "extremely dislike") is the standard subjective sensory evaluation tool used to measure consumers' degree of liking for food products.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Sensory difference tests determine whether discernible differences exist between food samples; paired comparison tests (b) and triangle tests (c) are standard difference methods. Paired preference tests measure subjective liking, not difference.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): At the freezing point and below it, microorganisms become dormant because: *
Rationale: At freezing temperatures and below, microorganisms are rendered dormant because available free water is locked up as ice (lack of available moisture) and cellular enzymatic metabolic rates are drastically retarded.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Blanching green vegetables expels microscopic pockets of trapped air surrounding plant tissues, allowing light to reflect uniformly and intensifying the vivid green chlorophyll color.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The ideal internal temperature of a well-done pork: *
Rationale: According to culinary and food safety safety standards, pork must be cooked to an internal temperature of at least 77°C (170°F) to ensure doneness and pathogen destruction.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Chocolate ice cream contains cocoa butter, milk solids, and stabilizers that provide a rich, stable emulsion structure, allowing it to maintain its texture and store better against freezer crystallization compared to lighter fruit flavors.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): All are vegetables except: *
Rationale: Botanically and culinary, potatoes are classified as starchy tubers, whereas carrots (roots), garlic (bulbs), and onions (bulbs) are classified under vegetable classifications.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale:
Spot-checking finished products is a verification or quality control activity, whereas Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) is a preventive management system built on 7 core principles: hazard analysis, critical control points (CCPs), critical limits, monitoring procedures, corrective actions, verification procedures, and record-keeping.

• Establish corrective actions: Principle 5 of HACCP.
• Establish critical limits: Principle 3 of HACCP.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A system of regular, scheduled inspection and service of equipment which may break, wear out, or become impaired is: *
Rationale:
Preventive maintenance is a scheduled system of routine inspections and servicing designed to prevent equipment breakdowns, wear, and operational impairment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): The floor and wall material recommended for use in storerooms, receiving areas, and laundry areas: *
Rationale:
Concrete floors and walls provide durable, non-absorbent, and easily scrubbable surfaces ideal for high-traffic or heavy-load areas like storerooms, receiving docks, and laundry facilities.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

A steam generator is an integral, built-in functional component of commercial dishwashing machines used to supply high-temperature sanitizing rinse water.

• Kawa / Broiler / Steam-jacketed kettle: Cooking or boiling vessels, not dishwashing components.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Food storage sanitation standards mandate that storage shelves must be placed at least 6 inches off the floor and maintain a minimum clearance of 3 inches away from walls to ensure adequate air circulation and pest inspection access.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: Socialization is the onboarding and orientation process designed to integrate new employees into the company's organizational culture, norms, and operational values.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A trend in foodservice whose aim is to expand operations of a particular concept. *
Rationale: Franchising is a business model and foodservice trend designed to rapidly expand operations of a established brand concept through independent operators.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A concept in manpower utilization that enables one to maximize effort of employees: *
Rationale:
Multi-tasking in manpower utilization cross-trains employees to perform multiple varied tasks, enabling management to maximize employee effort and operational efficiency.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A concept in foodservice with the aim of ensuring quality in all aspects of an operation. *
Rationale: A Quality Improvement Program (QIP) is a structured operational concept specifically aimed at ensuring continuous quality across all operational aspects of a foodservice facility.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A concept that refers to the systematic comparison of a company’s product or operation against that of the best company with a similar operation. *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A food concept that is a combination of Oriental and Western cuisine. *
Rationale:
Fusion cuisine combines distinct culinary traditions, cooking techniques, and flavor profiles from different cultures (such as Oriental and Western cuisine) into novel hybrid dishes.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A food concept whose final product reflects the individual characteristics of its component cuisines. *
Rationale: An eclectic food concept features menu items from diverse origins where each final dish reflects the distinct, recognizable individual characteristics of its component cuisines.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This foodservice system requires the least number of equipment and personnel. *
Rationale:
An assembly-serve foodservice system (convenience-food system) requires the absolute least amount of specialized production equipment and kitchen personnel because foods are purchased fully prepared and only require thawing, heating, or portioning.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): Storage area appropriate for hydrogenated fat. *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale:

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale: A standardized volumetric ladle is the ideal portion control tool used for liquid or semi-fluid items like cheese sauces, gravies, and soups.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): A type of door recommended to be installed in dry storage areas. *

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Rationale:
Off-premise catering involves a caterer transporting food, facilities, equipment, and service staff to a customer's chosen outside venue.

• On-premise catering: Conducted within the caterer's permanent banquet hall or establishment.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): This section of the food preparation area is also known as the range section: *
Rationale:
The hot food preparation station in a kitchen layout—where ranges, broilers, and ovens are housed—is commonly referred to as the range section or hot food preparation area.

• Garde manger: Cold food and salad preparation station.

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)

Deck Title: CHNI - Mockboards3 Foods & Foods Service System (FFSS)
Question (Front): If the cost of a whole cake is P500, having a yield of 10 slices and selling price is P90 per slice, what is the food cost percentage? *
Rationale:
To calculate food cost percentage:

Total cost of the cake = P500. Yield = 10 slices. Cost per slice = P500 ÷ 10 = P50.

Selling price per slice = P90.

Food cost percentage = (Cost per slice ÷ Selling price per slice) × 100 = (P50 ÷ P90) × 100 = 55.56%.

A type of dispersion consisting of two immiscible liquids is called an emulsion. In an emulsion, one liquid is dispersed in the form of small droplets throughout another liquid. Common examples include oil-in-water (O/W) and water-in-oil (W/O) emulsions, where the two liquids do not mix completely but are stabilized with the help of emulsifiers to prevent separation.

• Gel: a semi-solid system where a network of polymer chains forms a three-dimensional structure, trapping a liquid within it. Examples include gelatin desserts and certain types of cheese.
• Foam: a collection of gas bubbles dispersed in a liquid or solid. Examples include whipped cream (air in cream) and mousse.
• Suspension: mixture in which solid particles are dispersed in a liquid but not dissolved. The particles in a suspension are typically larger and can settle over time. Examples include salad dressings and some types of sauces.

Rationale:
The emulsifying agent in egg yolk is lecithin. Lecithin is a phospholipid present in egg yolk that helps stabilize emulsions by reducing the surface tension between immiscible liquids, such as oil and water. It allows for the formation and maintenance of a stable emulsion, such as in mayonnaise or hollandaise sauce, where oil and water are combined into a smooth, creamy mixture.

• Ovomucin: This is a glycoprotein found in egg whites. It contributes to the gel-like consistency of egg whites and has properties that help stabilize foams. It also plays a role in the structural integrity of the egg white.
• Albumin: Albumin is a major protein found in egg whites (also known as egg albumen) and is responsible for the egg white’s ability to form foams and stabilize mixtures. It also helps in binding and thickening in various food preparations.
• Lysozyme: Lysozyme is an enzyme found in egg whites and other bodily fluids. It has antimicrobial properties and can break down bacterial cell walls, contributing to the preservation and safety of the egg.

Question (Front): A potential carcinogen on charcoal-broiled meat is
Rationale:
The potential carcinogen formed on charcoal-broiled meat is benzopyrene. Benzopyrene is a type of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) that forms when meat, especially fatty meat, is cooked at high temperatures such as grilling or broiling over charcoal or open flame. PAHs like benzopyrene are known to be carcinogenic and can pose health risks when consumed in significant quantities over time.

• Aflatoxin is a different type of carcinogen produced by certain molds on food, particularly nuts and grains, under certain conditions.
• Nitrosamines can form in certain preserved or processed meats, but they are not specifically associated with charcoal-broiled meats. Therefore, the correct answer to the question is benzopyrene.

Question (Front): When moisture removal is achieved by utilizing a chamber where heat and humidity are controlled, the process is known as:
Rationale:
Dehydration involves removing moisture from food products using controlled conditions of temperature and humidity. This process helps to preserve the food by inhibiting the growth of microorganisms that require moisture to thrive.

• Freeze-drying is a different preservation method that involves freezing the food and then subjecting it to a vacuum to remove ice crystals directly as vapor (sublimation). 
• Sun-drying involves drying food products using the heat of the sun, while candying involves preserving fruit or peel by coating it with sugar syrup.

Therefore, the correct term for controlled moisture removal in a chamber is dehydration.

Question (Front): Which of the following is not one of the interlocking and interrelated roles of managers?
Rationale:

• Informational roles: Roles that involve receiving, collecting, and disseminating information, including monitor, disseminator, and spokesperson roles.
• Decisional roles: Roles that involve making decisions to solve problems or take advantage of opportunities, including entrepreneur, disturbance handler, resource allocator, and negotiator roles.

“Organizational” does not fit into any of these categories directly as described by Mintzberg. Therefore, Organizational is not one of the interlocking and interrelated roles of managers according to this framework.

Question (Front): Ropiness refers particularly to spoilage of bread characterized by:
Answer (Back): formation of viscous, sticky material like slime
Rationale:
Ropiness refers particularly to spoilage of bread characterized by the formation of a viscous, sticky material like slime. This condition occurs due to microbial activity, typically from certain bacteria, Bacillus subtilis, that produce polysaccharides or exopolysaccharides that give the bread a slimy or rope-like texture. It is considered a form of spoilage that renders the bread unappealing and potentially unsafe to consume.

• Retrogradation: This is the process where starch molecules, particularly amylose and amylopectin, re-associate and crystallize after gelatinization, leading to the firming of bread over time. It’s one of the main causes of bread staling, making the bread crumb harder and less palatable.
• Staling: This refers to the overall process of bread becoming stale, which includes retrogradation, moisture loss, and changes in texture. Staling makes bread crumb dry, crumbly, and less flavorful.
• Drying: This occurs as bread loses moisture over time, contributing to the staling process. The bread becomes harder and less soft, affecting its texture and palatability.

Question (Front): Burong Talangka is an example of:
Rationale:
Burong Talangka is a Filipino delicacy made from fermented rice and field crabs (talangka). The fermentation process involves the natural breakdown of carbohydrates by microorganisms (often lactic acid bacteria) present in the rice, which produces acids that help preserve and flavor the crab meat. This fermentation process gives Burong Talangka its distinctive tangy and salty flavor.

While pickled and salted products also undergo preservation processes, Burong Talangka specifically relies on fermentation to achieve its characteristic taste and texture. Therefore, the correct answer is fermented product.

• Pickling vs. Fermentation: Pickling typically involves immersing food in an acidic solution (like vinegar) to preserve it, which is different from the natural fermentation process that occurs in Burong Talangka. While pickling can also involve brine (saltwater), it does not involve the same microbial activity that defines fermentation.
• Salted Product: While salt is a key ingredient in Burong Talangka, the product is not merely salted; the primary preservation and flavor development come from fermentation, not just the salting process.

Question (Front): Addition of salt or sugar to a liquid will affect its boiling point by:
Rationale:
When a non-volatile solute (such as salt or sugar) is dissolved in a solvent (such as water), it disrupts the formation of solvent molecules at the surface, which are responsible for vapor pressure and boiling.

The presence of the solute lowers the vapor pressure of the solvent. According to Raoult’s Law, the boiling point of a solution is higher than that of the pure solvent, depending on the concentration of the solute.

Therefore, adding salt or sugar to a liquid (such as water) will increase its boiling point compared to pure water.
Option 3: increase and then decrease boiling point

Question (Front): Produced by fermentation involving lactic acid bacteria.
Rationale:
Yogurt is made by fermenting milk with lactic acid bacteria, such as Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus, which convert lactose (milk sugar) into lactic acid, giving yogurt its tangy flavor.

• Vinegar: Produced by the fermentation of ethanol (alcohol) into acetic acid by acetic acid bacteria, not lactic acid bacteria.
• Coffee: Not produced by lactic acid fermentation. While some lactic acid bacteria may be involved during the fermentation process of coffee beans, the final product is not a result of lactic acid fermentation.
• Beer: Produced by the fermentation of sugars by yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) into alcohol and carbon dioxide. Lactic acid bacteria are not typically involved in the main fermentation process, although they can be involved in sour beers.

Rationale:
Bread flour is high in protein, usually around 12-14%. The higher protein content contributes to gluten formation, which gives bread its structure and elasticity.

Question (Front): Hygroscopicity is property associated with:
Rationale:
Hygroscopicity refers to the ability of a substance to absorb moisture from the air. Sugars, such as sucrose, glucose, and fructose, are known to be hygroscopic, meaning they readily attract and hold water molecules from their surroundings. This property can affect the texture and stability of foods, especially in baked goods and confections.

Water itself is not hygroscopic since it is the substance that other materials absorb. Oils are generally non-hygroscopic.

Question (Front): Known as the most heat resistant spore-former found in food.
Rationale:
Clostridium botulinum is a bacterium that forms highly resistant spores capable of surviving harsh conditions, including heat. These spores can withstand temperatures higher than those that typically kill other bacteria. This resilience is a concern in food safety because if foods contaminated with Clostridium botulinum spores are improperly prepared or stored, conditions may allow the spores to germinate and produce botulinum toxin, which can cause severe foodborne illness (botulism) if ingested.

In canned foods, if the canning process does not achieve high enough temperatures or if there is a failure to seal the cans properly, C. botulinum spores can survive. Under these conditions, the spores can germinate and produce the toxin, which can cause botulism, a rare but serious illness characterized by symptoms like muscle weakness, difficulty swallowing, and respiratory issues. Proper canning techniques, including adequate heating and ensuring an airtight seal, are critical to preventing botulism.

Question (Front): Black discoloration in canned products may be caused by:
Rationale:

• Iron sulfide formation: Reaction between iron in the can and sulfur compounds in the food can lead to black or dark discoloration.
• Hard water containing minerals: The minerals in hard water can interact with the food and contribute to color changes, including black discoloration.

Question (Front): Basis of pasteurization time and temperature.
Rationale: Pasteurization is primarily designed to ensure the destruction of Coxiella burnetii, the most heat-resistant pathogen found in milk. This bacterium is more resistant to heat compared to other pathogens like Escherichia coli and Salmonella, making it a key target for pasteurization processes. Effective pasteurization parameters are established to ensure the safety of milk and dairy products by targeting this particularly resilient microorganism.

Question (Front): It is a psychrotrophic foodborne pathogen.
Rationale:
Listeria monocytogenes is a bacterium that can grow and thrive at refrigeration temperatures (psychrotrophic conditions), making it a significant concern in food safety. It can cause listeriosis, a serious illness primarily affecting pregnant women, newborns, elderly individuals, and those with weakened immune systems. Listeria monocytogenes is often associated with ready-to-eat foods such as deli meats, soft cheeses, and smoked seafood.

Question (Front): The pH of chili garlic is 6.0, therefore it is considered as:
Rationale:
According to food safety and regulatory guidelines (such as the FDA), foods are classified based on a critical pH threshold of 4.6:

• Low-acid food: Any food with a finished equilibrium pH greater than 4.6 and a water activity greater than 0.85. Because the chili garlic has a pH of 6.0 (which is above 4.6), it falls squarely into this category.
• Acid food: Foods that naturally have a pH of 4.6 or below.
• Acidified food: Low-acid foods to which acid(s) or acid food(s) are manually added to deliberately reduce the final equilibrium pH to 4.6 or below.

Because unacidified low-acid environments with a pH of 6.0 can support the growth of dangerous spores like Clostridium botulinum (botulism), commercial or shelf-stable chili garlic typically undergoes acidification to bring its pH down safely.

Question (Front): It refers to the behaviors that can lead to good health and improve cleanliness.
Rationale: Hygiene encompasses practices and behaviors that promote health and cleanliness, such as handwashing, personal grooming, maintaining clean environments, and following proper food handling practices. It is essential for preventing the spread of diseases and maintaining overall well-being.

Question (Front): Among the advantages of this food service system are the savings from large volume purchasing, reduced labor duplications, and effective quality control from having only one kitchen that deliver to satellite units.
Rationale:
In a Commissary system, food production is centralized in one main kitchen (commissary) where bulk food preparation and cooking take place. The prepared food is then distributed to satellite units or service points where it is served to customers. This centralized approach allows for efficient purchasing in bulk, reduces duplication of labor (since not every satellite unit needs its own full kitchen), and enables better quality control because all food production is managed centrally.

• Conventional System:
Description: In the conventional food service system, food is prepared, cooked, and served at the same location. It involves on-site preparation and serving, with all food being made fresh daily.
Advantages: Flexibility in menu changes, control over the preparation process, and immediate serving of freshly cooked food.

• Ready Prepared System:
Description: Also known as the cook-chill or cook-freeze system, this involves preparing and cooking food in advance, then chilling or freezing it for later reheating and serving.
Advantages: Efficiency in labor and time, reduced peak-hour pressures, and extended service hours with consistent food quality.

• Assembly/Serve System:
Description: This system involves assembling pre-prepared food items into final meals at the service site. The food is usually purchased fully prepared and only needs to be heated or assembled before serving.
Advantages: Minimal on-site labor required, consistency in food quality, and reduced need for complex food preparation equipment.
Each system has its own set of advantages tailored to different operational needs and goals.

Question (Front): This leadership theory sets an assumption that employees have an inherent dislike of work and will avoid it if possible.
Rationale:
Theory X is part of Douglas McGregor’s Theory of Motivation and Management, which suggests that employees are inherently lazy and dislike work. According to Theory X, employees need to be closely supervised and controlled to ensure they work effectively.

• Scientific Approach: This approach, developed by Frederick Taylor, focuses on improving work efficiency through scientific methods, such as time studies and work specialization. It emphasizes optimizing tasks and productivity rather than assumptions about employee motivation.
• Human Relations Approach: This approach highlights the importance of employee morale and interpersonal relationships in improving productivity. It emerged from studies such as the Hawthorne Studies and emphasizes the psychological and social aspects of work.
• Theory Y: Proposed by Douglas McGregor, Theory Y is the counterpart to Theory X. It assumes that employees are self-motivated, enjoy work, and seek responsibility. This theory suggests that workers are motivated by intrinsic factors and can be creative and productive if given the right environment.

Question (Front): An inventory system where stocks are maintained at a certain level each time an order regardless of the amount on hand and the of order.
Rationale:
In a par stock system, inventory is maintained at a predetermined level (par stock) regardless of current inventory levels. When the stock reaches or falls below this set level, an order is placed to replenish it back to the par level. This system focuses on keeping inventory consistently at the desired level to ensure smooth operations.

In a Par stock system:

A predetermined minimum quantity (the par level) of each item is maintained in stock. Whenever the inventory level drops to the par level due to sales or usage, a replenishment order is placed. The order quantity is typically fixed and does not depend on the current inventory level.

This system helps in maintaining consistent stock levels and ensures that inventory is replenished promptly when it reaches the par level.

FIFO (First-In, First-Out):
Description: An inventory management method where the oldest stock (first-in) is sold or used first before newer stock (last-in). This approach helps prevent inventory from becoming obsolete and is often used for perishable goods.

Buffer System:
Description: Also known as a safety stock system, this approach involves maintaining an additional quantity of stock (buffer or safety stock) to protect against variations in demand or supply delays. It ensures that there is always a reserve to cover unexpected changes.

Question (Front): In resource conservation, this term applies to the consideration of the design and manufacture of products and packaging with minimum toxic content and volume of material and its longevity.
Rationale: Source reduction focuses on reducing the amount of waste generated at the source by designing products that use less material, are less toxic, and have longer lifespans. It aims to prevent waste before it is created.

Rationale: Food production involves the actual preparation and assembly of ingredients and materials to create finished dishes or food items that are ready to be served to customers. Question (Front):
Sentence A. In traditional ice cream making, salt is added to ice in the “garapinyera” during the freezing of ice cream mixture.
Sentence B. The addition of salt to ice prevents the melting of ice, thus ensuring quick freezing.
Rationale:
Sentence A is correct. In traditional ice cream making, particularly in the use of an ice cream maker like the ‘garapinyera,’ salt is added to ice to lower the freezing point of the ice, which helps in freezing the ice cream mixture.

Statement B is incorrect. The addition of salt to ice actually causes the ice to melt at a lower temperature. The process of melting absorbs heat from the surrounding environment (in this case, the ice cream mixture), which helps to freeze the ice cream more quickly. Salt lowers the freezing point of water, which allows the ice to absorb more heat as it melts, leading to a more effective freezing process.

When you add salt to ice, it lowers the freezing point of the water (a process known as freezing point depression). Normally, ice melts and freezes at 0°C (32°F), but when salt is added, the melting point drops below this temperature. As a result, the ice melts because the surrounding temperature is above the new, lower freezing point.

However, as the ice melts, it absorbs heat from its surroundings (an endothermic process), which creates a colder environment. This is why the salted ice can freeze the ice cream mixture faster, even though it actually causes the ice to melt more quickly.

Question (Front):

Sentence B. Rigor mortis is the stiffening of muscle.

“During rigor mortis, actomyosin dissociates to actin and myosin resulting in tough meat.”

This statement is incorrect. During rigor mortis, actomyosin, a complex formed by actin and myosin, is what actually causes muscle stiffening. The dissociation of actomyosin into actin and myosin happens after rigor mortis, during the resolution phase when the muscle starts to soften again.

“Rigor mortis is the stiffening of muscle.”

This statement is correct. Rigor mortis is the post-mortem stiffening of muscles due to chemical changes in the muscle fibers, primarily the formation of actomyosin as ATP is depleted.
