According to the official National Nutrition Council (NNC) Guidelines, the Governing Board is the highest policy-making body on nutrition in the Philippines. It is composed of 10 national government agencies and three representatives from the private sector:

1. Department of Health (DOH) – Chairperson
2. Department of Agriculture (DA) – Vice-Chairperson
3. Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG) – Vice-Chairperson
4. Department of Budget and Management (DBM)
5. Department of Education (DepEd)
6. Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE)
7. Department of Science and Technology (DOST)
8. Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)
9. Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
10. National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA)

Question (Front): Who is the first director of the National Nutrition Council?
Rationale: Dr. Florentino S. Solon, widely regarded as the "Father of Nutrition" in the Philippines, served as the first Executive Director of the National Nutrition Council beginning in 1974, and concurrently founded the Nutrition Center of the Philippines the same year (NNC, 2025).

Question (Front): The nutrient that is considered most difficult to meet during pregnancy:
Rationale:
Iron requirements roughly double during pregnancy to support the expansion of maternal blood volume, fetal and placental growth, and stores for the newborn, and this increased demand is very difficult to meet through diet alone, which is why iron-folic acid supplementation is routinely recommended for pregnant women (WHO, 2001). 

Among the macro- and micronutrients needed in pregnancy, iron is consistently identified as the nutrient hardest to obtain in adequate amounts from food sources alone.

Question (Front): It is a statement of general thrust of the organization.
Rationale: A mission statement articulates an organization's general thrust or overarching purpose, why it exists and what it broadly seeks to accomplish, distinct from a vision (the aspirational future state it seeks to achieve), a goal (a broad long-term aim derived from the mission), and an objective (a specific, measurable, time-bound target that operationalizes a goal).

Question (Front): The national government agency that makes sure that nutrition concerns are integrated in both national and sub-national development plans.
Rationale: The Department of Economy, Planning, and Development (DEPDev) created under Republic Act No. 12145 through the reorganization of the former National Economic and Development Authority (NEDA) serves as the primary planning agency responsible for issuing and integrating nutrition and other socioeconomic concerns into the Philippine Development Plan, Regional Development Plans, and related national and sub-national planning instruments (DEPDev, 2025).

Question (Front): A level of health care facilities which includes rural health units, chest clinics, and malaria eradication units.
Rationale:
Primary level health care facilities serve as the first point of contact between community members and the formal healthcare system. According to the Department of Health (DOH) structural framework, this level manages simple, routine, and specialized community-wide preventive and promotive health programs.

It encompasses:
• Rural Health Units (RHUs) and Barangay Health Stations (BHS)
• Chest clinics (for tuberculosis management and screening)
• Malaria eradication units and other specialized disease surveillance outposts
• Private medical clinics and community health centers

• Tertiary level: Consists of highly specialized national or regional medical centers and teaching hospitals equipped with advanced diagnostic and treatment facilities (e.g., specialized surgeries, intensive care units).
• Secondary level: Consists of smaller, departmentalized hospitals (such as district, provincial, or municipal hospitals) capable of providing basic surgical, pediatric, obstetric, and medical treatments that require hospitalization but not highly specialized equipment.

Question (Front): This measures how fast people are added to the population through births.
Rationale: The crude birth rate, computed as the number of live births per 1,000 population in a given year, measures the overall rate at which a population is being added to through births, without adjusting for age or sex structure. Fertility rate measures births relative to women of reproductive age, and crude birth rate the broader population-growth-through-births indicator being described.

Question (Front): What is the acceptable Minimum Diet Diversity?
Rationale:
According to the updated World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF guidelines (which are officially utilized by the Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) and the Department of Science and Technology - Food and Nutrition Research Institute (DOST-FNRI) for reporting), Minimum Dietary Diversity (MDD) for infants and young children aged 6–23 months is defined as consuming items from at least 5 out of 8 defined food groups.

The indicator was updated globally to include breast milk as its own distinct eighth group to eliminate measurement disparities between breastfed and non-breastfed children.

The 8 defined food groups are:
1. Breast milk
2. Grains, white/pale starchy roots, tubers, and plantains
3. Legumes (pulses) and nuts
4. Dairy products (milk, infant formula, yogurt, cheese)
5. Flesh foods (meat, fish, poultry, and organ meats)
6. Eggs
7. Vitamin A-rich fruits and vegetables
8. Other fruits and vegetables

Question (Front): Which agency leads the implementation of HAPAG (Halina't Magtanim ng Prutas at Gulay)?
Rationale:
The HAPAG (Halina't Magtanim ng Prutas at Gulay) sa Barangay Project is a community-based agriculture initiative spearheaded and implemented by the DILG pursuant to DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2023-001.

While it is heavily supported by the Department of Agriculture (DA) as a key technical partner supplying seeds, tools, and agricultural training, the DILG serves as the primary leading agency tasked with mandating and overseeing barangays nationwide in establishing their communal food gardens.

Question (Front): Which of the following questions are not answered by monitoring?
Answer (Back): Were the intervention strategies appropriate to the target population?
Rationale:
Monitoring tracks what is happening (activities, inputs, participation numbers). It cannot tell you if the fundamental design or strategy of the intervention was inherently appropriate for that specific cultural or demographic group in the first place. Assessing whether a strategy is "appropriate" is a qualitative judgment that belongs strictly to formative evaluation or process evaluation.

	• Needs met: In basic operational monitoring (like supply-chain or emergency relief monitoring), managers constantly track target outputs to see if immediate operational needs (e.g., "Did everyone get their ration?") are being met.
	• Appropriate for the problem: Operational monitoring can flag immediate mismatches between a program's activities and the problem on the ground (e.g., if a program provides food but the actual problem is a water shortage, monitoring will immediately show zero uptake).
	• Stakeholder participation: This is a textbook monitoring metric (tracking attendance and engagement levels).
Option 2: Were the intervention strategies appropriate to the target population?
Option 3: What is the level of participation of various stakeholders?
Option 4: Was the program appropriate for the problem identified?

Question (Front): How many micronutrients are included in the micronutrient powder?
Rationale: The multiple micronutrient powder (MNP) formulation used in the Philippines and recommended for home fortification of complementary foods for children 6–23 months contains 15 essential vitamins and minerals, including iron, zinc, vitamin A, and iodine, in a single daily sachet (Department of Health, n.d.).

Question (Front): Which theory explains aging as the result of chemical and mechanical exhaustion of the cells?
Rationale:
The Wear-and-Tear Theory (first proposed by Dr. August Weismann in 1882) compares the human body to a machine. It posits that aging is the direct result of continuous use, where cells, tissues, and vital body parts accumulate chronic chemical and mechanical exhaustion over time from internal or external stressors. Once the damage exceeds the body's natural capacity to repair itself, overall biological function progressively declines.

• Clinker Theory: Focuses on the accumulation of metabolic waste products and chemical byproducts within normal cells, combining elements of mutation and cross-linking.
• Free Radicals Theory: Specifically attributes cellular aging and damage to the destructive nature of unstable, highly reactive molecules with unpaired electrons produced during normal oxygen metabolism.
• Generalized Errors Theory: Argues that aging occurs due to random, progressive transcription or translation mistakes during ribonucleic acid (RNA) and protein synthesis, resulting in faulty cellular structures.

Question (Front): A study will be conducted to test the effects on the fat content of fried chicken using two different frying techniques. What is the appropriate research design to use?
Rationale:
Because the researcher actively manipulates an independent variable (the frying technique) under controlled conditions to measure its effect on a dependent variable (fat content), this is a true experimental design. 

Correlational and observational designs, by contrast, examine naturally occurring relationships or exposures without researcher-controlled manipulation, and a descriptive survey merely characterizes existing conditions without testing a causal intervention.

Question (Front): Ryzza Mae is lactose intolerant. Which Starbucks order is not appropriate to be given to her?
Rationale: Oatmilk Cocoa Frappuccino typically contains standard dairy-based chocolate chips/sauce and whipped cream unless requested non-dairy. In individuals with lactose intolerance, consuming dairy solids or milk fat triggers gastrointestinal symptoms.

Question (Front): Based on the latest NNS results, what is the trend of wasting in adolescents?
What is the name of this campaign character of the 10 Kumainments introduced by the NNC?
Rationale: The National Nutrition Council (NNC) introduced Mang Moi (also known as Moises "Mang Moi" Dalisay) as the official campaign character and mascot patterned after the biblical Moses. He serves as the friendly messenger who carries the "10 Kumainments," which are simplified, easy-to-remember nutritional guidelines aimed at helping Filipinos practice healthier eating habits and live active lifestyles.

Question (Front): This award is given to a province, city, or municipality that has shown outstanding nutrition implementation for three consecutive years.
Rationale:
The Green Banner Award (or Green Banner Seal of Compliance) is given by the NNC to a city, municipality, or province that demonstrates very satisfactory performance in implementing its local nutrition action plan for a given year. 

An LGU that wins the Green Banner for three consecutive years becomes eligible for the higher Consistent Regional Outstanding Winner in Nutrition (CROWN) award, and sustained performance beyond that can lead to the Nutrition Honor Award, the highest distinction the NNC gives to an LGU.

Question (Front): What is the law that stipulates the provision of allowances and incentives to Barangay Health Workers (BHW)?
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 7883, the "Barangay Health Workers' Benefits and Incentives Act of 1995," grants accredited barangay health workers benefits such as hazard allowance, subsistence allowance, and other incentives in recognition of their voluntary community health services (Republic Act No. 7883, 1995). 

• RA 7875: National Health Insurance Act 
• RA 7305: Magna Carta of Public Health Workers 
• RA 7160 is the Local Government Code

Question (Front): An innovation made by former president FE Marcos with the proclamation of Martial Law, serving to arrogate unto the Chief Executive the lawmaking powers of congress. In the Freedom Constitution of 1986, former president Corazon Aquino recognized its validity unless otherwise repealed.
Rationale:
Presidential Decrees (PDs) were issuances with the force of law used by former President Ferdinand E. Marcos to exercise the legislative powers of Congress during Martial Law, when the regular legislature was effectively supplanted. 

Under the 1986 Freedom Constitution, President Corazon Aquino recognized existing Presidential Decrees, such as PD No. 1569 establishing the Barangay Nutrition Scholar Program, as remaining valid unless subsequently amended or repealed.

Question (Front): What is also known as the "sickness of the older child when the next child is born"?
Rationale: The term "kwashiorkor" originates from the Ga language of Ghana and translates roughly to "the sickness of the older child when the next child is born," describing the protein-energy malnutrition that develops in a toddler abruptly weaned from breastmilk after the birth of a younger sibling and shifted to a low-protein, starchy diet.

Question (Front): Computed as the annual number of deaths between 28 days and 1 year divided by the number of live births per year
Rationale:
The post-neonatal mortality rate specifically measures deaths occurring between 28 days and 1 year of age per number of live births in a year.

• Infant mortality rate: Annual number of deaths in the first year (0–12 months) 
• Neonatal mortality rate: Annual number of deaths within the first 28 days 
• Perinatal mortality rate: Annual number of stillbirths and deaths in the first 7 days

Question (Front): Having a sense of truthfulness and reliability with regard to the performance of roles and functions
Rationale: Integrity is the value that describes a person's consistent truthfulness, honesty, and reliability in carrying out their duties and responsibilities. It is distinguished from accountability (being answerable for outcomes and decisions), transparency (openness of processes to scrutiny), and efficiency (achieving results with minimal waste of resources). These are recognized as related but distinct standards of good governance and public service conduct.

Question (Front): It is a comprehensive and integrated package of services and communication on health, nutrition, and environment for children available everyday in various settings (home, school, health facilities, and communities) by government, NGOs, private sectors, and civic organizations.
Rationale:
Under Department of Health (DOH) Administrative Order No. 36 s. 2010, the Expanded Garantisadong Pambata (GP) Program was redesigned from a biannual institutional campaign into a comprehensive and integrated package of services and communication on health, nutrition, and environment for children available every day in various settings (such as the home, school, health facilities, and communities).

While it is led by the DOH and National Nutrition Council (NNC), it relies heavily on inter-agency and intersectoral cooperation with other government bodies, NGOs, private sectors, and civic organizations to systematically manage child survival interventions.

• Applied Nutrition Program: A historic nutrition initiative in the Philippines launched in the 1960s and 1970s primarily focused on school food production and feeding, which later evolved into broader national nutrition strategies.
• Healthy Settings Approach: A broader WHO health promotion framework that targets structural environments (e.g., Healthy Cities, Healthy Workplaces, Healthy Schools) but is not a package specifically called out by this child-survival definition.
• Promote Good Nutrition Program: A component under the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN) primarily focused on social marketing, behavioral change communication (BCC), and nutrition education regarding infant and young child feeding (IYCF).

Question (Front): Compared with cow's milk, breastmilk contains:
Rationale: Human breastmilk has a substantially lower protein and mineral (ash) content than cow's milk.

Question (Front): A process whereby an individual influences a group of individuals to achieve a common goal and relating with followers and making them change.
Rationale:
Leadership is defined as the process by which one individual influences and guides a group toward the achievement of a shared goal, engaging and motivating followers to adopt new behaviors or directions. 

This is broader than advocacy (influencing policy or decision-makers), mobilization (organizing resources or people for a specific action), or nutrition education (imparting knowledge), though leadership often makes use of all three.

Question (Front): The extended global nutrition target for exclusive breastfeeding rates by 2030.
Rationale:
As of 2024, nearly half (48%) of infants under six months were exclusively breastfed, bringing the world close to the 50% target set for 2025. 

When WHO and UNICEF proposed extending the 2025 Global Nutrition Targets to 2030. By 2030, that target is to increase the rate of exclusive breastfeeding in the first six months up to at least 60%.

Question (Front): The policy also known as the Universal Health Care (UHC) Act, which aims to provide a comprehensive set of quality and cost-effective, promotive, preventive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative health services by fostering a whole-of-system, whole-of-government approach, and whole-of-society approach in development, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation of health policies, programs, and plans.
Rationale: Republic Act No. 11223, the Universal Health Care Act of 2019, institutionalizes automatic health coverage for all Filipinos and mandates a whole-of-system, whole-of-government, and whole-of-society approach to delivering promotive, preventive, curative, rehabilitative, and palliative health services.

Question (Front): Nutrition PPAs are commonly charged against GAD funds in the LGU. How much of the LGU fund is allotted for Gender and Development?
Rationale:
Pursuant to Section 36(a) of Republic Act No. 9710 (the Magna Carta of Women) and the DILG-NEDA-DBM-PCW Joint Memorandum Circular guidelines, all Local Government Units (LGUs) and national government agencies are legally mandated to allocate at least five percent (5%) of their total annual budget appropriations to support Gender and Development (GAD) plans, programs, and activities.

Because public health nutrition interventions (such as supplemental feeding for pregnant women or addressing maternal and child malnutrition) target specific vulnerable gender groups, nutrition Programs, Projects, and Activities (PPAs) are frequently funded or attributed through this mandatory 5% LGU allocation.

Question (Front): A community health program seeks to understand why mothers are not practicing recommended complementary feeding. The assessment examines mothers' knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, available resources, social support, and encouragement from family members and health workers. Which phase of the PRECEDE-PROCEED model is being conducted?
Rationale:
In the PRECEDE-PROCEED model, Phase 3: Educational and Ecological Assessment categorizes the factors that influence a specific health behavior into three distinct groups:
• Predisposing factors: A person's internal knowledge, attitudes, beliefs, values, and perceptions (e.g., mothers' knowledge, attitudes, and beliefs about complementary feeding).
• Enabling factors: The availability, accessibility, and affordability of resources or skills needed to perform the behavior (e.g., available resources).
• Reinforcing factors: The feedback, social support, and encouragement from others that either reward or discourage the behavior (e.g., social support and encouragement from family members and health workers).

• Epidemiological assessment (Phase 2): This phase focuses on identifying the specific health problems, distribution of diseases, and health trends within a population (e.g., statistics on malnutrition or stunting rates).
• Social assessment (Phase 1): This phase evaluates the community's quality of life, subjective concerns, and social problems (e.g., poverty, unemployment, or overall well-being).
• Behavioral and environmental assessment (Phase 2/3 transition): This phase identifies the specific behaviors and external environmental conditions that contribute directly to the health problem (e.g., the actual act of not feeding the child complementary food, or a lack of clean water supply).

Question (Front): This law institutionalized the national poverty reduction strategy of the Philippine government, providing conditional cash transfers to poor and near-poor households to invest in health, nutrition, and education to break the intergenerational cycle of poverty.
Rationale:
Republic Act No. 11310, signed on April 17, 2019, is the 4Ps Act. It legally institutionalized the Pantawid Pamilyang Pilipino Program (4Ps).

It legally institutionalized the 4Ps as the national poverty reduction strategy and human capital investment program of the Philippines, ensuring its long-term continuity and funding through the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD).

The program provides monthly human development grants (conditional cash transfers) focusing explicitly on health, nutrition, and education for qualified poor and near-poor households with children aged 0–18 or pregnant members.

• RA 11130: This is the Charter of the City of Carcar (converted into a component city).
• RA 11210: This is the 105-Day Expanded Maternity Leave Law, which is also highly relevant to public health but covers maternal leave benefits.
• RA 11120: This is the Declaration of a National Shrine or specific regional landmark declarations, unrelated to national poverty interventions.

Question (Front): The DOH package list for emergencies and disasters refer to the following except:
Rationale: The DOH standard nutrition in emergencies (NiE) package for disaster response focuses on nutrition-specific items (micronutrient supplements, weighing and measuring equipment, and processed or ready-to-use foodstuff for supplementary feeding) rather than clothing, which falls under general relief or social welfare provisions handled by other response agencies (DOH, n.d.).

Question (Front): According to the latest NNS results, binge drinking, 58.7% of Filipino adults are binge drinkers. Binge drinking is defined as the excessive consumption of alcoholic beverages, specifically the intake of ___ or more (females) or ____ or more(males) standard drinks in a row by those who reported drinking alcoholic beverages in the past 30 days.
Rationale: The excessive consumption of alcoholic beverages, specifically the intake of four or more (females) or five or more (males) standard drinks in a row by those who reported drinking alcoholic beverages in the past 30 days.

Question (Front): You are training BNS on OPT Plus. What topic should you discuss with them first?
Answer (Back): Role of the BNS, their tasks, and skills needed
Rationale: Standard BNS training protocols begin with orienting new volunteers to their overall role, responsibilities, and the skills they will need, before proceeding to technical tasks such as operating equipment or conducting anthropometric measurement (NNC, n.d.). Establishing this foundational understanding of the BNS's purpose and duties ensures BNS grasp why the technical skills that follow matter within the Operation Timbang Plus (OPT Plus) activity.
Option 1: Role of the BNS, their tasks, and skills needed
Option 2: History of the Philippine Nutrition Program

Question (Front): The minimum monthly income that enables a family of 5 to buy the needed food to meet their nutritional requirements and other non-basic food needs is called:
Rationale: The poverty threshold (or poverty line) is officially defined as the minimum income required by a family or individual to meet their basic food and non-food needs, including the cost of a nutritionally adequate food basket (PSA, n.d.). Families whose income falls below this threshold are classified as poor, making the poverty threshold a key benchmark used in nutrition and socioeconomic planning.

Question (Front):
What are the four components of PIMAM?
I. Community mobilization and outreach
II. Outpatient department
III. Counseling
IV. Outpatient Therapeutic care
V. Home visit
VI. Inpatient Therapeutic care
VII. Supplementary Feeding Program
VIII. Referral
Rationale:
The four components of the Philippine Integrated Management of Acute Malnutrition (PIMAM) are:

1. I. Community mobilization and outreach
2. IV. Outpatient Therapeutic care (OTC)
3. VI. Inpatient Therapeutic care (ITC)
4. VII. Supplementary Feeding Program (SFP) (also known as Targeted Supplementary Feeding Program / Management of MAM)

Question (Front): Maternal death is the death of a woman while pregnant or within ___ days of termination of pregnancy.
Rationale: The WHO defines maternal death as the death of a woman while pregnant, or within 42 days of the termination of pregnancy, from any cause related to or aggravated by the pregnancy or its management, excluding accidental or incidental causes (WHO, 2019).

Question (Front):
Arrange in chronological order the stages in developing a planned behavior change in nutrition education.
I. Recognizing the existence of a problem
II. Attempting or trialing the new behavior
III. Integrating the new behavior into daily routine
IV. Realizing that meaningful change is achievable
Rationale: Planned behavior change typically follows a sequence beginning with the person recognizing that a problem exists (I), followed by recognizing that a change is actually possible for them (IV), then attempting or trialing the new behavior (II), and finally, integrating that behavior as a lasting part of their routine (III) — a progression consistent with staged models of behavior adoption such as the Diffusion of Innovation and Precaution Adoption Process frameworks.

Question (Front): Based on the latest national nutrition survey, which regions in the Philippines have the highest prevalence of overweight and obesity among adults?
Rationale: Compared with the national estimate, the National Capital Region has the highest obesity prevalence with 52.7%, followed by the Cordillera Administrative Region (50.6%) and Central Luzon (49.6%).

Question (Front): Who is this Filipino nutritionist and politician who served as Deputy Minister of Health from 1983 to 1986 during the presidency of Ferdinand Marcos?
Rationale:
Dr. Florentino S. Solon was a highly influential public health physician and nutritionist widely recognized as the country's "champion of nutrition". He served as the first Executive Director of both the National Nutrition Council (NNC) and the Nutrition Center of the Philippines (NCP).

In politics, he was appointed by President Ferdinand Marcos Sr. as the Mayor of Cebu City, serving from 1978 until 1983. He resigned from his mayoral post in 1983 when Marcos appointed him to the national level to serve as the Deputy Minister of Health, a role he held until 1986.

Among his structural legacies in nutrition, he pioneered the establishment of specialized malnutrition wards ("malwards"), nutri-huts, nutri-buses, and early food-fortification initiatives like the iron and vitamin A-fortified pan de sal.

• Dr. Francisco Santos: A pioneer agricultural chemist and nutritionist known for his extensive studies on the nutritional values of local Filipino foods and crops.
• Dr. Coronado Pascual: A major public health figure who served as a Director of the Food and Nutrition Research Center (FNRC) and led early coordination attempts through the National Coordinating Council on Food and Nutrition (NCCFN) in 1959.
• Dr. Juan Salcedo, Jr.: A celebrated National Scientist and former Secretary of Health renowned for leading the historic Bataan Rice Enrichment Project which helped eradicate beriberi in the Philippines.

Question (Front): The ECCD System Act (RA 12199) that strengthens the country's ECCD system to address gaps in healthcare, nutrition, early childhood education, safety, security, and social services for children aged five and below. This law also transferred the ECCD Council under which agency?
Rationale:
Under the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) System Act (Republic Act No. 12199), the ECCD Council was officially attached to the Department of the Interior and Local Government (DILG).

Previously, under the Early Years Act of 2013 (RA 10410), the ECCD Council was attached to the Department of Education (DepEd). The strategic shift to the DILG was made to strengthen local government unit (LGU) accountability and compliance, ensuring that local communal Day Care and Child Development Centers across every barangay are fully funded, maintained, and operational.

Republic Act No. 12199, the Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) System Act signed in May 2025, repealed the earlier Early Years Act of 2013 (RA 10410) and reorganized comprehensive health, nutrition, and early education services for children from conception through age eight, assigning children below five to the ECCD Council and those aged five to eight to the Department of Education (Republic Act No. 12199, 2025).

Question (Front): Sa palabas ng ABS-CBN Foundation na Dok Ricky, Pedia ng Barangay, sino ang gumanap na Dok Riki Bautista na katambal ni Dominic Ochoa?
Rationale: Ang tamang sagot ay Alessandra de Rossi, na gumanap bilang si Dra. Marikina "Dok Riki" Bautista sa "sitcom-mentary" na palabas na Dok Ricky, Pedia ng Barangay.

Question (Front): Si Nash Aguas ay bumida sa anong programang pang-nutrisyon na pinalabas ng ABS-CBN?
Rationale: Ang Why Not? ay isang edu-infotainment at nutritional television show para sa mga bata na ipinalabas sa ABS-CBN Channel 2 at Knowledge Channel noong 2011. Ito ay pinangunahan nina Nash Aguas (bilang si Bot) at Kelly Nakanishi (bilang si Vi) sa pakikipagtulungan ng National Nutrition Council (NNC) at ABS-CBN Lingkod Kapamilya Foundation, Inc. Layunin ng programa na hikayatin ang mga bata na magkaroon ng masusustansyang gawi sa pagkain sa pamamagitan ng mga nakatutuwang kuwento at parodies tungkol sa mga prutas at gulay.

Question (Front): Which is NOT a theme of the Philippine Nutrition Month?
Answer (Back): Bayan at nutrisyon, alagaan natin ngayon
Rationale:
• Malnutrisyon: tuklasin at pugsain (1990)
• Buto at ngipin patibayin, gatas ating inumin (1996)
• Kumain nang RIGHT, para maging batang BRIGHT (2006)
Option 1: Bayan at nutrisyon, alagaan natin ngayon
Option 2: Kumain nang RIGHT, para maging batang BRIGHT
Option 4: Buto at ngipin patibayin, gatas ating inumin

Question (Front): Lactose is composed of:
Rationale:
Lactose is a disaccharide composed of glucose and galactose.

• Glucose and fructose form sucrose, not lactose.
• Fructose and galactose do not form lactose.
• Glucose and sucrose are not the two monosaccharides that make up lactose.

Question (Front): Which type of amino acid must be obtained from the diet because the body cannot synthesize it in sufficient amounts?
Rationale:
Essential amino acids cannot be synthesized by the body in adequate amounts and therefore must be supplied by the diet.

Remember the Essential AAs: PVTTIMHALL Phenylalanine Valine Threonine Tryptophan Isoleucine Methionine Histidine Leucine Lysine

• Non-essential amino acids can generally be synthesized by the body.
• Structural amino acid is not the nutritional classification described in the question.
• Neutral amino acid describes a chemical property rather than the nutritional requirement being tested.

Question (Front): All are biological contaminants except:
Rationale:
Biological contaminants are hazards that come from living organisms or their products:
• Paralytic shellfish poisoning — Biological. It is caused by toxins produced by certain marine microorganisms, particularly dinoflagellates.
• Hepatitis A virus — Biological. Viruses are biological contaminants and can be transmitted through contaminated food or water.
• Aflatoxin from molds — Biological. Aflatoxins are toxins produced by certain molds, particularly Aspergillus species.
• Pesticide residue — Chemical, not biological. Pesticides are chemical substances that can remain on or in food.

Remember:
• Biological = bacteria, viruses, parasites, molds, and their toxins
• Chemical = pesticides, cleaning chemicals, heavy metals, etc.

Question (Front): A triglyceride is composed primarily of:
Answer (Back): One glycerol molecule and three fatty acids
Rationale:
One glycerol plus three fatty acids describes the basic structure of a triglyceride.

• A triglyceride has a glycerol backbone esterified with three fatty acids.
• Triglycerides are lipids, not compounds made from amino acids and glycerol.
• Glucose is not the backbone of a triglyceride.
Option 1: One glycerol molecule and three fatty acids
Option 2: Three glycerol molecules and one fatty acid
Option 3: One glucose molecule and three fatty acids
Option 4: Three amino acids and one glycerol molecule

Question (Front): During dry heating of starch, the formation of shorter-chain products is known as formation of:
Rationale:
Dextrins are shorter-chain products formed when starch is subjected to dry heat.

• Gluten is a protein complex associated with wheat dough, not a starch breakdown product.
• Casein is the principal protein of milk.
• Pectin is a structural polysaccharide found in plant tissues.

Question (Front): Which enzyme is associated with the tenderizing activity of figs?
Rationale:
Ficain is a proteolytic enzyme found in figs and can contribute to meat tenderization.

• Papain is associated with papaya.
• Bromelain is associated with pineapple.
• Lactase hydrolyzes lactose and is not the fig enzyme used for meat tenderizing.

Question (Front): Which type of cooking method is generally most appropriate for a tender cut of meat?
Rationale:
Dry-heat methods are generally appropriate for tender cuts because they do not require prolonged moist cooking.

Tender cuts of meat come from muscles that do the least work (such as the loin or rib areas) and contain very little tough connective tissue (collagen).

Because these cuts are already naturally tender, they do not require prolonged cooking to break down tough fibers. Dry-heat cooking methods—such as grilling, broiling, roasting, sautéing, or pan-frying—cook the meat quickly at high temperatures, preserving its natural juices and preventing it from becoming overcooked and dry.

Question (Front): A nonenzymatic browning reaction associated with sugar undergoing heating; prolonged heating above one hundred sixty (>160) degrees Celsius (three hundred twenty (32) degrees Fahrenheit) resulting in dark brown, highly viscous syrup with distinctive taste and odor.
Rationale:
Caramelization is a type of non-enzymatic browning that involves the thermal decomposition and pyrolysis of sugars alone, completely independent of proteins or amino acids.

Common disaccharides like sucrose (table sugar) and monosaccharides like glucose melt and begin to caramelize rapidly at around 160°C (320°F). Prolonged heating creates complex polymers (caramelans, caramelens, and caramelins) and volatile flavor compounds, transforming clear sugar crystals into a dark, thick, highly aromatic syrup.

• Oxidation is a reaction with oxygen. 
• Maillard Browning is sugar + amino acids, not pure sugar.
• Reduction is the process of simmering or boiling a liquid uncovered so that water evaporates

Question (Front): Cooking an egg primarily causes its proteins to undergo:
Rationale:
Egg proteins denature and then coagulate during cooking, changing the egg from a fluid to a firmer structure.

• Gelatinization is a starch phenomenon involving starch and water under heat.
• Caramelization is a nonenzymatic browning reaction involving sugars.
• Retrogradation refers primarily to reassociation of starch molecules after gelatinization.

Question (Front): Acrolein is associated with:
Rationale:
Acrolein can form when fats are overheated, particularly when glycerol components break down.

• Fermented milk is associated with lactic acid fermentation rather than acrolein formation.
• Gelatinized starch results from starch absorbing water and swelling during heating.
• Fresh fruits are not the food phenomenon described by acrolein formation.

Question (Front): A menu that repeats according to a planned sequence over a specified period is called a:
Rationale:
A cycle menu features a series of menus that repeat in a set pattern (such as weekly, bi-weekly, or monthly) over a designated period.

 This is widely used in institutional settings like schools, hospitals, long-term care facilities, and corporate cafeterias to simplify purchasing, control costs, and maintain dietary variety.

• Du jour menu: A menu "of the day" that changes daily depending on what is fresh or left over.
• Single-use menu: A menu planned and used only once, typically for a special event, holiday banquet, or one-time catered function.
• Static menu: A fixed menu that remains the same every day, commonly found in commercial restaurants.

Question (Front): The soul of every foodservice operation.
Rationale:
In foodservice management, the menu is universally referred to as the "soul," focal point, or primary control of the entire operation.

It dictates everything that happens in the facility—including purchasing, budget, required equipment, staff skill levels, kitchen layout, and guest satisfaction.

Question (Front): Which statement best describes dietary fiber?
Answer (Back): It consists largely of nondigestible carbohydrate components and related substances
Rationale:
Dietary fiber is a broad term for the structural components of plant foods—including polysaccharides like cellulose, hemicellulose, pectins, and non-carbohydrate polymers like lignin.

Unlike sugars and starches, the human digestive system lacks the specific enzymes needed to break down the chemical bonds found in dietary fiber. As a result, it passes through the stomach and small intestine relatively intact.

• It is a form of animal protein: Fiber is exclusively derived from plant foods (fruits, vegetables, grains, legumes, nuts); animal products contain zero dietary fiber.
• It is composed entirely of dietary fat: Fiber belongs to the carbohydrate family of macronutrients, not fats or lipids.
• It is completely digested in the small intestine: Fiber resists enzymatic breakdown in the small intestine completely. Instead, it moves into the large intestine (colon), where it is either partially fermented by beneficial gut bacteria (soluble fiber) or excreted unchanged (insoluble fiber).
Option 1: It is completely digested in the small intestine
Option 2: It consists largely of nondigestible carbohydrate components and related substances
Option 3: It is composed entirely of dietary fat
Option 4: It is a form of animal protein

Question (Front): The desired product of jelly making is generally a:
Rationale:
By culinary and food science standards, a perfect jelly must be a clear, sparkling liquid that has been trapped in a firm, shimmering gel network. It should hold its shape when turned out of a container but remain tender enough to cut or spoon easily.

This specific texture is achieved through the precise chemical balance of three structural elements: pectin (the gelling agent), acid (which prompts the pectin to form a network), and sugar (which bonds with water to assist the pectin).

• Thick emulsion: This describes a mixture of two unmixable liquids, like oil and water (e.g., mayonnaise or hollandaise sauce).
• Foamy suspension: This is a mixture of gas bubbles trapped in a liquid or solid (e.g., whipped cream or meringue). In fact, foam is an undesirable byproduct in jelly making that must be skimmed off during boiling.
• Crystalline sugar mass: This occurs when a jelly fails, and the sugar recrystallizes, resulting in a gritty, grainy texture instead of a smooth gel.

Question (Front): Carotenoid pigments are generally:
Answer (Back): Relatively stable to mild acid compared with chlorophyll
Rationale:
Compared with chlorophyll, carotenoids are relatively stable to mild acid conditions. They contain around 40 carbon backbone, atleast 8 isoprene units.

• Carotenoids are not generally destroyed immediately by mild acid.
• Acid does not convert carotenoids into chlorophyll. These are two completely different structures.
• Chlorophyll, not carotenoids, is primarily responsible for green vegetable color.
Option 1: Relatively stable to mild acid compared with chlorophyll
Option 2: Highly destroyed immediately by mild acid

Question (Front): Which food is a well-known source of lycopene?

Lycopene is a powerful antioxidant and a bright red carotenoid hydrocarbon.

Tomatoes and tomato-based products (like tomato paste, ketchup, and sauces) are the most abundant dietary sources of lycopene. Interestingly, cooking tomatoes and combining them with a little fat (like olive oil) actually increases the bioavailability of lycopene, making it easier for the body to absorb.

Question (Front): Which vitamin is particularly susceptible to losses during food processing?
Rationale:
Vitamin C is highly sensitive to heat, oxygen, and water and is readily lost during some processing methods.

• Vitamin D is generally more stable under ordinary food-processing conditions.
• Vitamin K is not typically identified as the vitamin most susceptible to processing losses in this context.

Question (Front): Chevon refers to meat from:
Rationale:
Chevon is the official culinary term for the meat of an adult goat. It comes from the French word for goat, chèvre.

You may also see young goat meat referred to as cabrito or simply called mutton in certain regions (like India and parts of Asia), though in formal culinary terms, mutton belongs to another animal.

• Sheep meat is commonly called mutton (2-3yo) or lamb 
• Deer meat is commonly called venison.
• Rabbit meat is usually referred to simply as rabbit or lapan (in some culinary contexts).

Question (Front): Which of the following is a recommended minimum internal temperature for cooked seafood?
Rationale:
According to USDA Food Safety and Inspection Service

• All Poultry: 165°F (74°C) for whole birds, breasts, legs, thighs, wings, and ground poultry.
• Stuffing & Casseroles: 165°F (74°C).
• Leftovers: 165°F (74°C) to reheat thoroughly.
• Ground Meats: 160°F (71°C) for beef, pork, veal, and lamb. 
• Egg Dishes: 160°F (71°C) for frittatas and quiches.

Question (Front): A fish with its viscera removed but its head, fins, and tail retained is described as:
Rationale:
A drawn fish is a whole fish that has had only its internal organs (viscera or entrails) removed. The head, fins, scales, and tail all remain completely intact.

• A whole fish has not had the viscera removed.
• A dressed fish has undergone additional preparation beyond simply drawing. A fish that has been drawn, but has also had its head, tail, fins, and scales completely removed.
• A filleted fish has the flesh separated from the bones, usually into fillets. The boneless side of a fish cut lengthwise away from the backbone.

Question (Front): Which of the statements is correct:
Answer (Back): Balut is a fertilized duck egg that has been incubated before cooking
Rationale:
Balut is a famous Filipino street food consisting of a fertilized duck egg. It is traditionally incubated in heated rice husks for roughly 14 to 21 days (usually 18 days) to allow a semi-developed duck embryo to form inside before it is hard-boiled or steamed.

Penoy: is an unfertilized duck egg that is boiled and consumed. It does not contain a developing duck embryo.

Question (Front): TRUE OR FALSE: Mutton (meat of an older sheep) is lighter in color and flavor than the lamb.
Rationale:
Why Mutton is Darker
• Myoglobin buildup: Older animals have muscles that work for years. This increases myoglobin, the protein that stores oxygen in muscle tissue and turns red meat dark.
• Diet accumulation: Years of grazing on grass and forage deposit rich nutrients and minerals into the animal's muscle and fat tissues.

Why Mutton is More Flavorful
• Fat and fatty acids: Mutton develops a higher concentration of species-specific fatty acids and heavier fat deposits that carry a robust, earthy, and gamey taste.
• Mature muscle chemistry: As the sheep ages, the chemical compounds responsible for deep savory flavors multiply and concentrate, moving past the mild and milky taste profile of young lamb.

Question (Front): Which condition can cause milk proteins to coagulate?
Rationale:
Lowering milk pH through acidification can cause milk proteins, particularly casein, to coagulate.

• Freezing alone does not describe the usual mechanism of milk-protein coagulation. 
• Homogenization reduces fat globule size and does not itself cause the described coagulation.
• Refrigeration alone does not normally coagulate milk proteins.

Question (Front): Which artificial sweetener is associated with phenylketonuria?
Rationale: Aspartame is associated with phenylketonuria (PKU) because it contains phenylalanine. Individuals with PKU cannot properly metabolize phenylalanine, so they need to restrict their intake. This is why products containing aspartame carry a warning for people with PKU.

Question (Front): Which of the following is a microorganism commonly used in bread production?
Rationale: Yeast, particularly Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is a microorganism commonly used in bread production. It ferments sugars in the dough and produces carbon dioxide (CO₂). The CO₂ becomes trapped within the gluten network, causing the dough to rise and giving bread its characteristic volume and texture.

Question (Front): Which of the following is a chemical leavening agent?
Rationale:
Baking soda is a fine white chemical salt called sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3). It acts as a base that reacts with acids to create carbon dioxide gas. This reaction makes baked goods rise.

• Yeast is a biological leavening agent.
• Whipped egg white can provide physical aeration rather than chemical leavening.
• Gluten provides structure and gas retention but is not itself a leavening agent.

Question (Front): Which of the following is a non-perishable food?
A cooked mixture of about equal weights of flour and fat used to thicken soups, sauces, and gravies.
Rationale:
A roux is the culinary term for a thickener made by cooking equal parts by weight of fat (usually butter) and flour.

It serves as the foundational thickening agent for classic French mother sauces (like Béchamel and Velouté) as well as various soups, stews, and gravies.

• Sherry is a wine.
• White wash is flour + water, not flour + fat.
• Custard is simple base of milk/cream, eggs or egg yolks and sugar.

Question (Front): The most suitable wall material for institutional kitchen is:
Rationale:
Ceramic Tiles are Durable, smooth, and easy to clean.

Question (Front): At higher altitudes, the boiling point of water:
Rationale:
At higher altitudes, atmospheric pressure is lower because there is less air pressing down on the Earth’s surface. A liquid boils when its vapor pressure becomes equal to the surrounding atmospheric pressure.

Therefore: Higher altitude → lower atmospheric pressure → liquid reaches its boiling point at a lower temperature → lower boiling point

Question (Front): A common mixing method used to incorporate fat into flour for pie crust is:

Cutting in distributes solid fat through flour to create the desired pastry texture.

Question (Front): A central facility prepares meals in large quantities and distributes the prepared meals to several remote service locations. Which system best fits this arrangement?
Rationale:
The commissary foodservice system (also referred to as a central kitchen or central production facility) concentrates food procurement and production in a single, large-scale facility.

Once the meals are prepared in bulk, they are packaged and transported to distinct, remote service locations (often called satellite units or receiving kitchens) for final finishing and service.

• À la carte system: A style of menu where items are priced and ordered separately, rather than a production and distribution system.
• Conventional system: The traditional model where food is purchased, prepared from scratch, and served on the same premises.
• Individualized system: A specialized approach focused on custom dietary tailoring (often used in clinical healthcare), not a bulk production and remote distribution network.

Question (Front): Under PD 856, the minimum kitchen size for a 40 m² dining area is _____ .
Rationale:
According to the Implementing Rules and Regulations (IRR) of Chapter III (Food Establishments) of the Code on Sanitation of the Philippines (Presidential Decree No. 856), the kitchen area must be at least ¼ (25%) of the total dining area, provided it is not less than a base minimum of 9.30 m² (100 sq. ft.).

Calculation: Required Kitchen Size = 40 m² x ¼ = 10 m²

Since 10 m² meets the legal ratio and exceeds the minimum threshold of 9.30 m², it serves as the absolute statutory minimum required floor area for that setup.

• 12 m² – Not prescribed.
• 8 m² – Too small.
• 15 m² – Above requirement.

Question (Front): Which menu term means "of the day"?

Du jour is a French phrase that literally translates to "of the day".

In restaurants, a du jour menu or item changes daily depending on what fresh ingredients are available or what specials the chef has created (e.g., "Soup du jour" means soup of the day).

• À la cart: Means "by the menu" or "from the menu"; items are listed, ordered, and priced individually.
• Table d'hôte: Means "the host's table"; it offers a complete, multi-course meal with limited choices at a single fixed price.

Question (Front): Which organization, together with WHO, established the Codex Alimentarius Commission?
Rationale:
The Codex Alimentarius Commission (CAC) was established in 1963 as a joint initiative between the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations and the World Health Organization (WHO).

Together, they created the Codex Alimentarius (Latin for "Food Code") to protect consumer health globally and promote fair, harmonized practices in international food trade.

Question (Front): A manager finds that one leadership approach is effective with one employee but ineffective with another because their abilities, motivation, and work circumstances differ. Which approach recognizes that management practices should be adapted to the situation?

• Bureaucratic management: formal structure, rules, and authority
• Classical management: broad principles of structure and efficiency

Question (Front): According to the updated Labor Code (RA 11360) of the Philippines, what percent of the service charge goes to the management?
Rationale:
Under Republic Act No. 11360, which amended Article 96 of the Labor Code, 100% of the service charges are distributed among covered employees, excluding managerial employees from the distribution. Thus, management receives 0% as a statutory share. 

Historical Context 
• Old Rule (Pre-2019): Under the original text of Article 96 of the Labor Code, 85% went to the employees and 15% was retained by management.
• New Rule (2019 Onward): The 15% management share was completely removed, making the employee share 100%.

Question (Front): Which statement best describes ergonomics in foodservice facility design?

Option 3: Designing menus according to customer preferences
Option 4: Designing storage systems according to food cost

Question (Front): [Image: Diagram]A diagram shows a server approaching a seated guest with a beverage. According to conventional service, from which side should the beverage generally be served?

Question (Front): A foodservice manager wants to reduce the risk of microbial growth in cooked food during preparation, holding, and service. Which practice best demonstrates proper time-temperature control?
Answer (Back): Monitoring food temperatures and minimizing the time food remains at unsafe temperatures
Rationale:
Foodborne pathogens multiply rapidly in the Temperature Danger Zone, which is between 41°F and 135°F (5°C to 57°C).

Proper time-temperature control for safety (TCS) requires food managers to constantly measure temperatures using food thermometers and ensure that foods move through or stay out of this danger zone as quickly as possible to prevent dangerous microbial growth.
Option 1: Monitoring food temperatures and minimizing the time food remains at unsafe temperatures
Option 2: Checking on appearance and odor to determine whether food is safe
Option 3: Storing cooked food to remain at room temperature until needed

Question (Front): What is the Temperature Danger Zone?
Rationale:
The Temperature Danger Zone represents the environmental range where foodborne pathogenic bacteria (such as Salmonella, E. coli, and Staphylococcus aureus) reproduce most rapidly. Under optimal conditions inside this window, bacterial populations can double in number in as little as 10 to 20 minutes.

To protect public health, regulatory standards mandate keeping cold foods strictly below 41ºF and hot foods above 140ºF (or 135ºF depending on the specific municipal framework) to prevent bacteria from reaching dangerous, illness-causing thresholds.

Question (Front): The following is the purpose of producing quality foods in large volumes, except:
Rationale:
In quantity food production (such as institutional catering or commercial food service), food items must be processed in bulk to feed a large number of people efficiently. While massive industrial production successfully drives safety, flavor modification, and nutrient conservation via standardized operational formulas, it strips away the ability to execute delicate, artistic, or customized plating.

Producing food in massive batches requires prioritizing uniform output speed, thermal safety, and broad scale-stability over intricate visual designs. Because bulk distribution environments (like hospital lines, cafeteria trays, or packaging conveyor belts) inherently limit individual presentation, enhancing or customizing the refined aesthetic beauty of a dish is generally not an achievable technical objective or purpose of mass cooking.

Question (Front): The following is the importance of food safety, except:
Answer (Back): To reverse the spread of diseases
Rationale:
Food safety is a preventive discipline, not a curative treatment. While proper food handling, sanitation, and temperature control work effectively to prevent the transmission of foodborne pathogens, food safety measures alone cannot "reverse" or cure the spread of diseases once a population or individual is infected. Dealing with the active spread or reversal of clinical diseases falls under the scope of medical treatments, epidemiology, pharmaceutical interventions, and clinical healthcare protocols.

• To create and maintain healthful and hygienic conditions for the family: This is a fundamental, domestic goal of everyday food hygiene to protect household health.
• To gain market access: Under national regulations such as the Food Safety Act of 2013 (RA 10611), ensuring rigid food safety compliance is a legal mandatory prerequisite to protect consumer health and facilitate market access for local commercial food products globally and locally.
• To prevent food contamination and food spoilage: This is a primary technical purpose of food safety frameworks—keeping biological, chemical, and physical hazards out of the food supply chain.
Option 1: To create and maintain healthful and hygienic conditions for the family
Option 2: To prevent food contamination and food spoilage
Option 3: To reverse the spread of diseases

Question (Front): What is the right temperature for dry storage?
Rationale:
In foodservice and meal management, dry storage areas are designed to preserve dry staples and canned goods by protecting them from heat and moisture.

Standard foodservice guidelines specify that dry storage temperatures should ideally be maintained between 50ºF and 70ºF (10ºC to 21ºC).

60 – 70ºF fits securely within this recommended parameters. Keeping the room within this temperature range slows chemical reactions, prevents premature food spoilage, and extends the overall shelf life of dry goods.

• 29 to 33ºF: This represents the temperature range used for chilled or super-chilled food storage (such as fresh fish, meat, or poultry holding sections), which is just slightly above or at freezing point.
• 34 – 40ºF: This is the standard operational temperature range for refrigeration / cold storage to prevent bacterial multiplication in perishable commodities.
• 0 to -10ºF: This is the legal threshold required for freezer storage to ensure food remains solidly frozen and safe over long periods.
