Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The wide variety of activities to "sell" the products, ideas or concepts that involves media and interpersonal channels is ________
Rationale: In the classic 4 Ps of social marketing (Product, Price, Place, Promotion), Promotion encompasses the diverse range of advertising, public relations, mass media broadcasts, community outreach, and interpersonal communication strategies used to raise awareness and persuade target audiences.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): When year was the Food Fortification Law of the Philippines enacted?
Rationale: Republic Act No. 8976, known as the 'Philippine Food Fortification Act of 2000', was signed into law on November 7, 2000. It instituted mandatory fortification of staple foods (rice with iron, wheat flour with iron and vitamin A, cooking oil and refined sugar with vitamin A).
Tags: Philippine Laws, RA 8976, Food Fortification, Legislation

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Maternal ________ is associated with babies with low weight (<2500 g) at birth.
Rationale: Maternal iron deficiency and iron-deficiency anemia in pregnancy impair uteroplacental perfusion, oxygenation, and tissue synthesis, significantly increasing the clinical risk of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), low birth weight (< 2,500 g), and preterm birth.
Tags: Maternal Nutrition, Iron Deficiency, Low Birth Weight

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following is NOT a major program area of the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition for the Year 2011 to 2016?
Rationale: Under the PPAN 2011–2016, the core strategic nutrition intervention programs focused on: 1) Infant and Young Child Feeding / Maternal and Child Health, 2) Micronutrient Supplementation, 3) Mandatory and Voluntary Food Fortification, 4) Supplementary Feeding, and 5) Nutrition in Emergencies. Human resource development is an institutional support / enabling mechanism rather than a primary intervention program area.
Tags: PPAN, Nutrition Policy, National Nutrition Council

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): During the first year, infants increase their height by ________ %.
Rationale: An infant's average birth length is approximately 50 cm. By 12 months (1 year) of age, the infant reaches an average length of approximately 75 cm. This represents a 25 cm increase, or exactly a 50% increase over birth length.
Tags: Infant Growth, Growth Velocity, Pediatric Anthropometry

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): After birth, fetal iron storage diminishes during the period ________ months.
Rationale: Endogenous neonatal hepatic iron stores established in utero sustain blood volume expansion and tissue growth until 4 to 6 months of age, after which iron stores diminish and dietary complementary foods become imperative.
Tags: Infant Nutrition, Iron Stores, Complementary Feeding

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Anemia is caused by ________ deficiency/deficiencies. (select the best answer)
Rationale: While folate, B12, and protein deficiencies can cause specific forms of anemia, iron deficiency accounts for approximately 50% or more of all anemia cases globally and is the single most prevalent nutritional deficiency worldwide. On the examination paper, option A (iron) is circled as the best answer.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the factor in food choices that relates to policies on agricultural subsidies, trade regulations and taxes that enhances individual's financial capacity to obtain foods?
Rationale: Economic access/accessibility refers to whether individuals and households have the purchasing power and financial resources to acquire adequate foods, heavily influenced by fiscal policies, agricultural pricing, subsidies, and trade tariffs. On the exam paper, option B (Accessibility) is circled.
Tags: Food Security, Economic Accessibility, Food Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The products intended to address the nutrients gap that contain one or more dietary ingredients is called ________
Rationale: Dietary Supplements are manufactured products intended to supplement the daily diet and address nutritional gaps, formulated to contain one or more dietary ingredients such as vitamins, minerals, herbs, amino acids, or enzymes in concentrated dosage forms.
Tags: Dietary Supplements, Public Health Interventions, Nutrition Products

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The WHO recommendation for daily fruit and vegetable intake is ________ grams.
Rationale: The World Health Organization (WHO) and FAO recommend a minimum consumption of 400 grams (equivalent to five servings of 80 grams each) of fruits and vegetables per day (excluding starchy tubers like potatoes and cassava) to prevent chronic non-communicable diseases.
Tags: WHO Guidelines, Fruit & Vegetable Intake, NCD Prevention

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): How many indicators are contained in the MDG?
Rationale: The Millennium Development Goals (MDGs, 2000–2015) were structured around 8 overarching Goals. On the examination paper, option C (8) is circled, with a margin note clarifying 'eight goals'. (Technically, the MDG monitoring framework contained 8 goals, 21 targets, and 60 official indicators).
Tags: MDGs, Global Goals, Public Health Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following lays out targets, directions, and priority actions in 2030?
Rationale: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development, adopted by all UN Member States in 2015, establishes the 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) with 169 targets to guide global and national priority actions and policies through the year 2030.
Option 4: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the type of monosaccharides that provides energy to the brain?
Rationale: D-Glucose is the obligate and primary metabolic monosaccharide fuel utilized by the human brain under normal non-fasting physiological conditions, crossing the blood-brain barrier via GLUT-1 transporters to support neuronal oxidative phosphorylation.
Tags: Carbohydrate Metabolism, Brain Energy, Biochemistry, Glucose

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The Maternal, Neonatal and Child Health and Nutrition guidelines states that the third pre-natal visit of a pregnant woman must be on the ________ weeks.
Rationale: Under the DOH Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health and Nutrition (MNCHN) strategy, pregnant women must receive a minimum of four antenatal care (ANC) visits: 1st visit in 1st trimester (<12 weeks); 2nd visit in 2nd trimester (around 24–28 weeks); 3rd visit in early 3rd trimester (around 32 weeks); and 4th visit in late 3rd trimester (around 36–38 weeks).
Tags: MNCHN, Antenatal Care, DOH Guidelines, Maternal Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The additional daily requirement of folate during pregnancy is
Rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake (RENI) for folate for non-pregnant adult women is 400 mcg DFE/day. Pregnancy requires an additional +200 mcg DFE/day (total 600 mcg DFE/day) to support rapid fetal cell division, uterine enlargement, and prevent neural tube defects (NTDs).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the type of study in which the researcher collects data at one point in time?
Rationale: A Cross-sectional study (also known as a prevalence study) collects exposure and outcome data from a defined population simultaneously at a single specific point in time, providing a 'snapshot' of community nutritional status.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A LBW infants may need to catch up ________ fold increase in weight to have optimal growth.
Rationale: Low birth weight (LBW) infants generally require compensatory accelerated growth during infancy, typically reaching a four-fold (4-fold) increase in their initial birth weight by 12 months to achieve appropriate growth percentiles.
Tags: Infant Growth, Low Birth Weight, Catch-up Growth

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the indicator to assess the severity of Vitamin A deficiency in most age groups in the population?
Rationale: According to the World Health Organization (WHO), subclinical Vitamin A Deficiency (VAD) is defined by a serum or plasma retinol concentration of less than 0.70 umol/L (or < 20 ug/dL). A population prevalence of serum retinol < 0.70 umol/L of >= 15% signifies a severe public health problem.
Tags: Micronutrient Assessment, Vitamin A Deficiency, Serum Retinol, WHO Cut-offs

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): How many indicators are contained in the Sustainable Development Goals?
Rationale: The United Nations 2030 Agenda consists of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Although the monitoring framework includes 169 targets and 232 official statistical indicators, board exam questions frequently refer to the 17 headline goals.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Food choices at the communal and individual level are influenced by ________
Rationale: Food choices and dietary consumption patterns are determined by a complex interplay of environmental and economic factors, notably physical food availability in the market, geographical accessibility, and economic affordability/purchasing power.
Tags: Food Choices, Food Security, Determinants of Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The addition of a nutrient to a food vehicle commonly consumed by the population to prevent or correct a micronutrient deficiency is ________
Rationale: Under RA 8976 and WHO/FAO standards, Food Fortification is the addition of essential micronutrients (e.g. vitamin A, iron, iodine) to widely consumed staple foods (food vehicles) to prevent or correct population-wide nutritional deficiencies.
Tags: Food Fortification, RA 8976, Public Health Interventions

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The activities that aim to prevent diseases in populations before they occur is ________
Rationale: Primary Prevention intervenes before the onset of disease or pathological changes occur, through health promotion, immunization, universal food fortification, clean water/sanitation, and dietary education to eliminate underlying risk factors.
Tags: Levels of Prevention, Primary Prevention, Public Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): During pregnancy the additional daily water requirement is ________ ml.
Rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015) and maternal nutrition guidelines, pregnant women require an additional fluid intake of approximately 300 ml/day (about 1 additional cup/glass of water) to support blood volume expansion, amniotic fluid, and fetal circulation.
Tags: PDRI, Water Requirements, Maternal Nutrition, Pregnancy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A concrete definition of the major steps taken by an organization to achieve its mission and vision is termed as ________
Rationale: In strategic management, Goals represent the broad, concrete developmental steps and strategic milestones an organization establishes to translate its vision and mission into operational reality. On the exam paper, option C is marked.
Tags: Program Planning, Goals & Objectives, Strategic Management

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The RENI is intended to meet the nutrient needs of ________ people.
Rationale: Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intakes (RENI / PDRI) are explicitly formulated to meet the physiological requirements of practically all (97.5%) healthy individuals in a given population group. They do not apply to individuals suffering from acute illness, severe malnutrition, or therapeutic metabolic disorders.
Tags: RENI, PDRI, Nutritional Standards, Healthy Populations

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the indicator used to describe age-specific mortality rate, morbidity rates, or infant deaths?
Rationale: Mortality rates (such as infant mortality rate, neonatal mortality, under-five mortality) and morbidity rates broken down by age cohorts are vital demographic statistics and demographic health indicators used to assess population survival and disease burden.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the measure of detecting early changes in body metabolism & nutrition before the appearance of overt clinical signs?
Rationale: Biochemical assessment (measuring serum micronutrients, enzyme activities, or urinary metabolites) detects early subclinical alterations in nutritional status and metabolic pathways prior to clinical manifestations.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Biochemical Assessment, Subclinical Deficiencies

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The average weight gain during the first trimester of pregnancy is ________ kgs.
Rationale: According to the Institute of Medicine (IOM) and Philippine clinical nutrition guidelines, the expected maternal weight gain for a woman with normal pre-pregnancy BMI during the entire first trimester is approximately 1.0 to 2.0 or 2.3 kg (2.2 to 5.0 lbs).
Tags: Maternal Nutrition, Gestational Weight Gain, First Trimester

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The amino acid essential to infants is ________
Rationale: Histidine is well established in nutritional biochemistry as conditionally indispensable (essential) for infants due to immature endogenous biosynthetic pathways. Dietary histidine is required to maintain positive nitrogen balance and normal linear growth in infancy.
Tags: Biochemistry, Amino Acids, Infant Nutrition, Histidine

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The detailed operational plans, including budgets, and goals and targets that are specific, measurable, attainable, relevant and time-bound is ________
Rationale: In program management terminology, a Project is an operational undertaking characterized by defined SMART goals, specific deliverables, assigned budget, and a fixed operational timeframe. On the exam paper, option B is marked.
Tags: Program Planning, Project Management, SMART Objectives

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The Sustainable Development Goals contains ________ goals and targets.
Rationale: The UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development consists of 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), underpinned by 169 targets.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The basic principle in planning that refers to the active participation of everybody in the decision making process is ________
Rationale: The principle of Involvement (or participatory planning) asserts that all stakeholders, community representatives, and program implementers must actively participate in identifying priorities and formulating decisions to ensure local ownership and sustainability.
Tags: Program Planning, Participation, Principle of Involvement

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the global reference diet for adults that is symbolically represented by half a plate of fruits, vegetables and nuts and the other half consists of primarily whole grains, plant proteins, unsaturated plant oils, modest amounts of meat and dairy, and some added sugars and starchy vegetables?
Rationale: The EAT-Lancet Commission on Food, Planet, Health (2019) introduced the 'Planetary Health Diet'. It establishes a global reference diet designed to nurture human health and stay within environmental planetary boundaries, characterized by a plate where half is fruits, vegetables, and nuts, and half is whole grains, plant-source proteins, and unsaturated oils.
Tags: Planetary Health Diet, EAT-Lancet, Global Nutrition, Sustainable Diets

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): This pertains to a public health nutritionist who has communication skills, ranging from writing professional reports to the development of health and nutrition information based on scientific evidences.
Rationale: The Public Health Nutrition Administrator leads communication systems, translating scientific evidence into health promotion materials, technical program reports, and multi-sector policy briefs.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What activity could be done to help the program planners understand their allies, neutral parties, and opponents in order to decide the most feasible route to accomplish their goals?
Rationale: Stakeholder Analysis (option A, 'Stakeholder') is the strategic planning tool used to systematically identify individuals and groups, analyze their interests, influence, and stance (allies, neutral parties, or opponents), and formulate effective advocacy and coalition strategies.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Vitamin ________ is required for growth, epithelial integrity and immunity and essential for the maintenance of visual purple for vision in dim light.
Rationale: Vitamin A (11-cis-retinal) conjugates with the protein opsin in retinal rod cells to form Rhodopsin ('visual purple'), the photoreceptor pigment essential for scotopic (dim light) vision. Vitamin A (retinoic acid) also maintains epithelial tissue integrity and cellular immune defense.
Tags: Micronutrients, Vitamin A, Rhodopsin, Visual Purple

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Human milk has higher proportion of ________ a protein like lactalbumin which has a soft fluorescent curd in the infant's stomach.
Rationale: Human mature milk contains a whey-to-casein ratio of approximately 60:40 (and up to 80:20 in colostrum), compared to bovine milk which is 20:80. The predominant whey protein is alpha-lactalbumin, which forms a soft, flocculent (curd-like), easily digestible precipitate in the infant stomach.
Tags: Infant Nutrition, Human Milk, Biochemistry, Whey

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following contains tabulated data on quantities of different nutrients and energy value per 100g per food item?
Rationale: The Philippine Food Composition Tables (FCT), developed and maintained by the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI-DOST), provide standardized analytical data on macro- and micronutrient quantities and caloric density per 100 grams edible portion of Philippine foods.
Tags: Food Composition Table, FNRI, Dietary Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the Act on Salt Iodization Nationwide popularly known as ASIN Law?
Rationale: Republic Act No. 8172, enacted on December 20, 1995, is an 'Act for Salt Iodization Nationwide' (ASIN Law). It mandates the iodization of all salt for human and animal consumption to eliminate Iodine Deficiency Disorders (IDD) in the Philippines.
Tags: Philippine Laws, RA 8172, ASIN Law, Iodine Deficiency

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following nutrients supplies oxygen from the lungs to the different parts of the body?
Rationale: Iron is the central metal cofactor of the heme moiety within Hemoglobin, the erythrocyte metalloprotein that coordinates molecular oxygen in the pulmonary alveoli and transports it via systemic circulation to peripheral tissues.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): How many programs does the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition 2017 to 2022 compose of?
Rationale: The Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN 2017–2022) comprises exactly 12 strategic programs: 8 Nutrition-Specific programs, 1 Nutrition-Sensitive program cluster, and 3 Enabling support programs (subdivided into 46 specific projects).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The world's time-bound and quantified targets for addressing extreme poverty in its many dimensions while promoting gender equality, education, environmental sustainability and basic human rights by 2030 is the ________
Rationale: The Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), spearheaded by the United Nations, represent the 15-year global commitment (2015–2030) targeting poverty eradication, reduced inequalities, quality education, universal healthcare, and environmental sustainability.
Option 4: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Translating the PPAN into a dynamic action plan and program at the grassroot level is called ________
Answer (Back): Barangay Plan of Action for Nutrition
Rationale: In the Philippine decentralized local governance framework, the Barangay Nutrition Committee (BNC) translates national PPAN priorities into local operational reality via the Barangay Nutrition Action Plan (BNAP / BPAN).
Option 1: A. Barangay Plan of Action for Nutrition
Tags: Local Governance, BNAP, Barangay Nutrition, PPAN Localization

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the process of sharing information using different channels?
Rationale: Communication is the interactive process of generating, transmitting, receiving, and interpreting messages, information, and ideas through various interpersonal, print, electronic, and digital channels.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The interpretation of data to determine whether a person or groups of people are well nourished or malnourished is called ________
Rationale: Nutritional Assessment is the systematic process of collecting, interpreting, and integrating anthropometric, biochemical, clinical, and dietary information to determine whether individuals or populations are adequately nourished or malnourished.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Core Principles, Nutritional Status

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Among underfive children, 25% are stunted. What is the severity of stunting using the WHO cut-off?
Rationale: Under the WHO/UNICEF (2018) revised thresholds for public health significance of stunting among children under 5 years: Very Low = < 2.5%; Low = 2.5 to < 10%; Medium = 10 to < 20%; High = 20 to < 30%; Very High = >= 30%. A prevalence of 25% falls directly into the 'High' severity category.
Tags: WHO Cut-offs, Stunting Prevalence, Public Health Severity

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The type of research that employs systematic reviews of several research results and conduct statistical analysis to arrive at a conclusion is
Rationale: A Meta-Analysis is a high-level quantitative epidemiological study design that pools and statistically integrates the results from multiple independent primary studies identified through a systematic review to generate a single pooled effect size.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the process of integrating nutrition activities with other programs within the same sector?
Rationale: Intra-sectoral coordination/integration involves aligning and coordinating nutrition activities among different departments, divisions, or services within the same sectoral agency (e.g., integrating nutrition counseling within the Maternal, Neonatal, and Child Health program inside the Department of Health). Inter-sectoral involves distinct sectors (Health, Agriculture, Social Welfare, Education).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The program and activities of DOH that aims to reduce childhood illnesses and eliminates micronutrient malnutrition.
Rationale: Garantisadong Pambata (GP) is the institutionalized DOH national child health campaign conducted semiannually to deliver a comprehensive integrated package: Vitamin A capsules, deworming tablets, routine immunizations, iron drops, and infant feeding promotion to under-five children.
Tags: Garantisadong Pambata, DOH Programs, Child Survival, Micronutrients

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The 24-hour urinary nitrogen is a recovery biomarker for calcium. This statement is ________
Rationale: This statement is FALSE. 24-hour urinary nitrogen (UUN) is the gold-standard recovery biomarker for dietary PROTEIN intake (since ~80–90% of nitrogen from catabolized dietary protein is excreted in urine as urea), not calcium.
Tags: Biomarkers, Urinary Nitrogen, Protein Intake, Nutritional Biochemistry

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The amino acid essential to infants is ________
Rationale: On this examination paper, option D ('tryptophan') is circled. In classical biochemistry, histidine (Option A) is widely recognized as the conditionally essential amino acid specific to infants due to rate-limiting biosynthetic capacity. Note candidate circled D here, while Item 132 featured the same question.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A strategy to encourage food manufacturers to fortify their products with one or more nutrients is called the ________
Rationale: The Sangkap Pinoy Seal Program (SPSP) is a voluntary fortification advocacy initiative developed by the Department of Health (DOH) under RA 8976, granting a recognizable seal of quality to processed food products fortified with essential micronutrients (Vitamin A, Iron, or Iodine).
Tags: Sangkap Pinoy Seal, RA 8976, Food Fortification, DOH

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): This pertains to planned actions that are implemented to improve nutrition and well-being of designated groups.
Rationale: Nutrition Interventions are purposefully planned and targeted actions designed to positively modify nutritional intake, eating behavior, physiological status, or environmental determinants in specific high-risk groups.
Tags: Nutrition Interventions, Program Planning, Public Health Principles

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the collegial body of NNC that is chaired by the Secretary of Health with other member agencies?
Rationale: The NNC Governing Board is the apex collegial and multi-sectoral policy-making body for nutrition in the country, chaired by the Secretary of Health and composed of heads of 10 executive departments and 3 private sector representatives.
Tags: NNC Governing Board, National Governance, Nutrition Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): During infancy the brain reaches ________ % of its adult size at 12 to 24 months.
Rationale: During the first two years of life (the First 1,000 Days), brain development accelerates dramatically: reaching ~50% of adult brain weight by 6 months, ~60–70% by 12 months, and approximately 75% to 80% by 24 months of age, underpinning the urgency of early nutritional protection against stunting.
Tags: Brain Development, First 1000 Days, Neurodevelopment, Infancy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The President can use this document to set policy while avoiding public debate and opposition and it does not require congressional approval.
Rationale: Historically during the martial law era (1972–1986), the Philippine President issued Presidential Decrees (PDs) having the full force of national law without congressional debate or approval (e.g. PD 491 creating the NNC). In constitutional republics, Executive Orders direct executive operations without congress. On this exam paper, option A is marked.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The method/s to assess moderate or severe malnutrition among children is/are ________
Rationale: Comprehensive screening and diagnostic evaluation of acute malnutrition in community and clinical settings integrates Mid-Upper Arm Circumference (MUAC < 115 mm for SAM, 115–<125 mm for MAM), assessment of bilateral pitting edema, and head/growth parameters. On the exam paper, option A (all of these) is marked.
Tags: Nutritional Assessment, SAM Management, MUAC, Bilateral Pitting Edema

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the award given to a municipality, city, or province that has shown outstanding performance in implementing its local nutrition action plan in the region?
Rationale: The Green Banner Award (now Green Banner Seal of Compliance under MELLPI Pro) is conferred annually by Regional Nutrition Evaluation Teams (RNET) and the NNC to LGUs (municipality, city, province) that achieve exemplary performance in nutrition program implementation and significant malnutrition reductions.
Tags: NNC Awards, Green Banner Award, MELLPI Pro, LGU Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the Executive Order that has regulated the marketing of breast milk substitutes or also known as Milk Code of the Philippines.
Rationale: Executive Order No. 51, signed on October 20, 1986 by President Corazon Aquino, is the 'National Code of Marketing of Breastmilk Substitutes, Breastmilk Supplements and Other Related Products', commonly known as the Philippine Milk Code. It regulates promotional activities, advertising, and donations of formula milk, feeding bottles, and teats.
Tags: Philippine Laws, Milk Code, EO 51, Breastfeeding Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term given to a collection of organizational resources that is geared to accomplish a certain major goal and have limited duration and a defined set of deliverables?
Rationale: In project management terminology, a Project is defined as a temporary endeavor with a defined beginning and end, undertaken to meet specific goals with designated deliverables. On the candidate's exam paper, option C ('Plan') is marked. Both concepts are central to public health administration.
Tags: Program Planning, Project Management, Operational Definitions

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The science and art of applying the principles of nutrition to the planning and preparation of foods, and management of the diet in relation to both health and disease.
Rationale: Verbatim duplicate of Item 9. On this question, the candidate marked option D ('meal planning and mangement'), while on Item 9 option A ('dietetics') was marked.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The nutrient that prevents hemorrhagic disease during pregnancy is vitamin ________
Rationale: Vitamin K is an obligate cofactor for hepatic gamma-glutamyl carboxylase, which carboxylates glutamic acid residues on prothrombin (Factor II) and clotting factors VII, IX, and X. Maternal vitamin K adequacy and newborn intramuscular prophylactic Vitamin K1 (phytomenadione) prevent Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn (Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding / VKDB).
Tags: Micronutrients, Vitamin K, VKDB, Maternal & Child Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The process of collecting information to determine whether activities are implemented as planned is ________
Rationale: Monitoring is the routine, continuous tracking of project activities, inputs, and outputs to assess whether activities are being carried out according to the planned schedule, budget, and operational protocols.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A combination of two anthropometric measurements is called ________
Rationale: In anthropometric methodology, an Index is formed by combining two raw measurements (such as weight and height to create weight-for-height) or a measurement with a biological variable (such as height and age to form height-for-age).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The long range direction that answers the question of what you must focus on to achieve the vision is ________
Rationale: A Mission statement clearly articulates the fundamental focus, core activities, and operational purpose of an organization or program to fulfill its long-term Vision.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front):
Situation 1 - Nutrition education and other nutrition interventions are implemented in a community-based approach with core programs and services that involve and engage the community - wide participation. The development and utilization of a documented plan will assist the Nutritionist - Dietitian in developing goals, message, and methods in an effective and cohesive way, resulting in better use of resources and more targeted outcomes.

What is your first step in developing your program plan?
Rationale: Situation 1 Question 1: Problem identification / situational assessment is invariably the prerequisite first phase of the program planning cycle. Planners must assess local needs, epidemiologic burden, and root causes before setting targets or formulating strategies.
Option 3: C. Know and identify the problem

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Situation 1 - In gathering data, you need to collect qualitative data. What are the commonly used methods for gathering qualitative data?
Answer (Back): Conduct of key informant interviews, focus groups, and participant observation
Rationale: Situation 1 Question 2: Qualitative data collection methodologies in community nutrition research comprise participatory techniques: Key Informant Interviews (KIIs), Focus Group Discussions (FGDs), direct participant observation, and semi-structured community dialogues.
Option 4: D. Conduct of key informant interviews, focus groups, and participant observation
Tags: Situation 1, Qualitative Methods, KII, FGD, Community Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Situation 1 - What are the most common methods for collecting quantitative data?
Rationale: Situation 1 Question 3: In epidemiological research, surveys with structured questionnaires and standardized measurements yield numerical, prevalence, and incidence data. On the candidate's examination paper, option B ('Getting biochemical markers') is marked as a quantitative laboratory method.
Option 1: A. Surveys and questionnaires revealing measurements in numbers or prevalences
Tags: Situation 1, Quantitative Methods, Biochemical Markers, Surveys

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Situation 1 - What is type of data that offers descriptive information that may capture experience, behavior, opinion, value, feeling, knowledge, sensory response, or observable phenomena?
Rationale: Situation 1 Question 4: Qualitative data provides rich descriptive, narrative, and contextual insight into human behavior, cultural beliefs, values, emotions, and motivations that cannot be reduced to simple numerical scores.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following agencies, as member of the NNC Board, that implements the basic needs program as a safety net provision of Republic Act 8435?

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of these methods of nutritional assessment deals with the individual and measures objective criteria on a face - to - face mode?
Rationale: Direct nutritional assessment evaluates objective physiological, clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical criteria directly on individual subjects face-to-face, contrasting with indirect assessment which analyzes aggregated community indicators.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The Pres. Duterte's development pillars are: malasakit, pagbabago, and ________ and the vision of Ambisyon 2040.
Rationale: Under the Philippine Development Plan (PDP 2017–2022) anchored on AmBisyon Natin 2040, the national framework is structured around three strategic pillars: 1) Malasakit (Enhancing the Social Fabric), 2) Pagbabago (Inequality-Reducing Transformation), and 3) Patuloy na Pag-unlad / Kaunlaran (Increasing Growth Potential).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following nutrients helps maintain muscle and body tissues?
Rationale: Dietary proteins provide the essential amino acids required for the synthesis, repair, and ongoing maintenance of skeletal muscle, vital organ tissues, collagen matrix, enzymes, and peptide hormones.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the step in program planning where the program manager will articulate what the program does and what to accomplish?
Rationale: Describing the program (program description/narrative) articulates the core mission, target population, structural components, specific activities, and what outcomes the program intends to accomplish.
Tags: Program Planning, Program Description, Project Narrative

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Albendazole ________ mg is usually given to pregnant women during the 2nd trimester.
Rationale: Under WHO and Philippine DOH guidelines for pregnant women in soil-transmitted helminth (STH) endemic areas (>20% prevalence), a single oral dose of Albendazole 400 mg (or Mebendazole 500 mg) is administered after the first trimester (in the 2nd or 3rd trimester) to treat intestinal worms and prevent maternal anemia.
Tags: Maternal Health, Deworming, Albendazole, DOH Guidelines

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the type of study design in which it answers the question "what will happen" and it is a prospective observation of subjects?
Rationale: A prospective Cohort study follows a defined group of exposure-free individuals forward in time to observe incidence rates and determine 'what will happen' regarding disease or nutritional outcomes.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): It refers to the regular or periodic collection and evaluation of data that can be used to indicate present and future changes in nutritional status.
Rationale: In public health administration and NNC training manuals, systematic collection and evaluation of progress indicators to assess present trends and inform management decisions is termed evaluation and management (or monitoring/surveillance in broader epidemiological contexts). On the exam paper, option C is marked.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): During lactation the additional daily energy requirement is ________
Rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the additional daily energy allowance during the first six months of exclusive lactation is +500 kcal/day (to support human milk synthesis yielding ~750–800 ml/day). In pregnancy (2nd/3rd trimester), the additional energy is +300 kcal/day.
Tags: PDRI, Lactation, Energy Requirements, Maternal Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following are you going to use to answer the question of how much you should eat in one meal in order to be healthy?
Rationale: Pinggang Pinoy, developed by FNRI-DOST in collaboration with DOH and WHO, is an intuitive visual food guide specifically designed to demonstrate recommended food group proportions and portion sizes per single meal (half plate Glow foods: fruits and vegetables; one-quarter Grow foods: protein; one-quarter Go foods: carbohydrates). The Food Pyramid depicts daily food choices.
Tags: Pinggang Pinoy, FNRI, Food Guides, Meal Planning

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the act of conducting systematic appraisal of the success of a program?
Rationale: Evaluation is the systematic and objective assessment of the design, implementation, and overall success or impact of an ongoing or completed public health initiative.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): When do you give iron-folic acid supplements in malaria endemic areas?
Rationale: Under WHO guidelines for malaria-endemic areas, iron and folic acid supplementation should be integrated alongside active screening, prevention (bed nets, vector control), and prompt antimalarial treatment. Option A is marked on the examination paper.
Option 4: D. Simultaneous with screening/treatment of malaria
Tags: Micronutrient Supplementation, Malaria, Iron-Folic Acid, WHO Guidelines

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): When is the period of second growth spurt?
Rationale: Human postnatal physical growth exhibits two major rapid velocity spurts: the first occurs during infancy (first year of life), and the second occurs during adolescence (the pubertal growth spurt driven by sex steroids and growth hormone).
Tags: Growth & Development, Adolescence, Pubertal Growth Spurt

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following is the guide for all who want to be involved in nutrition action because it lays out targets, directions, and priority actions, among others?
Rationale: On the candidate's examination paper, option A ('Sustainable Development Goals') is circled. In Philippine national policy, the Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition (PPAN, Option D) is the comprehensive national multi-sectoral blueprint that articulates precise targets, directions, and priority nutrition actions.
Option 4: D. Philippine Plan of Action for Nutrition
Tags: PPAN, SDGs, Nutrition Policy, National Framework

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term used to describe the complex disorder involving an excessive amount of body fat?
Rationale: Obesity is medically and epidemiologically defined as a chronic, complex relapsing non-communicable disease characterized by abnormal or excessive accumulation of body fat (adiposity) that impairs physical and metabolic health.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The long range direction that answers the question of what you must focus on to achieve the vision is ________
Rationale: In strategic management and program planning, the Mission defines the fundamental purpose, scope of operations, and core operational focus of an organization or program—answering what must be done to attain the long-term Vision.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What R.A was enacted in Year 2016 to promote and upgrade the practice of the professionals in the country?
Rationale: Republic Act No. 10912 is the 'Continuing Professional Development (CPD) Act of 2016', enacted on July 21, 2016. It mandates continuing education and credit units for the renewal of Professional Identification Cards across all regulated professions under the PRC.
Tags: Philippine Laws, RA 10912, CPD Act, PRC Regulations

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the type of study in which the effect of a given treatment is observed and assessed?
Rationale: In an Experimental study design (such as a randomized clinical trial or community intervention trial), the investigator deliberately manipulates or assigns the independent variable (treatment/intervention) and observes the outcome effects.
Tags: Research Methodology, Study Designs, Experimental Research

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following is an example of direct method of nutritional assessment?
Rationale: Nutritional assessment methods are divided into direct and indirect methods. Direct methods evaluate individual human subjects directly using the ABCD framework: Anthropometric, Biochemical/laboratory, Clinical, and Dietary methods. Vital health statistics, demographic data (age, sex), and agricultural/economic indicators are indirect ecological indicators.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Direct vs Indirect, Biochemical

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What are the different contaminants of foods?
Rationale: Under food safety science and HACCP principles, food hazards and contaminants are classically classified into three major categories: 1) Biological/microbiological (bacteria, viruses, parasites), 2) Chemical (pesticides, toxins, heavy metals), and 3) Physical (glass, metal fragments, stones, bone splinters).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the process of 'working collaboratively with relevant partners who share common goals and interests' or 'working collaboratively with and for groups of people affiliated by geographical proximity, special interest, or similar situations to address issues on nutrition and well-being of people'?
Rationale: Community engagement / community participation is the process of working collaboratively with and through groups of people affiliated by geographic proximity, special interest, or shared circumstances to address issues affecting their health, nutrition, and well-being.
Tags: Community Engagement, Public Health Nutrition, Community Development

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The proportion of children 6 to 23 months meeting both the minimum meal frequency to ensure both dietary and nutrient adequacy is ________
Rationale: In WHO/UNICEF Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) indicators, the Minimum Acceptable Diet (MAD) is a composite indicator measuring the proportion of children 6–23 months of age who receive both the minimum dietary diversity (consuming foods from >= 5 of 8 food groups) and minimum meal frequency.
Tags: IYCF Indicators, WHO Standards, Minimum Acceptable Diet

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the measure of detecting early changes in body metabolism & nutrition before the appearance of overt clinical signs?
Rationale: Biochemical assessment (laboratory measurement of nutrients, metabolites, or enzyme cofactors in blood, urine, or tissue) detects subclinical nutrient depletion and cellular metabolic alterations long before physical signs or anatomical growth deficits emerge.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Biochemical Assessment, Subclinical Malnutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Maternal ________ is associated with overweight babies at birth.
Rationale: Pre-pregnancy maternal obesity and excessive gestational weight gain increase fetal glucose exposure and hyperinsulinemia (Pedersen hypothesis), leading to macrosomia (birth weight > 4,000 g) and large-for-gestational-age (LGA) infants.
Tags: Maternal Nutrition, Obesity, Fetal Macrosomia, Pregnancy Outcomes

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): After the age of 59, caloric requirements is generally ________
Rationale: In older adults (> 59 years), resting metabolic rate decreases by approximately 2–3% per decade due to progressive age-related loss of lean skeletal muscle mass (sarcopenia) and concurrent reduction in voluntary physical activity, leading to lower total daily caloric requirements.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Megaloblastic anemia is caused by ________ deficiency/deficiencies.
Rationale: Megaloblastic anemia is characterized by large, immature nucleated erythroblasts in the bone marrow caused by impaired thymidylate and DNA synthesis due to deficiency of Folic Acid (Vitamin B9) or Vitamin B12 (cobalamin). Iron deficiency causes microcytic hypochromic anemia.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The transition in an infant's diet from breastmilk to other sources of foods is called ________
Rationale: Complementary Feeding is the recommended term describing the period starting at 6 months when breast milk alone is no longer sufficient to meet nutritional requirements, and other solid/semi-solid foods are introduced alongside continued breastfeeding.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What period after birth is considered as exclusively breastfed?
Rationale: WHO, UNICEF, and the Philippine Department of Health recommend exclusive breastfeeding for the first 6 months of life (0 to 180 days). During this period, the infant receives only breast milk, with no other liquids or solids, not even water (with the exception of oral rehydration salts, vitamins, minerals, and medicines).
Tags: Breastfeeding, Exclusive Breastfeeding, WHO Guidelines, IYCF

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): This pertains to a public health nutritionist who has communication skills, ranging from writing professional reports to the development of health and nutrition information that is inclusive and appropriate to target populations with appropriate financial management system.
Rationale: The Administrator role in public health nutrition encompasses comprehensive executive leadership, program communication, strategic technical reporting, stakeholder coordination, and fiscal/financial resource management systems.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term used to define low weight for height?
Rationale: Under WHO Child Growth Standards adopted by the DOH and NNC: Low Weight-for-Height/Length (<-2 SD) defines Wasting (acute malnutrition/thinness); Low Height/Length-for-Age (<-2 SD) defines Stunting (chronic malnutrition); and Low Weight-for-Age (<-2 SD) defines Underweight (composite index).
Tags: Anthropometry, Child Growth Standards, WHO Cut-offs, Wasting

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the tool needed to be developed in order to have a clearer overview of the objectives, the possible causal factors, and related data that will aid the RND in identifying relevant indicators to be collected for program proposal?
Rationale: A Causal Model (problem tree or UNICEF conceptual framework of malnutrition) maps the immediate, underlying, and basic determinants of nutritional problems. It provides a visual schematic connecting causes to outcomes, guiding program planners in selecting target intervention points and measurable indicators.
Tags: Program Planning, Causal Analysis, Conceptual Framework

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What period after birth does infant receives colostrum from the mother?
Rationale: Colostrum is secreted immediately following birth and is richest during the first 24 hours postpartum. Timely feeding within 24 hours delivers high concentrations of antibodies, lactoferrin, and oligosaccharides essential for gut protection.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is that document that outlines the decisions of the government to control malnutrition through the various sectors, indicating the precise objectives, targets and plan of action of each sector over a given time frame?
Rationale: A National Nutrition Policy (or strategic national nutrition plan such as the PPAN) represents the official multi-sectoral government statement and commitment detailing overarching targets, sectoral responsibilities, and specific strategic frameworks to eliminate malnutrition over a specified timeframe.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The birth weight of an infant is dependent on ________
Rationale: Maternal nutritional status—encompassing pre-pregnancy body mass index, micronutrient stores, and appropriate gestational weight gain throughout pregnancy—is the foremost modifiable determinant of fetal growth and birth weight.
Option 1: A. fat intake of the mother
Tags: Maternal Nutrition, Birth Weight, Fetal Development

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following agencies, as member of the NNC Board, that implements the research programs as basis for program planning?
Rationale: The Department of Science and Technology (DOST), through its attached research agency the Food and Nutrition Research Institute (FNRI-DOST), conducts the periodic National Nutrition Surveys (Expanded National Nutrition Survey / ENNS), generating empirical scientific data that forms the basis for national nutrition planning.
Tags: NNC Board, DOST, FNRI, National Nutrition Surveys

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the basic principle in planning that pertains to specific activities and must all be implemented contributing to the achievement of the objectives?
Rationale: The planning principle of Comprehensiveness dictates that all relevant intervention components, complementary activities, support systems, and resource requirements are systematically incorporated into the program design so they work synergistically toward achieving the objectives.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is a marker of suboptimal intrauterine growth and poor maternal nutrition; it increases the risks for poorer outcomes in growth, development and health in both the short and the long term?
Rationale: Low Birth Weight (LBW, defined as birth weight < 2,500 grams) is a primary marker of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) and/or preterm birth. LBW significantly elevates infant mortality risk, childhood stunting, and the developmental origins of adult chronic disease (Barker hypothesis).
Tags: Low Birth Weight, Maternal Nutrition, Intrauterine Growth

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A birth weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age based on a reference population is ________
Rationale: Small-for-Gestational-Age (SGA) is clinically and epidemiologically defined as a birth weight below the 10th percentile for sex and specific completed weeks of gestational age, distinguishing infants with pathological fetal growth restriction from those born early but appropriately sized.
Tags: Anthropometry, Small for Gestational Age, Pediatric Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The techniques that enhance learning among older adults is called ________
Rationale: Geragogy (or eldergogy) refers specifically to the instructional methodologies and educational strategies tailored to the cognitive, sensory, and psychosocial learning needs of older adults (the elderly). Pedagogy refers to teaching children, and andragogy refers to teaching adults in general.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following is one of the major activities in the identification of the causal causes of the nutritional problems?
Answer (Back): Identification of the causes of the problem
Rationale: In situational analysis and causal analysis (such as constructing a problem tree), systematically identifying immediate, underlying, and root causes is the core analytical activity that determines why the nutritional problem exists.
Option 1: A. Identification of the causes of the problem
Tags: Program Planning, Situational Analysis, Causal Analysis

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term used to define a situation in which food security is combined with a clean environment, adequate health services, and appropriate care and feeding practices, to ensure a healthy life for all household members?
Rationale: Nutrition Security extends beyond Food Security (which guarantees availability, accessibility, and affordability of food). Nutrition security integrates food security with sanitary environments, clean water, adequate primary healthcare, and optimal maternal and child caring/feeding practices to ensure physiological nutrient utilization for a healthy life.
Tags: Nutrition Security, Food Security, Public Health Framework

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the measure that reflects body composition such as body fat and lean body mass, and is considered a more accurate indicator than height/weight tables?
Rationale: Body Mass Index (BMI = weight in kg / height in m2) is an anthropometric index of weight adjusted for height that correlates closely with total body fatness and adiposity-related health risks across adult populations, offering a standardized measure superior to simple height-weight tables.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): In anthropometric measurement, a combination of an index and a cut-off is called ________
Rationale: In nutritional epidemiology: A raw measurement is an unadjusted value (e.g., weight); an Index is a combination of two measurements or a measurement and age (e.g., weight-for-height); an Indicator is an index combined with a predefined statistical cut-off point used to classify or estimate prevalence (e.g., WFH < -2 SD defines the indicator of wasting).
Tags: Anthropometry, Indices vs Indicators, Nutritional Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the important nutrient that is needed in protein, RNA, and DNA synthesis, cell division, and differentiation?
Rationale: Zinc is an essential trace element required as a structural and catalytic component of over 300 metalloenzymes, including RNA polymerases, DNA polymerases, and zinc-finger transcription factors that regulate gene expression, cell division, and cellular differentiation.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the main category of research in which subjects are looked over or are being watched?
Rationale: Observational research encompasses study designs (cohort, case-control, cross-sectional) wherein investigators passively observe exposures, behaviors, and health outcomes in study participants without introducing clinical interventions or experimental manipulations.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The desirable weight gain during pregnancy is ________ kgs.
Rationale: Institute of Medicine (IOM) and Philippine maternal guidelines recommend total gestational weight gain based on pre-pregnancy BMI: for underweight women (BMI < 18.5), recommended gain is 12.5 to 18.0 kg (averaging around 16–17 kg). On this exam paper, B (16.8 kg) is marked.
Tags: Maternal Nutrition, Gestational Weight Gain, Pregnancy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The basal metabolic rate during pregnancy is increased by ________ % by the end of the term.
Rationale: By the late third trimester of pregnancy, maternal Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) increases by roughly 20% to 25% due to the metabolic demands of the growing fetus, placental active transport, expanded maternal circulatory volume, and increased uterine and cardiac workload.
Tags: Maternal Physiology, Pregnancy, Basal Metabolic Rate

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of the following are the pillars of the sustainable development goals?
Rationale: The United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) framework is founded upon three interdependent, mutually reinforcing pillars of sustainable development: Economic Growth/Development, Social Inclusion/Development, and Environmental Protection/Sustainability.
Tags: SDGs, Sustainable Development, Global Health Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the practice of adding an essential micronutrient in a food to improve the nutritional quality and provide a public health benefit with minimal risk to health.
Rationale: According to the Codex Alimentarius and WHO/FAO guidelines, Food Fortification is the practice of deliberately increasing the content of an essential micronutrient in a food vehicle to improve nutritional quality and provide a public health benefit with minimal health risk.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The ________ mg daily calcium requirement for adolescents is the same for boys and girls.
Rationale: According to the Philippine Dietary Reference Intakes (PDRI 2015), the Recommended Energy and Nutrient Intake (RENI) for calcium for adolescents aged 10–18 years is 1000 mg/day for both boys and girls to optimize peak bone mass accretion during pubertal growth.
Tags: PDRI, Calcium, Adolescent Nutrition, Bone Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The basal metabolic rate during pregnancy is increased by ________ % by the end of the term.
Rationale: Maternal basal metabolic rate rises progressively over gestation, peaking in the third trimester at an elevation of 20% to 25% above pre-pregnancy baseline.
Tags: Maternal Physiology, Pregnancy, Basal Metabolic Rate

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): As a RND, you are task to develop a program plan. What is the first step in developing your plan?
Rationale: The standard community nutrition program planning cycle always initiates with Situation Analysis / Community Assessment to identify and define the nutritional problems, their magnitude, distribution, and root causes before objectives can be formulated or interventions selected.
Option 1: A. Plan for monitoring and evaluation
Option 4: D. Set the goals and objectives
Tags: Program Planning, Planning Cycle, Community Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term used to describe the complex disorder involving an excessive amount of body fat?
Rationale: Obesity is a complex multifactorial disease characterized by excess adiposity resulting from prolonged positive energy balance, predisposing individuals to cardiovascular, endocrine, and metabolic comorbidities.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): After birth, fetal iron storage is still sufficient until the period of ________ months.
Rationale: Full-term healthy newborns possess hepatic iron stores accumulated during late pregnancy that satisfy erythropoiesis and tissue requirements for the first 4 to 6 months of life. Beyond 6 months, iron stores deplete, necessitating iron-rich complementary foods.
Tags: Infant Nutrition, Iron Stores, Complementary Feeding

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The implementation of planned and systematic activities necessary to ensure that products or services meet quality standards is ________
Rationale: Quality Assurance (QA) comprises planned, systematic operational and managerial activities implemented within a quality system to provide adequate confidence that health and nutrition services or products satisfy stated standards.
Tags: Quality Assurance, Public Health Administration, Standards

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Serum calcium, are tightly controlled metabolically and are poor reflections of dietary intake or nutritional status. This statement is ________
Rationale: This statement is TRUE. Serum ionized and total calcium concentrations are maintained within strict homeostatic limits (8.5–10.5 mg/dL) by parathyroid hormone (PTH), calcitonin, and calcitriol acting on bone resorption and renal reabsorption. Consequently, serum calcium levels do not reflect dietary calcium intake or bone mineral density.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): A LBW infant may need to catch up ________ fold increase in weight to have optimal growth.
Rationale: Low birth weight (LBW) infants undergo rapid compensatory catch-up growth during the first year of life, frequently quadrupling (4-fold increase) their birth weight by 12 months to converge toward normal developmental centiles.
Tags: Infant Growth, Low Birth Weight, Catch-up Growth

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): Which of these refers to the set of interrelated projects that presents personnel, facilities, budget, equipment and supplies and other items directed to accomplish specific goals and objectives?
Rationale: A Program is an organized portfolio of interrelated projects and ongoing activities coordinated with institutional resources (personnel, budget, facilities, equipment) to achieve broad, long-range strategic goals and objectives.
Tags: Program Planning, Program vs Project, Administration

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The average increase in height of infants during the first year of life is ________ cm.
Rationale: During the first year of life, an infant's length increases substantially from an average birth length of ~50 cm to ~74–75 cm, representing an increment of approximately 24 to 25 cm. On the examination paper, option A (21 to 24 cm) is marked.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): In statistics, the number that occurs most often within a set of number is called the ________
Rationale: In descriptive statistics, the Mode is the measure of central tendency defined as the value or category that appears with the greatest frequency in a distribution.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The document that details for implementation of the action plan; specific projects are defined is called ________
Rationale: An Action Plan is an operational document that outlines the specific tasks, timelines, responsibilities, resource allocations, and operational procedures necessary to implement strategic objectives and programs.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The proportion for breastfed and non-breastfed children 6 to 23 months who receives solid, semi-solid, or soft foods consumed at the minimum number of times per day.
Rationale: Minimum Meal Frequency (MMF) is a core WHO/UNICEF IYCF indicator measuring the proportion of breastfed and non-breastfed children 6–23 months who receive solid, semi-solid, or soft foods (plus milk feeds for non-breastfed) at or above minimum age-specific frequencies (2 times for 6-8 mos, 3 times for 9-23 mos breastfed; 4 times for non-breastfed).
Tags: IYCF Indicators, Minimum Meal Frequency, WHO Standards

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The science and art of applying the principles of nutrition to the planning and preparation of foods, and management of the diet in relation to both health and disease is
Rationale: Under Republic Act No. 10862 (Nutrition and Dietetics Law of 2016) and classical professional definitions, Dietetics is the science and art of applying the principles of food and nutrition to the health and wellness of individuals and groups, disease prevention, and dietary management in illness.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The condition when "all people, at all times, have physical, social and economic access to sufficient, safe and nutritious food which meets their dietary needs and food preferences for an active and healthy life" is termed as ________ security.
Rationale: This is the universal definition of Food Security adopted at the 1996 World Food Summit by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO). It rests on four pillars: availability, access, utilization, and stability.
Tags: Food Security, FAO Definitions, Public Health Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the term given when planning is done at the national level?
Rationale: Macro-level planning refers to high-level strategic, policy, and budgetary planning conducted at the central or national level (e.g., national development plans, PPAN), whereas micro-level planning occurs at local, municipal, or community levels.
Tags: Program Planning, Macro-level Planning, National Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): STATISTICS is the science of conducting studies to.......
Answer (Back): collect, organize, summarize, analyze, and draw conclusions from data
Rationale: Statistics is formally defined as the scientific discipline concerned with designing studies, and collecting, organizing, presenting, analyzing, and drawing valid inferences and conclusions from numerical data.
Option 1: A. monitor, study, and report on a subject.
Option 2: B. solve a system of equations
Option 3: C. hypothesize, experiment, and form conclusions
Option 4: D. collect, organize, summarize, analyze, and draw conclusions from data

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The NNC Governing Board has ________ members who are the Secretaries of different government agencies.
Rationale: Under Executive Order No. 234 and Executive Order No. 472, the National Nutrition Council (NNC) Governing Board includes the heads/Secretaries of 10 key government departments: DOH (Chair), DA (Vice Chair), DILG (Vice Chair), DepEd, DSWD, DOST, DBM, NEDA, DTI, and DOLE, alongside 3 private sector representatives.
Tags: NNC Governing Board, National Governance, Nutrition Policy

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What are the interventions that address the underlying determinants of foetal and child nutrition and development?
Rationale: According to the Lancet Commission on Maternal and Child Nutrition and the PPAN: Nutrition-sensitive interventions address the underlying determinants of malnutrition (food security, agriculture, safe water, sanitation, female education, social safety nets); Nutrition-specific interventions address immediate causes (adequate food intake, disease control, micronutrient feeding).
Tags: PPAN, Nutrition Sensitive, Lancet Framework, Determinants of Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the daily fluid intake (in ml) of an infant weighing 1000 grams?
Rationale: In neonatal fluid calculation questions from PRC board examinations, option D (800 to 850 ml or scaled volume per body weight category) is marked on the test paper.
Tags: Pediatric Nutrition, Neonatal Fluids, Preterm Infant Care

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): That which inhibits intracellular viral replication is called
Rationale: Interferons (IFN-alpha, IFN-beta, IFN-gamma) are cytokine glycoproteins synthesized and secreted by virus-infected cells. They bind to neighboring cell surface receptors, inducing an antiviral state and activating protein kinase R (PKR) and 2',5'-oligoadenylate synthetase, which directly degrades viral RNA and inhibits intracellular viral protein translation.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): The adolescent growth spurt in boys begins between the ages of ________ years.
Rationale: The adolescent pubertal growth spurt in boys typically commences between ages 12 and 14 years, peaking between 14 and 16 years (Tanner stage 3–4), which is approximately two years later than in girls (who spurt between ages 10 and 14).
Tags: Adolescent Nutrition, Pubertal Growth Spurt, Growth Velocity

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): It pertains to targeted activities in individuals or groups with early signs of disease to prevent progression
Rationale: Early Intervention (corresponding to secondary prevention in public health) involves detecting early, subclinical, or initial pathological signs and delivering prompt targeted clinical and nutritional therapies to halt disease progression and prevent permanent complications.
Tags: Levels of Prevention, Early Intervention, Public Health Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2019 - Community & Public Health Nutrition
Question (Front): What is the R.A. that was enacted and is known as the "Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act"?
Rationale: Republic Act No. 11148, enacted on November 29, 2018, is officially known as the 'Kalusugan at Nutrisyon ng Mag-Nanay Act'. It scales up maternal and child nutrition programs across the First 1,000 Days of life (from conception up to the child's second birthday) to end stunting and malnutrition.
Tags: Philippine Laws, RA 11148, First 1000 Days, Maternal & Child Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Garlic, onions and shallots are examples of ___.
Rationale: Garlic, onions, and shallots are bulbs (underground storage structures consisting of a stem surrounded by fleshy leaves). Sweet potato and cassava are examples of roots and tubers.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Plant Foods, Vegetable Classification

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Where is the best location of a school cafeteria?
Rationale: A first/ground floor location ensures straightforward access for heavy delivery trucks, direct receiving dock connection, efficient trash removal, and safe, barrier-free student access.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Facility Planning, Layout & Design

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Identify a wild berry which can be found in the Philippines.
Rationale: Mulberries (genus Morus) and Philippine wild raspberries (sampinit / Rubus rosifolius) grow readily in the Philippine highlands. Acai and Maqui are South American; Atis is a sugar apple (custard fruit).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): The desirable pink color in cured meat is due to:
Rationale: When nitrite is added to curing brine, it converts to nitric oxide and binds to reduced myoglobin to form nitrosomyoglobin, which converts into stable pink nitrosohemochrome upon heating.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Meat Science, Food Chemistry

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Difference between the cost and the selling price:
Rationale: Markup is the amount or percentage added to the total product cost to establish the retail selling price (Selling Price − Cost = Markup).
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Costing & Calculation, Pricing Strategies

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Philippines: rice; Saudi Arabia: ___.
Rationale: Rice is the primary staple grain in the Philippines; spiced rice pilaf (Kabsa / Majboos pilaf) is the premier traditional grain staple of Saudi Arabia and the Arabian Peninsula.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, International Cuisines, Staple Foods

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Overcooking or overheating of oil can cause ___.
Rationale: When frying oil is heated past its smoke point, triglycerides hydrolyze into free glycerol, which dehydrates into acrolein—a pungent, acrid, eye-irritating aldehyde vapor.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Fats & Oils, Food Chemistry

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): To avoid foods spoiling in the refrigerator or freezer, which of the following actions is always recommended?
Answer (Back): Placing a date of arrival on all foods
Rationale: Clear labeling with arrival/preparation dates and expiration dates is the core operational prerequisite for executing FIFO (First-In, First-Out) inventory rotation.
Option 1: Smelling the food to make sure it is fresh
Option 2: Placing a date of arrival on all foods
Option 3: Ordering foods for a few days at a time only
Option 4: Placing the oldest product on top of newer product

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): 1 cup fresh milk: ___; 1 cup of low fat milk: ___.
Rationale: Under the Philippine Food Exchange Lists (PEL): 1 exchange of Whole Milk provides 12g CHO, 8g PRO, 10g FAT = 170 kcal; Low Fat Milk provides 12g CHO, 8g PRO, 5g FAT = 125 kcal.
Tags: PRC-2021, FFSS, Food Exchange Lists, Nutrition Math

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Identify the ESSENTIAL amino acids.
Rationale: Threonine, Tryptophan, and Valine are essential amino acids that humans cannot synthesize de novo. Alanine, aspartic acid, and proline are non-essential.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Broken mayonnaise is due to ___.
Rationale: Mayonnaise requires oil to be incorporated drop by drop initially into the egg yolk emulsion; pouring oil too rapidly overwhelms the lecithin interfacial tension and causes phase separation (broken sauce).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): Beth is a graduate of BS Nursing in one province in the Philippines. She was appointed by the City Mayor to occupy the position of a Nutritionist-Dietitian in an LGU. As there is an ND Law, what should the mayor do?
Answer (Back): Comply with the law and replace Beth's position with an RND
Rationale: Republic Act No. 10862 strictly mandates that only Registered Nutritionist-Dietitians (RND) holding valid Professional Identification Cards issued by the PRC can hold Nutritionist-Dietitian plantillas.
Option 1: Give a copy of the ND law to Beth and let her decide
Option 2: Wait until Beth resigns or retires and get an RND
Option 3: Ask the HR in the city health office to explain the law to Beth
Option 4: Comply with the law and replace Beth's position with an RND

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Foods & Food Service Systems
Question (Front): A 550g organic kale costs Php300 per kg. The edible portion is 70%. What is the EP price of organic kale per kg?
Rationale: For 550g purchased at Php300/kg, AP cost = 0.550 kg × Php300 = Php165. The purchased cost of the 550g bunch is Php 165.
