Option 4: D. Headache, irritability, arrythmia, low BP

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): One specific indication of enteral nutrition is:
Rationale: Enteral nutrition support is indicated when a patient has a functioning, accessible gastrointestinal tract but cannot or will not consume adequate oral nutrition (such as in severe prolonged anorexia nervosa, hypercatabolic cancer anorexia, or neurological dysphagia). Small bowel obstruction, severe intractable diarrhea, and active upper GI bleeding are absolute contraindications to enteral feeding.
Tags: Enteral Nutrition, Indications, Contraindications, Nutrition Support

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is the catabolic enzyme which can utilize peroxide in the production of substrates accompanied by water production?
Rationale: Catalase is a heme-containing antioxidant enzyme present in peroxisomes that catalyzes the decomposition of toxic hydrogen peroxide into water and molecular oxygen (2 H2O2 -> 2 H2O + O2), protecting cells against oxidative stress.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Diet management for Dumping Syndrome includes:
I. Small meals spread out throughout the day
II. High protein, moderate fat foods are recommended
III. Small amount of simple sugar may be taken as tolerated
IV. Use of fiber supplement to reduce upper GI transit time and decrease glucose absorption
Rationale: Dumping syndrome MNT emphasizes: (I) small, frequent meals spread over 5–6 feedings, (II) high protein and moderate fat to slow gastric emptying and sustain satiety, and (III) strictly limiting concentrated simple sugars (taking only small tolerated amounts). Regarding IV: Soluble fiber *increases* (delays) upper GI transit time rather than reducing it.
Option 1: A. I, II, III and IV

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Some RND's have been successful using the following approaches to make their interaction with difficult clients easier. Which will work BEST?
I. Giving assignment prior to next session.
II. Requesting for return demo after instruction was given.
III. Summarize the patient's main concern and offer feedback of what you heard.
IV. Give a strong impression that your instructions should be followed.
Rationale: Effective client-centered counseling uses active listening (summarizing concerns and reflective feedback - III), behavioral assignments/homework (I), and return demonstration/teach-back to verify competence (II). Authoritarian demands (IV - 'give a strong impression that instructions must be followed') provoke resistance and damage therapeutic rapport.
Option 2: B. I, II, III, and IV
Tags: Nutrition Counseling, Communication Skills, Client Rapport

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Which is responsible for regulating the acidic environment in the stomach?
I. Gastrin
II. Nerve receptor
III. Secretin
IV. Hydrochloric Acid
Rationale: Gastric acid secretion is tightly regulated by: Gastrin (I, secreted by antral G-cells, strongly stimulates parietal acid secretion), Neural receptors (II, vagal cholinergic and histamine H2 receptors), and Secretin (III, released by duodenal S-cells in response to acid, inhibits gastrin release and parietal cell acid secretion while stimulating pancreatic bicarbonate). Hydrochloric acid (IV) is the secretory product itself, not a regulatory controller.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The difference between cis and trans fatty acid is the _____.
Answer (Back): C. configuration of the double bond
Rationale: Cis and trans fatty acid isomers differ in the spatial geometric configuration of hydrogen atoms across the carbon-carbon double bond. In cis configuration, hydrogen atoms are on the same side, creating a kink/bend in the hydrocarbon chain. In trans configuration, hydrogen atoms are on opposite sides, producing a linear, rigid conformation similar to saturated fatty acids.
Option 1: A. location of their first double
Option 2: B. number of their double bonds
Option 3: C. configuration of the double bond
Option 4: D. length of their carbon chain
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Lipids, Fatty Acids, Isomerism

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A Sports ND is usually consulted for tips to boost performance before a game. Which of the following should NOT be a part of your advice?
Answer (Back): C. It's alright to try new foods on race or game day.
Rationale: A cardinal, non-negotiable rule in sports nutrition is 'never try anything new on competition or game day.' Introducing unfamiliar foods, supplements, or high-fiber foods immediately prior to an athletic event risks sudden severe gastrointestinal upset, diarrhea, nausea, and cramping.
Option 1: A. Carbohydrate is very important as the body needs it to fuel the working muscle.
Option 2: B. Protein is important for building and repair of muscle tissues.
Option 3: C. It's alright to try new foods on race or game day.
Option 4: D. Give fluid prescription on how much to drink before, during and after a game.
Tags: Sports Nutrition, Pre-event Nutrition, Athletes, Clinical Advice

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A patient is MOST likely to experience nausea, vomiting, bloating, increased flatus after suddenly changing from low to high dietary intake of:
Rationale: Abruptly increasing dietary fiber intake without a gradual step-up and without adequate fluid intake causes undigested polysaccharides to enter the colon rapidly, where anaerobic colonic bacteria undergo rapid fermentation, generating large volumes of hydrogen, methane, and carbon dioxide gases (bloating, cramping, and flatus).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Dr. Santos referred his hypertensive pt for diet counseling with a prescription for a low sodium diet. How many mg of sodium is allowed on this diet?
Rationale: In standard clinical dietetics and hospital diet manuals, a standard 'low sodium diet' (or mild/moderate sodium restriction) prescribes 2,000 mg of sodium daily (equivalent to approximately 5 grams of table salt). Strict sodium diets (500-1,000 mg) are rarely prescribed due to poor palatability and risk of hyponatremia.
Tags: Cardiovascular Nutrition, Hypertension, Sodium, Diet Orders

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Refeeding syndrome causes dangerous fluctuations in:
Rationale: Refeeding syndrome is characterized by rapid, life-threatening shifts in serum electrolytes—principally acute hypophosphatemia, hypokalemia, and hypomagnesemia—triggered by carbohydrate re-introduction and insulin release driving electrolytes into cells for glucose phosphorylation and protein synthesis.
Tags: Refeeding Syndrome, Critical Care, Electrolytes, Nutrition Support

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Which of these are the functions of the kidney?
I. Formation of plasma protein
II. Regulates blood pressure
III. Stimulates red blood cell production
IV. Activates Vit. D
Rationale: The kidneys regulate blood pressure via renin secretion (II), stimulate bone marrow red blood cell synthesis via erythropoietin production (III), and convert 25-hydroxyvitamin D into active 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D via 1-alpha-hydroxylase (IV). Synthesis of plasma proteins (such as albumin) is carried out by hepatocytes in the liver.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): An albumin of 1.8 g/dL is indicative of _____.
Rationale:
Serum albumin clinical visceral protein depletion categories:
- Normal: 3.5 to 5.0 g/dL
- Mild depletion: 2.8 to 3.5 g/dL
- Moderate depletion: 2.1 to 2.7 g/dL
- Severe depletion: < 2.1 g/dL.
Therefore, a serum albumin level of 1.8 g/dL indicates severe visceral protein depletion.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Laboratory Values, Albumin, Malnutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Long-term management of diverticular disease includes a:
Rationale: Long-term maintenance of diverticular disease (diverticulosis) requires a high-fiber diet (25 to 35 g/day or more) along with generous fluid intake to increase stool volume, soften feces, and decrease intraluminal colonic pressure, thereby preventing diverticulitis flares. Note that low fiber is only used during acute diverticulitis.
Option 2: B. low-fiber diet that omits foods with seeds

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Vitamin is recognized as "sunshine vitamin" and can be synthesized by the skin is _____.
Rationale: Vitamin D is universally designated the 'sunshine vitamin' because 7-dehydrocholesterol stored in the epidermal layer of the skin is photochemically converted to previtamin D3 upon solar ultraviolet B (UVB) irradiation, which then isomerizes to cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3).
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamin D, Sunlight, Vitamins

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is the RDA protein intake for maintenance of patients receiving hemodialysis?
Rationale: According to KDOQI and KDIGO clinical practice guidelines for chronic kidney disease on maintenance hemodialysis, the recommended daily dietary protein allowance is 1.2 g/kg standard body weight/day (or 1.0–1.2 g/kg/day, with >=50% high biological value) to compensate for free amino acid and peptide losses into the dialysate and hypercatabolism.
Tags: Renal Nutrition, Hemodialysis, Protein Requirements, KDOQI, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Branched chain amino acid are emphasized in enteral formulas for patients with hepatic failure because they;
Answer (Back): C. are not metabolized in the liver but in the fat and muscle
Rationale: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs: leucine, isoleucine, valine) bypass primary hepatic metabolism due to lack of hepatic BCAA aminotransferase, and are metabolized extrahepatically in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue. Providing BCAAs normalizes the plasma Fischer ratio (BCAA to aromatic amino acids: phenylalanine, tyrosine, tryptophan), competitive crossing of the blood-brain barrier, and improves hepatic encephalopathy.
Option 3: C. are not metabolized in the liver but in the fat and muscle
Option 4: D. are the essential amino acids
Tags: Hepatic Nutrition, BCAA, Hepatic Encephalopathy, Enteral Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Isoniazid, a drug used in the treatment of tuberculosis, is an agonist of _____.
Rationale: Isoniazid (INH), a primary antitubercular agent, acts as a structural antagonist of Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine). It binds pyridoxal-5-phosphate (PLP) to form an inactive hydrazone complex excreted in urine, and inhibits pyridoxal kinase, precipitating clinical peripheral neuropathy unless prophylactic pyridoxine (25–50 mg/day) is administered.
Tags: Pharmacology, Drug-Nutrient Interactions, Vitamin B6, Tuberculosis

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): During metabolism, released energy is captured and transferred by _____.
Rationale: Adenosine Triphosphate (ATP) is the universal cellular energy currency. Free energy liberated during the exergonic oxidation of macronutrients is conserved in the high-energy phosphoanhydride bonds of ATP and transferred to drive endergonic physiological work (muscle contraction, active transport, biosyntheses).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A sensible weight reducing program includes _____.
Answer (Back): B. diet, exercise and behavior modification
Rationale: The gold standard, evidence-based triad for sustainable long-term weight reduction and maintenance consists of: (1) a nutritionally balanced, hypocaloric diet, (2) regular aerobic and resistance exercise, and (3) cognitive-behavioral lifestyle modification (self-monitoring, stimulus control, cognitive restructuring).
Option 1: A. drugs that will lead to rapid weight loss
Option 2: B. diet, exercise and behavior modification
Option 3: C. use formula diets to ensure appropriate calorie intake
Option 4: D. use of herbal preparations as an adjunct to diet
Tags: Weight Management, Obesity, Behavior Modification, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): When monitoring for food allergy, which outcome should be measured?
Answer (Back): A. Reduction of food related reactions
Rationale: In the Nutrition Care Process (NCP) for food allergy management, the definitive clinical outcome indicator is the documented reduction, alleviation, or total prevention of adverse allergic clinical manifestations.
Option 1: A. Reduction of food related reactions
Option 2: B. level of knowledge about causes of food allergies
Option 4: D. Frequency of patient failure to comply with instructions
Tags: Food Allergy, Nutrition Monitoring and Evaluation, NCP

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following increase disease risk?
Rationale: Central (abdominal/visceral) adiposity (android fat distribution) is metabolically active and secretes free fatty acids, pro-inflammatory adipokines (TNF-alpha, IL-6), and resistin into the portal system, strongly predisposing to insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, systemic hypertension, and cardiovascular disease.
Tags: Nutritional Assessment, Anthropometry, Visceral Fat, Cardiometabolic Risk

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Exercise is beneficial in weight management because it _____.
I. helps regulate appetite
II. decreases BMR
III. reduces stress related eating habit
IV. increases the "set point" for fat deposit
Rationale: Regular exercise assists weight management by modulating hunger hormones (ghrelin suppression, PYY elevation) to help regulate appetite (I), preserving lean muscle mass to prevent drops in metabolic rate, and serving as a healthy emotional coping strategy to curb stress-induced emotional overeating (III). Exercise increases (not decreases) metabolic rate and lowers (not increases) the set-point.
Tags: Weight Management, Exercise Physiology, Appetite Regulation

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Called the "feasting hormone" because its release is enhanced by a high glucose level.
Rationale: Insulin is known as the 'feasting hormone' (or hormone of abundance) because postprandial elevations in blood glucose and amino acids stimulate its secretion from pancreatic beta cells, promoting nutrient storage pathways (glycogenesis, lipogenesis, and protein translation) while inhibiting catabolic pathways.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The cells that secrete the HCL in the body.
Rationale: Parietal (oxyntic) cells located in the gastric glands of the stomach fundus and corpus secrete hydrochloric acid (HCl) and intrinsic factor. Chief cells secrete pepsinogen; G-cells secrete the hormone gastrin.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which one of the following statements about ascorbic acid is INCORRECT?
Answer (Back): A. Its requirement varies with caloric intake.
Rationale: Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C) requirement does NOT vary with caloric intake; its RDA is established based on neutrophil saturation and antioxidant protection. (In contrast, thiamin, riboflavin, and niacin scale with caloric intake). Ascorbic acid reduces ferric iron to absorbable ferrous iron (B), is rapidly oxidized in the presence of Cu2+ and Fe3+ (C), and its degradation pathway produces oxalate (D).
Option 1: A. Its requirement varies with caloric intake.
Option 2: B. It facilitates the absorption of dietary iron.
Option 3: C. It is readily oxidized by divalent metal ions.
Option 4: D. It is metabolized in part of oxalate, which can form an insoluble salt calcium.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamin C, Ascorbic Acid, Iron Absorption

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A person watching TV reaches for a snack during a commercial break in response to:
Rationale: Eating prompted by environmental stimuli—such as TV food commercials, the sight or smell of food, or habitual sedentary activities—is governed by external cues rather than internal physiological hunger sensations (appetite vs. physiological hunger).
Tags: Behavior Modification, Appetite, External Cues, Nutrition Counseling

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): When expressed as a percentage of body weight, at what level of dehydration does performance level notably decrease?
Rationale: Body water deficits of 2% to 3% of body weight significantly impair aerobic athletic performance, muscular endurance, cognitive processing, and core thermoregulation, increasing cardiovascular strain and perceived exertion.
Tags: Sports Nutrition, Dehydration, Fluid Balance, Thermoregulation

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Mr. P wants to lose weight and has a BMI of 30 and a waist circumference of 41. Initially Nutritionist Dietitian should advise Mr. P to _____.
Answer (Back): A. Self-monitor and write down his food intake and physical activity
Rationale: Self-monitoring (keeping a detailed, real-time food and physical activity log) is the most effective initial behavioral assessment and intervention tool in weight management counseling. It establishes baseline caloric patterns, increases self-awareness, and identifies dietary triggers before prescribing specific caloric deficits.
Option 1: A. Self-monitor and write down his food intake and physical activity
Option 2: B. Ask his doctor for a medication to assist in weight reduction
Option 3: C. see a physician for consultation
Tags: Weight Management, Nutrition Counseling, Self-Monitoring, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the hormones is responsible for promoting appetite?
Rationale: Ghrelin is a 28-amino acid peptide hormone secreted primarily by oxyntic endocrine cells of the gastric fundus that acts on the arcuate nucleus of the hypothalamus (NPY/AgRP neurons) to stimulate appetite and meal initiation ('the hunger hormone'). Leptin and PYY suppress appetite.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Ghrelin, Appetite Regulation, Hormones

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): One of the typical symptoms of food allergies is _____.
Rationale: Acute IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reactions trigger mast cell and basophil degranulation with release of histamine and leukotrienes, causing rapid cutaneous manifestations—most classically urticaria (hives), pruritus, and angioedema.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Clinical sign/s of edema is/are _____.
Rationale: Edema is an abnormal expansion of the interstitial fluid volume manifesting clinically as palpable puffiness, swelling, tightness of the skin, and pitting on pressure in dependent extremities (pedal edema) or generalized anasarca.
Option 3: C. extreme wasting and wrinkled skin
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, NFPE, Edema, Fluid Balance

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): In patients with moderate renal insufficiency, restriction of which of the following dietary constituents slows the progression of chronic renal failure?
Rationale: In moderate chronic kidney disease (Stages 3–4), dietary protein restriction (0.6–0.8 g/kg/day) reduces glomerular hyperfiltration and blunts intraglomerular capillary hypertension, while dietary phosphorus restriction (800–1,000 mg/day) prevents hyperphosphatemia, secondary hyperparathyroidism, FGF-23 elevation, and renal osteodystrophy/vascular calcification.
Tags: Renal Nutrition, CKD, Protein Restriction, Phosphorus, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Other name for dextrose, grape sugar and blood sugar.
Rationale: D-glucose is commonly referred to as dextrose (due to its dextrorotatory optical activity), grape sugar (because of its abundance in ripe grapes), and blood sugar (as it is the primary circulating hexose monosaccharide in human blood).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is a function of a phytochemical?
Rationale: Bioactive phytochemicals (e.g., curcumin, resveratrol, epigallocatechin gallate, sulforaphane) exert potent antineoplastic effects by suppressing oncogenic signaling pathways, inhibiting tumor angiogenesis, arresting malignant cell cycles, and inducing apoptosis.
Option 2: B. Diminish activity of certain enzymes.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Sudden hyperglycemia in a person who has consistently maintained good blood glucose control can be precipitated by _____.
Rationale: Acute infection, trauma, or systemic illness triggers a massive surge of stress and counter-regulatory hormones (epinephrine, cortisol, glucagon, growth hormone) and inflammatory cytokines. These hormones induce peripheral insulin resistance and stimulate hepatic glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, precipitating acute severe hyperglycemia.
Option 2: B. conditions that lower levels of counter-regulatory hormones

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): An allergy is a hypersensitivity to a/an:
Rationale: An allergy is an immunologically mediated hypersensitivity reaction directed against a specific environmental or dietary substance known as an allergen (a specific antigen, usually an intact glycoprotein, capable of inducing IgE production and hypersensitivity).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following fruit or fruit products can easily cause drug interactions?
Rationale: Grapefruit and grapefruit juice contain furanocoumarins (such as bergamottin and 6',7'-dihydroxybergamottin) that irreversibly inhibit the intestinal cytochrome P450 3A4 (CYP3A4) enzyme system. This inhibits first-pass drug metabolism and causes substantial, unpredictable increases in bioavailability and toxicity for many medications, including statins (atorvastatin, simvastatin), calcium channel blockers, and immunosuppressants (cyclosporine, tacrolimus).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Triggers the GI secretory action.
Rationale: The intrinsic enteric nervous system, specifically the submucosal (Meissner's) plexus (the 'inner plexus' embedded in the submucosa of the intestinal wall), directly innervates glandular epithelial cells to control and trigger local gastrointestinal secretions and blood flow.
Tags: Physiology, Enteric Nervous System, Gastrointestinal Secretions

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): People at risk of dumping syndrome should avoid;
Rationale: In post-gastrectomy dumping syndrome, concentrated simple sugars and sweets (sucrose, glucose, corn syrup) create a hyperosmolar bolus that rapidly empties into the jejunum, drawing massive fluid from circulating plasma into the gut lumen (causing osmotic diarrhea, abdominal cramping, hypovolemia, tachycardia, and late reactive hypoglycemia).
Tags: Gastrointestinal, Dumping Syndrome, Simple Sugars, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is required for the absorption of calcium from the intestine and the uptake of calcium and phosphorous by the bones and teeth?
Rationale: Active Vitamin D (1,25-dihydroxycholecalciferol or calcitriol) stimulates the genomic transcription of intestinal calcium-binding protein (calbindin-D9k) and TRPV6 channels, enabling active transcellular calcium and phosphorus absorption across enterocytes, and facilitates osteoblast-mediated bone matrix mineralization.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamin D, Calcium, Bone Metabolism

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which fluid deficit would lead to a decrease of 20 - 30 % in physical work capacity?
Rationale: A body fluid deficit of 5% of body weight severely compromises intravascular circulating volume, reduces stroke volume, elevates heart rate, impairs cutaneous heat dissipation, and diminishes physical aerobic work capacity by 20% to 30%.
Tags: Sports Nutrition, Fluid Balance, Dehydration, Work Capacity

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following statement is TRUE about the sources of Vit. K?
Answer (Back): C. Most of our Vit. K is produced by the intestinal bacteria.
Rationale: While phylloquinone (Vitamin K1) is supplied by green leafy vegetables, a substantial portion of human physiological Vitamin K needs is provided by menaquinones (Vitamin K2) synthesized endogenously by normal commensal bacterial microflora (Bacteroides, Escherichia coli) in the ileum and large intestine.
Option 1: A. Rarely fund in foods so a natural deficiency develops.
Option 2: B. Found in a wide variety of foods so no deficiency occurs.
Option 3: C. Most of our Vit. K is produced by the intestinal bacteria.
Option 4: D. It is easily absorbed in the body.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamin K, Gut Microbiota, Vitamins

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is the BEST way to determine if an athlete's weight gain is muscle gain?
Rationale: Hydrostatic (underwater) weighing utilizes Archimedes' principle of water displacement to determine total body density, serving as a classic laboratory gold standard method to distinguish fat-free mass (muscle, bone) from fat mass, thereby accurately verifying true lean muscle hypertrophy.
Tags: Sports Nutrition, Body Composition, Hydrostatic Weighing, Assessment

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Preparation of formula is of utmost importance for enteral feeding. To prevent bacterial contamination, your instruction to the caregiver should include all of the following EXCEPT;
Answer (Back): D. To add a new supply of formula to an old formula to save money
Rationale: Pouring fresh enteral feeding formula into residual formula left in a hang bag ('topping off') introduces retrograde bacterial contamination and permits exponential pathogen proliferation, causing infectious gastroenteritis or enteral formula sepsis. Formula sets should be rinsed and discarded according to protocol (open systems discarded after 4-8 hours).
Option 1: A. Do not allow formula to stand longer than 4 to 8 hours at room
Option 2: B. Refrigerate prepared formula if not used immediately
Option 3: C. Prepare formula with clean hands in a clean environment
Option 4: D. To add a new supply of formula to an old formula to save money
Tags: Enteral Nutrition, Food Safety, Infection Control, Caregiver Education

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): One specific indication of enteral nutrition is:
Rationale: Severe, persistent anorexia (resulting in severe caloric deficit in a patient with a functioning gastrointestinal tract) is an established indication for enteral tube nutrition support. In contrast, mechanical bowel obstruction, active GI bleeding, and intractable diarrhea are absolute contraindications.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The recommended fiber intake is _____ grams per day.
Rationale: Standard clinical nutrition guidelines (including the Academy of Nutrition and Dietetics and ADA) recommend a dietary fiber intake of 20 to 35 grams per day for healthy adults, or approximately 14 grams per 1,000 kcal.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Mrs. Santos is scheduled to have her body fat measured by bioelectrical impedance. The test involves _____.
Answer (Back): C. attachment of electrodes to the extremities to measure resistance in the tissues
Rationale: Bioelectrical Impedance Analysis (BIA) involves introducing a safe, imperceptible, high-frequency alternating electrical current via contact surface electrodes placed on the distal extremities (hand/wrist and foot/ankle) to measure electrical resistance (impedance) across bodily water compartments, from which total body water and fat-free mass are estimated.
Option 1: A. weighing the client while she is immersed in tank of water
Option 2: B. measurement of weight and height as well as use of mathematical formula to compute body mass
Option 3: C. attachment of electrodes to the extremities to measure resistance in the tissues
Option 4: D. measurement of a skin fold on the arm or abdomen using calipers
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Body Composition, BIA, Anthropometry

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A gradual transition from IV feeding to oral diet is primarily designed to:
Answer (Back): A. ensure that nutrient needs will continue to be met
Rationale: Transitional feeding (weaning from parenteral nutrition to enteral or oral intake) requires gradual tapering while concurrently stepping up oral intake, maintaining total caloric and protein coverage until oral intake reliably provides >=60% to 75% of estimated nutrient requirements.
Option 1: A. ensure that nutrient needs will continue to be met
Tags: Nutrition Support, Parenteral Nutrition, Transitional Feeding, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): For clients who want to meet goals you set, let them consider and explain the following factors EXCEPT:
Answer (Back): A. ambitious goals are good, but overly ambitious goals are hard to follow
Rationale: In behavioral goal-setting theory, goals should be realistic, achievable, and incremental (SMART). Framing that 'overly ambitious goals are good' is contradictory and counterproductive because unrealistic targets promote failure and demotivation.
Option 1: A. ambitious goals are good, but overly ambitious goals are hard to follow
Option 3: C. regular feedback on progress improves outcomes
Option 4: D. the more specific the goal, the more likely it can be achieved
Tags: Nutrition Counseling, Goal Setting, Behavioral Theories

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A 50 year old business man was admitted to the hospital with diagnosis kidney failure. He has been following his renal diet of limited protein for the past 3 years. He's now scheduled to have a permanent fistula to be ready for hemodialysis. You will advise him that his diet will change once he is on hemodialysis to _____ exchanges.
Rationale: Prior to dialysis, non-dialyzed CKD patients follow a protein-restricted diet (0.6–0.8 g/kg/day) to slow decline of GFR and minimize uremic toxins. Once maintenance hemodialysis is initiated, dialysate losses (10–13 g amino acids per session) and dialysis-induced inflammation require liberalizing dietary protein to 1.2 g/kg/day (more protein exchanges).
Option 4: D. more high potassium fruits and vegetable
Tags: Renal Nutrition, Hemodialysis, Protein Requirements, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A dietary management that is NOT indicative of pre-dialysis
Rationale: In pre-dialysis (non-dialyzed CKD Stages 1–4), kidneys generally retain sufficient urine concentrating and volume-regulating ability, so routine fluid restriction is NOT indicated unless the patient develops congestive heart failure, severe oliguria, or refractory edema. In contrast, protein and phosphorus restrictions are hallmark pre-dialysis interventions.
Tags: Renal Nutrition, Pre-Dialysis, CKD, Fluid Management

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The simplest treatment for a food allergy is _____.
Rationale: Complete and strict dietary elimination of the causative food allergen is the single most effective, safe, and foundational treatment for food hypersensitivity.
Tags: Food Allergy, Elimination Diet, Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the hormones plays an important role in inhibiting appetite?
Rationale: Leptin is an adipokine synthesized by white adipose tissue in proportion to fat mass that crosses the blood-brain barrier to bind receptors on POMC/CART neurons in the hypothalamic arcuate nucleus, exerting tonic long-term inhibition on appetite and stimulating energy expenditure.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Leptin, Appetite Regulation, Adipokines

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the fat soluble vitamins will a NON-ambulatory elderly patient be at risk of deficiency?
Rationale: Non-ambulatory, bedridden, or institutionalized elderly individuals lack sunlight exposure, compound by aging skin having a 75% reduced capacity to synthesize 7-dehydrocholesterol and declining renal 1-alpha-hydroxylase activity, placing them at very high risk for Vitamin D deficiency and osteomalacia.
Tags: Geriatric Nutrition, Vitamin D, Micronutrient Deficiencies, Bone Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is the BEST advice to increase oral intake for a chemotherapy client who suffers from nausea and vomiting?
Answer (Back): B. Take only foods that are well liked
Rationale: For oncology patients undergoing chemotherapy with severe nausea and anticipatory aversions, clinical dietitians advise consuming whatever appealing, well-tolerated foods the patient prefers in small, frequent amounts. High-fat foods delay gastric emptying and fluids with meals cause gastric distension, both aggravating nausea.
Option 1: A. Eat slowly and chew thoroughly
Option 2: B. Take only foods that are well liked
Option 4: D. Drink plenty of fluids with the meal
Tags: Oncology Nutrition, Chemotherapy, Nausea Management, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Nutrients are _____.
Answer (Back): A. chemical elements / compounds in foods that have a specific metabolic function
Rationale: By scientific definition, nutrients are specific chemical substances (elements or organic compounds) provided by foods that are indispensable for energy, cellular structure, growth, tissue maintenance, and metabolic regulation in the body.
Option 1: A. chemical elements / compounds in foods that have a specific metabolic function
Option 2: B. metabolic control substances such as enzymes
Option 3: C. nourishing foods used to cure illnesses
Option 4: D. foods that are necessary for good health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following describes water-soluble vitamins?
Rationale: Water-soluble vitamins (B-complex vitamins and Vitamin C) are hydrophilic, dissolve freely in body fluids, are easily absorbed into the portal bloodstream, and excess amounts are readily excreted by the kidneys into urine. They have minimal tissue storage (except B12 in the liver) and rarely cause toxicity under physiological intakes.
Option 1: A. It includes vitamins C, D and E
Option 3: C. It is stored extensively in the tissues.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): All are functions of electrolytes EXCEPT _____.
Answer (Back): C. maintenance of the normal immune system
Rationale: Electrolytes (Na+, K+, Cl-, HCO3-) function fundamentally in regulating fluid compartment volumes, establishing colloidal and crystalloid osmotic pressures, maintaining physiological acid-base buffers, and conducting nerve action potentials. Adaptive and innate immune system defenses are protein- and cellular-mediated, not a direct primary function of electrolytes.
Option 1: A. maintenance of the normal fluid balance
Option 2: B. maintenance of the acid-base balance
Option 3: C. maintenance of the normal immune system
Tags: Physiology, Electrolytes, Acid-Base Balance, Fluid Balance

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): conversion of non-carbohydrate material to glucose is _____.
Rationale: Gluconeogenesis is the metabolic pathway through which glucose is synthesized de novo from non-carbohydrate carbon substrates, including glucogenic amino acids (e.g., alanine), glycerol, lactate, and pyruvate, predominantly in the liver and renal cortex.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Carbohydrate Metabolism, Gluconeogenesis, Liver

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Which of these are the characteristics of Vitamin A?
I. Fairly stable to heat.
II. Highly soluble in water.
III. Requires bile for absorption.
IV. Has a precursor. (Beta - Carotene)
Rationale: Vitamin A is fat-soluble (NOT soluble in water, making II incorrect), is relatively heat-stable under normal cooking temperatures (I), requires bile salts and dietary lipids for micellar incorporation and intestinal absorption (III), and has plant provitamin precursors such as beta-carotene (IV). Therefore, I, III, and IV are correct.
Option 2: B. I, II, III and, IV
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamin A, Fat-Soluble Vitamins, Characteristics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The NCEP Step I diet recommends _____% saturated fat/day.
Rationale:
Under the National Cholesterol Education Program (NCEP) Adult Treatment Panel guidelines:
- Step I Diet: Saturated fatty acids < 8–10% of total daily calories, cholesterol < 300 mg/day.
- Step II Diet: Saturated fatty acids < 7% of total daily calories, cholesterol < 200 mg/day.
Hence, NCEP Step I recommends 8-10% (Choice A: 10%).
Tags: Cardiovascular Nutrition, NCEP Guidelines, Lipids, Saturated Fat

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Choose the CORRECT energy value per gram.
Rationale:
According to standard Atwater general physiological fuel values:
- Carbohydrate: 4 kcal/g
- Protein: 4 kcal/g
- Fat: 9 kcal/g
- Alcohol: 7 kcal/g.
Thus, Protein - 4 kcal is the only correct statement.
Tags: Basic Nutrition, Atwater Factors, Energy Calculations, Macronutrients

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A deficiency caused by an inadequate dietary intake is a/an deficiency.
Rationale: A primary nutrient deficiency results directly from insufficient dietary intake of the nutrient. A secondary nutrient deficiency occurs when dietary intake is adequate, but underlying disease, malabsorption, genetic defects, or drug interactions impair digestion, absorption, utilization, or excretion.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Derangements like a drop of potassium, phosphorous, magnesium among severely malnourished patients will indicate which condition?
Rationale: The rapid drop of intracellular electrolytes—potassium, phosphorus, and magnesium—occurring upon aggressive nutrition repletion in a severely malnourished or starved patient is the hallmark hallmark of Refeeding Syndrome.
Tags: Refeeding Syndrome, Critical Care, Electrolytes, Malnutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The consequences of cirrhosis are primarily due to:
Answer (Back): C. liver cell damage and altered hepatic blood flow
Rationale: The clinical and metabolic complications of liver cirrhosis (ascites, varices, hepatic encephalopathy, jaundice, coagulopathy) stem pathophysiologically from two fundamental structural derangements: (1) extensive hepatocellular destruction (liver cell damage) causing impaired synthetic and metabolic capacity, and (2) diffuse fibrous scarring that alters sinusoidal hepatic blood flow, generating portal hypertension.
Option 2: B. elevated blood ammonia, amino acids and sodium levels
Option 3: C. liver cell damage and altered hepatic blood flow
Tags: Hepatic Nutrition, Cirrhosis, Pathophysiology, Portal Hypertension

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A hand dynamometer tool is used to measure the muscular strength of a person. It is used for _____.
Rationale: Handgrip dynamometry measures isometric hand muscle grip force, serving as a validated, objective functional test of skeletal muscle quality and physical performance in the Nutrition Focused Physical Exam (NFPE) to identify and classify malnutrition.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, NFPE, Handgrip Dynamometry, Functional Status

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Minerals that are involved in carbohydrate metabolism
Rationale: Chromium enhances insulin receptor tyrosine kinase activity (acting via the oligopeptide chromodulin / Glucose Tolerance Factor), and Zinc is essential for insulin crystallization, storage, and hexamer stabilization in pancreatic beta cells, as well as serving as a cofactor for glycolytic enzymes.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Micronutrients, Trace Minerals, Carbohydrate Metabolism

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Nutrition support at the end of life should be carefully based on the following EXCEPT:
Rationale: In ethical clinical nutrition and palliative care, decisions regarding artificial nutrition support at the end of life must be centered primarily on patient autonomy (the patient's documented wishes or advance directives), overall prognosis, clinical burden vs. benefit, and palliative therapy goals. Family wishes cannot override competent patient wishes or clinical futility.
Tags: Clinical Ethics, Nutrition Support, Palliative Care

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) is:
Answer (Back): D. characterized by frequent backflow of the stomach's gastric secretion into the esophagus
Rationale: Gastroesophageal Reflux Disease (GERD) is a chronic digestive disease defined by the retrograde reflux of acidic and peptic gastric contents past an incompetent or transiently relaxed lower esophageal sphincter (LES) into the esophagus, producing symptoms (heartburn, regurgitation) and mucosal injury.
Option 1: A. swelling of a portion of the stomach above the lower esophageal sphincter
Option 2: B. an erosion of the lining of the stomach caused by excess gastric acid secretions
Option 3: C. an obstruction of the lower esophagus that results in dysphagia
Option 4: D. characterized by frequent backflow of the stomach's gastric secretion into the esophagus
Tags: Gastrointestinal, GERD, Lower Esophageal Sphincter, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Which of the following is taking place in the esophagus?
I. Digestion of starch
II. Secretion of lipase
III. Peristalsis starts
IV. Activation of pepsinogen
Rationale: As a swallowed food bolus passes down the esophagus, swallowed salivary amylase (ptyalin) continues the enzymatic cleavage of starch within the bolus before encountering the acidic gastric environment. In standard exam answer keys for this set, Choice A (I and IV) is designated by the board examiners, with peristalsis facilitating transit.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A clinical sign of edema is _____
Rationale: Edema is clinically manifested by puffy, swollen tissues with skin stretched tight, and upon digital pressure leaves a depression (pitting edema) due to abnormal accumulation of extracellular interstitial fluid.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following will most likely increase iron absorption in the diets of children?
Answer (Back): C. Giving dalanghita juice and enriched cereals for snacks.
Rationale: Dalanghita (native Philippine mandarin citrus) is rich in ascorbic acid (Vitamin C). Ascorbic acid reduces insoluble ferric iron (Fe3+) to soluble ferrous iron (Fe2+) and forms stable chelates in the acidic duodenum, significantly enhancing the absorption of non-heme iron from iron-fortified cereals.
Option 1: A. Including scrambled eggs for breakfast everyday.
Option 2: B. Giving fish sticks once a week.
Option 3: C. Giving dalanghita juice and enriched cereals for snacks.
Option 4: D. Including kangkong in the diet once a week.
Tags: Pediatric Nutrition, Iron Deficiency, Micronutrients, Food Synergies

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The food label description "reduced" means:
Rationale: According to Codex Alimentarius and FDA food labeling regulations, a comparative nutrient descriptor of 'reduced' (or 'less') means the product contains at least 25% less of a nutrient (e.g., fat, sodium, calories) than the standard reference regular food.
Tags: Food Labeling, Regulatory Nutrition, FDA Claims, Dietary Standards

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Where is the gallbladder produced? (Intended: Where is bile produced?)
Rationale: This is a well-documented typographical error on the official PRC NDLE questionnaire (the paper notes 'bile?'). The intended physiological question is 'Where is bile produced?'. Bile is produced continuously by hepatocytes in the liver and transported via hepatic ducts to the gallbladder for storage and concentration.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Giving cytotoxic chemotherapeutic agents produces all of the following nutrition impact symptoms except:
Rationale: Cytotoxic chemotherapy produces gastrointestinal and nutritional toxicities: nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomatitis/mucositis, and anorexia. Hypotension is a hemodynamic disturbance, not a direct gastrointestinal nutrition impact symptom.
Tags: Oncology Nutrition, Chemotherapy, Nutrition Impact Symptoms

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is NOT a probable cause of hepatic encephalopathy?
Rationale: Precipitating triggers of Hepatic Encephalopathy include hyperammonemia (ammonia crossing the blood-brain barrier), fluid/electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia and metabolic alkalosis promoting NH3 transfer), gastrointestinal bleeding, constipation, and systemic infection. Serum cholesterol plays no causative or precipitating role.
Tags: Hepatic Nutrition, Hepatic Encephalopathy, Pathophysiology, Liver

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Mr. Romero was advised to consume only 5 exchanges of fat per day. Which of the following can he include in his daily diet?
Answer (Back): D. 1 strip of bacon + 4 ex. Oil
Rationale:
According to the Philippine Food Exchange Lists (PEL):
- 1 Fat exchange = 1 tsp vegetable oil = 1 strip bacon (crisp) = 1 tsp butter/margarine.
Therefore:
- Choice D: 1 strip bacon (1 fat exchange) + 4 exchanges oil (4 fat exchanges) = 5 fat exchanges exactly.
- Choice A: 6 tsp oil = 6 exchanges.
- Choice B: 3 tsp oil (3) + 4 ex nuts (4) = 7 exchanges.
- Choice C: 2 tsp peanut butter (~2/3 ex) + 2 tsp oil = ~2.6 exchanges.
Option 3: C. 2 tsp peanut butter + 2 tsp. oil
Option 4: D. 1 strip of bacon + 4 ex. Oil
Tags: PEL, Food Exchange System, Fat Exchanges, Calculations

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following seasonings are permitted on a sodium controlled diet?
Answer (Back): C. Chili powder, mixed peppercorn, caraway seeds
Rationale: Chili powder, whole/cracked peppercorns, and caraway seeds are natural spices containing virtually zero sodium. In contrast, meat tenderizer (MSG), teriyaki sauce, Worcestershire sauce, ketchup, and commercial tartar sauce contain very high amounts of hidden sodium.
Option 1: A. celery seeds, seasoned meat tenderizer, and teriyaki sauce
Option 2: B. dry mustard, garlic and worcestershire sauce
Option 3: C. Chili powder, mixed peppercorn, caraway seeds
Option 4: D. catsup, mustard and tartar sauce
Tags: Cardiovascular Nutrition, Sodium Restriction, Culinary Nutrition, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The body can make niacin from _____.
Rationale: The essential amino acid tryptophan serves as an endogenous precursor for nicotinic acid / nicotinamide (niacin). In human biochemistry, approximately 60 mg of dietary tryptophan can be converted into 1 mg of niacin equivalent (1 NE), a pathway requiring Vitamin B6 (PLP), riboflavin, and iron.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Vitamins, Amino Acids, Niacin

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): In general, fatty fish and seeds are rich in:
Rationale: Fatty cold-water fish (salmon, mackerel, sardines, tuna) are rich sources of long-chain omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA and DHA), while oilseeds (chia, flax, sunflower, sesame) are rich in omega-3 alpha-linolenic acid (ALA) and omega-6 linoleic polyunsaturated fatty acids.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Wasting in people with COPD is associated with all of the following EXCEPT:
Answer (Back): C. increase capacity to excrete CO2
Rationale: Pulmonary cachexia and wasting in COPD are caused by: high energetic work of breathing (increased resting energy expenditure), chronic hypoxemia and cytokine-mediated anorexia, and bronchodilator/corticosteroid side effects. COPD patients have DECREASED (impaired) capacity to excrete CO2 due to alveolar destruction and expiratory airflow obstruction, not an increased capacity.
Option 1: A. anorexia and reduced food intake
Option 3: C. increase capacity to excrete CO2
Tags: Pulmonary Nutrition, COPD, Pulmonary Cachexia, Pathophysiology

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A result of 20% -30% physical work capacity is caused by a fluid deficit of:
Rationale: Acute hypohydration corresponding to a 5% loss of body weight produces profound cardiovascular strain and impairs maximal aerobic and physical work capacity by 20% to 30%.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is the chief protein in the connective tissue and bone matrices?
Rationale: Collagen is the principal fibrous insoluble structural protein representing approximately 25-30% of total body protein, forming the primary organic matrix of bones (osteoid), tendons, ligaments, cartilage, skin, and connective tissues. (Keratin forms hair and nails; Myosin is the muscle contractile protein).
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Proteins, Collagen, Bone Matrix

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following nutrient requirement is higher in female than the male?
Rationale: The Recommended Daily Allowance (RDA) for iron in premenopausal women of childbearing age is 18 mg/day (or higher), compared to only 8 mg/day in adult men, to compensate for obligatory monthly iron losses during menstruation.
Tags: Nutrient Requirements, Iron, Female Nutrition, Micronutrients

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): There is much evidence in favor of diets high in monounsaturated fat. The potential drawback of this diet compared with diets high in complex carbohydrates is that, monounsaturated fat may result in higher _____.
Rationale: Dietary fats supply 9 kcal/gram compared to only 4 kcal/gram for complex carbohydrates. Although monounsaturated fatty acids (MUFAs, such as oleic acid in olive oil, avocados, and nuts) offer substantial cardiovascular benefits, high-MUFA diets are calorie-dense and can promote inadvertent excess caloric/energy intake and weight gain if portion sizes are not monitored.
Tags: Lipids, MUFA, Energy Density, Cardiovascular Nutrition

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A patient with respiratory failure should limit his intake of;
Rationale: Carbohydrate oxidation has a high respiratory quotient (RQ = 1.0), producing excessive carbon dioxide (CO2) that must be cleared by ventilatory effort. In respiratory failure, excess carbohydrate intake increases CO2 retention and mechanical ventilatory burden.
Tags: Pulmonary Nutrition, Respiratory Failure, RQ, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): If alcohol is consumed by a person with diabetes, it should be computed as part of _____ exchange.
Rationale: In the diabetes meal planning and food exchange system, alcohol (which provides 7 kcal/g and is metabolized primarily by hepatic oxidation into acetate/acetyl-CoA similar to fatty acids) is calculated as part of the Fat exchange list (e.g., 1 standard alcoholic drink = 2 Fat exchanges = ~90–100 kcal) so that essential carbohydrate exchanges are not omitted, which could precipitate hypoglycemia.
Tags: Diabetes Mellitus, Food Exchange System, Alcohol, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which type of fiber binds bile and therefore reduces one's risk of atherosclerosis
Rationale: Soluble, gel-forming dietary fibers (pectin, gums, mucilages, beta-glucan) bind bile acids in the lumen of the small intestine and excrete them in the feces, forcing the liver to deplete hepatic cholesterol to synthesize new bile acids, thereby lowering atherogenic serum LDL-cholesterol.
Tags: Fiber, Cardiovascular Nutrition, Cholesterol, Bile Acids

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): A trace mineral which helps maintain glucose homeostasis.
Rationale: Trivalent Chromium (Cr3+) is an essential trace mineral that enhances the physiological action of insulin by binding to the low-molecular-weight chromium-binding substance (chromodulin), amplifying insulin receptor tyrosine kinase signaling to maintain normal glucose homeostasis.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Chromium, Trace Minerals, Glucose Homeostasis

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):
Characteristics of objectives must be:
I. Specific and patient centered
II. Time bound
III. Realistic
IV. Measurable
Answer (Back): B. I, II, III and IV
Rationale: In Medical Nutrition Therapy and nutrition counseling, goal-setting follows the SMART framework: Specific, Measurable, Attainable/Realistic, Relevant/Patient-centered, and Time-bound. Thus, all Roman numerals I, II, III, and IV are essential characteristics of sound clinical objectives.
Option 2: B. I, II, III and IV
Tags: Nutrition Care Process, Nutrition Counseling, Goal Setting

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Sucrase, maltase and lactase are secreted by the _____.
Rationale: Disaccharidases—sucrase, maltase, and lactase—are brush-border enzymes embedded in the microvillar membrane of enterocytes in the small intestinal mucosa, where they hydrolyze disaccharides into monosaccharides for absorption.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The order of the three segments of the small intestines are _____.
Rationale: From the pylorus of the stomach to the ileocecal valve of the large intestine, the anatomical sequence of the three small intestinal segments is: duodenum -> jejunum -> ileum.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Absorption is the same as _____.
Rationale: Assimilation refers to the uptake and absorption of digested nutrient molecules across the intestinal mucosal barrier into the bloodstream or lymph, followed by their incorporation into living body cells and tissues.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Diet recommendations for the nephrotic syndrome includes _____.
Rationale: Nephrotic syndrome is characterized by heavy proteinuria, profound hypoalbuminemia, hyperlipidemia, and severe edema. Sodium restriction (1 to 2 g/day, or 2 to 3 g salt) is essential to manage edema and hypertension. Dietary protein is maintained at normal levels (0.8–1.0 g/kg/day); high-protein intakes (>1.2 g/kg) are contraindicated because they accelerate glomerular hyperfiltration and worsen renal damage.
Option 1: A. protein intakes that are less than the RENI
Tags: Renal Nutrition, Nephrotic Syndrome, Sodium, MNT

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Anti-cancer properties of phytochemicals include the following, EXCEPT;
Answer (Back): B. deactivation of detoxification system of the liver
Rationale: Phytochemicals (such as isothiocyanates, sulforaphane, indoles, and polyphenols) exert anti-cancer effects by INDUCING and activating Phase II hepatic detoxification enzymes, scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS), inhibiting tumor cell proliferation and angiogenesis, and inducing apoptosis. They do not deactivate hepatic detoxification systems.
Option 2: B. deactivation of detoxification system of the liver
Option 3: C. blocking of the metabolic pathway that can lead to carcinogenesis

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The diet principle that provides all the essential nutrients in sufficient amount to support health is _____.
Rationale: Dietary adequacy is the foundational diet-planning principle ensuring that a diet supplies sufficient energy and all essential nutrients to meet the physiological requirements of healthy individuals.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): There are lots of variants to vegetarianism. The very strict variant is vegan while the least strict is _____.
Rationale: A semi-vegetarian (flexitarian) diet is the least restrictive vegetarian variant because it focuses primarily on plant-based foods while occasionally incorporating poultry, fish, seafood, dairy, and eggs. Veganism strictly excludes all animal products and byproducts.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Increasing motivation through reinforcement is:
Answer (Back): C. Achieved by encouraging desirable behavior, while discouraging undesirable behavior
Rationale: In operant conditioning and behavioral counseling, reinforcement is used systematically to strengthen and maintain target healthy behaviors (positive reinforcement) while withholding reinforcement or applying corrective boundaries to extinguish maladaptive lifestyle habits.
Option 3: C. Achieved by encouraging desirable behavior, while discouraging undesirable behavior
Option 4: D. only effective in producing short-term results

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Dietary fibers are useful in preventing hypercholesterolemia because they:
Answer (Back): A. bind cholesterol containing bile acids which are eventually excreted
Rationale: Soluble viscous dietary fibers (pectin, beta-glucan, psyllium, gums) bind bile acids in the small intestine, interrupting enterohepatic circulation and causing bile acids to be excreted in feces. The liver is consequently forced to synthesize new bile acids from endogenous hepatic cholesterol pools, upregulating LDL receptors and lowering circulating serum cholesterol.
Option 1: A. bind cholesterol containing bile acids which are eventually excreted
Option 3: C. are carriers of omega-3 fatty acids

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of these fruits is a good source of Vitamin A?
Rationale: Papaya is an excellent tropical fruit source of provitamin A carotenoids (notably beta-carotene and beta-cryptoxanthin), which are enzymatically cleaved into retinal and retinol in enterocytes.
Tags: Vitamins, Vitamin A, Food Sources, Carotenoids

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which theory of counseling did you use in the following scenario: You were asked to counsel a single-parent of a two-year old due to excessive temper tantrums at meal-times. Determine which model theory for healthy eating behavior at meal-times and sharing parenting tips of this age group would be beneficial?
Rationale: Albert Bandura's Social Learning Theory (Social Cognitive Theory) emphasizes that behaviors are acquired and modified through observational learning, modeling, reciprocal determinism, and social interactions. In pediatric feeding counseling, parental role-modeling and shared peer-group learning reinforce healthy mealtime behaviors.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): The serving portion of each food on any given list provide the same amount of:
Rationale: In the Food Exchange Lists (Exchange System / PEL), foods are grouped into lists based on similarity in macronutrient composition (carbohydrates, proteins, fats). Consequently, any serving portion within a given exchange list yields approximately the same amount of energy (calories).
Tags: Food Exchange System, Meal Planning, PEL

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Mouth sores in people with HIV infection are most frequently due to:
Rationale: Due to impaired cell-mediated immunity (CD4+ T-lymphocyte depletion), patients with HIV/AIDS frequently suffer from opportunistic oral infections, most commonly oral candidiasis (thrush, Candida albicans), herpes simplex virus (HSV) stomatitis, oral hairy leukoplakia, and aphthous ulcers.
Tags: HIV/AIDS, Infectious Disease, MNT, Oral Health

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): An obese child client is on your Weight Loss Program. After the initial interview, you found out that she doesn't eat vegetables and fruits, is fond of processed foods, loves cakes and ice cream. Establishing rapport is the first thing you do. Mention the award/reward will be given to encourage the child to cooperate. Which theory of counseling is used in this kind of scenario?
Rationale: Using contingency management, positive incentives, and reward systems to motivate and reinforce dietary compliance and lifestyle modifications in children falls under rewards compensation / reinforcement theory.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Essential fatty acids includes:
Rationale: Linoleic acid (18:2 n-6) and alpha-linolenic acid (18:3 n-3) are the two true essential fatty acids in human nutrition because mammalian cells lack delta-12 and delta-15 desaturase enzymes required to introduce double bonds beyond carbon 9 from the carboxyl terminal.
Tags: Nutritional Biochemistry, Fatty Acids, Lipids, EFA

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Choose an accurate non-invasive test seen in dehydrated patients.
Rationale: Urine color assessment (using validated urine color charts) is an immediate, accurate, bedside non-invasive indicator of hydration status. Dark, concentrated amber urine reflects elevated urine specific gravity and osmolality caused by maximal renal water reabsorption under ADH stimulation in dehydration.
Tags: Nutrition Assessment, Dehydration, Fluid Balance, NFPE

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): JM is a 10 years old boy, diagnosed with Nephrotic Syndrome. His laboratory test results show that his sodium level is low, and his potassium level is borderline. What is the primary manifestation of Nephrotic Syndrome?
Rationale: The primary and initiating pathophysiological hallmark of Nephrotic Syndrome is heavy glomerular proteinuria (>3.5 g/24 hr in adults or >40 mg/m2/hr in children) caused by loss of glomerular podocyte charge and size selectivity. This massive protein leak triggers hypoalbuminemia, decreased oncotic pressure, and third-spacing edema.
Tags: Renal Nutrition, Nephrotic Syndrome, Pediatrics, Pathophysiology

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Vitamins whose requirements are dependent on a person's energy intake.
Rationale: Thiamin (B1), Riboflavin (B2), and Niacin (B3) serve as indispensable coenzymes in cellular energy metabolism (TPP, FMN/FAD, and NAD/NADP in glycolysis, Krebs cycle, and electron transport chain). Their recommended daily allowances are directly calculated per 1,000 kcal of total energy intake.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is NOT a component of bile?
Rationale: Hepatic bile consists primarily of bile salts (conjugated bile acids), phospholipids (principally phosphatidylcholine/lecithin), cholesterol, and bile pigments (bilirubin glucuronide). Sodium bicarbonate is predominantly secreted by pancreatic ductal cells in response to secretin to neutralize acidic gastric chyme in the duodenum, not a major constituent of gallbladder bile.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Digestion and absorption are coordinated by the _____.
Rationale: Gastrointestinal motility, secretomotor functions, and absorptive capacities are coordinated via neuroendocrine feedback mechanisms: the enteric and autonomic nervous systems (vagal parasympathetic and sympathetic innervation) and peptide gastrointestinal hormones (gastrin, secretin, cholecystokinin, GIP, GLP-1).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is function of the pyloric sphincter?
Answer (Back): C. Regulates the flow of partially digested food into the small intestine
Rationale: The pyloric sphincter is the smooth muscle band separating the gastric pylorus from the duodenal bulb that acts as a dynamic valve, regulating and metering the rate at which acidic, partially digested chyme empties into the duodenum.
Option 1: A. Holds food in the stomach long enough for it to be liquified
Option 2: B. Prevents the small intestines from backing up to the stomach
Option 3: C. Regulates the flow of partially digested food into the small intestine
Option 4: D. Holds food in the stomach long enough for it to be liquified

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Diverticulosis is a condition associated with:
Rationale: Chronic low-fiber intake results in small-caliber, hard stools that require high segmental intracolonic pressures to propel during peristalsis. Over decades, this excessive pressure herniates colonic mucosa through weakened areas of the muscular circular layer, forming diverticula.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Question (Front): Why is it important to regulate the release of chyme into the duodenum?

Rationale: Controlled gastric emptying through the pyloric sphincter is essential because the duodenum has a limited intraluminal volume and buffering capacity. Rapid entry of hypertonic, acidic gastric chyme causes duodenal distension, fluid shifts, cramping, and vasomotor dumping syndrome.

Hepatocytes express alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH), aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH), and the microsomal ethanol oxidizing system (CYP2E1) to metabolize ethanol, as well as Phase I and Phase II cytochrome P450 enzyme complexes to neutralize xenobiotics, drugs, and poisons for biliary or urinary elimination.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): What is the maximum amount of alcohol a man with diabetes can take per day?
Rationale: According to the American Diabetes Association (ADA) and clinical nutrition guidelines, if adult patients with diabetes choose to drink alcohol, intake should be limited to a maximum of 2 standard drinks per day for men and 1 standard drink per day for women, always consumed with food to prevent delayed nocturnal hypoglycemia.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Vitamin E acts as a _____ of free radicals.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Major organ where intermediary metabolism takes place.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): You are counseling a person with Type 1 Diabetes who intends to do regular exercise. Which of the following advise should you EMPHASIZE?

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Diet therapy for people with delayed gastric emptying most often includes;
Rationale: In gastroparesis (delayed gastric emptying), dietary fat is restricted because it stimulates cholecystokinin (CCK) secretion, which physiologically inhibits gastric motility. Meals should also be small, frequent, and semi-liquid or puréed.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of these water-soluble vitamins will increase with energy intake?
Rationale: Niacin (along with thiamin and riboflavin) functions directly as an electron carrier (NAD+/NADH and NADP+/NADPH) across all fuel catabolic pathways. Because higher caloric intake demands greater flux through glycolysis, the citric acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation, niacin requirements scale directly with total caloric expenditure.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which is considered as fuel for the gut?

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following medical nutritionals contains partially digested?

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which of the following is NOT a clinical consequence of refeeding syndrome?

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front):

Question (Front): Two activities that contribute to the basal metabolic rate are:

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics

Question (Front): The primary goal of medical nutrition therapy in diabetes is to _____.
Answer (Back): C. maintain near-normal blood glucose levels
Rationale: While cardiovascular risk reduction and weight management are vital components of comprehensive diabetes management, the primary and central therapeutic goal of MNT in diabetes is to achieve and maintain near-normal blood glucose levels (glycemic control, HbA1c < 7.0%) to prevent acute ketoacidosis/hypoglycemia and long-term microvascular and macrovascular complications.
Option 2: B. control blood lipids and blood pressure
Option 3: C. maintain near-normal blood glucose levels
Tags: Diabetes Mellitus, MNT Goals, Glycemic Control

Question (Front):
Which of the following will you advise a patient who is suffering from peptic ulcer?
I. No smoking
II. Avoid taking aspirin
III. Diet should be caffeine free
IV. Take a liberal bland diet
Answer (Back): A. I, II, III and IV
Rationale: Comprehensive MNT and lifestyle advice for Peptic Ulcer Disease (PUD) includes: smoking cessation (nicotine impairs mucosal blood flow and bicarbonate secretion), eliminating aspirin/NSAIDs (which inhibit protective prostaglandin synthesis), avoiding caffeine and decaffeinated coffee (which stimulate gastric acid secretion), and following a liberalized bland diet omitting individual trigger foods and gastric irritants.
Option 1: A. I, II, III and IV
Tags: Gastrointestinal, Peptic Ulcer, MNT, Diet Therapy

Question (Front): The patient with chronic pancreatitis benefits from the following diet-related advice:
Answer (Back): A. use enzyme replacements to improve fat absorption
Rationale: Chronic pancreatitis leads to progressive loss of pancreatic exocrine tissue, causing lipase deficiency and severe steatorrhea. Pancreatic Enzyme Replacement Therapy (PERT) taken concurrently with all meals and snacks restores lipid digestion, improves nutrient absorption, and relieves abdominal pain and diarrhea. Note: Alcohol must be strictly eliminated, not moderately restricted.
Option 1: A. use enzyme replacements to improve fat absorption
Option 2: B. follow a very low fat diet
Option 3: C. eat three meals a day and avoid snacks

Question (Front): Which of the following represents a potential affect of infection on nutritional status?
Rationale: Systemic infection stimulates inflammatory cytokines (IL-1, IL-6, TNF-alpha) and glucocorticoids, accelerating skeletal muscle proteolysis (protein catabolism) to mobilize amino acids for hepatic acute-phase protein synthesis and gluconeogenesis, producing negative nitrogen balance.

Question (Front): For the person undergoing a liver transplant:
Answer (Back): B. attention to nutrients before a transplant improves chances of recovery
Rationale: Malnutrition is present in up to 80-90% of end-stage liver disease patients awaiting transplantation and is an independent predictor of operative morbidity, prolonged mechanical ventilation, sepsis, and post-transplant mortality. Pre-transplant nutrition intervention significantly enhances graft survival and surgical recovery.

Question (Front): Ammonia is detoxified when the liver converts it to _____.
Rationale: Free neurotoxic ammonia (NH3/NH4+) produced by amino acid deamination and colonic bacterial ureases is transported to the liver, where hepatocytes convert it into non-toxic, water-soluble urea via the hepatic urea cycle (ornithine cycle) for ultimate renal clearance.

Question (Front): Which of the following results fall within the normal blood glucose levels?
Rationale: According to the American Diabetes Association (ADA) diagnostic guidelines, normal fasting plasma glucose is defined as 70 to 99 mg/dL (or 70 to 100 mg/dL). Fasting glucose from 100 to 125 mg/dL is categorized as impaired fasting glucose (prediabetes), and >= 126 mg/dL indicates diabetes mellitus.

Question (Front): Ammonia is detoxified when the liver converts it to:
Rationale: Free ammonia is metabolized exclusively via the hepatic ornithine-urea cycle into neutral, water-soluble urea, which enters systemic circulation and is filtered by renal glomeruli.

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): When renal tissue has been destroyed to a point at which it can no longer filter the blood, the following occurs _____.
Rationale: When end-stage renal disease (ESRD) develops and the glomerular filtration rate falls profoundly, kidneys can no longer clear nitrogenous wastes, electrolytes, and water. This profound intoxication of tissues and organs by accumulated nitrogenous waste products is termed uremia (uremic syndrome).

Deck Title: PRC NDLE 2021 - Nutritional Biochemistry & Clinical Dietetics
Question (Front): Which type of fiber binds bile and therefore reduces one's risk of atherosclerosis?
Rationale: Soluble viscous fiber (such as beta-glucan from oats, pectin from citrus fruits, and psyllium) forms viscous gels in the intestinal lumen that bind bile acids and dietary cholesterol, preventing micellar reabsorption and stimulating hepatic conversion of cholesterol into bile acids, reducing serum atherogenic LDL cholesterol.
